title: Sean Payton says he didn't know about the communication with Drew Brees
summary: On Monday night, a report emerged that multiple Broncos coaches had reached out to retired quarterback Drew Brees about the possibility of joining the Broncos for the AFC Championship after starter Bo Nix suffered a season-ending foot injury.
full_text: On Monday night, a report emerged that multiple Broncos coaches had reached out to retired quarterback Drew Brees about the possibility of joining the Broncos for the AFC Championship after starter Bo Nix suffered a season-ending foot injury. The report overlooked key details, such as Brees no longer being able to throw with his right arm. Most importantly, it ignored the fact that it would have been impossible to sign Brees, since he remains on the Saints' reserve-retired list. (There's also a tampering issue arising from the report that then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael contacted Brees, presumably without permission from the Saints.) Coach Sean Payton was asked if he had a comment on the report, following the Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. “No, I just know I was the odd man out, and I never heard anything about it, so it never came to anything," Payton told reporters. "I was only told about it later. I didn’t; I was just like you guys.” Even without Payton directly contacting Brees, a potential tampering issue arises if Lombardi and Carmichael did indeed contact Brees without permission from the Saints. The broader point for any retired player is this: Find a way to get released, so that you can return at any time. That's why Philip Rivers was able to rejoin the Colts late last year. Placement on the reserve-retired list complicates a potential return to play for another team — especially since he'd have to pass through waivers before signing, if his current team is willing to release him from the reserve-retired list.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken responds to Mike Tomlin: It's not Browns being Browns, it's Browns playing poorly for one week
summary: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville.
full_text: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville. "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster," Tomlin said, "the Browns is the Browns." Smith-Schuster made those words famous back in 2020, ironically before the Browns then pounded the Tomlin-led Steelers in the wild card round. But the saying has stuck in part because the Browns have had just one winning season since — and even that ended with an ugly postseason loss. Asked about Tomlin’s comments in his Monday video conference, first-year head coach Todd Monken seemed to take some exception to them. “Well, again, everybody’s afforded their opinions. That’s what you do when you go from coaching to television,” Monken said. “ We have to own that . We have to own that. We didn’t play very well. I don’t see it that way, Browns being Browns. I don’t see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn’t play well. That’s one week. That’s not Browns being Browns, that’s Browns being poorly on one week. “So, again, everybody’s afforded their opinion. And the only way to change people’s opinion is to play better. That’s a fact. We don’t want to be considered an also-ran, then we have to play better. We have to coach better, and we have to play better.” At this point, Monken is right — the only way the Browns can change their perception is by winning. We’ll see if they can at least be competitive against the Buccaneers on Sunday, though that will be unlikely if Deshaun Watson does not play any better at quarterback.
author: Myles Simmons

title: 49ers-Rams from Australia attracts 21.7 worldwide viewers
summary: With the usual Thursday night opener moving to Wednesday night, the recent Friday night international game moved to Thursday.
full_text: With the usual Thursday night opener moving to Wednesday night, the recent Friday night international game moved to Thursday. And the game between the 49ers and Rams from Australia did solid but not spectacular numbers. Via Eric Fisher of Front Office Sports , the Netflix stream attracted 18.5 million domestic viewers and 3.2 million international viewers. The U.S. number matched the YouTube audience from last year's Chiefs-Chargers game in Brazil. The foreign audience was larger this year. Given that Netflix is a paid service and the YouTube game streamed for free, that's good news — even though the YouTube numbers were widely regarded as disappointing. Last December, a pair of NFL games on Christmas generated 23.7 million U.S. viewers, on average. On one hand, the Netflix number exceeded by more than three million viewers the 2025 Thursday night average viewership on Amazon. On the other hand, the excitement of Week 1 tends to generate bigger numbers. It didn't help that the game wasn't very good. The 49ers slowly suffocated the Rams in a 27-7 game that was competitive in the first half but not in the second. Netflix will stream four more games this season. The next one comes in November, on the night before Thanksgiving. Then, Netflix will have two Christmas games for the third straight year. The slate ends on the Saturday of Week 18.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Jets WR Omar Cooper week-to-week with ankle sprain
summary: Jets first-round pick Omar Cooper appears set to miss some time after injuring his ankle in the team's Week 1 win over the Titans.
full_text: Jets first-round pick Omar Cooper appears set to miss some time after injuring his ankle in the team's Week 1 win over the Titans. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Cooper is considered week-to-week after an MRI showed he suffered a sprain. Rapoport adds that the hope is that he is able to return within the next four weeks, which suggests that the wide receiver is not considered a candidate for injured reserve as that move would rule him out for at least four games. Cooper made one catch before leaving Sunday's win and the 30-yard gain set up the first touchdown in their 23-10 victory. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams, and Arian Smith are the other wideouts on the Jets' 53-man roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons have "no updates" on Week 2 quarterback situation
summary: The Falcons are not ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 2.
full_text: ' The Falcons are not ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 2. Cooper Rush got bumped into the starting role after Tua Tagovailoa injured his oblique during practice last week and went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers. Undrafted rookie Jack Strand was the only other available quarterback because Michael Penix was inactive and head coach Kevin Stefanski said that he never considered putting Strand in against Pittsburgh. On Monday, Stefanski said, via multiple reporters, that he had "no updates" on the health of Tagovailoa or Penix. Penix tore his ACL last season and was cleared for full football activities in late August. He also said that he has no timeline in mind to settle on a starter for Atlanta's home opener against the Panthers. The Falcons will return to practice on Wednesday and the participation levels in that workout should give some idea of what direction things will go in Week 2.
author: Josh Alper

title: ESPN, NFL Network now simulcast the same Monday night pregame show
summary: For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options.
full_text: For years, NFL fans who wanted to watch a Monday Night Football pregame show had their pick of two different options. Now? Not. Monday Night Countdown, ESPN's longtime pregame show, is now shown on both ESPN and NFL Network, as a result of the deal that made ESPN the owner of NFL Media and the NFL a 10 percent owner of ESPN. It's easy to see why ESPN and the NFL see this as a good thing, a cost-cutting move that means they're only producing one show instead of two. For fans, however, fewer choices is a bad thing. Some fans preferred the NFL Network pregame show, which is now gone. And even for viewers who were watching Monday Night Countdown anyway, there are legitimate concerns that the stronger ties between ESPN and the NFL will mean even less independence in the coverage of the sport. More propaganda, less journalism. Ultimately, the ESPN-NFL Media merger wasn't done for the fans. It was done for the bottom lines of ESPN and NFL Media, who can save money on production costs when putting one show on two channels.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Todd Monken says Deshaun Watson to start Week 2: "There were really good things on film"
summary: Despite Sunday's blowout loss, the Browns will continue to start Watson at quarterback.
full_text: If you thought the Browns would stop playing Deshaun Watson after their Week 1 stinker — why? Head coach Todd Monken said in his Monday video conference that Watson is set to start the team's Week 2 matchup with the Buccaneers in Tampa on Sunday. Watson finished Sunday’s 34-10 loss 16-of-22 for 205 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Forty-six of those yards came on that TD pass to Denzel Boston, which came with 1:52 left in the fourth quarter. “It’s only been two weeks that he’s gotten all the reps,” Monken said. “And there were some really good things on film — some things that you can build on. And there were some others that — you know, operationally, we’ve got to get better at. There’s concepts that, there’s only so many looks you get from week to week, be it red zone concepts, third-down concepts. “I did think that when he had time, when he understood the concepts, he didn’t play tentative, that he let it rip. Even the touchdown at the end, sure that was garbage time, but that was on their [No.] 1 corner. That was one of their starters out there. And that was a communication between him and the receiver. So, there were a lot of things to build on. Was it perfect? Of course not, otherwise we wouldn’t have scored as few of points as we did. But I’d like to see how we can build on that. I like his week of practice last week. And I think he’s only going to continue to get better.” Monken said there wasn’t much discussion about potentially replacing Watson as QB1 after his Sunday performance. “No, just confirmed it when I looked at the tape,” Monken said. “We’ve got to play better around him. We’ve got to call it better. And he’s got to play better. “Our inability to function consistently as an offense was a byproduct of we — coaching and playing.” While Watson threw an interception to end Cleveland’s first drive, Monken said he didn’t feel like the quarterback got tentative when it came to throwing downfield after that play. “I would say that some of those weren’t called,” Monken said. “[T]here were times where we were trying to push the ball down the field and he did have a missed throw once we moved the pocket one time. But I know right before halftime, he made two great throws that put us in position. And then we got a couple of holding calls that had nothing to do with Deshaun. “So, without watching the tape, you could say that — you could say, hey, he looked a little tentative there. And it’d be like, no, not really. Really, we just didn’t call certain routes to push it down the field, or we didn’t execute.” The real issue, according to Monken, is that the club had “too many Browns hurting Browns moments.” “And then even as we got later in the game, I did not see that one bit — that he was tentative in terms of trying to throw it down the field,” Monken said. “Sure, there’s a couple of times maybe he could’ve pumped it down there. But in my mind, I didn’t see that.” Maybe we’ll all see something different in Week 2 when Cleveland plays Tampa Bay.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks say Sam Darnold's "very unique" injury has "no firm timeline"
summary: Seattle offers more transparency than the injury report requires.
full_text: The silver lining in the dark cloud of a quarterback injury is the potential strategic advantage it can create. And the Seahawks seem to be leaning fully into the potential uncertainty flowing from Sam Darnold's Week 1 mishap, which reportedly caused a strained glute tendon. Via Andrew Destin of The Athletic , a Seahawks spokesperson said Monday that Darnold has a " very unique, soft-tissue injury .” The Seahawks call it "short term," but they also acknowledged there is “no firm timeline.” On Sunday, we reported that Darnold could be out four to six weeks . The Seahawks have no obligation to say anything about Darnold, beyond the rules of the injury report. And that's a basic, bare-bones mandate — whether and to what extent he practiced on three days before a given game (limited or full) and, in the final report, whether he's questionable, doubtful, or out. Teams love to force opposing defenses to prepare for multiple quarterbacks. If Darnold does enough on Wednesday, Thursday, and/or Friday to be described as participating in practice on a "limited" basis, they can keep the Cardinals guessing as to whether it will be Darnold or Drew Lock on Sunday. And the Seahawks can keep doing that until Darnold returns. Whatever the specific problem, it was sufficiently unique and confounding to result in up to four second opinions , as Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported on Sunday. The thinking is they'll be cautious with Darnold, given that their team is good enough to win without him — and given the risk that he could suffer an aggravation that extends his absence.
author: Mike Florio

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans defense: I don't believe in hype, this isn't 2025, we have to earn it
summary: Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run.
full_text: Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run. But then Week 1 happened, with the Texans letting up 409 yards and 36 points in the loss to the Bills. Buffalo does have one of the league’s best quarterbacks in Josh Allen and continuity on offense with former coordinator Joe Brady getting promoted to head coach. So the Bills have the potential to do that to many teams. Still, it was a disappointing opening for a team that finished No. 1 in yards allowed and No. 2 in points allowed last year. So did the Texans buy into the offseason hype too much? Did they consume the proverbial rat poison? “I don't know,” head coach DeMeco Ryans said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. “You have to ask those guys about the hype. I don't believe in hype. You've heard me stand here many times and talk about people talking about how great the defense was. Yeah, that was 2025. You don't just line up, and it's 2026, and just because you were good last year, you got to go out and make the plays. We made plays. “The difference in this game on Sunday, versus the time we played the guys last year, we took the ball away three times. We go into this game, we don't take the ball away at all. We turn the ball over two times and we don't play smart defensively. We're not where we're supposed to be. We know the quarterback is going to scramble out to our left — if we don't stay out to our left and the quarterback runs for a touchdown, they're going to make plays.” Ryans added that whatever Houston does this year, it’s not about how good the unit has been in the past. “You have to put your stamp each and every year on who you're going to be,” Ryans said. “This is a new team. This isn't 2025. You have to go earn it. That's every year in the league, you have to go prove yourself. You can talk about it all you want to, how good you want to be, what are you going to do. You have to go out and make plays. “That's always been my message. My message never changes. Talk never matters. When the ball is snapped, what are you doing?” The Texans will be challenged defensively once again in Week 2, as the Bengals will be in town to face the club at 1 p.m. ET.
author: Myles Simmons

title: PFT's Week 2 2026 NFL power rankings
summary: The champs hang on, barely.
full_text: 1. Seahawks (last week No. 1; 1-0): They can win with Drew Lock. It's unknown how long they'll have to try to do that. 2. Bills (No. 5; 1-0): If winning a regular-season game got Joe Brady to take off his shirt, he'll be butt naked if they win in the playoffs. 3. Bears (No. 6; 1-0): The 59 offense is possibly better than the 46 defense. 4. Texans (No. 3; 0-1): Scoring 31 points should be more than enough for that defense. 5. Jaguars (No. 9; 1-0): They won 34-10, and it felt way more lopsided than that. 6. Ravens (No. 10; 1-0): Derrick Henry may never lose a step. 7. Bengals (No. 11; 1-0): In past years, they would have fully blown a 27-10 lead. 8. Chiefs (No. 13; 1-0): Kenneth Walker III earned every penny of his contract in his debut, and then some. 9. Eagles (No. 8; 1-0): A Week 1 escape vs. the Commanders answered no questions about whether they'll be true contenders. 10. 49ers (No. 15; 1-0): They turned the page decisively on all of those bizarre offseason storylines. 11. Rams (No. 2; 0-1): They're already all alone in last place of the NFC West. 12. Broncos (No. 4; 0-1): Maybe they should have tried to get Drew Brees to come back for last night's game, too. 13. Patriots (No. 7; 0-1): Fortunately, blowing it twice in the same game counts as only one loss. 14. Lions (No. 14; 1-0): The Lions had better hope the Saints are destined to be really good this year. 15. Vikings (No. 19; 1-0): For the second straight year, the Vikings woke up just in time to get a key division win in Week 1. 16. Giants (No. 20; 1-0): Jaxson Dart is the real deal, as long as he can stay healthy. 17. Steelers (No. 18; 1-0): For the second time in three years, T.J. Watt personally delivered a win over the Falcons in Week 1. 18. Cardinals (No. 32; 1-0): Jacoby Brissett is better than you realize. 19. Chargers (No. 12; 0-1): Who's got it better than us? Don't ask. 20. Packers (No. 16; 0-1): Matt LaFleur should be very happy he got that extension. 21. Saints (No. 24; 0-1): They may already be the best team in the division. 22. Cowboys (No. 17; 0-1): Like every year, the offseason's delusion gets a hard dose of reality. 23. Panthers (No. 21; 0-1): The Panthers have only themselves to blame for giving the Bears the pick that became Caleb Williams. 24. Buccaneers (No. 22; 0-1): The Browns are the perfect antidote to a Week 1 clunker. 25. Colts (No. 23; 0-1): They get plenty of hype every year, and they ultimately don't deliver. 26. Jets (No. 29; 1-0): Welcome back, Geno. 27. Raiders (No. 30; 1-0): They started 1-0 last year, too. 28. Commanders (No. 27; 0-1): At least they didn't get blown out. 29. Falcons (No. 25; 0-1): Maybe they should have just kept Kirk Cousins. 30. Titans (No. 26; 0-1): It could be another long year in Nashville. 31. Dolphins (No. 28; 0-1): They aren't tanking; they're just not good. 32. Browns (No. 31; 0-1): Prediction — Dillon Gabriel will be the starter by Week 10.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay: We thought Myles Garrett's knee injury was something he could work through
summary: Before Sunday's games kicked off, there was big news involving a team that had opened its season earlier in the week.
full_text: Before Sunday's games kicked off, there was big news involving a team that had opened its season earlier in the week. Rams defensive end Myles Garrett needs knee surgery and will miss at least four games because he'll be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. The news came after Garrett made no impact in last Thursday's loss to the 49ers and cited his health — his practice time was limited all summer because of the knee — as a reason for his ineffectiveness. On Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay said, via multiple reporters, that the team thought the injury was ""something that he would be able to work through." "Thought we would take an approach where he'd be feeling good enough to go contribute positive change and be the player that he's capable of," McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. "That wasn't the case. And so the next right thing for us is to be able to get this thing fixed." McVay said the team will not have a firm idea about Garrett's timeline to return to action until after the surgery. They know that it will be at least four games, however, and they know that their margin for error got a lot slimmer with or without him thanks to their dud in the opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker runs for 60-yard TD on fourth down
summary: The Chiefs needed 1 yard on a fourth-down play at their own 40.
full_text: ' The Chiefs needed 1 yard on a fourth-down play at their own 40. They got 60. Kansas City's prize offseason acquisition, Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, got loose around the right side after Broncos cornerback Riley Moss missed the tackle. Safety Brandon Jones was the only defender who had a chance to stop Walker after that and appeared to have the angle. He didn't. Walker has 16 carries for 149 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs' debut, the second-most yards of his career. He had 23 carries for 167 yards and two touchdowns in his sixth career game, which was against the Chargers. Walker is 4-for-4 on third-and-1 or fourth-and-1 tonight. The Chiefs lead 21-7.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bo Nix throws TD on Broncos' second drive to forge a tie
summary: Bo Nix didn't get his season off to the best start, throwing an interception that set up the Chiefs at the Denver 46.
full_text: Bo Nix didn't get his season off to the best start, throwing an interception that set up the Chiefs at the Denver 46. The Broncos quarterback responded on the next drive, though. He completed passes of 13, 4, 8, 11 and 19 yards on his five passes on the second possession. The 19-yarder was a touchdown throw to Evan Engram. It tied the game 7-7. Nix is now 5-of-6 for 55 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Wide receiver Pat Bryant has three catches for 32 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: With 42 points in Broncos-Chiefs, the Week 1 scoring record will be broken
summary: Through 15 games, 750 points have been scored.
full_text: Led by the Bears' 59-point explosion in Charlotte, the NFL's first week of the season has seen pinball machine-level scoring. And the all-time Week 1 record is in reach. Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports , the 750 total points scored through 15 games fall only 41 short of the all-time Week 1 record. So with 42 or more between the Broncos and Chiefs on Monday night, the record will fall. In his first Week 1 without coaching one of the NFL's 32 teams since 2006 (when he was the Vikings' defensive coordinator), Mike Tomlin shared his thoughts on the matter on NBC. He pointed to the current methods of practice and preparation. "There's less violence in team development," Tomlin said. "There are less padded practices. And even the drills that they do are more geared toward skill development, 7-on-7, and things of that nature. Defenses spend less time shedding blocks and tackling than they used to 25 years ago when I came in the league." Tomlin has also said that mobile quarterbacks have an edge early in the year, because defenders aren't allowed to tackle quarterbacks in practice. The NFL likes high-scoring games. Over the years, the rules have been tweaked to encourage more of it. Which means that there surely will be a press release on Tuesday with all sorts of statistics about the scoring in the Week 1 games. And, with at least 42 points tonight, a headline that Week 1 of the 2026 season was the highest-scoring Week 1 of all time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drew Brees couldn't have unretired to play for Broncos in AFC Championship
summary: Brees remains on the Saints' reserve-retired list, and he couldn't have returned that last in the season.
full_text: Sometimes, facts get in the way of a good story. On Monday night, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that quarterback Drew Brees considered emerging from retirement to play for the Broncos in the AFC Championship, given the injury that happened to starter Bo Nix late in the divisional-round win over the Bills. There's only one problem with that. Brees, as PFT has confirmed, remains on the Saints' reserve-retired list. A retired player must return by the Tuesday after Week 13 in any given year. After that, he can't play for anyone. Then there's the fact that the Saints would have had to release Brees from the reserve-retired list. He then would have been subject to waivers. That doesn't mean the Broncos didn't talk to Brees, as Schefter reports. If, however, then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael spoke to Brees without permission from the Saints, it would have been tampering. Which leads to the next question. Will the league investigate the Broncos for tampering, based on Schefter's report? Even without a complaint from the Saints, the league could take action. It never got to the point at which the Broncos or Brees realized that the rules would block the move, because Brees had "discomfort" in his wrist. Then there's the fact that Brees has said he can’t throw at all with his right arm due to his shoulder injury from 2005 — and that he throws better with his left. So while the whole thing sounds good, it's a big, fat nothing burger which, if anything, will get the Broncos in hot water for tampering with a player whose rights remain with another team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Kenneth Walker, Chiefs run by Broncos 31-10 in Patrick Mahomes' return
summary: Walker, who had a career-high 173 rushing yards, had more totals (191) than the Broncos had as a team (176).
full_text: Kenneth Walker shared carries with Zach Charbonnet in Seattle. He is the man in Kansas City. With Patrick Mahomes returning nine months after tearing his ACL and LCL, the Chiefs leaned on Walker and their run game in a 31-10 shellacking of the Broncos. The Chiefs threw 27 passes for 184 yards and ran 38 times for 220 yards. It was the third-most rushing yards for an Andy Reid team in Kansas City. Walker, the Super Bowl LX MVP who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, ran for 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries and caught three passes for 18 yards and a touchdown. It was the most rushing yards in his career, topping the 167 he had in his sixth career game. Walker had more yards from scrimmage (191) than the Broncos had as a team (176). Mahomes ran for a 15-yard touchdown and threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Rashee Rice and a 2-yard touchdown pass to Walker, but he was only 15-of-27 for 184 yards and threw an interception. Bo Nix had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day in his first game with Davis Webb as his playcaller and in his return from a season-ending ankle injury. The Broncos quarterback threw an interception and lost a fumble — and nearly lost another — while completing 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards with a touchdown and an interception. His touchdown went 19 yards to Evan Engram, who led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards. The Broncos, who trailed only 14-7 at halftime, had only 15 carries for 61 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Travis Kelce now second all-time in receiving yards for a TE
summary: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's longest reception last season was 44 yards.
full_text: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's longest reception last season was 44 yards. His second catch of 2026 went 59 yards. It was his longest reception since 2021, when he had a 69-yard catch against the Chargers in a Thursday night game. On the catch, Kelce passed Jason Witten for second all-time in receiving yards by a tight end with 13,067. Tony Gonzalez holds the record with 15,127. Kelce got the Chiefs to the 4, with Jahdae Barron saving the touchdown. They had to settle for Harrison Butker's chip-shot, 28-yard field goal. The Chiefs lead 24-10.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean Payton: Broncos' loss starts with me, starts with our coaching staff
summary: Payton handed off play calling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb for the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs.
full_text: Broncos head coach Sean Payton was not happy with anyone on the team, least of all himself, after Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Chiefs. "Obviously not a great evening. Didn't do a lot well at all in the game," Payton said. "That starts with me, that starts with our coaching staff. I thought they won, really, in every phase." Payton handed over play calling to offensive coordinator Davis Webb, and Payton was asked afterward whether it was especially frustrating not to be in control of the offense. "As a head coach, always, whether you're calling the plays or not — regardless of who's calling the plays, when you have a game like that and you're the head coach, it's frustrating, it's disappointing. I don't know that the feeling is any different whether you're calling them or not, honestly," Payton said. The Broncos' two running backs, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, combined for just 11 carries for 54 yards. Payton said he would have liked to see more running the ball, but he wasn't necessarily blaming Webb for that. Payton noted that the Broncos consistently found themselves in long-yardage passing situations and were trailing for the entire second half. "Our third down numbers weren't good, our rushing numbers weren't good, pick your spot," Payton said. "Lot of long yardage, lot of throws, not enough runs." Asked how he'll evaluate Webb as a play caller going forward, Payton said he'll review his performance the way he would a player's. "No different than a player, just evaluating the first quarter, the game, and then making the corrections and learning," Payton said. The Broncos have a lot of corrections to make.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Patrick Mahomes: Rushing TD gave me confidence I could be myself
summary: Mahomes also threw two TDs in his return from a torn ACL.
full_text: One of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes's greatest gifts on the football field has been his ability to make plays with his feet when things break down and whether he'd be able to do that after last season's torn ACL was one of the biggest questions around his return to action on Monday night. It didn't take long for Mahomes to show that he still has that part of his game. On the 10th play of Kansas City's opening drive, Mahomes took off for a five-yard touchdown run only to see the play get called back for a holding penalty. Mahomes repeated the feat from 15 yards out on the next play and the Chiefs were on their way to a resounding 31-10 win over the Broncos. In his postgame press conference, Mahomes said that "gave me that confidence that I can go out there and be myself." “Physically, I think that’s the moment ," Mahomes said. "I want to get some of these passes down the field a little bit more — I think that’ll help me out mentally and kinda get back in the rhythm of things. That was definitely the moment, physically, to say all this work has paid off. I didn't feel anything. It’s still a process, I got to still keep getting better and better, but this is obviously a great first week." Mahomes ran seven times for 23 yards overall and was 15-of-27 for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception through the air. Those numbers don't jump off the page the way some of his past performances do, but context matters and the context of Monday night made it everything that the Chiefs could have hoped to see from their quarterback.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker: Means a lot that the Chiefs trust me
summary: Kenneth Walker played his first game with the Chiefs on Monday night and head coach Andy Reid made it clear right off the bat that the free agent addition is going to be playing a major role in the offense.
full_text: Kenneth Walker played his first game with the Chiefs on Monday night and head coach Andy Reid made it clear right off the bat that the free agent addition is going to be playing a major role in the offense. After rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane intercepted Broncos quarterback Bo Nix to end Denver's first possession, Reid called four straight runs with Walker. The fourth of them was a fourth down conversion and Walker would get three more carries on the opening drive before Patrick Mahomes ended it with a touchdown run. That set the Chiefs on their way to a 31-10 win and Walker would end the night with 26 total touches. "It means a lot," Walker said. "It means they trust me . It’s good to feel that way." Walker's touches resulted in 191 yards and two touchdowns, including a 60-yard lightning bolt on another fourth down early in the third quarter. Reid called that run "a thing of beauty" on a memorable night for the new Chief. "You never know, going in, how many times you're going to give him the ball," Reid said. "That’s not a calculated thing, you gotta be making yards. For him to play the way he did, I thought it was spectacular. It was something you hope for, and you got to see it, where he was the main guy. Did a great job with it.” Walker's final game with the Seahawks was Super Bowl LX and he was named the MVP of that victory. His first game with the Chiefs carried a little less weight, but he left just as strong an impression on those who were watching him in action.

title: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane to have MRI on shoulder
summary: Chiefs first-round pick Mansoor Delane had a brief, but eventful NFL debut on Monday night.
full_text: Chiefs first-round pick Mansoor Delane had a brief, but eventful NFL debut on Monday night. Delane recorded his first interception as a pro when he snagged a pass from Broncos quarterback Bo Nix on the third play of the game. That would be the last contribution of the night for the rookie cornerback, however. Delane went to the locker room with a shoulder injury during the Broncos' second offensive possession. Head coach Andy Reid did not have an update on his condition after the game and Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that he will have an MRI on Tuesday. Garafolo adds that X-rays were negative and that there is hope that Delane, who also dealt with a shoulder injury in the spring, emerged with a sprain. Tuesday's test should provide a better picture of how long it will be before he's back in the Kansas City secondary.

title: Mike LaFleur: Confidence is great, but we have to reset and get back to work
summary: The Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of Week 1, but Monday wasn't a day for reveling in their 26-14 win over the Chargers.
full_text: The Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of Week 1, but Monday wasn't a day for reveling in their 26-14 win over the Chargers. Head coach Mike LaFleur's message was about the next game on the schedule rather than on rehashing all that went right in his Arizona debut. The Cardinals will face the Seahawks in Week 2 and the coach said that he is drilling down on the message that the Cardinals have to start back from square one as they prepare to host the defending champs. "Confidence is great, but like I told them today, 'We got to reset and get right back to work ,'" LaFleur said, via the team's website. "This is a week-to-week league, and your goal is to go 1-0 every weekend. We're not going to talk anything past that. Obviously we got the result, but we're right back to work." LaFleur's directive met a willing recipient in wide receiver Kendrick Bourne. He acknowledged that "building from success is better" than the alternative, but added that the team has to hone "little details" in order to be more than a one-week wonder.

title: Sunday Ticket prices increase, while NFL decreases the number of Sunday afternoon games
summary: A quarter-century ago, NFL Sunday Ticket felt like a modern miracle to football fans.
full_text: A quarter-century ago, NFL Sunday Ticket felt like a modern miracle to football fans. What once was an impossible dream, being able to watch any NFL game you wanted on Sunday afternoon, was now a reality. Fans who could previously only watch a game or two on Sunday could now have their pick of more than a dozen. It was an astonishing luxury to have all those games just a remote click away. Sunday Ticket is still a popular item for football fans, but it has lost some luster. There are now so many opportunities to watch the NFL, on so many days of the week, that it's much easier for fans to feel like they're getting their fill by watching only the games that air on prime time or on their local affiliates on Sunday afternoon, without needing Sunday Ticket. In 2002, the first season when the NFL had 32 teams, there were 17 Monday night games, 16 Sunday night games, three Thursday games and five Saturday games. Everything else was on Sunday afternoon. In 2025, there were 21 Monday night games, 18 Sunday night games, six Sunday morning international games, 21 Thursday games (including three on Christmas Day), six Saturday games and two Friday games. Far fewer games were on Sunday afternoon. So for the 2002 season, 215 of the NFL's 256 games (84 percent) were on Sunday afternoon. By 2025, when the season was one week longer, only 198 of 272 games (73 percent) were on Sunday afternoon. Many Sunday Ticket subscribers get the service because they want to watch their favorite team, but don't live in their favorite team's market. But Sunday Ticket is increasingly unnecessary for fans of popular teams that are frequently shown on national television. Last year the Chiefs and Cowboys each played eight games that were either on Sunday night or another day of the week, and many of their Sunday afternoon games were shown across most of the country by Fox or CBS. If you're a Chiefs fan outside Kansas City or a Cowboys fan outside Dallas, it's a rare week when you need Sunday Ticket to watch your team. And missing a game just isn't as big a deal today as it was in the early days of Sunday Ticket because there are so many opportunities to see what you're missing: If you have RedZone channel, you'll see all the big plays from every game, and even if you don't have RedZone, highlights are all over social media. As the necessity of Sunday Ticket decreases, its prices increase: In 2023, YouTube took Sunday Ticket over from DirecTV, which had it from its inception. According to the Wall Street Journal , YouTube has increased the price of Sunday Ticket by almost 30 percent while the number of games available has declined. The biggest NFL fans, the ones who love nothing more than spending a Sunday afternoon watching multiple games on multiple screens, will keep paying. But for a lot of fans, more money for fewer games is increasingly looking like a bad deal.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Matt LaFleur saw "protection busts that should not and cannot happen" on Vikings film
summary: Packers quarterback Jordan Love was pressured relentlessly by the Vikings' defense in Sunday's 39-22 loss, and Matt LaFleur said after watching the film that the pass protection needed to be a lot better.
full_text: Packers quarterback Jordan Love was pressured relentlessly by the Vikings' defense in Sunday's 39-22 loss, and Matt LaFleur said after watching the film that the pass protection needed to be a lot better. "I saw some of the things we have to clean up," LaFleur said. "What’s disappointing is, we had a few protection busts that should not and cannot happen. We knew that was the challenge going in. They were gonna give some tough looks. That’s the toughest test you’re going to face Week 1, to play that defense in that environment. I thought there was some really good stuff, but when your quarterback gets hit 15 times, that's too many times. There are some things we could do schematically that we've got to do a better job with and there are some things we have to go out and execute. But we have to have everybody on the same page if we want to give ourselves a chance." LaFleur also noted that the Packers' passing game had several explosive plays when they took advantage of the Vikings' blitzing. Love finished with 387 passing yards and an impressive average of 18.4 yards per completion, but ultimately the Vikings' defense got to Love too often. "We had some great moments when we feasted on it, certainly, but at the end of the game when we needed to make plays, they did what they do," LaFleur said. What the Vikings do under defensive coordinator Brian Flores is relentlessly pressure the quarterback, and that happened a lot on Sunday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Monday Night Football: Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime
summary: Patrick Mahomes isn't completely back from his knee injury, but he has accounted for two touchdowns and the Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime.
full_text: Patrick Mahomes isn't completely back from his knee injury, but he has accounted for two touchdowns and the Chiefs lead the Broncos 14-7 at halftime. Mahomes ran for a 15-yard touchdown on the Chiefs' first series. The 10-play, 46-yard drive was set up by rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane's interception of Bo Nix on the third play. The Chiefs had only 15 plays for 39 yards on their next three possessions before going 80 yards in 10 plays. Rashee Rice had a 13-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown on a pass from Mahomes. Mahomes is only 8-of-18 for 62 yards and a touchdown after starting 2-for-12. He has completed a pass to six different wide receivers. He also has two rushes for 23 yards and a touchdown. Mahomes was a long shot to play the season opener after tearing the ACL and LCL in his left knee on Dec. 14. He underwent reconstructive surgery the following day. The Chiefs, though, have leaned on their running game and their Super Bowl MVP running back. Kenneth Walker has 14 carries for 89 yards, tying the most rushes in the first half of a game started by Mahomes, and also has two catches for 16 yards. The Chiefs have outgained the Broncos 182 to 113. Nix is 12-of-17 for 98 yards with a touchdown and an interception, with Pat Bryant catching four passes for 42 yards. Evan Engram scored on a 19-yard reception. The Broncos have only six rushes for 23 yards.

title: NAACP president Derrick Johnson will appear on ESPN to discuss Protect College Sports Act
summary: After ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the Protect College Sports Act, with no opposing view offered, the NAACP challenged ESPN to provide its president, Derrick Johnson, with a similar opportunity this weekend, when College GameDay goes to Oxford, Mississippi.
full_text: After ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the Protect College Sports Act, with no opposing view offered, the NAACP challenged ESPN to provide its president, Derrick Johnson, with a similar opportunity this weekend, when College GameDay goes to Oxford, Mississippi. Johnson will appear on ESPN, but not on Saturday. Via John Ourand of Puck , ESPN has booked Johnson to appear on Tuesday's SportsCenter at 6:00 p.m. ET. ESPN offered airtime on Tuesday, in the event the Senate votes on the bill before Saturday. Regardless, it will be a much smaller audience than the GameDay viewership. And even if the Senate votes by Saturday, the bill will still go to the House of Representatives. The only way to truly balance Saturday's gesture would be to give someone from the opposing side the same runway Cruz received on Saturday. At this point, of course, it's more about P.R. and less about truly presenting the opposing view. Based on Disney's lobbying efforts, the company wants the bill to pass.
author: Mike Florio

title: Landon Dickerson: I was a complete liability; I should not be out there until healthy
summary: The Eagles will place left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve with a knee injury.
full_text: The Eagles will place left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve with a knee injury. Dickerson appeared on WIP's "Players Lounge Show" as news hit that he was headed to IR with what he described as a bone bruise in his right knee. He said he "played like shit" in the Eagles' 24-22 win over the Commanders on Sunday. “I was a complete liability yesterday," Dickerson said, via Alexis Chassen of bleedinggreennation.com. "Again, that was my fault. I know I said earlier in camp I shouldn’t be out there until I feel healthy. A few weeks ago, [I] got rolled up on in practice. I thought as weeks went by it would get better. It didn’t, and we kind of went out there and finally got some imaging on it today, figured out what was wrong with it. "Really the best plan going forward is to put me on IR, so I can get this thing better to have a good stretch at the back end of the season versus kind of what happened last year, go out there limping through 18 weeks. I don’t think anyone wants to see that again because that was just ugly. I don’t want to do that again, because that was just some BS.” Dickerson underwent surgery in August 2025 to repair an injured meniscus and appeared in 15 games, though he later admitted he could have used more rehab time. He went to Columbia for stem cell therapy this offseason. Drew Kendall, a fifth-round pick in 2025, could replace Dickerson.

title: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane questionable to return with shoulder injury
summary: Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane intercepted Bo Nix on his third career play.
full_text: Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane intercepted Bo Nix on his third career play. He was in the training room while the Chiefs were on the field for the Broncos' second drive. The Chiefs list him as questionable to return. Chiefs linebacker Cooper McDonald injured a knee while covering a kickoff after Patrick Mahomes' 15-yard touchdown run. He also is questionable to return with a knee injury that is being further evaluated.

title: Mansoor Delane's INT sets up Patrick Mahomes' TD run
summary: Patrick Mahomes is still Patrick Mahomes.
full_text: Patrick Mahomes is still Patrick Mahomes. If there was any doubt about his knee, he answered it on the Chiefs' first drive. The quarterback ran for a 15-yard touchdown, giving the Chiefs a 7-0 lead. Mahomes tore the ACL and LCL in his left knee on Dec. 14 during a Week 15 game against the Chargers and underwent reconstructive surgery the following day. He ran for a 5-yard score on the previous play, but both tackles were called for holding. Tight end Travis Kelce got away with a hold on Mahomes' touchdown run that counted. Andy Reid had vowed to run the ball more this season, and the Chiefs did that on their first drive of 2026. They ran on eight of their 10 plays, picking up 57 yards. Kenneth Walker, the Super Bowl LX MVP, had seven carries for 32 yards. Mahomes threw two passes and completed one for 9 yards to Xavier Worthy. The Chiefs started the drive on the Denver 46 after rookie first-round pick Mansoor Delane picked Bo Nix and returned it 5 yards.

title: Eagles put Landon Dickerson on injured reserve
summary: Eagles guard Landon Dickerson will miss at least the next four weeks.
full_text: Eagles guard Landon Dickerson will miss at least the next four weeks. Dickerson is going on injured reserve, according to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer . In Sunday's opener against the Commanders, Dickerson had a rough day in pass protection, although Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni praised his run blocking. Although the exact nature of Dickerson's injury has not been reported, it appears Dickerson was playing through something, and he and the team have now decided he needs at least a month to get healthy. Dickerson said this offseason that he has rethought his approach to playing through injuries, although he denied talk that he was thinking about retiring because of the physical toll that football has taken on his body. The 27-year-old Dickerson was a second-round pick of the Eagles in 2021 and is a three-time Pro Bowler. The Eagles will likely go with either Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin at left guard while Dickerson is out.

The Carolina Panthers ' defense is awful.
The Chicago Bears will break the single-season scoring record.
The Houston Texans ' vaunted defense is now a sieve.
Same for the Denver Broncos .
The Dallas Cowboys are toast.
The Green Bay Packers won't ever hold a lead.
On and on it goes. The Week 1 overreaction bucket is full. Don't be guilty of buying into any of it.
Be more like NFL coaches talking to their teams today: It's just one week. Move on.
Week 1 is full of teases over the years. Remember when the Las Vegas Raiders went to Foxborough and beat the New England Patriots in Week 1 last year. All the Pats did was get to the Super Bowl , while the Raiders were a season-long disaster in 2025.
So don't fall victim to the overreactions.

That doesn't mean there aren't changes. How can the Los Angeles Chargers not fall after losing at home to the Arizona Cardinals ? The Dallas Cowboys looked terrible on defense Sunday night in losing to the Giants , so they drop a few.
I just want to be cautious that one week won't greatly impact my rankings. One thing that didn't change is Miami in the bottom spot. The Dolphins didn't look good in their loss to the Raiders, but the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans have the look of teams that will challenge Miami all year long for the cellar.
Then agin, it's just one week.

title: Six lessons learned from Week 1: Caleb Williams is taking another leap, don't forget about Trevor Lawrence
summary: Plus, Kenneth Walker III might just be the answer to the Chiefs' biggest problem
full_text:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season was many things, but it certainly wasn't boring. The highest-scoring opening weekend in league history included a 56-39 offensive bonanza between the Bears and the Panthers and plenty of other eye-popping numbers. The Bills scored 36 points against the Texans , who were expected to have the best defense in the NFL this year, but the Texans put up 31 themselves after a tough finish to 2025 for C.J. Stroud, which might have been just as unexpected. The Ravens scored 41 points as Lamar Jackson looked excellent in his new offense, and the Lions held off the Saints by the skin of their teeth despite a 410-yard day from Tyler Shough .
And then Monday night. Oh, baby. The Chiefs might just be back.
Amid all the scoring, drama and winners and losers, we can sift through Week 1 and learn lessons to carry forward. Here's what we learned through the first weekend.
Chiefs running backs had exactly one 20-yard rush last year. Kenneth Walker III had two last night alone.
149 yards and counting on the ground for Kenneth Walker III DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5feESVSs7Q
Yes, it's only been one week, but we might be seeing in real time the third iteration of the Chiefs' offensive attack, and it's, for the first time, dependent on the run game. The play above is, 10 times out of 10, a play where past Chiefs running backs put their heads down and try to get 1 yard on fourth-and-1. Walker III is -- breaking news -- not like past Chiefs running backs.
In the early years of Patrick Mahomes , the Chiefs' deep passing game blew the doors off defenses. From 2018-20, Kansas City led the NFL in explosive play rate, and only the Buccaneers had more completions of 20+ yards. But eventually defenses adapted, and Tyreek Hill left town. So Mahomes became a game manager in the best sense of the word. Kansas City was 20th in explosive play rate but second in success rate. If he couldn't hit on big plays, Mahomes could at least keep things on schedule and make timely conversions.
And now, finally, the Chiefs are back to being explosive. This time, though, it's on the ground. Walker III was one of the NFL's most explosive backs in Seattle, and now, he is a full-time bell cow in Kansas City, which has long had a good offensive line but no runner who could take full advantage.
It'll be new for Andy Reid, and maybe that's a good thing. Reid has long been one of the most pass-heavy play callers in the league. Monday, the Chiefs ran on 51% of their first-half plays, the fifth-highest rate Kansas City has ever had in a Mahomes start. With the passing offense basically non-existent, the Chiefs still led, 14-7, at the break.
Again, it's Week 1. There's a long way to go. But if Walker III can provide a boost like this, and the passing game slowly gets back to the norm as Mahomes re-acclimates post-ACL tear, Kansas City's offense is very much on its way back to elite status.
I wrote Sunday that the Bears could score and allow the most points in the NFL this season , and while the "allow" part is very concerning, the "score" part is a whole lot of fun.
Actually, "fun" isn't the right word. Perhaps "ruthless" is. Caleb Williams last year was fun, with lots of late-game heroics powering the Bears to the NFC North crown. But if Williams plays like he did in Week 1, he can be absolutely ruthless, and so, too, can the offense. Williams' laser beam to Cole Kmet was one of several highlights.
CALEB TO KMET FOR 6 CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KedXXw4da5
We, of course, have to account for the fact that Carolina's defense was abysmal, but even on its good plays, Williams was better. According to Next Gen Stats , Williams had a +11.4 completion percentage over expected. Last year, he was at -6.7, the second-worst mark in the league ahead of only Brady Cook .
Williams got spectacular catches from Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond , which certainly boost that completion percentage over expected number, but there were several pinpoint passes that must have had Ben Johnson ecstatic. This one (posted by Jacob Gibbs, who does excellent work for CBS Sports on the fantasy side) is one such example.
2nd and 10 from the 47 0:38 left in the half Great timing route from Luther Burden, perfect read/throw from Caleb Williams. Next play is a 29-yard scramble to the house. pic.twitter.com/mQ6LU5m4UL
Look at where Luther Burden's head is pointed when Williams starts his throwing motion!
Many people -- myself included -- predicted regression incoming for the Bears. They can't force as many turnovers or win as many close games as last year, right? That may still be true. But perhaps we underestimated how much Williams could improve in his second year of Johnson's offense. And it's not just Williams, but Burden, Odunze and several offensive linemen. The Bears scored 59 points without Colston Loveland catching a pass.
It's a tiny sample size, of course, but Williams was 3 for 5 on throws 20+ air yards downfield, and only one of those five throws was deemed "off-target" by PFF. Compare that to his first three years.
Caleb Williams -- Throws 20+ yds downfield
The completion percentage will fall, and the off-target rate will rise. But if Williams is making another significant leap as a downfield passer, he -- combined with the running game and his own scrambling -- will be lethal.
While everyone was tuning into the offensive explosion in Carolina, they probably weren't paying much attention to the Trevor Lawrence show in Jacksonville. And I get it. Deshaun Watson and the Browns are as close to unwatchable as it gets, though the Titans might challenge them for that designation.
But my goodness, was Lawrence good. All of these are awesome, but the first play of this highlight tape is a jaw dropper.
Trevor Lawrence was pretty, pretty, pretty good in Week 1 pic.twitter.com/XwF5PyNbtY
Liam Coen has unleashed the beast. It took a while, but Lawrence began playing at an elite level over the second half of last year and was even better in Week 1. His 16.2 completion percentage over expected (expected to complete 62.1% of his throws, actually completed 78.3%) is ridiculous.
Only Josh Allen averaged a higher air yards to the sticks than Lawrence's 2.1; his ability to push the ball downfield is outstanding and finally on display. This is what we thought Lawrence could be coming out of college. It just took far too long due to awful coaching, surroundings and/or his own stunted development, in part due to the environment around him.
The Jaguars had a quiet offseason. They likely weren't going to generate a ton of headlines regardless, and playing the Browns in Week 1 didn't help. But ignore this team and this quarterback at your own peril.
Trevor Lawrence since Week 11, 2025
Expected points added per dropback
The Broncos ' struggles on both sides of the ball Monday night were shocking. At least offensively, though, there's a plausible explanation: It was Davis Webb's first game as play caller. Sean Payton gave up play-calling duties this offseason, and after one game, he might be regretting that decision. But it's important to remember that these changes can and do take time.
Here's how some notable new coordinators fared in Week 1:
Of course, some hires look great off the bat. The Raheem Morris-coordinated 49ers defense looked great against the Rams . Daronte Jones impressed in his first game as the Commanders' defensive coordinator. Declan Doyle had the Ravens' offense dominating all day against the Colts . The Giants' offense thrived with Matt Nagy. It's a mixed bag. But just because some teams were bad in Week 1 doesn't mean they're guaranteed to be bad all season (though that will be the case for some).
The Steelers beat the Falcons 20-13 in Week 1, and I wish I could tell you I was excited about quite literally any of it. But I am sad to report I am not. Say it with me: "The definition of insanity is doing the same thing and expecting different…

title: NFL Week 2 picks and score predictions: Bills top Lions in Thursday shootout, Seahawks suffer shocking loss
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
The NFL season is barely one week old and it's already out of control.
I mean, the Falcons are in first place despite having no wins and no quarterback, the trip to Australia may or may not have ruined the Rams and I'm pretty sure the Browns have already been eliminated from the playoffs. OK, so apparently, that's not mathematically possible after one week, but I think we can all agree that the Browns won't be making the playoffs.
The biggest shock of Week 1 might have been the fact that the Raiders , Jets , Giants and Cardinals all won. The last time all four of those teams opened with a win in the same season was never.
The only thing that was normal about Week 1 was the Chargers . You can always count on the Chargers to let down their fans and not only did they do that on Sunday, but they also let down pretty much every person who entered a survivor pool this year.
The Los Angeles Chargers' loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday eliminated $10.3 million worth of Circa Survivor entries, per @dustinswedelson . ➡️It's the most $$ lost on any single pick in Circa's NFL contest history
Only the Chargers could eliminate $10.3 million worth of entries from a survivor pool. If that's not the most Chargers stat ever, I don't know what is.
Although Week 2 might not top the craziness of Week 1, my picks are definitely going to get a little crazy, so let's get to them.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . However, if you don't want to click over, I totally understand. As someone who is easily sidetracked, if I leave this page to go read another story, there's a 100% chance I will end up going down some sort of internet rabbit hole and if that happens, I'll never make it back to the story I was originally reading. So I guess maybe you shouldn't click over.
Anyway, let's go down the rabbit hole of my picks.
The Bills ' new stadium will be hosting its first regular-season game ever on Thursday night and I have to say, I'm already looking forward to the complaints on social media. The Bills unofficially opened the stadium with a preseason game last month and, well, you know how the dinosaurs ate people when they tried to open Jurassic Park, that's kind of what happened here. No one got eaten, but this was definitely wasn't a smooth dry run and that's mostly because several hundred season-ticket holders found out that they couldn't actually see the entire field because they had an obstructed view .
Whoever designed the new Bills stadium should wasn't very keen to detail. Imagine paying tens of thousands on PSLs and season tickets and walk into a view like this... pic.twitter.com/mGhzbCaMVs
The good news for anyone with an obstructed view is that this game is on Amazon, so you can just stream it from your phone and watch everything there. Would that defeat the purpose of buying a ticket to the game? Probably, but that's not for me to decide.
I think the best solution here is to just tear the entire stadium down and start again from scratch, but only if the Bills lose. You can't tear down a stadium while they're on a winning streak.
So is there any chance the Bills are going to lose? If Week 1 is any indication, it's certainly possible. The Lions and Bills combined to play zero defense last week. The Bills gave up 31 points to the Texans while the Lions defense gave up 30 to the Saints .
What I'm trying to say here is that I'm fully expecting a shootout.
Thursday night games can sometimes turn into a slog, but that usually doesn't apply to the first Thursday game of the season (And yes, I know there was a Thursday game last week, but this is the first Thursday game where the teams are coming in on a short week). In eight of the past 11 seasons, the first short-week Thursday matchup of that year has been decided by one score. In seven of the past 11 seasons, it's been a game where both teams scored at least 23 points.
When you think of short-week Thursday games, you think of boring, low-scoring games, but I don't think that's going to be the case here. The last time these two teams played came in 2024 in a game the Bills ended up winning 48-42. We got 90 total points we might top that here. The Over/Under should be set at 104.
The unfortunate part for the Lions is that their Week 1 game went to overtime, which means not only do they have to play on the road on a short week, but they have to do it after playing an extra 10 minutes on Sunday. That's brutal.
You know what else is brutal? The fact that I can never remember my Amazon Prime password and I'm going to need it to watch this game. If you need me, I'll be spending the next three hours asking my wife what the password is. I'm starting to think that she keeps me in the dark about the password so I can't see everything she's buying on Amazon. If the Bills score a point for every Amazon box that came to my house over the past month, they're going to win by 40.
THE PICK: Bills 38-31 over Lions
After four years of waiting, we're finally getting what might go down as the greatest revenge game in NFL history: Baker Mayfield vs. the Browns.
In the movie "Gladiator," Maximus' sole purpose in life is to get revenge on Emperor Commodus and I feel like that about sums up Mayfield's life at this point. I think I can confidently say that there's no one in the history of sports who wants to beat his old team more than Baker Mayfield wants to beat the Browns this week.
The Browns have made hundreds of bad decisions over the past decade, but we all know what the worst one was: It came in March 2022 when they decided to mortgage their franchise by making a trade for Deshaun Watson . At the time, Mayfield was still on the roster, but the Browns ended up getting rid of him four months later in a trade with the Panthers .
In 2020, Mayfield led the Browns to their first playoff win in 18 years, but the Browns don't handle success well, which is why he was out the door less than two years later.
Instead of sticking with Mayfield, who the Browns drafted with the first overall pick in 2018, Cleveland decided to dump him in favor of a guy who didn't play a single snap in 2021 and was being accused of sexual misconduct by dozens of massage therapists. Any normal team would have slammed the door shut on a possible trade if just one of those two things happened, but not the Browns. Not only did they end up making a deal for Watson, but they also gave him a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract.
Since leaving Cleveland, Mayfield has won two division titles in Tampa Bay, but I think he would trade those in if it meant he could get just one chance to beat Watson and the Browns by 45 points.
In 2022, Mayfield actually got to face the Browns, but he didn't get to face Watson, because Watson was serving the first week of an 11-game suspension .
At the time the Watson trade happened, it was already being called one of the worst deals of all time, and four years later, you could argue that it holds the title for "worst trade in NFL history."
Mayfield originally signed with the Buccaneers in 2023 and due to the NFL scheduling formula, he has known for three years that the Bucs would be playing the Browns in 2026. I am fully convinced that he has been counting down the days, possibly in blood, until the kickoff of this game.
The Buccaneers didn't win in Week 1, but their defense did give Joe Burrow some trouble, and if they gave Burrow some trouble, they are absolutely going to terrorize Watson. He might throw three interceptions. I will definitely be starting the Buccaneers' defense in Fantasy this week.
As for Mayfield, I think he's going to go off. The Browns' defense got exposed by the Jaguars in Week 1, especially in the passing game with Trevor Lawrence throwing for 245 yards and four touchdowns. I feel like Mayfield is going to want to double those numbers. That probably won't happen, but I do think Baker…
