title: Bears offense shows no rust in shootout win over Panthers
summary: Going into the 2026-27 regular season, Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson indicated that his goal was for Chicago to break the NFL’s record for single-season scoring on offense. Purely based on how the team performed in Week 1 against the Panthers, it appears that it’s on its way to achieving that goal. It wasn’t […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks to pass against the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter of the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the 2026-27 regular season, Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson indicated that his goal was for Chicago to break the NFL’s record for single-season scoring on offense. Purely based on how the team performed in Week 1 against the Panthers, it appears that it’s on its way to achieving that goal. It wasn’t always pretty on the defensive side of the ball, but the Bears started the new year with a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers to begin the season with a 1-0 record. The game marked the highest-scoring season debut the Bears have had in franchise history, as well as the most points they’ve scored in a single game under Johnson. To kick off the season, these are our day-after takeaways from the Bears’ victory. Caleb Williams makes it look easy Finishing out the Bears’ season opener, Caleb Williams scored four touchdowns with no interceptions, surpassing 260 passing yards and reaching a passer rating in the triple digits in an incredible performance to kick off his third year with Chicago. He looked accurate moving the ball down the field, he looked poised avoiding pressure in and out of the pocket, he knew when to throw the ball away or take off running, and his patented elastic arm was on full display, too. Any time you can lead your team to a performance scoring over 50 points, it’s worth celebrating. Williams looked the part in Week 1, showing off improved accuracy and demonstrating the poise that helped Chicago secure the NFC North crown in the second half of the season. He ended the year ranked No. 20 in the NFL in PFN QB Impact Scoring , and once the scores are solidified for the week, he’ll surely rank higher than that after Week 1. The best RB duo in the NFL? Both of the Bears’ primary running backs scored touchdowns on Sunday, as D’Andre Swift ended the game with two rushing touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai ended up with one. Both running backs had big gains against Carolina, with Swift gaining 32 yards on one run and Monangai picking up 61 yards on a touchdown run in the second half. Chicago’s offensive line continued to look the part, executing assignments up front and paving the way for its running backs to find open running lanes in between the tackles. Swift especially showed off impressive burst and a relentless demeanor on a snap-by-snap basis, while Monangai’s massive touchdown run played a big role in the Bears creating separation in an offensive shootout. As easy as it can be to be impressed with how Williams threw the ball on Sunday, the Bears’ running back tandem looked the part, as well. Defense is a major concern The Bears ultimately broke away thanks to great play from their offense, but their defense was a lot more rocky than many in the fanbase would have hoped this week. They gave up 37 points on Sunday, with the secondary giving up multiple big plays in coverage. In particular, Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson looked especially shaky throughout the course of the afternoon. It wasn’t all bad, as rookies Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad both made some nice plays. Montez Sweat and Kentavius Street both contributed sacks on Sunday. There’s a lot for defensive coordinator Dennis Allen to get locked down, and the hope is that the return of Xavier Woods at safety will free up Cam Lewis into more of a chess piece role, rather than a full-time starter. Obviously, Chicago won’t score 59 points every game, as fun as that would be. It will need to sharpen a lot of things on defense going forward. Weapons for days If you told me that the Bears would score 59 points against the Panthers without Colston Loveland tallying a single reception all afternoon, I would have thought you were crazy. That says a lot about how much other weapons stepped up for Chicago on Sunday. Kalif Raymond led the team with eight receptions for 84 yards. Luther Burden III contributed five catches on five targets for 63 yards. Rome Odunze had a stellar 47-yard jump ball grab early in the game, and both Cole Kmet and Jahdae Walker secured receiving touchdowns against Carolina’s porous defense. Ryan Poles has invested heavily in the Bears’ group of pass-catchers, and that heavy investment paid off with how many players were able to contribute in Week 1.
author: Jacob Infante

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: 1-0 and ready for Houston
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 1-0 after defeating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home by a score of 33-27 on Sunday. For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, he’s won Week 1 games in back-to-back seasons, and while it wasn’t always pretty, the Bengals soundly defeated a pretty solid team that should push for the […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88) makes a catch at the end of the third quarter at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals are 1-0 after defeating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home by a score of 33-27 on Sunday. For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, he’s won Week 1 games in back-to-back seasons, and while it wasn’t always pretty, the Bengals soundly defeated a pretty solid team that should push for the NFC South title. There’s a lot to talk about, so here are some things that stood out to me : First, I was a little shocked that Landon Robinson was a healthy scratch. I get that he’s a seventh-round pick, but I thought he played really well throughout the preseason. Having too many defensive tackles is a good problem to have, I guess, but I was hoping to see the young kid—especially after seeing him arrive for his first NFL game in his dress uniform from the Naval Academy. I’m convinced at this point that Burrow is just a slow starter. He wasn’t terrible on Sunday, but he wasn’t his normal self, and his pick-six thrown to linebacker Josiah Trotter was very un-Burrow-like. I’m not overly concerned about the offense, though. There’s way too much talent for this group not to find its stride. It’s clear the Bengals really do want to emphasize Burrow playing under center to set up the play-action game. I can see the potential, even if Burrow doesn’t look completely comfortable with it yet. Amarius Mims absolutely shut down the Bucs’ first-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. Had the Bengals not traded the No. 10 overall selection for Dexter Lawrence, I would have liked to see them land Bain. Instead, Mims—whose arms are six inches longer than Bain’s—just kept him completely out of the game. It’s not that Bain won’t be good (though his short arms might be an issue), but I think Mims has the potential to become one of the best right tackles in the league. Boye Mafe was outstanding. He had a sack, a tackle for loss, multiple hurries, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. I still think Trey Hendrickson is probably the best free-agent signing the Bengals have pulled off over the last decade or so, but Mafe showed Sunday that he could potentially fill those big shoes. Al Golden’s defense had waves of pressure coming from all directions. Baker Mayfield was sacked four times, with five different players getting credit for them. The Bucs aren’t a bad team, and bringing down Mayfield four times while forcing four turnovers was huge. With the Bengals’ slow offensive start, I doubt they win this game without the additions of Lawrence, Mafe, Jonathan Allen and Bryan Cook. Tackling was still an issue on Sunday, but I’m willing—for now—to write it off as Week 1 jitters. Players were generally in the right place at the right time, but there were several instances where Bucs players bounced off tackles and picked up extra yards. That needs to be cleaned up. I questioned the Bengals’ decision to stick with Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter in 2026. They missed six tackles between them—three each—sharing the team leads in that category. However, they both made some great plays, including Knight’s touchdown and Carter’s sack and forced fumble. With the deep and talented defensive line in front of them, I think I could get on board with the duo… as long as they stop missing tackles. Samaje Perine is still a pretty big part of the Bengals’ offense. Tahj Brooks only took two offensive snaps all day. Burrow was sacked only once, and that sack was given up by tight end Drew Sample. The offensive line played very well all day long. The defensive line was outstanding, too. When was the last time we could say that about both the Bengals’ offensive and defensive lines? Lawrence had PFF’s highest pass-rushing grade on the Bengals’ defense (71.1) and was credited with one hit and two hurries. He had an 18.2% pass-rush win rate, which was best on the team and seventh-best in the league before Monday Night Football. Worth every little bit of that No. 10 overall selection. If you’re worried about Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, don’t be. They’re going to be just fine. Instead, be thankful the Bengals held on to Mike Gesicki, who essentially served as WR3 and found himself in space all day long. Let teams focus all their attention on the best wide-receiver duo in the league. Burrow will find someone else. There’s more, but we need to talk a little about the Houston Texans. The Bengals head to Houston to face the Texans, who have, in my opinion, the worst team name in the NFL. You’re named the Texans because you’re proud to be from Texas? Neat. The Bengals were named after a professional football team that existed in Cincinnati in the late ’30s and early ’40s. Plus, in a battle between your average Bengal tiger and your average dude from Texas (no weapons)… well, I’ll always put my money on the giant murder cat. Now that I’ve gotten that off my chest, I do think the Texans are a good team . They lost at home in Week 1 to a very good Buffalo Bills team by a score of 36-31, but they nearly pulled off the upset. Houston took a one-point lead in the fourth quarter but couldn’t keep Josh Allen and company out of the end zone. The Texans don’t want to start the season 0-2 and losing both games in front of their home crowd, and they’re going to come out swinging to make sure that doesn’t happen. The Bengals can win this game. I think they’re the better team, but they’ll need to clean up some of the issues from Week 1 if they want to head to Pittsburgh in Week 3 with a 2-0 record. Quick thoughts from around the AFC North: The Steelers beat Cooper Rush and the Falcons in Pittsburgh by a score of 20-13. Color me unimpressed. The Ravens went to Indy and beat the pants off the Colts, 41-23. Derrick Henry, who is somehow still doing this at 32 years old, carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns. Color me impressed. The Browns are the Browns. The score was closer than the game ever really felt on Sunday , but that doesn’t mean there aren’t things the Bengals need to clean up. They got the most important thing they needed from Week 1—a win. Now comes Houston. And if they don’t clean up a handful of those mistakes, they won’t be leaving Texas with another one. Relative Song Lyrics: All my exes live in Texas And Texas is the place I’d dearly love to be But all my exes live in Texas Therefore I reside in Tennessee

title: Texans dealing with significant injury concern ahead of Bengals matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are about as healthy as one could hope for two weeks into the regular season. Their next opponent? Not exactly. While the Houston Texans did technically enter Week 1 with a fully healthy 53-man roster, it didn’t tell the whole story, as they’d already placed a host of key players on injured […]
full_text: Oct 1, 2023; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans celebrates with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o (39) after a play during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Cincinnati Bengals are about as healthy as one could hope for two weeks into the regular season. Their next opponent? Not exactly. While the Houston Texans did technically enter Week 1 with a fully healthy 53-man roster, it didn’t tell the whole story, as they’d already placed a host of key players on injured reserve. That includes wide receivers Tank Dell and Jayden Higgins, defensive tackle Kayden McDonald, offensive tackle Braden Smith, and linebacker E.J. Speed. That last one is especially important, as the Texans suffered two more linebacker injuries in Sunday’s 36-31 defeat to the Bills. The main concern is starter Henry To’oTo’o suffered a shoulder injury in the fourth quarter and left the stadium in a sling. To’oTo’o is expected to be out this week and possibly longer. Adding to their troubles is that To’oTo’o’s backup, Jake Hummel, suffered a groin injury during the third quarter and is also expected to miss this week. The injuries helped pave the way for Buffalo to rack up 36 points on a Texans defense that didn’t allow that many points in a single game last year. They actually held this Bills team to just 19 points in a 23-19 home win last season. Having so many injuries at linebacker makes the Bengals’ newfound commitment to play-action passing even more pivotal to having success this week. Guys like career reserve Jake Hanson and rookies Wade Woodaz (fourth-rounder out of Clemson) and Aidan Fisher (seventh-rounder out of Indiana) will potentially get significant snaps for Houston this week. Hansen actually missed time with a leg injury in the preseason, while Woodaz missed time due to thumb surgery, so they may not even be 100% this week. This could pave the way for a big day from running backs Chase Brown and Samaje Perine, who combined for 29 total touches vs. Tampa Bay. That, in turn, could open up more big plays down the field if the Bengals can keep the Texans on their heels with more play-action. Saying this, the Bengals will have their work cut out for them against a defense that still has plenty of firepower, namely All-Pro defensive end Will Anderson, who helped the Texans rack up 13 total pressures and three sacks vs. the Bills. And while the offensive line performed well at home in Week 1, they’ll have to contend with a stronger Texans pass rush this week while also playing on the road for the first time this season against a team desperate to avoid the dreaded 0-2 start. The potential for a 2-0 start is there for the Bengals, despite the fact that they’re currently three-point road underdogs .

full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 13: Demetrius Knight Jr. #44 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts to 33-27 win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after the game at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. title: Bengals’ Ted Karras recounts the time he saved Mike Gesicki’s life during their time with the Dolphins
summary: Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki came up big in Week 1. In a game where Ja’Marr Chase was contained and Tee Higgins was limited, Gesicki became Joe Burrow’s top target as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers focused their attention outside. Gesicki came up big in clutch moments all game. Gesicki helped save the Bengals on […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88) celebrates a touchdown reception in the first quarter of the NFL Week 1 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki came up big in Week 1. In a game where Ja’Marr Chase was contained and Tee Higgins was limited, Gesicki became Joe Burrow’s top target as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers focused their attention outside. Gesicki came up big in clutch moments all game. Gesicki helped save the Bengals on this day, but there was a time when he needed real-life saving from one of his teammates. In a recent appearance on the Fitz & Whit podcast with Ryan Fitzpatrick and Andrew Whitworth, Bengals center Ted Karras told the story of how he very well may have saved Gesicki’s life. Ted Karras had to save Mike Gesicki’s life… Turns out it was a pretty common day for Mike? pic.twitter.com/3kUZGlV62Z — Fitz & Whit (@fitzandwhit) September 14, 2026 The incident happened back in 2020 when Fitzpatrick, Gesicki, and Karras were all teammates for the Miami Dolphins. During a team meal, the three were eating steaks together when Gesicki began to choke on his steak, leading Karras to leap into action and perform the Heimlich maneuver to dislodge the meat. “Mike gets his steak well done, so here’s a lesson in that,” said Karras. “And all of a sudden, Mike is sick. He looks at me, fear and tears in his eyes, and I immediately recognize it as choking. I kind of went into action. I’ve never had a harrowing moment like that in my life. Bent him over the sink and performed the Heimlich. “We were about 30 seconds away from an actual, like, this is gonna be a serious thing here.” Fitzpatrick originally told the story to Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson back in 2024 . This doesn’t seem like it was a small choke or food just going down rough; it sounds like Karras was genuinely concerned for his teammate’s safety. Karras also explained that this has been sort of a theme for Gesicki. “But then it comes out later in the night. That’s the third time he’s been Heimliched. He’s a three-time Heimlich. You’re getting medium rare if you’re eating steak around me from now on,” Karras joked. Three times in one lifetime is a lot, so maybe Gesicki needs to evaluate his chewing tactics. In the end, Karras saved the day, and Gesicki was able to do the same for the Bengals in Week 1.

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals held on for a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Here’s what we learned. The defense is hungry and confident After a long offseason of conjecture, we finally know what the defense can actually do. Yes, they’re still a little leaky, missing tackles. And they were flagged for being line up […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 13: Cade Otton #88 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is tackled by Demetrius Knight Jr. #44 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the second half of the game at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals held on for a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Here’s what we learned. The defense is hungry and confident After a long offseason of conjecture, we finally know what the defense can actually do. Yes, they’re still a little leaky, missing tackles. And they were flagged for being line up offsides multiple times. But they’re bold and chomping at the bit to make a big play. It’s somewhat similar to those playmaking defenses in 2021 and 2022. Bend but don’t break, with some turnovers in between that give the offense a nice boost. The four fumbles and four sacks were a lot more than we would’ve seen out of the defenses in 2024 and 2025, and three early fumble recoveries are what gave the Bengals a nice cushion for the game. It’s not an injury thing; Joe Burrow just needs real reps to warm up For a QB with as high of a football IQ as Joe Burrow, his interception was a head scratcher. The only real explanation is that Burrow just needs some time to get back into a rhythm in the regular season. It kinda makes sense when you consider how little the seventh-year QB has played in the preseason. The good news is, he was able to do just enough to secure a victory in Week 1, so the offense should only be better from here on out. Touches on offense are going to be more evenly distributed With Ja’Marr Chase being the focus of the Bucs’ secondary and only getting four targets, Burrow looked elsewhere. Chase Brown had six targets, which was as many as Tee Higgins. But it was Mike Gesicki who led the team with seven targets. Drew Sample, Andrei Iosivas, and Samaje Perine had three targets, and Dohnte Meyers and Tanner Hudson even got a look each. And the run-to-pass ratio was solid, with 27 runs and 35 passes. There has been talk of a move to a more traditional approach on offense with Dan Pitcher more involved in play design, but now it seems to be official.

title: Browns Week 1: Cleveland’s identity is now in question
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars revealed plenty about the team beyond what the final score showed. There were plenty of assumptions made about this team heading into the season. Many of those assumptions were validated in Week 1, while others told a different story about where this team is currently at. Many expected Cleveland’s defense to be the team’s […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars revealed plenty about the team beyond what the final score showed. There were plenty of assumptions made about this team heading into the season. Many of those assumptions were validated in Week 1, while others told a different story about where this team is currently at. Many expected Cleveland’s defense to be the team’s biggest strength and the key to keeping them competitive this season, but Week 1 showed that may not be the case. The defense allowed 24 points and 234 yards in the first half alone. They struggled to get any pressure on Trevor Lawrence . While the offense did little to help them, it was even more disappointing to see how the defense performed. The Jaguars won 13 games last season and have a strong offense, so this performance may not indicate what the defense will look like in the coming weeks. Still, the initial showing was far from promising. On the offensive side of the ball, there wasn’t much positivity going into the season about Deshaun Watson and the passing game. That feeling was clearly validated by what happened in this game. There was optimism that the offensive line would improve from last season with the addition of several new players, but the group continued to struggle in Week 1. Again, it is not truly indicative of what they will look like for the rest of the season. It was difficult to find many positives from the group, outside of a strong performance from Austin Barber , who was the highest-graded PFF rookie offensive lineman in Week 1. Hopefully Barber can inspire the rest of the offensive line as the team prepares for their Week 2 game matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. For now, the Browns identity, which was assumed to be a good defense and solid rushing attack, is in question, added to all the questions about the quarterback position. title: HC Todd Monken changes tune, not about Deshaun Watson but about team’s buy-in with the QB
summary: If Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken was expecting a honeymoon phase in his first time leading an NFL team, Week 1’s performance all but shut the door on that. The Browns performance versus the Jacksonville Jaguars was so bad that it was hard to tell if the problem was scheme/coaching or talent on the roster. […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - AUGUST 03: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns instructs Deshaun Watson #4 during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images If Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken was expecting a honeymoon phase in his first time leading an NFL team, Week 1’s performance all but shut the door on that. The Browns performance versus the Jacksonville Jaguars was so bad that it was hard to tell if the problem was scheme/coaching or talent on the roster . The answer is probably both, but fans are putting much of the blame on Monken and QB Deshaun Watson . On Monday, Monken noted that he plans to stick with Watson as the starting quarterback . While Watson’s stat line was not horrible, the film told a different story … except the story Monken saw was one of optimism, while fans and media saw it as mostly pessimistic. When asked whether Cleveland’s roster backed Watson, Monken said : “They don’t have a choice; this isn’t a debate.” While that may not be a bad answer, overall, it flies in the face of what the Browns head coach said about the quarterback position in April when he noted that “players decide who plays, I don’t decide who plays” and “who does the team believe in” as seen below: #Browns HC Todd Monken on April 8: "Who’s got an inner toughness to move the offense and get us in the end zone? full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates with his teammate Derrick Henry #22 of the Baltimore Ravens after a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Cleveland Browns fans lament another terrible start to an NFL season, the beat goes on around the AFC North. The Browns are the lone team to lose in Week 1 , a drubbing handed to them by the Jacksonville Jaguars , with many turning their attention to the 2027 NFL draft to try to avoid thinking about what former Cleveland QB Baker Mayfield might do in Week 2 . As always, we still want to keep track of what is going on in the AFC North, including two big contract issues that could lead to rumors and a trade . Baker hands Bengals the game It is almost impossible to have an honest, good conversation about Baker Mayfield around Cleveland fans. For a lot of good reasons, as mentioned in The Feed . Those convesations, however, will probably never stop especially with Week 2’s matchup. In Week 1, the Cincinnati Bengals once again saw the full Baker experience. Mayfield completed 23 of 28 passes for 216 with zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. He willed the team back into the game, including five carries for 30 yards and a touchdown, while handing, almost quite literally, the game to the Bengals with three fumbles. For Cincinnati, the defense was much improved while the offense was good, not great, as they get ramped up. No one had two catches for 12 yards for Ja’Marr Chase also leading to a Bengals victory, but he we are. Steelers hold off Kevin Stefanski, 3rd-string QB Not sure what Stefanski did in a past life, but his quarterback options have been limited for quite a few years. On Sunday, that included starting third-stringer Cooper Rush , who completed just 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions, including a back-breaking pick-6. Pittsburgh’s offense did just enough, and the defense was solid. The opponent drops the excitement level for Steelers fans, although a victory is a victory. Ravens control the game, have injury concerns coming out With four straight touchdowns between the first and second quarter, the Baltimore Ravens were in control 28-6, then 31-13 heading into halftime. While the Bengals and Steelers didn’t have huge offensive days, the Ravens saw Lamar Jackson throw for 324 yards, Derrick Henry rush for 144 yards, and Zay Flowers have 150 yards receiving. The bad news for Baltimore is Flowers’ hamstring issue popped up, which isn’t expected to be long-term but is notable for a speedster. On top of that, hotshot rookie Jakobi Lane has a fractured wrist and could miss signficant time. Overall, the Ravens looked the most dominant of the three winning AFC North teams in Week 1. title: 4 thoughts from the Browns lackluster season opener versus the Jaguars
summary: Not ideal. The 2026 Cleveland Browns season opener was a disaster in a lot of ways. It would be lazy to say that everyone expected this to happen because no one thought it would be this bad. Beating the Jacksonville Jaguars, who were in the playoffs last season and are projected to be back in […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13:Kc Concepcion #1 of the Cleveland Browns runs a route in the second half during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Everbank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not ideal. The 2026 Cleveland Browns season opener was a disaster in a lot of ways . It would be lazy to say that everyone expected this to happen because no one thought it would be this bad . Beating the Jacksonville Jaguars, who were in the playoffs last season and are projected to be back in the postseason again this year, was not going to be easy, but the Browns didn’t give themselves a fair chance to cause an upset . Four thoughts from Sunday’s dismal performance: 1st Down: Offense was offensive but it’s a work in progress Going into the season, expectations for the Cleveland Browns offense were low. Despite the influx of talent, from revamping the offensive line and wide receiver room it would be hard to evaluate how the offense would look because the quarterback room could be the worst in the entire league. The stats will say quarterback Deshaun Watson played fine, but the film says otherwise. He held the ball too long, wasn’t as decisive as he should and lacked drive in terms of throwing the ball. Watson will take what the defense gives him and not take deep shots down the field, which limits an offense with a low ceiling. Shedeur Sanders is someone that fans want to see because he’s popular and well-liked (something Watson isn’t), but I don’t see the offense getting any better with him either. Could Sanders provide excitement to a fanbase that needs it? Yes, but at this point this fanbase would be excited about anything. The run blocking for the offensive line isn’t where it needs to be, but to be fair, this is a group with five new starters. Rookie Denzel Boston had a nice touchdown grab when the game was out of reach. Will the offense get better? Maybe. Maybe not. Keep in mind, this is a new offensive scheme that should get better as the season progresses. Hopefully. 2nd Down: Defense has an identity issue Going into the season, the Browns defense was considered to be a strength despite losing defensive end Myles Garrett and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz. Sunday, the defense looked anything but a strength. The pass rush was lacking, the secondary was picked apart, and they struggled to get a stop. Cornerback Tyson Campbell talked about the scheme and how defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg wanted to be more diverse: Browns CB Tyson Campbell postgame said that new DC Mike Rutenberg’s scheme is stylistically the same as last year “in some ways, but we got some more zone concepts that we run as well. So a little bit more diverse.” Per ESPN Research, the Browns played zone coverage on 67% of… — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 14, 2026 As mentioned, the Browns defense spent more time in zone today than they usually do, but the defense doesn’t have the players to run zone as frequently as they did. It’s not a bad thing to diversify and change your scheme, however, you have to pick and choose when to do it. This defense has blue-chip talent, and it’s clear that this unit needs to be better after having a performance like this. How do they fix it? Go back to what works, but be more diverse and not as predictable. 3rd Down: It’s Week 1. It’s fair to say out of all the Week 1 performances in the NFL, the Cleveland Browns had the worst performance. However, it’s Week 1. It’s the NFL. Week-to-week league (Insert fans “weak-to-weak” joke here). Yes, the Browns looked unprepared on both sides of the ball. The coaching wasn’t what it needed to be, and the players didn’t perform the way they were supposed to. Could things change? Absolutely. However, a performance like this didn’t do much to encourage fans, and it’s up to the team to fix it. 4th Down: Things are bad, but it doesn’t mean it will stay this way Let me get this out of the way. I grew up a Seattle Seahawks fan. My parents weren’t diehard Browns fans so it made it easier. As I scrolled through social media, I saw a post saying “Today felt like a low point in Cleveland Browns fandom.” To be honest, today wasn’t a low point. It was a bad loss, but this team has had numerous low points since they’ve come back, and today wasn’t one of those lowest points if you were a fan. That seems like an overreaction. Things will eventually get better for this team considering that this team has talent. You can choose to believe that things will get better or choose to believe things will get worse. The team has put a winning product out there before, even if it seems so long ago, so it’s not hard for the team to get back to it. Having young, talented players is always a good starting point for a team looking to turn things around, even if Week 1 was tough to watch. ( Editor’s addition : I’m a Lord of the Rings fan, and 4th down had me thinking of this clip, so it gets added.) After a night of sleep, what are some of your thoughts on Week 1? title: Assigning blame for Browns loss in Week 1: Deshaun Watson tops the list but is not alone
summary: In assessing the Cleveland Browns’ 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, several factors contributed to a performance in which Cleveland was never really in the game. Deshaun Watson threw an interception on his third pass attempt of the first quarter, setting the tone for what would become a disappointing game for the Browns. Watson was […]
full_text: In assessing the Cleveland Browns’ 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , several factors contributed to a performance in which Cleveland was never really in the game. Deshaun Watson threw an interception on his third pass attempt of the first quarter, setting the tone for what would become a disappointing game for the Browns. Watson was certainly a substantial part of what went wrong for Cleveland in this matchup, but several other factors also contributed to the Browns’ struggles. The Browns’ defense did little to help give the team a chance to win. They allowed Trevor Lawrence to go 18 of 23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns. With Myles Garrett no longer leading this defense, there was plenty of uncertainty around what the unit would look like. This group’s performance did little to give anyone confidence that they could replicate the dominant defense they used to be. Some of the blame also falls on Todd Monken , who seemed unprepared with his game plan and struggled with some game management decisions throughout the matchup. It only added to the struggles the team was already having, as did the lack of a solid run game. Watson finished 16 of 22 with 205 yards, one interception, and one touchdown. This stat line is not particularly concerning; however, much of the production came at the end of the fourth quarter when the game was already out of reach. The Browns trailed 31-0 at one point, making Watson’s lack of production and inability to run the offense effectively a major factor in the team’s struggles. title: Cowboys outcoached, outplayed at Giants to start 0-1 in division
summary: The 2026 Dallas Cowboys began their season with a loss that made things feel like 2025 all over again, for an abundance of reasons, and really not many of them good. The last loss of last season was at MetLife Stadium to the New York Giants, and now this new season began with a season-opening […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants celebrates a 28-20 win against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys began their season with a loss that made things feel like 2025 all over again, for an abundance of reasons, and really not many of them good. The last loss of last season was at MetLife Stadium to the New York Giants, and now this new season began with a season-opening loss at the Giants for the first time since 2016 – Dak Prescott’s first career start. This Sunday night marked the start of year number 11 for Prescott, and it took just four quarters for the vibe to feel like Dallas still has a mountain’s worth of work to do to make this a contending team around their veteran quarterback. Prescott led two touchdown drives for the Cowboys in the second half against the Giants, but it was not enough to keep this game from going in the ever-growing stack of recent Prescott starts where the defense couldn’t do enough to make it matter. Those two possessions were the only ones the Cowboys offense got in the second half, as the defense gave up touchdown drives of 12 and 13 plays, and then allowed the Giants to run out the final 5:21 of game time up by eight. The Giants won the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, shortened the game brilliantly, and put head coach John Harbaugh’s new culture to the test against that of Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys. In the end, the Giants became the second straight division rival to hand the Cowboys a road loss on Sunday Night Football in week one, with their young core of players all smiles about it as they sent the Cowboys home 0-1. There’s a whole lot to process about this loss for the Cowboys, so let’s get right to some notes on the 28-20 Giants win. Dubbing themselves the “greatest offense there is” in the offseason, the Cowboys put this to the test on the very first possession of the game, running out a cast of starters that for the most part did not play a single snap in the preseason. The result of trying to knock off this rust in real time under the lights was a three and out, assisted by an expedited review that turned a George Pickens slant route from a first down into fourth and inches. The Cowboys flirted with going for it in this spot, but ultimately took the delay of game and punted, a decision that would linger all night as it became a limited possession game. To make matters worse, the Giants went right down the field to open the scoring with a Cam Skattebo rushing touchdown from three yards out. The Cowboys defensive woes in setting the edge from the preseason absolutely carried over to this opener. On this play, linebackers Demarvion Overshown and Rashan Gary were both blown off the ball and never came close to Skattebo who walked in untouched off left tackle. This sequence was bad for Dallas to say the least, but a similar turn of events where the Cowboys were outcoached near the end of the first half may have went the longest way in making this a deflating loss. One thing the Cowboys defense did a nice job of on the night was punch the ball out, but they only recovered one of four forced fumbles. Just before halftime, the Cowboys had the ball on Shavon Revel’s fumble recovery, forced by Quinnen Williams in pursuit, and faced a 3rd-and-5 in their own territory. Unlike on the game’s very first drive, this time the Cowboys put trust in their offense by calling a timeout and stopping the clock before the third-down attempt, staring down leaving the Giants plenty of time if they did not convert. Out of the timeout, the Giants put their all-out pass rush package on the field, and the Cowboys were not ready for it. Not only did New York get pressure on Prescott, but the route concept never stood a chance for Dallas. Both CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson had leverage against their defenders off the snap, but neither were coming back to the ball as Prescott escaped the pocket either. Dak’s errant pass was picked off with a sliding catch on the sideline by safety Jevon Holland, creating a disastrous sequence for the Cowboys before the half. After Holland’s interception, the Giants faced a third down for themselves, even more of an obvious passing situation than the Cowboys just had with nine yards to go. Unfortunately, this became another huge coaching win and swing in momentum against the Cowboys though. Instead of getting pressure on Jaxson Dart like the Giants did Prescott, the Cowboys defense dropped edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku into coverage to try and be underneath a throw to Malik Nabers. The second-year pass rusher could not do so in time, Nabers made the catch to move the chains, and three plays later Isaiah Likely was in the end zone for a wide open touchdown and Giants 14-7 lead. In our keys to the game prior to kickoff about what to watch for if the Cowboys were going to be successful in primetime, we highlighted Jake Ferguson getting involved in the passing game as something that could really get Dallas going. Instead, it was Likely, a carryover from the Ravens that Harbaugh brought with him to New Jersey, that stole the show as the best tight end in this matchup. Likely scored a second straight touchdown coming out of the locker room to start the second half, on a drive where the Cowboys defense couldn’t even get the Giants into a third-down look. The Cowboys were now desperately chasing this game down 21-7, and ran out of time along with toughness defensively to make the stops needed. This was a bad night all around for the Cowboys. They were outcoached in a lot of phases, they couldn’t hold up physically on defense, they completed just 10 of 18 attempts to their “big three” receivers, they didn’t have a reception longer than 17 yards all night, and they put themselves in an early hole with a gauntlet of tough teams ahead. On a record-breaking Sunday for points scored around the league for a week one slate, the Cowboys tried-and-true method of finding a way to make Prescott the better quarterback in a game against division rivals fell apart completely at the hands of an ultra-confident year two starter in Dart, and a complete Giants team with a whole new attitude under Harbaugh. The Cowboys will have scheme, culture, and injury concerns to answer to as they try to turn the page and prep for old friend Dan Quinn and the equally-desperate Commanders, also off a division loss, coming to Arlington next Sunday. The Cowboys are 0-1 in the win/loss column but also winless in the “proving anything is really different” column after 60 minutes of this season.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys Week 1 fallout: 6 possessions and a funeral
summary: What a bunch of horse manure. Sorry for such a vivid description, but organic soil fertilizer is the only way to accurately capture the aroma of the broken spirit of this Cowboys fan. After months of begrudgingly building up excitement for this Dallas Cowboys football team, this is our reward. Maybe a little of that’s […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on while wearing a Never Forget shirt in honor of the 25th anniversary of 9/11 during warm ups prior to the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a bunch of horse manure. Sorry for such a vivid description, but organic soil fertilizer is the only way to accurately capture the aroma of the broken spirit of this Cowboys fan. After months of begrudgingly building up excitement for this Dallas Cowboys football team, this is our reward. Maybe a little of that’s on us, but they get us every time. Every. Time. And losing to the New York Giants? For perspective, we’re talking about a football team that hasn’t won 10 games in a single season since Dak Prescott was a rookie. A team so traditionally incompetent that they usually secure a top-10 draft pick, miss on a defender, and then rinse and repeat the following year. We count on those games for wins and confidence boosters. But this current Giants team is pretty good, which is a painful thing to type. Especially since they’re so hateable. Cam Skatteboo looks like a high school bully from an ’80s movie who hangs out with his Cobra Kai buddies. And his headbutt compatriot, Jaxson Dart, is equally nauseating. His arrogance is so insufferable that John Harbaugh had to get on him during practice because he was taunting his own teammates. Rivals or not, these guys are remarkably easy to hate. But who cares about the stupid Giants? The real, existential dread today comes from the Cowboys. There is plenty of blame, but the coaching staff will be the recipient of our complaints today. The new season began with two horrible plays that went nowhere. A one-yard stuff of Javonte Williams, and an incomplete pass intended for CeeDee Lamb. Just like that’s it’s third-and-long against the one thing the Giants defense can supposedly do well. Rush the quarterback. The Cowboys answer with a quick slant to George Pickens in what looks like a drive-sustainer, only replay shows he was just inches short of the first-down marker. No problem. Just sneak it. We all were thinking it. They’re at their own 37-yard line, but if you can’t get a few inches, you might as well just pack this thing up and head back to Texas. Let’s GOTI this thing already! Nope. Instead, they subject us to that embarrassing pre-snap charade where they are trying to get the Giants to jump offsides. So annoying. Please stop doing that. First possession of the year – THREE. AND. OUT. Yay! Why am I whining about one silly possession? Well, because the Cowboys only had six of them on the night. As it turned out, each one was pretty important. We’ll get to the why in a minute, but if you look at the Cowboys’ offensive possessions, it went like this… Punt Punt Touchdown Interception Touchdown Touchdown Note: We aren’t counting the three-play possession with only 14 seconds left in the first half. Instead, let’s focus on the six real possessions. There are two interesting things about this list. First, the Cowboys scored a touchdown on half of their possessions in the game. If teams do that, they’re usually going to light up the scoreboard. That’s a lot of touchdowns. But when they only get six total chances, half isn’t as rewarding. Equally as aggravating as the lack of opportunity was the grueling labor required for the Cowboys offense to move the ball. Nothing came easy. There was little creativity. Running back Javonte Williams had to fight for every inch, usually first running into the back of his own blockers. Dak Prescott had to deliver a lot of tight throws, and their most explosive chunk plays on the night came courtesy of pass interference penalties. Okay, enough dumping on the offense. Let’s switch it up. The Cowboys defense was terrible on Sunday night. For starters, they couldn’t stop the run. The defense allowed 165 rushing yards in this game, the most rushing yards they’ve allowed since Week 8 of last season when the Denver Broncos ran all over them. You remember that game. It was awful. That’s what we got on Sunday night. Instead of Christian Parker’s new scheme confusing the quarterback, the quarterback repeatedly confused them. Dart had them faked out all night, with defenders running the wrong way, and playing the chase game 10 yards down the field. It was terrible. About the only thing worse than their inability to stop the run was their coverage scheme. It’s hard to know exactly what the issue was, but watching the Giants’ receivers wander so comfortably in wide-open spaces was tough to witness. That was not the defense we signed up to watch. We saw that last season. Frustration continued as we sat back and essentially watched none of the new guys make an impact. Rashan Gary? Von Miller? Did those guys play? Caleb Downs had a nice play where he sacked Dart that would have stood out more if the ball didn’t flutter right into the hands of a Giants’ offensive lineman, but other than that, it was a quiet night from the team’s new safeties. Even the well-anticipated aggressiveness of rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham ran himself into an encroachment penalty on a crucial third and short. Fantastic. Everyone knows there will be growing pains with a new defensive coaching staff. It’s expected. Even so, there are still things you are hoping to see. We didn’t see them. This is only one game, and nobody should be running for cover as if the sky is falling. It’s not. Again. It’s just one game. But it was a terribly coached game. The team looked completely unready for the season and repeatedly committed the silliest infractions you can do in a football game. Offsides (twice), holding, illegal hands to the face. Pure silliness. And many of them came on crucial third-down situations. The coaches had to waste a precious second-half timeout when they only had 10 players on the field. It was pure sloppiness. There’s no other way to explain it. For the Cowboys, this is a tough one to swallow for a very simple reason. They just weren’t ready to play. Letting an opposing offense control the entire game to the point where they only got two second-half possessions was utterly painful to watch. The team must get their act together, and get it together quick. They suddenly find themselves in a crucial game against the Washington Commanders next week. If they drop another one, they’ll head to Baltimore, where they could likely start the season 0-3. And remember, the first half of the season is the easy part. Things get really difficult come November.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys add another running back to the active roster
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are continuing to add to the running back position. Before Malik Davis went down with season-ending hip surgery in practice last week, the team had already added Emari Demercado via waiver claims after training camp. Then, after Davis was placed on injured reserve, they signed Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Tyler Goodson #25 of the Atlanta Falcons rushes against Jahdae Barron #23 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are continuing to add to the running back position. Before Malik Davis went down with season-ending hip surgery in practice last week, the team had already added Emari Demercado via waiver claims after training camp. Then, after Davis was placed on injured reserve, they signed Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster. Now it looks like the Cowboys will be signing Atlanta Falcons running back Tyler Goodson from their practice squad, per Aaron Wilson . Goodson started his NFL journey as an undrafted free agent with the Green Bay Packers in 2022, but saw his first career snaps after signing with the Indianapolis Colts in 2023. He spent the next three seasons there and only eclipsed 100 rushing yards in a season once. Goodson joined the Falcons this offseason and had a few standout preseason moments, particularly against the Colts. RB Tyler Goodson deserved to be rostered somewhere instead of the Falcons practice squad Suwanee, GA native is Dallas bound ATL “RB3” is now Cash Jones pic.twitter.com/UkvGGOPhNl https://t.co/qnsqsBYpzD — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) September 15, 2026 Looking at the way Goodson broke free for the touchdown run, his running style looks very similar to what Dallas had in Malik Davis. Maybe the team views Goodson as a better replacement for that skill set than someone like Abanikanda. Stephen Jones says talent acquisition is 24/7, 365, and adding Goodson shows Dallas was looking to upgrade after what they saw against the New York Giants Sunday night, when the backups to Javonte Williams didn’t perform well. There’s no information yet on the corresponding move for the Cowboys to sign Goodson to the active roster.
author: Brandon_Loree

title: Cowboys news: Young defenders made mistakes, “critical” improvements needed
summary: The Dallas Cowboys week one defensive performance did not feel at all like the “graduation” Christian Parker said it should be, and now young players and veterans alike will have to get back in the classroom and learn quickly before another NFC East battle against the Washington Commanders. Quinnen Williams was vocal after the loss […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the second quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys week one defensive performance did not feel at all like the “graduation” Christian Parker said it should be, and now young players and veterans alike will have to get back in the classroom and learn quickly before another NFC East battle against the Washington Commanders. Quinnen Williams was vocal after the loss about the accountability this defense will have to get better, but they will also be spending this week sorting out who can fill in for Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown who were injured against the Giants. Schottenheimer: Cowboys’ young defenders ‘need to learn quickly’ after Giants’ lesson – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire It was trial by fire for a ton of new faces in the Cowboys defensive lineup, and frankly one they were not ready for. Schottenheimer acknowledged the inexperience as part of the reason for such breakdowns. “Not an excuse, guys: we did not play well, but you’ve got young players,” he said. “A young player closes and Jaxson Dart boots and gets outside. We don’t push three different times to the [expletive] flat route, excuse my language. Those are going to happen, and we have to coach the young players better. But when you play young players, it’s part of the deal. And they need to learn quickly.” Quinnen Williams: We really need to be critical to get better – Josh Alper, Pro Football Talk The Cowboys got pushed around in the trenches, and Quinnen Williams is taking accountability. “I think we definitely gotta be critical [of ourselves] in our approach , when we get to [preparing for Week 2]. And it’s a great week to learn, and to get things better,” Williams said, via the team’s website. “The guys we got in our locker room, especially on defense, are unbelievable when it comes down to taking constructive criticism and accountability, first of all, and let’s move,” he said. “We had a lot of mental errors, a lot of busts today, and just really need to be critical with that going into this week; and focus on getting better.” Malik Hooker, DeMarvion Overshown to miss a couple weeks with injuries – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Dallas defense comes out of Week 1 with major concerns at linebacker and safety after losing starters to injury at both positions. After saying following Dallas’ 28-20 loss to New York that initial tests showed a fractured forearm for Malik Hooker, Schottenheimer confirmed Hooker did in fact suffer a fracture in his forearm. He will have surgery on Tuesday. “It sounds like it’s one that doesn’t require as long a period of time [to recover]. So we’re hoping it’s a two week window.” Schottenheimer said. As for Overshown, Schottenheimer said Sunday night he wasn’t sure the extent of his hamstring injury. That ended up being a strain, and Schottenheimer said it could be “one to two weeks as well” to recover from. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 3 Cowboys Week 1 Takeaways: We Got Eberflused on Defense – Cody Warren, Inside The Star Cowboys fans are left wondering when the defense will ever look and feel any different at 0-1 for the second straight year. Dallas changed coordinators , but Sunday night wasn’t any different than last season under Matt Eberflus. No pressure, broken coverage, and mistake after mistake. Jaxson Dart dissected the defense, found his tight end, Isaiah Likely, so many times it felt like he was the only receiver on the field. On top of that, Dallas couldn’t keep Dart in the pocket. I felt like Dart could’ve had 10 yards running anytime he wanted. The Dallas Cowboys’ defense showed way too many flaws in Week 1, but there’s a worrisome one that’s close to unfixable – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys need another big time pass rusher in the worst way. In 20 plays rushing the passer with four players only, the Cowboys recorded two QB pressures, according to NextGen Stat s . It was their lowest pressure rate since 2021. When the Cowboys did blitz, the Giants usually had the right answer. Whether it was Dart taking off himself or him finding an open target down the field. Tyler Guyton a bright spot in Cowboys’ demoralizing loss – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys The Cowboys were able to trust Tyler Guyton on an island for a lot of snaps at left tackle, as his improvement is encouraging. While facing off against star pass rusher Brian Burns, the 25-year-old tackle allowed no pressures across 20 pass-blocking matchups. On the night as a whole, Guyton allowed just two pressures in his 36 total pass blocks in the game, a very solid mark going up against a talented Giants’ pass rush. This performance is even more impressive when you consider that Guyton did not have his usual running mate, All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith, lining up next to him every play. Daily discussion question: How much have your expectations been lowered moving forward?
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys at Giants Stock Report: Christian Parker, Javonte Williams lead disappointments
summary: The wounds had just healed. We all had moved on from the 2025 Dallas Cowboys and their historically bad defense. The team seemed to do this as well, especially with regards to action. The Cowboys front office operated this entire offseason, as it seemed, with a pledge for things to never be as bad as […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Defensive coordinator Christian Parker of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the fourth quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wounds had just healed. We all had moved on from the 2025 Dallas Cowboys and their historically bad defense. The team seemed to do this as well, especially with regards to action. The Cowboys front office operated this entire offseason, as it seemed, with a pledge for things to never be as bad as they just were. Mission failed. At least so far. Sunday night was a total and complete disaster did not go well for the Cowboys. In their first opportunity to prove that things were different, they gave life to the notion that maybe the present is simply more of the past. To make matters worse, unlike last season the offense is now under a bit of fire. They were not as bad as their defensive counterparts at MetLife Stadium (hardly saying anything), but ultimately the collective team has apparently taken an entire step back. Here is our stock report from it. Stock Up: Tyler Guyton We are starting with positives, there are a few, and need to give credit to someone who had as much negative press as anybody when training camp began: Tyler Guyton. NFL Pro’s insights noted after the game that Guyton recorded 20 pass-blocking matchups against Brian Burns in this game. He did not allow a single pressure. Overall Guyton allowed just a pair of pressures on 36 total pass blocks in the game. He lived up to the challenge. That is great news. Stock Up: Caleb Downs It is obviously difficult to feel positive about much on defense, but Caleb Downs was as advertised. The sack he made was the clear flash, but he held his own and was hardly why the defense got worked the way that it did. The sky is very high for him as we all believed. Stock Up: T.J. Bass It was around a week ago when we all found out that Tyler Smith would miss at least a month due to his thumb injury. Given that Smith is the best interior lineman in the NFL, there was a natural level of concern. Give T.J. Bass credit, though. Many expected him to be serviceable in Smith’s absence, the Cowboys did place a second-round tender on him after all, and he was. That is hardly an easy thing to do. Stock Down: Christian Parker You would have a very difficult time finding someone who had a longer honeymoon after initially joining the Cowboys. From January to Sunday afternoon, Christian Parker was heralded. He came from a strong lineage, said all of the right things, and he was given plenty of new tools to reconstruct the defense that was so bad last season. Sunday night was just one game and he could still wind up fulfilling the proverbial prophecy, but wow his group was overwhelmed. Grading the game in a vacuum it was about as big of a failure as it possibly could have been. Time to move on. Stock Down: Javonte Williams There are only so many ways to say this, and we have all said it: What are you doing taunting? In general! Down by a touchdown still? Responses I’ve seen to this vary, but the most defensive of Williams seem to be that the NFL is soft and that taunting penalties are lame. Fine if you feel that way. But Williams knows the rules. Arguably more importantly, Brian Schottenheimer knows the rules. They all have to operate within them and didn’t, and it literally costed the team a point. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer Williams was not the only player to commit a silly penalty. Recall that DeMarvion Overshown hit Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart clearly out of bounds early in the game. These are silly and avoidable mistakes. Those things start with the head coach, and Brian Schottenheimer has also been riding a bit of a positive wave for the last few months. I’ll speak for myself and say that I am willing to give him a bit of a mulligan for last season with how the front office went about handing things to him, but I put zero blame on the front office here in 2026. They have done their job. This is on the people who coach and play the games. Schotty has to get things in check as soon as possible. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey It feels unfair to penalize Brandon Aubrey for missing an extra point after Javonte Williams pushed him back, but he is now paid very handsomely. Expectations rise when things like that happen. What’s more is this continues to pick at the notion that maybe Aubrey has lost his fastball a little bit. He’s not always down the middle anymore on his kicks, even when making them. Concern feels somewhat warranted. Stock Down: DeMarvion Overshown Let us first say that we hope DeMarvion Overshown recovers quickly from his hamstring injury. Before he left the game though, Overshown was not exactly shining for on-field performance reasons. He had the penalty and was then critically missing just about every read. He was a high point of weakness in the heart of the defense. We are almost two years removed from when Overshown really shined for the Cowboys. Right now it is looking like this may not be in the cards. We will see. Stock Down: The entire pass rush Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart threw for 3+ touchdowns without any interceptions for the first time in his career on Sunday night. This is only his second NFL season and it’s not like he even started every game last year, but obviously that is pretty damning of the Cowboys defense. Consider that the highest point of pressure came from Caleb Downs as noted. The Cowboys were not able to generate any frustration for Dart up front and that inability led to them getting pushed around all game long. Where were Donovan Ezeriuaku and Rashan Gary? How were they not more frustrating to deal with? Stock Down: Division dominance Objectively speaking, the Cowboys have beaten up on the NFC East for much of the Dak Prescott era. Specifically, they have pushed around the Giants whenever they wanted. This was just one game to be clear, but it was not the meaningless contest that Dallas lost to New York in Week 18 last year. The Cowboys gave this game all of their might and the new-look Giants humbled them mightily. Next week will bring another test of this variety. The Washington Commanders took the Philadelphia Eagles the distance a few hours before the Cowboys failed against the Giants, and one of Washington and Dallas will fall to 0-2 by this time next week. Who will it be?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Tyler Guyton a bright spot in Cowboys’ demoralizing loss
summary: The Dallas Cowboys’ 2026 regular season got off to an abysmal start on Sunday night. As they do nearly every year, Dallas came into the season with high hopes. After the disaster that was last season, offseason upgrades had the Cowboys believing they could be a serious contender. Unfortunately for Dallas, it was hard to […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys’ 2026 regular season got off to an abysmal start on Sunday night. As they do nearly every year, Dallas came into the season with high hopes. After the disaster that was last season, offseason upgrades had the Cowboys believing they could be a serious contender. Unfortunately for Dallas, it was hard to spot the difference between the 2025 team and the one we saw on the field Sunday night. While the game finished 28-20, the score was not indicative of the play on the field. The Giants were clearly the most physical and fundamentally sound team, and it showed time and time again in big moments throughout the game. Dallas’ new-look defense looked almost identical to their defensive unit from last season, and their high-powered offense shot itself in the foot by shrinking in big moments. There was signifigantly more bad than good for Dallas on Sunday night, but there were a few bright spots in the loss. Maybe the brightest of which was the play of starting left tackle Tyler Guyton. The former first-round pick, who is facing a true make-or-break season this year, got off to an excellent start, earning him the Week 1 game ball award. While facing off against star pass rusher Brian Burns, the 25-year-old tackle allowed no pressures across 20 pass-blocking matchups. On the night as a whole, Guyton allowed just two pressures in his 36 total pass blocks in the game, a very solid mark going up against a talented Giants’ pass rush. One of the few (only?) bright sides tonight pic.twitter.com/7ugscwrIHl — Tom Downey (@WhatGoingDowney) September 14, 2026 Via @NextGenStats : Cowboys LT Tyler Guyton allowed two pressures on 36 total pass blocking snaps. Guyton did not allow a pressure to Giants OLB Brian Burns in 20 pass blocking snaps against him. — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) September 14, 2026 This performance is even more impressive when you consider that Guyton did not have his usual running mate, All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith, lining up next to him every play. For one of the few times in his brief NFL career, Guyton looked like the guy Dallas envisioned he could be when they selected him with the 29th overall pick back in 2024. On a night that was discouraging for the team, to say the least, the Cowboys have to feel encouraged on a personal level by what Tyler Guyton did against New York. If the left tackle can continue this preformance throughout the entirety of the regular season, Dallas may have themselves another Pro Bowl offensive lineman.
author: Matthew Holleran

Lamb began the season needing 44 receiving yards to surpass his predecessor in Club 88 for fifth in franchise history from a receiving yards standpoint. He has now done it. And he barely did so, at least in the season opener. Lamb finished the […]

title: 5 key plays that spelled disaster for the Cowboys vs. Giants
summary: After all the hype and build-up of what was a terrific, drama-free offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, the team came out flat against the New York Giants. The offense sleepwalked through much of the game, looking like a shell of the potent offense we saw last year. Dallas’ receivers weren’t productive for much of the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - SEPTEMBER 13: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys runs after the catch during the third quarter during the game against the New York Giants on September 13, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After all the hype and build-up of what was a terrific, drama-free offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, the team came out flat against the New York Giants. The offense sleepwalked through much of the game, looking like a shell of the potent offense we saw last year. Dallas’ receivers weren’t productive for much of the contest, and when they did wake up, it was far too little, too late. The defense looks different but produced eerily similar results as last year. Jaxson Dart toyed with them. On an emotional night at MetLife Stadium, the Giants beat the Cowboys more convincingly than the 28-20 score would suggest. Cowboys fans should be stunned at how we even got here. Here are the five key plays that decided Dallas disappointing loss. Not going for it on 4th and 1 The Giants were fired up going into this game. The atmosphere was electric. With the introduction of John Harbaugh, the Giants have renewed excitement, and that was felt from the coin toss. On the opening drive for the Cowboys, Dak Prescott completed a slant to George Pickens. Although initially it was ruled a first down, replay review overturned it. Dallas lined up on offense to give the impression they were going to try to pick up the first down. A hard count was unsuccessful in drawing the Giants offsides, and with a chance to sustain their drive to take some of the wind out of the Giants’ sails, head coach Brian Schottenheimer opted to punt the ball. The Giants capitalized on their drive led by a big run by Jaxson Dart. With the Cowboys’ offensive line, their quarterback, running back, and tight end, they elected to play it safe, and it cost them. The Giants took the early lead and never looked back. The Giants owned the time-of-possession battle, and you can point back to this moment as a starting point for New York’s control over the clock. Pickens Big Drop The Cowboys simply could not execute against the Giants’ secondary. Even though Prescott was under pressure, they had their opportunities. Following a terrific play by Quinnen Williams to force a fumble against Tyrone Tracy, the Cowboys had been able to stop the bleeding and manage to get off the field. At that point, the game was tied, and the Cowboys were in position to take the lead before the half . Prescott made a terrific throw to Pickens, who had beaten the Giants deep, but Pickens allowed the ball to slip right through his fingers. Pickens had multiple drops against the Giants, but that one especially stung. The Cowboys’ aerial assault was grounded Sunday night as all the explosiveness of their offense fizzled out. The Cowboys were unable to create any significant plays in the Giants’ secondary, and that play was the epitome of their passing futility in the loss. Dak’s interception Dak Prescott’s interception happened soon after Pickens’ drop, but the two plays are so directly correlated that they must be mentioned. Prescott makes the right play by eluding the pass rush to get out of harm’s way, that is until an ill-advised pass lands in the arms of Jevon Holland. Prescott claimed he was trying to throw the ball away, but upon looking at the replay, it doesn’t look that way. From that point, it killed whatever progress the Cowboys had made defensively. The Giants regained possession, and after several coverage breakdowns on the ensuing drive, scored to take a 14-7 lead. Prescott’s interception nullified the Giants turnover and set up the Giants’ chance of taking a two score lead after halftime, which in fact they did. Skattebo’s fumble takes an unfortunate bounce Despite their challenges, there were multiple times when the Dallas defense made a turnover-worthy play but couldn’t come away with the football. Having one turnover Sunday is very disappointing. DeMarvion Overshown and Caleb Downs forced fumbles that wouldn’t go the Cowboys’ way. Later in the game, Cam Skattebo almost gave the Cowboys’ defense a gift as they were sucking wind and panting for air. Early in the fourth quarter, Skattebo slipped a tackle on one of his many tough runs through the Cowboys’ defense. Cobie Durant forced a fumble, but the ball made its way back to Skattebo before Dallas could even get a chance to recover it, signifying it wasn’t going to be their night defensively. On the same drive, the Giants overcame a 2nd-and-17, a 3rd-and-9, and a 2nd-and-12 to find the end zone for the game-deciding score. Luck wasn’t on the Cowboys’ side Sunday, even when it presented itself repeatedly. Javonte Williams taunting penalty Dallas’ composure was compromised early. Overshown’s penalty early in the game was the precursor to what we would later see. In total, Dallas committed nine penalties, and awareness of the situations they were in was questionable. However, none more questionable than Javonte Williams’ penalty. Dallas had managed to answer New York’s early fourth-quarter drive and position themselves to be within one score. Yet Javonte Williams took it upon himself to taunt the Giants secondary even though the Cowboys were still trailing. His penalty was only magnified by Brandon Aubrey missing the extra point after Williams’ penalty had pushed the Cowboys back 15 yards. Although the Giants ran out the remainder of the clock after that point, Williams’ actions fully encapsulates how the Cowboys lacked disciplined in all facets, which proved to be their undoing.
