title: Value of Things: In the rearview mirror
summary: Week one is finally in the books. It is time for that feature that everyone knows and loves. This is where we look at the basic numbers from the game to determine if we can see any patterns in winning and losing. Obviously, there are no patterns with a sample size of one, but as […]
full_text: Week one is finally in the books. It is time for that feature that everyone knows and loves. This is where we look at the basic numbers from the game to determine if we can see any patterns in winning and losing. Obviously, there are no patterns with a sample size of one, but as we move forward we will start to see them. As you know, the Texans lost a nail biter 36-31, but the final score hardly ever indicates how close it was. The Texans drove it down to the nine for a go ahead score, but fizzled out when pass protection broke down two plays in a row. There is no way in a million years that anyone that watches this team could have predicted how this game would play out. Close game? Sure. Texans loss? The Bills were favored in the game. 67 total points scored? Not a chance in hell. That’s why they play the games as they say. So, let’s see what the basic statistics say about how this one turned out. Key Statistics Total Yards: Texans 73/381, Bills 52/409 Rushing Yards: Texans 32/124, Bills 21/86 Passing Yards: Texans 41/257, Bills 31/323 Sacks: Texans 2, Bills 3 Penalties: Texans 7/106, Bills 10/85 Turnovers; Texans 2, Bills 0 Time of Possession: Texans 36:17, Billa 23:43 It’s amazing how one or two plays can change the whole complexion of a game. Kamari Lassiter dropped a sure interception in the end zone that looked more like a wounded duck then a throw from Josh Allen. If he gets that interception then the Texans simply kneel on the ball and win the game 31-30. I won’t harp on one plays in terms of going good, bad, and ugly, but that one play is indicative of how close these games come. The Texans don’t have a second turnover, so the turnover battle ends in a draw. Take away the turnover battle and the Texans have the slight edge across the board. The Good It is safe to say that every football game has positives. Even when you lose 59-0 you can usually find something small to hang your hat on. There is nothing small about David Montgomery. Sure, he gained “only” 60 yards, but many of those were tough yards and he did score three of the four offensive touchdowns in the game. He added three more catches for 19 yards with one of those coming for a score. No one is going to call Canton for 79 yards for scrimmage, but clearly the Texans have found something there. Woody Marks gained 42 yards on the ground in nine carries in the kind of role the Texans envisioned last season for him. If the team gains an average of 124 yards every week they will be much improved offensively. In particular, while the turnovers hurt, this ball control offense is what they are looking for. If you control the ball for 35+ minutes and generate 31 points on offense then you win nine times out of ten. The Bad There are a lot of things on defense that did not go well. In particular, only getting to Josh Allen twice has to be a disappointment. Meanwhile, the secondary in general probably played their worst game in well over a season. Allen carved up the Texans defense and generated more big plays then we would expect in a month. I mentioned the Lassiter drop earlier. That is a play he would love to have back, but the bigger sins were the numerous chunk plays that made life easy for the Bills. The Ugly There is bad play and then there is alarmingly bad play. Anyone that looked at PFF and other sources had to express some concern when the Texans brought in Reed Blankenship. We were told they would use him differently, so a lot of us bought into the hype and hoped a return to his glory days were in the offing. It’s only one game, so that’s still possible, but this one is one where you want to burn the tape. Dalton Kincaid is a good tight end, but he turned into the reincarnation of Rob Gronkowski out there. If they continue to use him to cover tight ends it could be a long season. Focus on Stroud Since C.J. Stroud is angling for a new contract worth more money than 100 of us will make in a lifetime, it probably is a good idea to look at this week to week. The official stats say he had 274 yards passing with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. I’m not good at the math, but 17 weeks of that seems like it would be career highs (and lows) in every single category. The 106.7 rating is also something that would bode well for him at the end of the season. I’m not one to overly criticize because there are any number of reasons why the Texans lost the game. However, he needs to take better care of the football under pressure. Two key fumbles resulted in three Bills points and took points off the board at the end of the game. The Texans win the game without those fumbles. So, as much as I would love to give him an A, I can’t because key errors played a part in them losing. A solid B performance kicks the can down the road. It was a very Dak Prescotty kind of performance. Good numbers. Some great moments, but not quite enough. Let’s see if that trend continues.
author: Scott Barzilla

title: Can an optimist be optimistic after the Colts’ opening day loss?
summary: I guess the short answer is to say yes, but it is going to be a lot harder than I expected. When you get outclassed like we were against the Ravens, plenty had to go wrong. Starting with the defense, I think the play of the LBs stuck out to me as the biggest weakness. […]
full_text: I guess the short answer is to say yes, but it is going to be a lot harder than I expected. When you get outclassed like we were against the Ravens, plenty had to go wrong. Starting with the defense, I think the play of the LBs stuck out to me as the biggest weakness. That void in the intermediate middle, didn’t look improved with players who were supposed to be better in coverage. Walley looked bad chasing guys over the middle, but shouldn’t there have been some interior support? I’m not letting him off the hook, as he did not look as advertised in our first real look at him. Your pass defense has a hard time looking good, when one player can rack up 150 receiving yards before halftime and the run defense wont shine when you give up 144 rushing yards, even if it is to a first ballot HOFer. I don’t think Carlies had a stat? ADG was consistently in the wrong place. The bottom line is that they gave up over 500 yards. How long before Boettcher is a starter? On offense, the two turnovers stand out. You likely were not going to match scores with them, but the Ravens lived on the Colts side of the field. The INT was on the second play of a drive and the fumble was on the first play. This put us well behind in field possession and time of possession. Being behind dictated what we were trying to do and although JT put up good numbers and stopped the Ravens from pinning their ears back, we were too far behind to catch up in that manner. Is there anything to be optimistic about? I’ll try. The pass rush looked better. Maybe they didn’t get home as often as you would hope, but unless we were in a total coverage package, Jackson was being moved off his spot. It was actually his escape act on their second drive that made me think that it might not be our day. You know the play, two Colts allow him to simply duck the rush and pick up a first down, when the sack would have taken them out of FG range and given us the chance to stay in the game. It was a pretty big momentum swing and Jackson may have been the only QB to be able to pull it off. Keenan Allen seamlessly produced Pittman plays. I’m not sure that Dulin couldn’t have did the same, but Allen looked like a true pro out there, even as a willing blocker. I know that is not much on the good news side, but that is what happens when you get whooped. Some quick hits: I think Jones played well enough to win under better circumstances, but we can’t be a team that plays catch up. Pitch count. If Pierce is not ready to go, is a pitch count the answer? Maybe it is, but he did not appear to get a lot of separation. McGowen will not remain RB2 if he can’t pick up the free rusher with more authority. 4th and 6. Down big, you opt for a 59 yard FG? Allen. Allen? C.J. Allen? Still no sense of urgency. I’ll get a better feeling as last week fades a bit, but for now, it’s a tough pill to swallow.

full_text: HOUSTON, TX - JANUARY 04: Johnathan Edwards #35 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on from the sideline during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that the team has waived backup cornerback Johnathan Edwards, presumably to open a 53-man roster spot for fellow corner Cam Taylor-Britt, who served his league mandated one game suspension this past weekend: We have waived CB Johnathan Edwards. — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) September 14, 2026 Originally signed as an undrafted rookie free agent by the Colts in the 2025 offseason, Edwards, an athletic 6,’1”, 201 pound cornerback, appeared in 14 games last season, including making 5 starts. He recorded 26 tackles (19 solo) and 3 passes defensed as a rookie during the prior 2025 campaign. It’s fair to say, he showed some initial promise, albeit in limited action during his debut pro campaign. While Edwards had struggled during this preseason playing cornerback, the thought was with his speed and athleticism , he could continue to stick around for his special teams prowess—although he was a healthy inactive during Sunday’s blowout home opening loss. That no longer appears to be the case, although it’s possible that Edwards could re-sign to Indianapolis’ practice squad. It’s looking like the Colts elected to keep undrafted rookie Kapena Gushiken, who they snagged off league waivers from the Philadelphia Eagles after final 53-man roster cuts, at Edwards’ continued rostering expense. Unfortunately, sometimes in the positional room it can be a numbers game and with Taylor-Britt’s imminent return this week, Edwards appears to be the latest casualty from a football perspective.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Colts start the season on sour note, with “clunker” home loss to Baltimore
summary: It’s one game, but if the Indianapolis Colts lay a few more consecutive “clunkers” like that, and the already hot seats of both longtime general manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen will only get hotter in-season. The Colts got off to an early start on Sunday afternoon with an offensive touchdown (with a […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Derrick Henry #22 of the Baltimore Ravens scores rushing touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts during the first quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s one game, but if the Indianapolis Colts lay a few more consecutive “clunkers” like that, and the already hot seats of both longtime general manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen will only get hotter in-season. The Colts got off to an early start on Sunday afternoon with an offensive touchdown (with a missed PAT) on their opening offensive drive, but after that, it was all Baltimore beating and bruising up the Colts—to the tune of Indianapolis surrendering 500+ total offensive yards defensively. The final score may have read 41-23, but this one was already over at halftime with the Ravens up 31-13. In particular, the Ravens top offensive playmaker duo of Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers had huge afternoons against the Colts. Henry looked like he in the middle of his playing career prime as an All-Pro running back for the Tennessee Titans again, crushing the Colts to the tune of 144 total rushing yards and 3 rushing touchdowns, while debuting slot Justin Walley was no match for Flowers, who went off with 5 receptions for 150 total receiving yards and a touchdown reception. Let’s just be glad that Henry isn’t in the AFC South anymore! Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon has already stated this early offseason that there’s never been a greater sense of urgency regarding this team and her top football lieutenants, but their Week 1 ‘laugher’ of a showing against the Ravens didn’t do much to instill confidence that this regime remains the right recipe for success for the franchise going forward. It’s early, and the Colts still have the next few weeks to “round into better form,” albeit against a very tough early season schedule by virtue of playing both the Kansas City Chiefs and Houston Texans next up in back-to-back weeks. I agree that with NFL teams playing starters very little in preseason games these days, it takes at least a few weeks to know who your team really is from a talent, execution, and identity standpoint, but Indianapolis doesn’t have the luxury of a soft initial schedule to ease into finding that best version of themselves. The offense and field position battle also didn’t do the Colts any favors, as a Daniel Jones interception and Jonathan Taylor fumble lost swayed the scales in favor of Baltimore. The Colts were constantly behind the 8-ball regarding beginning their offensive drives, only adding to their ineptitude. If they aren’t careful, they could very well dig themselves into an initial hole and begin the 2026 campaign at 0-3, and given the results on Sunday, they may not be good enough to dig themselves out of as far as future AFC playoff contention is concerned. They need to put themselves in position to be successful later on this season, when their schedule thankfully lightens up a bit. That opener showing at Lucas Oil Stadium in front of their own home fans left A LOT to be desired. I wouldn’t say that NFL opening day carries the same significance as within the MLB among diehard fans, but at the same time, they’ve got to come out more prepared than that. That was flat out embarrassing. As veteran former Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner eloquently stated post-game , “Plain and simple. We got our ass whooped.” Which fine, every NFL team can lay an egg here and there, especially when you’re shaking off initial offseason rust, but there’s real concern right now, that this could be less of an aberration and more of the Colts’ new norm.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: What went wrong on defense against the Ravens?
summary: The Colts spent the offseason talking about urgency, change and a defense that was supposed to look better under Lou Anarumo in Year 2. Then they opened the season by giving up 41 points and 506 yards at home. There is some obvious context here as Baltimore is a difficult offense to defend. Lamar Jackson […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Chris Moore #17 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates a first down against the Indianapolis Colts during the third quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Colts spent the offseason talking about urgency, change and a defense that was supposed to look better under Lou Anarumo in Year 2. Then they opened the season by giving up 41 points and 506 yards at home. There is some obvious context here as Baltimore is a difficult offense to defend. Lamar Jackson is a two-time MVP, Derrick Henry is still one of the hardest backs in football to bring down and Zay Flowers is a tough cover for any cornerback, especially one making his first start after missing all of last season. That can all be true, and Sunday can still be unacceptable. The Ravens have eight explosive plays (runs of 12+, passes of 16+) in the first half against the Colts. The last game in which they had at least eight first-half explosives was Week 17 in 2023. 987 days ago. — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 13, 2026 The Ravens did not need a perfect game to move the ball. They had eight explosive plays in the first half alone, according to Ben Solak. Josh Wilson noted that 506 yards allowed were the most the Colts have ever given up in a season opener in the Indianapolis era. He also noted that this was the first time since 2015 that Indianapolis allowed 40-plus points and 500-plus yards in any game. The Colts had their worst season opener in decades – which is saying a lot, for this team. Allowed 41 points, t-3rd-most in opener in Indy era. Allowed 506 yards, most in opener in Indy. Lost by 18, 6th-worst defeat in opener in Indy. And it could have been much worse. — Josh Wilson (@JoshWilsonSB) September 13, 2026 That is not the kind of performance a team can explain away by pointing to the opponent. The pass rush was fine overall. It was not dominant, but it was not the main reason the defense fell apart. The bigger problems were behind it. The Colts struggled in man coverage, lost too often against Baltimore’s heavier run looks, got almost nothing from their linebackers and looked disorganized far too often for a unit that entered the year with this much pressure on it. Justin Walley and man coverage Colts played man in between the 20s at a 61.5% rate today, per @NextGenStats They allowed 13.4 yards per pass on those plays… — Brett Kollmann (@BrettKollmann) September 13, 2026 Justin Walley’s first start could not have gone much worse. That does not mean the Colts should give up on him. It does not mean he cannot become a good player. It does not even mean the team was wrong to trust him going into the season. It does mean that Sunday was a bad introduction to the NFL. Walley was picked on early, and the Ravens kept going back to him. Flowers beat him on the Ravens’ first play of the game for a 49-yard gain, and that set the tone for the rest of the afternoon. Walley looked late reacting to cuts, struggled to stay attached across the field and had a difficult time dealing with the type of movement Baltimore used to attack man coverage. Things have not started well for the Indianapolis defense. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Ravens #BALvsIND pic.twitter.com/vZhUszvDQd — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) September 13, 2026 Zay Flowers is a really brutal matchup for Walley's first career start. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Ravens #BALvsIND pic.twitter.com/39poOJASvN — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) September 13, 2026 Flowers was a brutal first assignment. He is quick, sudden and extremely difficult to cover when an offense is using motion, crossing routes and condensed formations to create traffic. The Ravens knew what they were doing. They put Walley in conflict and forced him to chase one of the league’s shiftier receivers through space. Still, that is the job. If the Colts are going to play this much man coverage, the corners have to hold up better than they did Sunday. Brett Kollmann posted that Indianapolis played man coverage between the 20s at a 61.5 percent rate, per Next Gen Stats. The Colts allowed 13.4 yards per pass on those plays. That is a defensive plan getting punished. Walley was the main target, but he was not the only problem. A.J. Haulcy was at fault on one of the Flowers plays. The Colts also failed to properly recognize Flowers when he was aligned in the backfield, which should not happen against a player who is clearly one of Baltimore’s most dangerous weapons. Charvarius Ward had a rough rep on a deep ball where his feet looked stuck in the ground, and instead of reacting cleanly, he ended up grabbing late after getting beaten. The linebackers did not help much underneath either. Baltimore hit crossing routes and man-beaters, and the Colts too often looked late sorting through it. That is the danger of playing man coverage against a team that knows how to manipulate matchups. If one defender is late, the ball comes out. If the linebackers are unsure underneath, the middle of the field opens up. If the safety help is late or the corner loses leverage, a modest gain can turn into a field-flipping play. The Colts wanted to be more aggressive defensively this season, which is fine but Anarumo’s defense was always going to ask more of the secondary. What Sunday showed is that playing man at that rate comes with a price if the corners are not winning and the rest of the defense is not connected. Run defense The run defense was not much better. Baltimore leaned into bigger personnel and jumbo looks, forcing the Colts to answer with heavier fronts. That brought Jerry Tillery onto the field more often, and he had a rough game. When teams go big-on-big, there is nowhere to hide up front. Every defensive lineman has to hold his gap, especially when the Colts are using five-man fronts with three interior defenders. Can't wait to post a Colts highlight again. What is Jerry Tillery doing? #Colts #ForTheShoe #Ravens #BALvsIND pic.twitter.com/l25t179V7o — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) September 13, 2026 Tillery did not do that well enough. Baltimore moved him too easily, and once the Ravens started creating movement inside, the linebackers had to clean up the mess… and they didn’t. Most rush yards after contact on Sunday so far Derrick Henry 104 Jahmyr Gibbs 82 Saquon Barkley 82 D'Andre Swift 79 Kyle Monangai 79 pic.twitter.com/I0Cuzf0ZSk — PFF (@PFF) September 14, 2026 Derrick Henry finished with 104 rushing yards after contact, according to PFF. Some of that is Henry being Henry. He is going to break tackles, fall forward and turn ordinary runs into bruising gains; that is part of playing Baltimore. The problem is that the Colts were not just losing to a great back as they were failing to finish plays they had chances to stop. #Colts starting LB Jaylon Carlies did not record a single stat in 42 snaps played, according to PFF. — Noah Compton (@nerlens_) September 14, 2026 The linebacker play was especially concerning. Jaylon Carlies played 42 snaps and did not record a single stat, according to PFF. That’s horrible… A linebacker can do some things that do not show up in the box score, but when the defense is giving up 41 points and getting pushed around in the run game, 42 snaps with no recorded production is a major problem. Akeem Davis-Gaither did not look comfortable either. He looked late diagnosing plays and just looking lost in space. There was a play where he completely followed his man all the way down the field without realizing Lamar Jackson was right behind him running the whole time. Baltimore makes linebackers think, and that is part of what makes the Ravens so hard to defend. They use Lamar, Henry, motion, tight ends and misdirection to stretch every rule. Still, the Colts needed their linebackers to settle things down, and instead they looked like part of the problem. The CJ Allen usage also deserves scrutiny. Chris Ballard called Allen a green dot…
author: Andrew Aziz

title: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence is your first BCC Player of the Week
summary: Win or lose, any football game is sure to include some standout individual performances. Luckily for us, the Jacksonville Jaguars obliterated the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, and there are plenty of game balls to pass around. Trevor Lawrence threw 4 touchdowns; Parker Washington had the coolest one of them; Foye Oluokun logged an interception […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 13: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars throws a pass during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cleveland Browns on September 13, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Win or lose, any football game is sure to include some standout individual performances. Luckily for us, the Jacksonville Jaguars obliterated the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, and there are plenty of game balls to pass around. Trevor Lawrence threw 4 touchdowns; Parker Washington had the coolest one of them; Foye Oluokun logged an interception and another pass breakup; Ventrell Miller had a team-high 9 tackles plus a sack and a forced fumble; and Josh Hines-Allen stuffed the stat sheet with 5 tackles, 1.5 sacks, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery (on different plays!). After the final whistle, we asked Jaguars fans to pick Big Cat Country’s Player of the Week. 81% of voters chose Trevor Lawrence. Trevor Lawrence looked completely in control to open the season for Jacksonville 🔥 18/23, 245 PYDS, 4 PTD, 0 INT, 150.6 Rating pic.twitter.com/IDJ4r51BcF — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 13, 2026 One of his touchdowns was a dime as he was rolling left (which is becoming a trend) that left Browns defenders in awe. Another was an impossibly tight-window dart near the goal line. According to Yahoo Sports’ Football 301 podcast , Lawrence had a 99th percentile Completion Percentage Over Expected and 98th percentile Expected Points Added per play. It was also the second-best single-game Success Rate of his career. As John says in the post below: pretty good! Via https://t.co/aCVE8BIvtv QBs pre-MNF. Trevor Lawrence was … pretty good! pic.twitter.com/vEAQDk31Hl — John Shipley (@_John_Shipley) September 14, 2026 Congrats on the first Big Cat Country POTW award, 16. title: Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 1: Jags Stomp Lowly Browns in All 3 Phases
summary: I truly don’t know of a much better way to start a season than what the Jaguars did on Sunday. Against the god-awful Cleveland Browns, the Jacksonville Jaguars did far more than handle business in their 34-10 season-opener win. It’s now 2-0 in season openers in Duval County for Liam Coen and the vibes couldn’t […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: Travon Walker #44 of the Jacksonville Jaguars reacts with teammates after a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first half of the game at EverBank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images I truly don’t know of a much better way to start a season than what the Jaguars did on Sunday. Against the god-awful Cleveland Browns, the Jacksonville Jaguars did far more than handle business in their 34-10 season-opener win. It’s now 2-0 in season openers in Duval County for Liam Coen and the vibes couldn’t be higher. When you have a win where arguably the worst play for your team is allowing a long kickoff return that didn’t go for a touchdown, resulting in just three points, you probably played pretty well. That’s how it seemed on Sunday. No real losers this week as the Jaguars ride high as the only AFC South team to win their opener, starting the season 1-0. Winners The Jaguars Everyone’s a winner collectively from yesterday’s game. Sometimes you just need to handle business, not play with your food and win a game outright. The Jags did that in all three phases. The offense scored on its first four drives, not having to punt until the final drive of the first half. The defense grabbed a pick on Cleveland’s first drive and forced about two dozen more fumbles throughout the game to go along with five sacks. Special teams did its job with a pair of long field goals from Cam Little and got some nice returns from Ameer Abdullah and Parker Washington. Handle business and move on. The decreased stadium capacity was a little strange and the heat definitely impacted the crowd, but the Jags fans showed up like they always do to see the team off right to start the season. We can’t play the Browns every week but it’s a start. On to Denver. THAT'S A TEAM WIN pic.twitter.com/D4BKU7lAiX — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 Trevor Lawrence Coen was asked postgame about the importance of starting Trevor Lawrence fast this season in the second season of this offense. The head coach said he and his staff were more intentional about working earlier in the week on the script. It paid off big time. Had it not been for some mammoth games by Caleb Williams (the Chicago variant) or Tyler Shough, Lawrence might have had the best quarterbacking day in the league on Sunday. Lawrence went a solid 18-23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns. He was sacked just once and was turnover-free. The offense moved at will with Lawrence slinging it. It was smooth, his throws were layered beautifully and it just looked all around clean. Juxtaposed to whatever the hell Deshaun Watson was doing, it made Lawrence look even that much better. Trevor Lawrence looked completely in control to open the season for Jacksonville 🔥 18/23, 245 PYDS, 4 PTD, 0 INT, 150.6 Rating pic.twitter.com/IDJ4r51BcF — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 13, 2026 The quarterback has a clear trust in every offensive weapon he has, with nine different guys catching at least one pass. The most catches on that list though did belong to… Parker Washington Hey look, Parker Washington is actually good and it wasn’t just a one-season thing. Maybe they should have paid him. In all seriousness, Washington was perhaps the best non-Lawrence player on the field yesterday with five catches for 83 yards and his leaping opening drive touchdown. He looks like a legit WR1 after just a game. Maybe the best part about Washington is that his newfound superstardom finds guys like Jakobi Meyers (two catches, 40 yards, one score) and Brian Thomas Jr. (three catches, 40 yards) that much more open. It all works in tandem. Sunday was a testament to that. Chop Wood. Carry Water. Catch touchdowns. Parker Washington with the DIVING CATCH for his first TD of the season 😱 CLEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FzpS0RbR6u — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Rookies Another guy who benefitted from the Washington hype train was rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron, who caught a touchdown in his first NFL game. Cameron looks the part through one game: a 2-catch, 20-yard, 1-score performance. His big frame is clearly something Jacksonville wants to take advantage of early and often. Nate Boerkircher hauled in a pass as well, highlighting another rookie who flashed in spurts Sunday. Brenton Strange led the tight end room in “moments” so to speak, but the rookie Boerkircher did his job. As did rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon, who got the start up front. At least offensively, the early returns look just fine for the rooks. Defense It probably doesn’t need to be stated just how horrific the Browns are, but the Jags defense had a lot to do with that. Travon Walker AND Josh Hines-Allen each walked away with 1.5 sacks. Foye Oluokun had a pick that resulted in a touchdown drive. Ventrell Miller looked like prime Brian Urlacher, leading the team with 10 tackles, two tackles for loss and a sack. Travis Hunter played both sides and played well. Those are your cornerstone guys who made the big plays all day long. You cannot ask for anything more. There is something to be said that Anthony Campanile stayed in Jacksonville and got another season with what was a good defense last year. All three levels of the defense played well all day long and coach Camp should be getting a lot of praise for that fact. Josh Hines-Allen told me he thought Ventrell Miller would lead the league in punch-outs. Miller just got his first punch-out of the season, and Hines-Allen got the fumble recovery 🔮🔮 pic.twitter.com/5kr0XqK8O9 https://t.co/mqgliUdBXe — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 13, 2026 Obligatory Cam Little Mention Little was solid again Sunday, connecting on his two kicks of 47 yards and 40 yards. I would’ve loved to see him actually make a tackle on that long kick return but oh well. Ross Matiscik laid the boom in his place later anyway. Ameer Abdullah I would’ve guessed that if I was mentioning Abdullah in any capacity after a Jags game, it would be because everyone else played so badly and I was grasping at straws. But not so fast. The Jags RB3-ish actually looked really good in his limited time. He had four carries for 32 yards and amassed 59 total kick return yards. He’s a veteran player and for what the Jags seemingly are going to use him for, he should be great. Credit to him. Losers Deshaun Watson This dude flat-out sucks, holy mother of Mary. The demons that follow Watson around and speak ancient phrases into his ears were working overtime Sunday. That first interception he threw was perfect timing for the defense. See ya next week. Deshaun Watson trying to wipe off whatever is in his visor that's making him throw the ball repeatedly to Jaguars players pic.twitter.com/Iy271MUtzO — Sam Monson (@SamMonsonNFL) September 13, 2026 Who do you think was the big winner from the Jags Week 1 win? Want to talk more on how well Lawrence played? Comment down below and we will see you right back here for the team’s Week 2 matchup next Sunday at the Denver Broncos.

title: NFL Power Rankings Week 2 Roundup: The Chiefs are back
summary: The 2026 NFL regular season’s opening weekend wrapped up with the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Denver Broncos and making a statement along the way. Let’s see how the national media responds in this week’s sampling of power rankings: NFL.com: 10 For the first time this decade, the Chiefs have a legitimately fearsome rushing attack. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY , MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes (15) of the Kansas City Chiefs hypes up the fans during the fourth quarter of the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri on Monday, September 14, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The 2026 NFL regular season’s opening weekend wrapped up with the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Denver Broncos and making a statement along the way. Let’s see how the national media responds in this week’s sampling of power rankings: NFL.com : 10 For the first time this decade, the Chiefs have a legitimately fearsome rushing attack. Kenneth Walker III won’t run for a career-high total every week, but he brings a punch that Kansas City’s backfield has lacked for most of the Patrick Mahomes era. That should make folks respect the Chiefs, even as Mahomes shakes off the rust accumulated by a lengthy recovery from knee surgery. — Nick Shook ESPN : 8 Week 1 result: Beat the Broncos 31-10 Preseason ranking: 13 Non-QB newcomer debut: RB Kenneth Walker III For one game at least, Walker was everything the Chiefs could’ve hoped for, bringing more explosive highlights to their rushing attack. Walker produced a career-high 173 rushing yards, with his best moment being a breakaway 60-yard touchdown on fourth-and-inches early in the third quarter. His best trait against the Broncos was his elusiveness, as he forced 14 missed tackles, the most by any Chiefs player in a game since 2018. Walker caught a short touchdown pass, too. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 7 Last week: 14 Monday: Beat Broncos 31-10 What we learned: They have a running game! After dealing with an inconsistent ground attack last season, the Chiefs went out and signed reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. It took Walker one game to make a big impact. All eyes in the opener were on Patrick Mahomes’ return, but it was Walker who stole the show, totaling 191 yards of offense and two touchdowns, and adding a new dimension to the K.C. offense. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 8 Kenneth Walker III earned every penny of his contract in his debut, and then some. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 1 0 Many buried this team, saying the dynasty was over. No it isn’t. Patrick Mahomes didn’t have to do a lot against Denver, but he’s healthy. That’s the good news. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 7 Kenneth Walker III was excellent and will transform the Chiefs’ offense. He had 173 yards rushing. Patrick Mahomes will be better as he get further removed from a torn ACL. He had just 184 yards passing and was off on many throws, but that didn’t take away from a successful return. But one of the best stories of the opener was left tackle Kahlil Benson. He is an undrafted rookie out of Indiana who got no guaranteed money to sign with the Chiefs and did not play left tackle in college. He was forced into the lineup due to a Josh Simmons injury and there was rightful concern over him protecting Mahomes’ blindside. But Benson, the first undrafted rookie to start Week 1 on the offensive line since Terence Steele with the Cowboys in 2020, played well and the Broncos rarely got any pressure on Mahomes. Offensive linemen don’t get too much attention, but Benson deserves a lot of credit for stepping up when he had to. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 6 Return of the King? Having a Super Bowl MVP tandem backfield of Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III was even more than it was cracked up to be in the opener, when K.C. made an emphatic statement that it’s ready to reclaim its AFC West throne from Denver. And maybe more. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 5 I think one of the singular most frustrating parts of covering professional football is spending an entire offseason attempting to understand what will be effective and will not be, and determining that Kansas City—a team starting an undrafted free agent tackle against one of the best defenses in football, having made a wing-and-a-prayer addition of a veteran running back to salvage the offense and starting a QB just nine months after a torn ACL—will struggle. Only to have the Chiefs absolutely demolish last year’s conference runner-up. The prediction game is a painful one, man. Don’t let your kids live this life. — Conor Orr FOX Sports : 1 2 They’re baaaaack. Patrick Mahomes didn’t even look like his old self Monday night and the Chiefs still dominated the Broncos. When Mahomes rounds into form, KC might be ready to reclaim its throne. — Ralph Vacchiano
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: 5 things we learned about the Chiefs from Week 1 win over Denver
summary: Well, that was fun. For all the fawning and saddle-riding the national media gave the Denver Broncos heading into this season, it turns out the burros were the paper champions all along. This game was a good old-fashioned AFC West beat down. Andy Reid and the Kansas City Chiefs dragged the NFL’s angriest little elf […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts after running with the ball against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that was fun. For all the fawning and saddle-riding the national media gave the Denver Broncos heading into this season, it turns out the burros were the paper champions all along. This game was a good old-fashioned AFC West beat down. Andy Reid and the Kansas City Chiefs dragged the NFL’s angriest little elf behind Arrowhead and took a switch to their backsides like my grandma did when I stole her pack of smokes as a kid. The Chiefs came out on a mission. They didn’t just want to win this game. They wanted to stake their claim back on the division. This was the Chiefs saying, time to get off the porch, lil pup; the big dogs are back. And although it’s just one win. It was a heck of a win, as the Chiefs force-fed Denver’s defense the rock like a kid who doesn’t want to eat their veggies at dinner time, rolling to a three-touchdown victory, winning 31-10. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs dominating the donkeys. 1. Chiefs can be a running team if they want to be The Chiefs made a point out of the gate to establish the run come hell or high water, and luckily they didn’t have to wait long for the benefits to take effect. Kenneth Walker was everything he was advertised as and more. Rushing for 173 yards on 23 carries, including an electric 60-yard touchdown run on 4th down. House call! #Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker just broke off a 60-yard rushing TD on 4th-and-1. Walker is up to 149 rushing yards on the night. pic.twitter.com/VDTwWmgJwd — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 15, 2026 Do I think the Chiefs will run the ball this much each week? I honestly don’t. But they can if they need to. If left tackle Josh Simmons is going to miss extended time. Or if the wide receivers struggle to create separation. I think there will be weeks where quarterback Patrick Mahomes passes for 300 yards and four touchdowns, but on the days when it’s not there, it’s good to know you can run the ball down the throat of one of the NFL’s best defenses. 2. Mahomes’ knee is fine Whether they will admit it or not, fan bases all around the NFL were hoping and praying that Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes would be limited in his first return to action since tearing his ACL last season. Because then there was at least a possibility that he would play like a mere mortal. But those hopes were dashed right off the back, when Mahomes tucked that ball and scrambled up the middle, scoring the team’s first touchdown of the season. PATRICK MAHOMES TD. HE IS BACK 🔥 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/OYNBfxBxun — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) September 15, 2026 In the words of the man himself, “You woke up the wrong mother******.” 3. Who said you can’t teach an old dog new tricks? They say you can’t teach an old dog new tricks. Well, it depends on the dog. If that old Saint Bernard is Andy Reid and you’re a competitive son of a buck who doesn’t want the final years of his legacy to be known as a guy who couldn’t change and adapt in the NFL. By running the ball 31 times, Andy Reid proved on Monday night that all he cares about is winning, and he is willing to change his stripes to get there. But Reid has never been afraid to evolve when the moment called for it. I don’t think this is any different. This is a coach leaning into his offense’s strengths and trying to offset the fact that he has an undrafted rookie starting at left tackle. It was a master class by one of the greatest to ever coach the game. 4. Kahlil Benson isn’t great, but he battled At times, the pass rush beat him. There were times he looked overwhelmed. But overall, the undrafted rookie free agent offensive tackle played passable football in his first NFL action. If the Chiefs’ regular starting left tackle, Josh Simmons, is going to miss significant time, then the Chiefs will be counting on Benson to hold things down until Simmons can return. The biggest question now is: how does Benson adapt now that there is an entire game of tape on him out there? You can believe that defenses are watching his reps, and his success will depend on how he responds to their counterpunch. 5. This team is going to be hard to pass against The severity of rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane’s injury hurts this defense. He is a special talent who looks like a cornerstone you can build around for years to come. But even without Delane for most of Monday night, the Chiefs secondary locked down Denver’s vaunted wide receivers, holding Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton to three receptions for 13 yards. Do I think this performance was an outlier? Nope. Fellow cornerbacks Nohl Williams and L’Jarius Sneed were all over the place, too. Now, I don’t think Bo Nix is anything special. But our defense might be. There is a good possibility that our defense is the reason we win games this year.
author: Rocky Magaña

title: Chiefs News: Travis Kelce moves into 2nd place for all-time TEs list
summary: Amid the Kansas City Chiefs’ 31-10 blowout of the Denver Broncos in Week 1, tight end Travis Kelce etched his name further into the stone of NFL history. He didn’t set any speed records on the big catch-and-run Kelce had in the second half, but he did inch closer to legendary Chiefs tight end Tony […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Travis Kelce #87 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts after a play against the Denver Broncos during the second half of an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Amid the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 31-10 blowout of the Denver Broncos in Week 1, tight end Travis Kelce etched his name further into the stone of NFL history. He didn’t set any speed records on the big catch-and-run Kelce had in the second half, but he did inch closer to legendary Chiefs tight end Tony Gonzalez on the all-time tight end receiving list. The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs’ Travis Kelce moves into second place for all-time tight end receiving yards | NFL.com Predictably, Kelce downplayed the individual milestone when speaking to ESPN’s Laura Rutledge after the game. “It’s a good feeling to get this win, all the other stuff is just hoopla now,” he said. Kelce caught a 59-yard pass from old friend Patrick Mahomes in the third quarter to put him past longtime Dallas Cowboys stalwart Jason Witten for second all-time. Ahead of Monday’s season opener, Kelce had 13,002 yards, needing 45 to surpass Witten (13,046). The catch was a turn-back-the-clock moment for Kelce, standing as his longest reception since Week 15, 2021, when he turned in a 69-yarder versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Patrick Mahomes Gets Win In Return: 3 Takeaways As Chiefs Beat Broncos | FOX Sports Chiefs Look Like Contenders In Mahomes’ Return There was punctuation as well – Mahomes found rookie running back Emmett Johnson for 25 yards on a third down, setting up a flip-toss touchdown to Walker for a 31-10 lead to put the game out of reach. Mahomes improved to 8-0 at home against Denver in his career, one of the longest home streaks for any quarterback against any opponent. After his shaky start, Mahomes went 11-for-13 for 145 yards and two touchdowns to pull away. Kenneth Walker III, Patrick Mahomes lead Chiefs’ win vs. Broncos | ESPN Mahomes’ toughness and athleticism were on display on his 10th snap, as he scrambled out of the pocket and dove — while being hit by two defenders — for a 15-yard touchdown. His top speed during that scramble reached 15.8 mph, which was 2.5 mph faster than his average speed on rushing attempts last season, according to Next Gen Stats. “Going for the end zone, it kind of gave me that confidence that I can go out there and be myself,” said Mahomes, who underwent surgery in December to repair a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. “I just wanted to play. I had done so much rehab and so much work to put myself in this position. I just wanted to get out there and play. This is what you do it for. “That was definitely the moment, physically, to say all this work has paid off. I didn’t feel anything.” From front to back, Chiefs’ defense brought the heat against the Denver Broncos | The Kansas City Star The Broncos finished with 176 total yards and nine first downs. They rushed for 61 and went 2 of 12 on third-down conversions. “Our third down numbers weren’t good, our rushing numbers weren’t good, pick your spots,” Broncos head coach Sean Payton said. Chiefs cornerback L’Jarius Sneed, who returned to Kansas City after spending the previous two seasons with the Tennessee Titans, said Monday’s performance should end any doubt about this defense’s capability. “We come into a new season trying to figure out where we’re at, and we come out and play like this,” Sneed said. “This should build great confidence.” Kansas City Chiefs manage to deliver rushing performance at Arrowhead Stadium not seen in 10 years | Yahoo! Sports This rushing performance also made a bit of history for the Chiefs, as it marked the first time in 10 years that they had rushed for 220 yards at Arrowhead Stadium. Ironically, their last 200-yard+ rushing performance at home came against the Denver Broncos as well, as the team rushed for 238 yards on Christmas Day 2016. What makes this stat even more prevalent is that both games resulted in the Chiefs picking up wins with almost identical scorelines. The Chiefs’ 2026 opener saw them beat the Broncos 31-10, while their Christmas Day outing in 2016 saw them defeat the Broncos 33-10. Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid proves he still has his fastball after dusting off a play from the 1930s for RB Kenneth Walker | A to Z Sports Week 1 against Denver, the Chiefs pulled out a play from even earlier. This time it was a 1936 play the team watched on grainy black-and-white film and mastered throughout training camp. The play, dubbed “Heisman,” resulted in a 2-yard touchdown reception for RB Kenneth Walker. It included QB Justin Fields, QB Patrick Mahomes, and TE Travis Kelce aligned in the backfield in a one-point stance. Kansas City, of course, has run other trick plays over the years. You’ll remember “Corn Dog”, “Snow Globe”, “Bloated Tebow Pass“, and “Hungry Pig Right.” All of these plays were hallmarks of Reid’s tenure with the Chiefs, and those moments captured what it was like to have fun playing football in Kansas City. He brought that back again with this latest iteration in Week 1’s 30-10 win. Around the NFL This Eagles offensive lineman admits he was ‘a complete liability’ and needed to be shut down | The Athletic Dickerson confirmed while speaking on his Monday night radio show on 94.1 WIP that the Eagles had informed him of their plan to place him on injured reserve. “I was a complete liability yesterday,” Dickerson said. “I know I said earlier in camp, I shouldn’t be out there until I feel healthy.” The Eagles lineman said he has bone bruising in his right knee and was told it would not heal if he kept “banging it up,” and that he needed to shut it down. Dickerson said the injury occurred when he “got rolled up on in practice” a few weeks ago. He had hoped that the injury would improve. He underwent imaging on Monday, when it was determined that time off would be the “best plan going forward.” Sources: Drew Brees mulled playing for Broncos in AFC title game | ESPN After the Denver Broncos lost starting quarterback Bo Nix to a fractured ankle in their overtime playoff victory against the Buffalo Bills, Denver’s then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael had discussions with Brees about the former star quarterback coming out of retirement to be ready for the AFC Championship Game, sources told ESPN. Brees had turned 47 years old just two days before Nix sustained the ankle injury Jan. 17. Brees spoke to Lombardi and Carmichael, his longtime assistant coaches with the New Orleans Saints, early in the week ahead of Denver’s AFC Championship Game showdown against the New England Patriots, telling them that he wanted to first work out to see how his body would respond. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride 3 takeaways from the Chiefs’ season-opening beatdown of the Broncos The pass game will open up It took a while for the Chiefs’ offense to get over 15 passing yards. It was almost comical how much of the offense’s output was on Walker’s shoulders for much of the game. In the first half, Mahomes had just two completions over 12 pass attempts; neither catch resulted in a first down. In the second half, Mahomes was much more efficient. He completed 13 of 15 passes; eight of those catches resulted in a first down or a touchdown. title: 7 Winners and 3 Losers from the Chiefs’ win over the Broncos
summary: As fans of the Kansas City Chiefs, we could not have asked for a better season opener. The biggest offseason questions were answered in the affirmative as Patrick Mahomes returned to the field to hand the ball off and watch the running game rack up yardage. There were incredible moments from rookies on both sides […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after defeating the Denver Broncos in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images As fans of the Kansas City Chiefs , we could not have asked for a better season opener. The biggest offseason questions were answered in the affirmative as Patrick Mahomes returned to the field to hand the ball off and watch the running game rack up yardage. There were incredible moments from rookies on both sides of the ball, and the Chiefs outclassed the most recent AFC West Champions. Here are a few who stood out as the Chiefs rolled to a 31-10 win on “Monday Night Football.” Winners Quarterback Patrick Mahomes : Exactly nine months after having multiple ligaments repaired, the MVP took the field against one of the NFL’s best defenses, and opened the scoring with a rushing touchdown (after his first one got called back for a penalty). His 184-yard, three-total-touchdown performance was plenty on this day, as he shook off any rust and got the ball in the hands of his new playmaker. Running back Kenneth Walker III: What a Chiefs debut it was for Walker, the prize of the team’s offseason process. It was the best performance from a KC running back since Jamaal Charles’ prime. Kenneth racked up 191 total yards and two touchdowns, while averaging over 7 yards per carry. It was a scene Chiefs fans, and Patrick Mahomes, have been missing— not just a competent running game, but an explosive one that can carry this offense. Cornerback Nohl Williams : We only got a brief look at the new CB tandem in Kansas City, as Nohl Williams sacked Bo Nix before Mansoor Delane picked him off. Unfortunately, Delane left with a shoulder injury— but Nohl was dominant all night. The future is bright in the Chiefs secondary. The defensive front seven: The numbers speak for themselves: 61 rushing yards allowed, 131 passing yards, 10 points allowed, 2 of 12 on third down, two turnovers, four sacks. It feels appropriate to recognize the entire front. Peter Woods knocked down a pass, Felix Anudike-Uzomah had a sack, R Mason Thomas had a sack, Chris Jones recovered a fumble, and Nick Bolton knocked down a pass that could have been ruled a fumble. The new-look rotation was fierce on Monday night. Tight end Travis Kelce: It’s looking like another banner year in the life of Kelce. He married one of the most famous and wealthy women in the world in the offseason. While she was in the suite with Tom Cruise, Travis rattled off a 59-yard catch-and-run, setting up a field goal. He led the Chiefs in receiving as if he’s not 35 years old. Running back Emmett Johnson: It’s easy to see why the Chiefs are so high on the new #10 in the backfield. Emmett racked up 68 total yards on his first 10 NFL touches, breaking tackles and refusing to give up on any play. Left tackle Kahlil Benson: How does an undrafted tryout player end up starting week one protecting the blind side of Patrick Mahomes? Andy Reid and his staff had faith in the kid—but not so much that they left him without help. Overall, it was a pretty clean game, especially given that Benson never played left tackle in college. Losers Center Creed Humphrey: The best center in the NFL had two bad snaps on opening night. Luckily neither ended in a turnover, but it’s not something you love to see. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen: It was a quiet Chiefs debut for the offseason standout. Allen didn’t record a single catch this week. He’ll look to get on track in week two, assuming he’s active on game day. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy : His six targets resulted in three catches for 18 yards. On one of those plays, it appeared Worthy ran the wrong route, resulting in an ugly interception. The Chiefs will need a lot more from the speedster this season, or the passing game will continue to struggle. Note: Applying the labels “losers” is not intended to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.
author: Matt Stagner

title: 3 takeaways from the Chiefs’ season-opening beatdown of the Broncos
summary: What a night it was for the Kansas City Chiefs. Facing the reigning AFC West champions, a team that took the division’s throne from the Chiefs after Kansas City’s nine-year run sitting upon it, the dynastic Chiefs made a statement: We’re back. With that theme from Monday night, here are three fresh takes from Kansas […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Kenneth Walker #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a night it was for the Kansas City Chiefs . Facing the reigning AFC West champions, a team that took the division’s throne from the Chiefs after Kansas City’s nine-year run sitting upon it, the dynastic Chiefs made a statement: We’re back. With that theme from Monday night, here are three fresh takes from Kansas City’s reminder to the NFL: 1. Andy Reid is willing to adjust You may have heard local media and certain bloggers talk about the Chiefs’ offensive identity shift to an under-center, run-centric approach this offseason. I can’t speak for everybody, but even the most optimistic version of myself didn’t see this coming. Walker gained 148 of his 173 rushing yards on under center runs against the Broncos. No other Chiefs running back has recorded 120 or more rushing yards from under center runs in a single game since at least 2016. #DENvsKC | #ChiefsKingdom — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 15, 2026 Quarterback Patrick Mahomes was under center plenty on Monday night, and that’s the way running back Kenneth Walker prefers it, as he told Kay Adams back in May . Walker did something Chiefs fans haven’t seen from a member of their favorite team’s backfield since 2016! The Chiefs’ offense not only adjusted to fit its personnel best, but the coaching staff also stayed committed to the game plan through a couple of stalled drives in the first half. Kansas City punted three consecutive possessions after the opening-drive touchdown, but the offense continued to ride Walker and a downhill ground attack. It’s a reminder that head coach Andy Reid (and general manager Brett Veach) had a vision for this team and didn’t waver from it since the start of the 2026 offseason. The makeover looks perfectly executed through one week. 2. This defense is very ahead of schedule Like the 2022 Chiefs, this year’s defense features rookies who will develop on the fly while playing prominent roles. However, this year’s unit may be ahead of schedule. Like, way ahead of schedule. Hey, Rookie! 👋 pic.twitter.com/zB7pxgej4n — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) September 15, 2026 Cornerback Mansoor Delane showed off elite coverage skills from the jump. On the opening drive, Delane manned up wide receiver Courtland Sutton, sticking to his hip pocket and covering up the route so well that when he turned to defend the pass, he barely needed to react, and he had an interception. Shortly after, Delane left the game with a shoulder injury, but one play is all it took for Delane to show why he could be one of the next elite cornerbacks in the NFL. Up front, defensive end R Mason Thomas ignited a pass rush that tormented a Broncos offense that surrendered the fewest sacks in the NFL last season. Quarterback Bo Nix was sacked four times and fumbled three times. Defensive tackle Peter Woods flashed as a pass rusher too, batting down a pass at one point. The 2022 Chiefs’ defense allowed 21 points to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1 and 24 points (and 401 total yards) to the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. There were clear growing pains early in that season; this year, it’s harder to tell where these rookies need to improve. 3. The pass game will open up It took a while for the Chiefs’ offense to get over 15 passing yards. It was almost comical how much of the offense’s output was on Walker’s shoulders for much of the game. In the first half, Mahomes had just two completions over 12 pass attempts; neither catch resulted in a first down. In the second half, Mahomes was much more efficient. He completed 13 of 15 passes; eight of those catches resulted in a first down or a touchdown. The commitment to the run game certainly helped the offense find a better dropback rhythm as the game went on. The biggest blemish in the second half seemed to be a miscommunication between Mahomes and wide receiver Xavier Worthy, one of the game’s most frustrating storylines. The third-year wideout needs to get on the same page with Mahomes one way or another. That said, Denver’s pass defense is truly elite. Mahomes will find softer coverages to exploit, and continuing to run the ball will only help.

(Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs saw immediate returns on investing the sixth overall selection in April’s NFL Draft on former LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane. On the third scrimmage play of Monday’s 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos , Delane intercepted a pass off of Bronco’s quarterback Bo Nix. The Chiefs then started their first drive at the Denver 46-yard line. Ten plays later, quarterback Patrick Mahomes punched in a 15-yard touchdown to give Kansas City the early lead. What a start to Mansoor Delane's NFL career 😳 DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QLLHsXsPqz — NFL (@NFL) September 15, 2026 Unfortunately, Delane’s night came to an end after delivering what may have ultimately been the game’s turning point during its third minute. The rookie was not on the field for Kansas City’s next defensive series. After he went to the locker room, the Chiefs declared him questionable to return with a shoulder injury. The Chiefs downgraded Delane to out after halftime. On the ensuing kickoff after Mahomes’ touchdown run, starting base linebacker Cooper McDonald also injured his knee while on coverage. Like Delane, McDonald was ruled out to start the second half. After the game, head coach Andy Reid had no real update on either player. “Delane hurt his shoulder,” Reid confirmed. “We’re just going to see where that goes from here. Cooper McDonald, he hurt his knee. So we’ve just got to see in the next day or so where that leaves us with both those guys.” Delane suffered a shoulder injury in offseason workouts and was limited for much of the team’s training camp. The Chiefs face a short week heading into Sunday’s matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. We will monitor both players’ participation in this week’s practices starting Wednesday. If either player misses time, they could benefit from Kansas City having the earliest possible bye in Week 5.

full_text: East Rutherford, NJ December 31, 2023 -- The Giants defense with Jihad Ward and Kayvon Thibodeaux of the Giants sack Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in the second half. The Los Angeles Rams edged the New York Giants 26-25 on December 31, 2023 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Week 1 of the NFL season is in the books and Week 2 is upon us. After a high-scoring opening weekend, there are plenty of questions waiting to be answered. The biggest matchups include the Bills hosting the Lions, the Bengals traveling to Houston to face the Texans, and the Jaguars traveling to Mile High to face the Broncos. Monday Night Football features the Los Angeles Rams (0-1) hosting the New York Giants (1-0) at SoFi Stadium. Three of the biggest disappointments from Week 1 were the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Chargers and Green Bay Packers, while the Minnesota Vikings, Arizona Cardinals, and New York Giants emerged as some of the biggest surprises. After going 10-6 with my Week 1 picks , I’m looking to build on that start as we dive into another exciting slate of NFL action. If you want to submit your Week 2 NFL picks: CLICK HERE Week 2 Picks: Detroit Lions @ Buffalo Bills — Thurs., 8:15 p.m. ET Both teams scored 30+ points in Week 1 and the same could happen again in Week 2 as both teams are still trying to find their defenses. My Pick: Bills 37-30 Carolina Panthers @ Atlanta Falcons — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET If the Panthers can bottle up Bijan Robinson, then they should be able to go into Atlanta and secure a Week 2 road win. My Pick: Panthers 29-24 Minnesota Vikings @ Chicago Bears — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET How Brian Flores gameplans for Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson will be interesting. Jalen Hurts is still a one dimensional quarterback. They get an easy road game in Tennessee. My Pick: Eagles 34-17 Pittsburgh Steelers @ New England Patriots — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Patriots have had 10 days off to get ready for the Steelers and should be able to come up with solution with AJ Brown’s absence. My Pick: Patriots 20-17 Green Bay Packers @ New York Jets — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Packers blew a pretty important Week 1 divisional game. Week 2 features an east coast contest against Aaron Glenn’s Jets. My Pick: Packers 30-20 Cleveland Browns @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET Baker Mayfield revenge game? Baker Mayfield bounce back game? Mayfield earned a huge payday and then turned in a dud in Week 1; fumbling the ball three times. My Pick: Buccaneers 28-17 New Orleans Saints @ Baltimore Ravens — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET Tyler Shough is showing signs of improvement and growth in year two. But the combination of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry is going to be too much for the Saints to handle outside of their dome. My Pick: Ravens 41-20 Cincinnati Bengals @ Houston Texans — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Texans get another elite quarterback early – who came up with their schedule? I have to believe that Demeco Ryans buttons up Burrow who is less mobile/twitchy than Josh Allen. My Pick: Texans 23-17 Jacksonville Jaguars @ Denver Broncos — Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET Trevor Lawrence vs. Bo Nix. Jacksonville will have an extra day to prepare but they will also have to fly across the country. I like Denver at home in afternoon game. My Pick: Broncos 23-16 Las Vegas Raiders @ Los Angeles Chargers — Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET The Chargers were one of the biggest disappointments in Week 1. Justin Herbert only throwing for 209 yards was shocking to say the least. Could Jim Harbaugh’s seat be getting hot? New offensive coordinator, a bad offensive line, and lack of offensive weapons make life for Jayden Daniels difficult. The Cowboys should bounce back in Week 2. If the Cardinals can shut down Justin Herbert, there is a chance they can pull off an upset. Mike LaFleur could be able to scheme up enough offense. My Pick: Cardinals 16-13 Miami Dolphins @ San Francisco 49ers — Sun., 4:25 p.m. ET Just when you think the 49ers are irrelevant, they find a way to be considered Super Bowl contenders. They have arguably the most NFL experience at key positions: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Deebo Samuel, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner. The 49ers could be a problem all season. My Pick: 49ers 33-10 Indianapolis Colts @ Kansas City Chiefs — Sun., 8:20 p.m. ET Patrick Mahomes. Sunday Night Football. Give me the Chiefs. My Pick: Chiefs 24-20 New York Giants @ Los Angeles Rams — Mon., 8:15 p.m. ET I am very worried about this game for the Rams. The offense was anemic in Week 1. The offense lacks a complimentary piece to Puka Nacua. The defense is now without Myles Garrett for the next four weeks at minimum. The Giants have a new offensive identity under Harbaugh where they can run the ball with the bruising force of Cam Skattebo. Not to mention Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers are issues in the passing game. The Rams need to be ready to play on Monday Night but I am skeptical… My Pick: Giants 27-24

title: Will Aaron Donald suit up for Rams on Monday?
summary: Will Aaron Donald make his 2026 debut on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants? The Rams may need him. With Myles Garrett out, and the entire team looking middle of the pack (at best) against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Rams may need Donald to help them get back in […]
full_text: Will Aaron Donald make his 2026 debut on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants? The Rams may need him. With Myles Garrett out, and the entire team looking middle of the pack (at best) against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Rams may need Donald to help them get back in the win column. It’s not time to panic, but it is time to seriously realize that if the Rams do not start stacking wins now, or at the very least show some improvement in Week 2, this season could get away from them quicker than they had ever considered. It’s Tuesday, time will tell who all will be officially active on Monday night. Could Donald be one of the Rams to come out of the tunnel? Stay tuned. Rams HC Sean McVay noncommittal on Aaron Donald’s Week 2 status (ramswire) “ Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay isn’t tipping his hand on whether Aaron Donald will suit up for Monday Night Football against the New York Giants , saying the Rams simply haven’t made a decision yet. “He’s going to continue to work his process,” McVay said, “and we’ll see what that looks like.” Sean McVay offers positive updates on 3 Rams injuries (ramswire) “McVay called the updates on safety Kam Curl , inside linebacker Nate Landman , inside linebacker Omar Speights and tight end Davis Allen “positive,” suggesting the Rams could get some of their key contributors back sooner rather than later. Curl exited Thursday’s game in the second half with an ankle injury. While he was officially listed as questionable to return, McVay said the veteran safety “is good,” downplaying the injury as ankle soreness. Curl has quickly become one of the most important pieces of the Rams defense, starting all 17 games last season while playing 99% of the defensive snaps. He signed a $36 million contract extension this offseason. Jaylen McCollough replaced Curl after going down, who had two tackles before exiting.“ 4 things Rams learned from Sunday’s games: Are LaFleur’s Cardinals…good? (ramswire) “As always in the opening weekend of the season, there were plenty of surprises and new developments across the league. Here are four things the Rams learned about their foes in the NFC, including a couple of impressive upcoming opponents in the Cardinals and Giants. Cardinals won’t be the easy out many people expected them to be The Cardinals’ projected win total was set at 3.5 before the season started. After just one game, they’re already a quarter of the way toward eclipsing that number set by oddsmakers. They beat the Chargers convincingly on Sunday, 26-14, in Mike LaFleur’s head coaching debut. And they were on the road in L.A., too.“ Did Browns Know More Than Rams Ahead of Myles Garrett Trade? Why Deal Timing Was Perfect (heavy.com) “Garrett earned his second Defensive Player of the Year award in 2025 after tallying 23 sacks and breaking the NFL’s single-season mark in that category. He wanted a raise heading into his age-31 campaign and didn’t make sense for Cleveland’s timeline, given the Browns don’t appear likely to have a true franchise QB before 2027, which probably means it will be at least 2028 before the team can seriously contend. The Browns executed a deal with the Los Angeles Rams , after which Garrett missed considerable time during the spring and summer with knee issues that included swelling. Now, after one wildly underwhelming performance in a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, Garrett is going to miss at least four weeks due to surgery.“ Reeling Rams defense can’t afford to underestimate Jaxson Dart and the Giants (ramblinfan) “While 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy picked apart the Rams, the Giants’ Jaxson Dart dominated the Cowboys secondary in similar fashion, completing 23-of-29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns. He was cooly efficient en route to averaging an impressive 0.73 EPA per play, wasting little energy in leading his offense to a touchdown in every quarter. And now the LA defense, which is already reeling , must step up and stop him in Week 2. Rams defense won’t be overconfident vs Giants in Week 2 Whatever exposed the Rams so badly, those factors have been scrubbed for Week 2. They are no longer anointed as default winners. The roster is no longer seen as bursting with insurmountable superstars, many of whom either struggled in the season opener , are injured entering Week 2 (i.e., Myles Garrett),or both.“ Texas A&M Legend Myles Garrett’s Injury Situation Takes New Turn (sports.yahoo) “ Myles Garrett ‘s highly anticipated debut with the Los Angeles Rams did not go according to plan, and now the former Texas A&M star is facing a significant absence after undergoing knee surgery. Garrett was dealing with the knee issue throughout the summer, limiting his participation during training camp and the preseason. However, the Rams believed the veteran defensive end would be able to manage the injury and contribute once the regular season arrived.“ Rams tumble in Week 2 power rankings: Is LA a top-5 team? (ramswire) “ 5. Los Angeles Rams (1): Woof. At least you couldn’t blame the special teams for this loss? But the Rams scored their fewest points of the Matthew Stafford era, while WR Puka Nacua had more tackles (1) than ballyhooed offseason acquisition Myles Garrett, who will be out at least the next month – apparently he should’ve stayed in L.A. with Aaron Donald. This was likely an anomalous defeat, if a reminder that the Lombardi Trophy is guaranteed to no team.“ Rams undecided if Donald will play vs. Giants (nbcsports) “Donald was kept off the Week 1 roster for last week’s opener against the 49ers, and the Rams did receive a two-game roster exemption for Donald after he agreed to return. Speaking on Monday, McVay said Donald will “continue to work his process” and that the team will see how things look from there. With the Rams losing Myles Garrett (knee) for at least the next four games, it’s safe to assume they would like to get Donald on the field sooner rather than later. – Zachary Krueger ” Broncos-Chiefs on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from Kansas City’s 31-10 win (nfl.com) “ Davis’ Denver offense stymied. As Patrick Mahomes made his much-ballyhooed return after tearing his ACL and LCL last season, his former Texas Tech teammate Davis Webb was making his debut as the Broncos play-caller and offensive coordinator. Monday went much better for Mahomes. Webb and Broncos QB Bo Nix , in his first game since breaking his ankle in the Divisional Round, never found any consistent success. Kenneth Walker’s 191 total yards for the Chiefs bested the Broncos’ 176. Nix looked sharper earlier passing than Mahomes, but it made no matter as the game wore on with Denver shockingly held to nine first downs and its ground game non-existent. J.K. Dobbins was the leading ground gainer with a meager 36 yards, while Nix’s 19-yard TD toss to Evan Engram to tie the game in the first quarter was really the last splash of any kind had by Webb’s offense. After the Chiefs vaulted ahead, 21-7, on a stellar 60-yard gallop by Walker in the third quarter, Mahomes was picked off by Brandon Jones on the Chiefs’ ensuing drive. Set up at the KC 5-yard line, Nix and the offense went backward and settled for a 31-yard field goal by Wil Lutz — Denver’s last points of the game. With such high expectations and such a disastrous debut for Webb and the offense, one has to wonder how long head coach Sean Payton will wait until snatching the offensive reins back.“ NFL ties Week 1 scoring record for Super Bowl era (nfl.com) “Thanks to the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos combining for 41 points on Monday night, the opening slate of games for the 2026 season has officially tied the 2012 season’s record for the most Week 1 points scored (791) during the Super Bowl era. Entering Monday’s AFC West showdown, teams had averaged 50.0 combined points per game, per NFL Research, with the Week 1 finale bringing the average down to 49.4.“ Comment of the Day: “McVay, I like you as a coach,…
