title: Rams believe Myles Garrett will only miss the minimum 4 games, per report
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and Myles Garrett decided together that it was best for him to get surgery now to address his knee injury with the hope that he will be 100-percent when he returns from injury reserve in a month, according to a report by Ian Rapoport on Monday. Rapoport detailed the thought process […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams and Myles Garrett decided together that it was best for him to get surgery now to address his knee injury with the hope that he will be 100-percent when he returns from injury reserve in a month, according to a report by Ian Rapoport on Monday. Rapoport detailed the thought process behind Garrett’s arthroscopic knee surgery that led to the reigning Defensive Player of the Year that led to him being placed on IR on Sunday , meaning he will miss at least four games on The Aftermath show. The Rams believe that Garrett will only miss those four games and be ready to return in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, according to Rapoport. From The Aftermath on @NFLNetwork : A look at where it stands for #Rams star Myles Garrett and what went into the decision to have surgery. pic.twitter.com/iy0ClVumkE — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 14, 2026 This is of course not something anyone can actually predict, including doctors. It depends on how Garrett’s rehab process goes and sometimes just the luck of the draw. Garrett will definitely miss the next four games: Giants, Broncos, Bills, and Eagles. Those aren’t four games that anyone on the Rams wants Garrett to miss, but L.A. and Garrett’s “team” of advisors believe it’s better to go with surgery now and be 100-percent for the rest of the season, rather than wait and see how his body responds to rest. If all goes to plan, Garrett would be his normal self beginning with the Cardinals in Week 6 and onto the rest of the season. In his first game with the Rams, Garrett recorded zero tackles. That’s the type of performance that led to the Rams discussing their options with Garrett after they return to L.A. and this is what they’ve decided on. Whether it will work as they hope is something only time will tell.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Giants aren’t the pushovers they were expected to be
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were supposed to get a soft landing when they returned from Australia with a Week 2 home game against the New York Giants, but if Week 1 is any indication then John Harbaugh’s new look G-Men are anything but an “easy win”. The Giants beat the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on Sunday […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams were supposed to get a soft landing when they returned from Australia with a Week 2 home game against the New York Giants, but if Week 1 is any indication then John Harbaugh’s new look G-Men are anything but an “easy win”. The Giants beat the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on Sunday Night Football, as Jaxson Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns in his first game with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, and Malik Nabers returned from a torn ACL to catch six passes for 69 yards . New York may have been even more impressive defensively, holding Dak Prescott to just 175 yards on 34 pass attempts and containing receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to a combined 76 yards on the night. It’s only been one week, but the Giants have not had a top-10 offense and top-10 defense since 2008, and this is easily their most complete team since the days of Tom Coughlin and Eli Manning. Will the Rams be able to get their rebound win in Week 2 or will the travel and the loss of Myles Garrett prove to be their undoing? 𝗥𝗘𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧: There is no timetable for Myles Garrett’s return after being placed on IR with a knee injury, per HC Sean McVay. pic.twitter.com/q8Osx5l0mu — JPA (@jasrifootball) September 14, 2026 Giants offense The Giants scored one touchdown in each of their four quarters against the Cowboys, a defense that was supposed to be vastly improved from last season under the guidance of first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. We even saw in L.A.’s joint practice against Dallas this year that the Cowboys looked far more competent on defense than they did in the joint practice in 2025. However, was that just because of who the Cowboys were facing? Giants running back Cam Skattebo had 18 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown against Dallas, the second-highest rushing yards total of his young career. Harbaugh brings that “rushing mentality” from the Baltimore Ravens to New York and instantly there’s a difference in the mentality and violence that the Giants have as a rushing team. Cam Skattebo meets DeMarvion Overshown in the hole. pic.twitter.com/W4vkaMmfOn — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 The Rams opened up some gaping running lanes for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 1. That won’t be good enough in Week 2 against Skattebo, Devin Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy. But the most success part of New York’s passing game was Dart to tight end Isaiah Likely, a free agent who followed Harbaugh from Baltimore to the Giants on a three-year, $40 million contract: 8 targets 8 catches 78 yards 2 TDs 1 fumble (recovered) That’s largely how Dart was able to complete so many of his passes and be so efficient on Sunday. Nabers did what he did, but Odell Beckham Jr had zero targets on 11 snaps in his return to New York. Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, and Theo Johnson make up the rest of the weapons, but Singletary also caught a touchdown and is a threat in the passing game. The Giants faced 11 third downs and converted nine of them. Giants defense The Cowboys were supposed to be this offensive “juggernaut” with Dak as an MVP candidate, but they basically looked terrible. DAK PRESCOTT DEEP BALL 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/TGWsOdZxhA — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) September 14, 2026 The fact that Dak has the third-HIGHEST QBR after Week 1 shows just how bad stats can be. Most of his yards (52%) came after the catch and he didn’t even have that many yards. Superstar receiver Lamb (5 catches for 44 yards and a TD on eight targets) and Pickens (three catches for 28 yards on six targets) were insignificant against New York’s secondary. Despite not having the biggest names back there — reclamation projects like Deonte Banks (2 pass breakups) and Greg Newsome II at corner — the Giants weren’t afraid of the Cowboys receivers. Safety Jevon Holland had an interception. The Giants ranked dead last in yards per carry allowed last season, but held Javonte Williams to 41 yards on 12 carries and Dallas as a whole to 69 yards on 18 carries. Rookie fifth overall pick Arvell Reese got no sacks, nor did anyone else on New York’s defense, but he had a TFL and a QB hit. The Giants front-seven includes Reese, Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, D.J. Reader, Kayvon Thibodeaux, and Shelby Harris. It could be a murderer’s row with Harbaugh and defensive coordinator and Dennard Wilson, considering what he was able to build on the Ravens. Giants special teams There’s not a lot to mention from Week 1, but just a reminder that Harbaugh is a former special teams coordinator who prides himself in the third phase. He brought punter Jordan Stout with him to New York after he had an All-Pro season in Baltimore in 2025. Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada went 4-of-4 on extra points and didn’t get any field goal attempts. There were no punt returns in the game for either team. Rams-Giants The Rams do not face a “do or die” in Week 2, but a loss to the Giants on Sunday would divide the fanbase by as much distance as there is from here to Melbourne. Some will say that it’s the end of the season if L.A. drops to 0-2. Others will say there’s a lot of football left. (Mostly people will probably be devastated though, if we’re being honest.) Well, the Rams are hardly underdogs in Week 2 against the Giants. In fact, the Rams are 8.5 point favorites at FanDuel which is fairly massive . However, what’s clear is that these aren’t the Giants most expected them to be. The Cowboys were popular preseason picks to win the NFC East, if not go to the Super Bowl, and they looked far outmatched by Harbaugh’s Giants in his New York debut. Between the new looks on offense, and the potential to be vastly improved on defense and special teams, the Giants are heading to SoFi this week with the intention to send a message: “We aren’t the same Giants.“ Is that true? We’ll find out in less than a week.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: The Giants stole 49ers’ playbook and that is bad news for Rams
summary: The San Francisco 49ers know the recipe for a win over the Los Angeles Rams—and that was on full display again in a stunning Week 1 upset in Australia. The bad news for the Rams is that their next opponent, the New York Giants, seem to have found San Francisco’s cookbook in the back of […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants celebrates a 28-20 win against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers know the recipe for a win over the Los Angeles Rams—and that was on full display again in a stunning Week 1 upset in Australia. The bad news for the Rams is that their next opponent, the New York Giants, seem to have found San Francisco’s cookbook in the back of the cabinet in their win against the Dallas Cowboys. LA enters Week 2 as 8.5-point home favorites over the Giants. A repeat performance by the Giants and Jaxson Dart could cook up a major upset and send the Rams to 0-2 on the young season. There are plenty of parallels between the Giants and 49ers that should make the Rams nervous: NY won time of possession with 36:40 and limited Dallas’ possessions. Despite fewer opportunities with the ball, Dak Prescott threw an interception just before halftime. New York took advantage and scored. That was ultimately the difference in this sped up contest. Make hay in the short passing game Dart gave his best Brock Purdy impression. He was decisive and accurate in the short area of the field, allowing his receivers room to run thereafter. Dart’s longest throw was 19 yards. Read how Purdy got the job done in Week 1 here. Totals by route type: Flat: 3/3 for 29 yards Slant: 2/2 for 18 yards Hitch: 6/8 for 46 yards Crossing: 4/4 for 60 yards Short out: 4/6 for 51 yards Stay committed to the run game New York rushed 37 times for 165 yards and manufactured 84 yards after contact. They remained committed to the ground attack with a 4.45-yard average and an EPA per play of -0.05. Their best work came out of 12 personnel, which is another similarity to San Francisco. Smart situational football San Francisco forced LA into long and unfavorable late downs and distances. The Giants won the early downs and finished 9/11 on third down to extend possessions and keep the ball away from Dallas. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are one of the most formidable duos in the NFL. They can’t impact the game without the football. Find hidden yardage The 49ers stuffed a Matthew Stafford sneak at the half-yard line and then drove 99.5 yards for a score. Fred Warner also forced a late fumble on Tyler Higbee. The Giants capitalized on a late first half interception and then manufactured three long second half drives to suffocate the Cowboys. What this all means for Monday night Despite Dart resembling Purdy in Week 1, he’s been more of an inefficient gunslinging playmaker so far in his career. Barring a stark shift in his style of play, this seems like an isolated storm of events that produced a limited game plan. I’ll need to see Dart do it again before I fully believe. Even without Myles Garrett , the Rams still enter Week 2 with the more talented roster. Winning on the margins in terms of late downs, time of possession, turnovers, etc. are the great equalizer. This is how the 49ers consistently surprise LA and the same recipe for how the Giants can secure their second primetime win in a row.
author: JB Scott

title: Sean McVay Meter: Fans’ confidence in coach after Week 1
summary: One game does not define a season, but Rams fans have every right to feel frustrated after what unfolded in Melbourne. The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 1 with high expectations, only to deliver a disappointing performance against the San Francisco 49ers. When a team struggles in multiple areas, the head coach is naturally going […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 26: Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams gathers the team during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 26, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images One game does not define a season, but Rams fans have every right to feel frustrated after what unfolded in Melbourne. The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 1 with high expectations, only to deliver a disappointing performance against the San Francisco 49ers. When a team struggles in multiple areas, the head coach is naturally going to face questions, and Sean McVay is no exception. McVay has earned the benefit of the doubt throughout his tenure in Los Angeles. His track record includes a Super Bowl championship, multiple playoff appearances and a reputation as one of the NFL’s best offensive minds. However, expectations have changed. Rams fans are no longer simply hoping for playoff football —they expect this team to win a championship come February. Sean McVay Fan Confidence Meter 9-10 — Unshakable 7-8 — Strong 5-6 — Cautiously Optimistic 3-4 — Frustrated 1-2 — Crisis The Week 1 performance could test the patience of a fan base that believes the Rams have enough talent to make a deep postseason run. Questions about game planning, execution and adjustments will inevitably lead back to McVay. There also could also be lingering frustration surrounding how the team handled Myles Garrett’s knee situation. If Garrett’s knee issues were already a concern in July, some fans may question why the situation wasn’t addressed more aggressively before the regular season. Seeing an important player deal with the consequences now can make those earlier decisions easier to scrutinize. The season is far from over, but the Sean McVay Meter has already moved. Whether it is a temporary reaction to one bad performance or the beginning of deeper concerns will depend heavily on how McVay and the Rams respond in Week 2 .
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams had amazing offseason, dud Week 1
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had one of the best on paper off-season’s in modern sports, then followed that up with a horrible Week 1. Things can always be worse, but the Week 1 that L.A. just has proven again why picking a Super Bowl winner in August is nearly an impossible task. Starting with the […]
full_text: Westchester, - July 26: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams speaks head coach Sean McVay along with owner Stan Kronke after the first day of the Los Angeles Rams Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Sunday, July 26, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams had one of the best on paper off-season’s in modern sports, then followed that up with a horrible Week 1. Things can always be worse, but the Week 1 that L.A. just has proven again why picking a Super Bowl winner in August is nearly an impossible task. Starting with the offseason, some would say the Rams received too much coverage the last few months, and that’s fair, but the Rams received so much coverage because they were constantly generating news. Trading for Trent Mcduffie, adding Jaylen Watson, trying to figure out their special teams, trading for Myles Garrett, keeping the offense in tact including Matthew Stafford, and Aaron Donald’s future with the team dominated NFL talk for months leading up to the 2026 season. Then, Week 1 actually happened. The Super Bowl favorite Rams got slapped in the face by the San Francisco 49ers. The Seattle Seahawks showed they can win with a backup quarterback and can still ride their defense. The Arizona Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Chargers in a major early season upset. Now, the Rams are looking up in the NFC West, and as of one week into the season, they look a bit lost. Myles Garrett is going to IR. AD must be wondering what he is coming back to? Sean McVay needs to figure it out. It’s been an interesting Week 1 for the Rams. They have more than a few games left. We’ll see what happens. A Whole Lot Changed In One Week For The Rams (defector) “How best to react to the latest news on the Los Angeles Rams? Easy: with complete abandon and logical recklessness. That’s how the veterans do it. Said latest news: that massive offseason acquisition Myles Garrett has fouled his knee, failed to will it healthy again, and now will have surgery that will take out all of September and a chunk of October as well. Garrett was the big swing of the summer , but the fact that it was the Rams that took it is no surprise. General manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay love acquisitional bat speed more than nearly any team not named Real Madrid or Barcelona, and between Garrett and veteran ace in the hole Aaron Donald, they surely constructed the most unsettling defensive front since their own Fearsome Foursome six decades ago.“ Myles Garrett Goes On IR After Knee Surgery: What Does It Mean For Rams? (foxsports) “Star edge rusher Myles Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his knee and will be placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least four games, The Ringer first reported . FOX Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer later confirmed the news. “Myles Garrett didn’t do a lot of practice in this training camp,” Glazer said on “FOX NFL Kickoff.” “He had a knee injury. You saw him there the other night against [San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle] Trent Williams; he just wasn’t right. So the team decided they’re going to have him undergo arthroscopic knee surgery.” Maxx Crosby reportedly turned down Rams interest after Ravens trade collapsed (sports.yah00) “League interest remained significant. Reports indicate that multiple teams contacted the Raiders after the Ravens trade collapsed. The Philadelphia Eagles , Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers were among clubs reported to have monitored the situation. Despite that interest, no offer matched what Las Vegas believed Crosby was worth, making a second trade unlikely. With Crosby remaining off the market , the Rams eventually shifted their attention elsewhere and later completed their blockbuster acquisition of Garrett. The move helped reshape Los Angeles’ defense, but the latest report suggests the organization may have initially preferred a different path.“ 3 things Rams can learn from Giants’ win ahead of Week 2 matchup (ramswire) “With the Rams looking to avoid a 0-2 start, here are three major lessons they must learn this week after New York dazzled in head coach John Harbaugh’s debut. Isaiah Likely will be a matchup problem Giants tight end Isaiah Likely impressed during his first few seasons with the Baltimore Ravens , even proving he was more productive than incumbent starter Mark Andrews when given an extended run of play. That chance never materialized, but in his debut with New York, he was ungardable. Rams gave Aaron Donald’s contract incentives creative nicknames (sports.yahoo) “The Los Angeles Rams do things their way, and one of the most defining elements of the team’s independent ideas is how they go about their roster. Their beliefs behind roster construction are often subjected to media attention, as the franchise leverages its top draft picks for star players, using its scouting and developmental departments to fill out the roster. However, that’s not the only aspect of their construction that is unique to Los Angeles . ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams give nicknames to incentive packages in their contracts, with Aaron Donald having monikers that define his return perfectly. He has one incentive named “I’m Back” and another called “I Got 99 Problems.” Rams’ Sean McVay reveals wife’s reality check after mulling media jump following losing season in 2022 (foxnews) “The Rams were 5-12 in 2022 – one year after beating the Cincinnati Bengals to win Super Bowl LVI. He said in an interview on “60 Minutes,” which aired Sunday night, that he was in a “dark” place and had to come to grips with the fact that a few losses weren’t a reflection on himself. He said his wife, Veronika Khomyn, hit him with a reality check. “I was ready to run away from coaching and hide behind a convenient narrative of some media opportunities,” he explained. “I’ll never forget, I was explaining to my wife, Veronika, it was a daunting task ahead for the ’23 season and I remember telling her, ‘Maybe I’ll take a year off,’ and she said, ‘That never sounded like the kind of leader you wanted to be.’” Rams coach Sean McVay “tormented,” even with the team as Super Bowl favorite (cbssports) “”You’re either in a storm, you’re coming out of one or you’re getting ready to go back into it,” McVay said. “And it’s one of those three things. But how you handle that is the separator.” How McVay’s handled winning and losing McVay’s Super Bowl win came after acquiring quarterback Matthew Stafford . But the coach’s joy over the win was fleeting. “The lies I told myself were, ‘I won’t be happy until I — until we win one.’ Or, ‘I win one,'” McVay said. “It was a lot more selfish. And, you know, you’re embarrassed to kind of look back on how you got to where you did.” The Rams’ 2022 Super Bowl win was followed by a losing season. “It revealed a lot of insecurities that I had. My identity was so tied up in winning and losing games, and that was where I felt like my self-worth lied,” McVay said. “It was very revealing of how fragile I was and all the insecurities that I did have.” NFL Week 1 winners, losers: Deshaun Watson disastrous in Browns offense, Bears light up scoreboard (cbssports) “While the small sample size of one game can cloud reality, there are some cases where Week 1 tells the football world all it needs to know about a particular team or individual player. In Watson’s case, a poor season debut might be all it takes to write the book on his run as the Browns’ starting quarterback. For the Bears, a 59-point onslaught is compelling evidence that they are in for a monster year. In an 18-week season, there is still ample time to right wrongs and for strengths to devolve into weaknesses. But for now, some are off to hot starts while others could not have opened the year in a worse fashion. Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday’s Week 1 action.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 1:…

title: Rams have mixed results rebounding from Week 1 losses
summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener for the third time under Sean McVay on Thursday against the 49ers. Los Angeles has a mixed track record in the McVay era when rebounding from a Week 1 loss. Under McVay, the Rams are 7-3 in season openers since the start of the 2017 campaign. The […]
full_text: LA Rams' head coach Sean McVay speaks to the media at Marvel Stadium in Melbourne on September 10, 2026. The first-ever regular-season NFL game in Australia takes place at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026, featuring the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / - IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE - | AFP via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener for the third time under Sean McVay on Thursday against the 49ers. Los Angeles has a mixed track record in the McVay era when rebounding from a Week 1 loss. Under McVay, the Rams are 7-3 in season openers since the start of the 2017 campaign. The 20-point loss to San Francisco was their worst opening-game loss since the 2022 NFL season opener, when they lost by 21 points to the Bills. Overall, LA has lost back-to-back games to begin a season only once since McVay became coach. That is promising enough as the team looks past its Australian adventure to its upcoming primetime matchup against the Giants. Here is how the Rams have fared in the game after their past two season-opening losses. 2024 Week 2 – Lost 41-10 to Cardinals Week 1 Result: Lost 26-20 to Lions in overtime This one stunk to high heavens all around. The Rams came into this one with injuries at wide receiver and offensive line. Regardless, no one expected Arizona to run them out of the stadium. Yeah, the same Cardinals team that would fall apart down the stretch and miss the playoffs. The Redbirds started the game with a 21-0 lead and later 34-3 in the third quarter, so the outcome was never in doubt. They also amassed nearly 500 yards of offense to the Rams’ 245. LA truly never stood a chance. Looking back, it’s amazing the Rams eventually recovered after such a poor start to win the NFC West and nearly advance to the NFC Championship. 2022 Week 2 – Won 31-27 over Falcons Week 1 Result: Lost 31-10 to Bills Following a humbling season-opening loss to Buffalo, the defending Super Bowl champions were making quick work of the Falcons. LA jumped out to a 28-3 lead, which, against Atlanta, should’ve been the sign that the game would go haywire at some point. Still, the Rams led 31-10 early in the fourth quarter, a complete reversal from the week before. Then, things began to go south. The Falcons scored touchdowns on two straight drives, narrowing the lead to six points. They drove all the way to LA’s 24-yard line before Jalen Ramsey saved the day with a jaw-dropping interception to seal the game. JALEN RAMSEY IS HIM 😤 📺: #ATLvsLAR on FOX 📱: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/bM69Jy3G4O pic.twitter.com/gBrFyR9NUa — NFL (@NFL) September 18, 2022 Los Angeles was certainly fortunate not to fall to 0-2 after the near-collapse. A win is a win, and it was a highlight for them in a season that didn’t have many. Rams facing pressure to rebound quickly If the Rams cannot get past the Giants in Week 2, they could be in some serious trouble. The schedule gets BRUTAL after New York, so they must get things figured out quickly. After the Giants come to town, LA will have road games at the Broncos and Eagles before returning home to face the Bills. Following the Buffalo game, the Cardinals will travel to Hollywood. Coming into the season, Arizona was expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. That could still be true, yet they kicked off the Mike LaFleur era in style with an upset win over the Chargers. It’s early, but they could be a tough out this season. Needless to say, the pressure is on for a team expected to be a Super Bowl contender. It will be tough with Myles Garrett now on IR. However, LA advanced to the NFC Championship without Garrett last season, so hope is not lost whatsoever. Several players could step up, including the returning Aaron Donald and Garrett’s backup Josaiah Stewart . They should be able to hold down the fort with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year out for a few games. The Rams have been very successful under McVay, especially within the first two weeks of the season. McVay’s track record largely speaks for itself, and his team will need every bit of it if they hope to rebound against the Giants this week.

title: Dolphins Week 1 review: Thoughts and reactions from Raiders loss
summary: For the first time in 16 years, I do not have NFL Sunday Ticket.  The good news is that NFL+ has a condensed version of the game, so I can skip a lot of the talk and in-between play stuff that the normal podcast.  I can watch kickoff to final whistle in about 45 minutes.  […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins leads teammates onto the field before the NFL game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in 16 years, I do not have NFL Sunday Ticket. The good news is that NFL+ has a condensed version of the game, so I can skip a lot of the talk and in-between play stuff that the normal podcast. I can watch kickoff to final whistle in about 45 minutes. The bad news is that I can’t watch live via that source. I say all of this to preface the fact I watched the game LATE Sunday night, and that process will not likely change this season. With weekends being what they are for me, all my immediate takes will be from the perspective of watching the game late and trying to remember everything I saw. So if things seem off, perhaps that’s why. Perhaps . Anyway, here we go. Youth and experience was front and center This has been THE major talking point all offseason and we all knew coming into this season that rookies were going to play a major factor. This Miami Dolphins team is loaded with players who have not played many NFL snaps on both sides of the ball. Profootballreference.com has the snap counts and starters from the game on their site. On offense, Miami started 3 rookies: Caleb Douglas, Will Kacmarek, and Kadyn Proctor. On defense, Miami started 3 rookies: Jacob Rodriguez, Chris Johnson, and Michael Taaffe. The Douglas, Kacmarek, and Proctor played 51, 14, and 56 snaps respectively, with 56 being all the offensive snaps. Rodriguez, Johnson, and Taaffe played 68, 68, and 51 snaps respectively, with 68 being all the defensive snaps. Other rookies like Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman Jr., and DJ Herman saw significant snaps. But it wasn’t just the rookies. There were several starters who have limited playing time at the pro level. Starting safety Zayne Anderson played 53 snaps yesterday, which represents over 25% of his career total. Malik Willis, whom I highlighted as an “experienced rookie” played 56 snaps, which represents about 10% of his career total. Jordan Phillips, Jason Marshall Jr., Dante Trader Jr., and Zeek Biggers are all second-year players who played significant snaps against Las Vegas that all have less than 500 NFL snaps in their careers. That’s a long-winded way of saying the Dolphins are about as wet behind the ears as they can be across the board. That is going to lead to sloppy play from everyone. There are going to be missed assignments. There is going to be miscommunication. I saw more than one occasion where the offensive line looked more confused than the defense. There is going to be a lot of splintery wood to sand down before this looks like what we want it to be. That doesn’t make it any easier to watch, but it does add some perspective when you realize that of 22 starters, only 8 had more than 1000 career snaps entering this contest. Coaching is a concern I read something somewhere that this game was only like the 6th time in NFL history that 2 rookie head coaches faced off against one another. Maybe that’s true; maybe it’s not. What I can say is that one set of coaches looked like they knew what they were doing and the other did not. The Raiders are not a good team and they know that. They have limited weapons and an older QB that is only there as a bridge for their rookie. That coaching staff knew that and did what any good coaching staff would do: protect their QB and let their one top playmaker carry the load. And by protect their QB, I mean get the ball out of his hands and don’t let him do stupid stuff. One might look at Cousins’s stat line and see 21-30 and 3 TDs. But he only threw for 160 yards on those 30 attempts. A high completion percentage and low YPA means what class? That’s right… Captain Kirk was Captain Checkdown. I don’t blame them one bit. They were smart to lean on the running game. They were smart to target a rookie cornerback – and Cousins is savvy enough to do that. When Cousins did look downfield, it was usually bad. He had a few completions. He also completed a few to the Dolphins. Cousins wasn’t particularly good this game despite his stat line looking somewhat nice. That team just played smarter and looked better coached. To counter that, the Dolphins didn’t sell out to stop the run. Or maybe they did. I don’t remember. It was late. But I would have had 8 in the box at all times and forced Cousins and limited pass catchers to beat me. Only one WR on the Raiders had a YPC average over 10 and that was because he caught the one decent downfield throw from Cousins. But no… the Raiders ran over the Dolphins and ran over them some more. It was a disappointing showing from a defensive calling standpoint. Now, I will give Hafley a slight break… typically offensive head coaches have an advantage over defensive head coaches starting out. But Hafley will need to improve. If he is going to sink or swim with rookies and green players, he might as well go all out with them. On the flip side (hat tip to WZB), Miami’s offense was like that annoying card player at the poker table that goes all-in every hand. Everything was a run or deep pass. I saw a screen pass or two, but that was it. No checkdowns, no easy passes, no “drive starters.” I recall the Raiders having several plays where Cousins threw a quick out for a 4-5 yard gain at most. Where was that for Miami? That’s how you protect your quarterback. That’s how you stay on schedule and maintain proper down and distance. I get the game script got out of hand late, but the play calling was very suspect (also hat tip to JUK – I was preparing this before I read his post, so make sure you read it ). This and that Caleb Douglas may be for real. I’m going to be a little hesitant because the Raiders don’t exactly have a shutdown secondary. But a “reach” in his debut game going 5-94 on 7 targets is nothing to write off. He should only improve. Sully may have struck gold here. Kadyn Procter looked ok out there. Perhaps an All-22 review is in order. I saw a player who missed several assignments, which is a communication issue. That’s not necessarily a rookie mistake, but the 1st team OL has been the same from day one. That’s something that should be mitigated by now. I also saw Achane get dropped for a loss because Proctor got obliterated. A 360 lbs. OL should NOT get pushed THAT far back on a run play. That is simply unacceptable. But he also had some good run blocks and held up decent in pass pro. OL reviews really require All-22 film and the condensed replay doesn’t rewind the easiest (on the TV anyway), but from what I could see, he had good and bad moments. Malik Washington can be a reliable target for Willis, but if he is used the right way. McDaniel had him running sweeps and behind the LOS kinda stuff and that’s good. But Slowik has a 6’4” and 6’2” receiver at his disposal and he’s running deep sideline routes to a 5’8” WR? Come on now. This comes back to the play-calling. Putting Washington in position to catch the underneath stuff and use RAC skills will best fit what he can do AND give Willis the needed “easy pass” option. Malik Willis was… ok. I don’t think he played poorly overall, but there were some issues that need to be addressed. Aside from the playcalling aspect, he took some bad sacks. Before fans jump on the “oh noes, the OL sucks again”, this is very likely ALWAYS going to be a part of Willis’ game. He is going to hold the ball longer than we have seen under the previous regime. Yes, some of it was poor blocking. Let’s give the Raiders some credit. They have one of the game’s best pass rushers in Crosby and edge rushers Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce are solid players. But Willis is going to take sacks that his predecessor never would because of how he plays. Play-calling can also help with the sack numbers. Getting the ball…

summary: Don’t you dare think I can’t see you rolling your eyes at your screen right now… Yes, despite the fact that the Miami Dolphins lost to the Las Vegas Raiders by a score of 27-13 on Sunday, marking a disappointing debut for new head coach Jeff Hafley, we will be naming a Most Valuable ‘Phin […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins runs after a catch against Jeremy Chinn #11 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t you dare think I can’t see you rolling your eyes at your screen right now… Yes, despite the fact that the Miami Dolphins lost to the Las Vegas Raiders by a score of 27-13 on Sunday, marking a disappointing debut for new head coach Jeff Hafley, we will be naming a Most Valuable ‘Phin for that contest. And yes, despite the fact that the 2026 season has the potential to be one of the most frustrating years of Dolphins football in recent memory, we will be picking an MVP each and every week this season. If that bothers you, don’t click. It’s really that simple. However, for those who are viewing the 2026 season through the right lens, we will be finding silver linings and highlighting players who are impressing despite the organization’s current struggles in an effort to put some attention on the positives this year — however few of those may exist. Miami Dolphins Week One MVP – WR Caleb Douglas In his professional debut, Douglas had an historic performance — nabbing five balls for 94 yards. His receiving yards total was the most for any Dolphins rookie receiver in his first NFL game, but was also tied with Tyreek Hill (2022) for the most receiving yards for any receiver in their first game with the team in the franchise’s history. For a player who many thought was overdrafted when he was selected by new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, Douglas’ debut was a delightful one to witness for Dolphins fans. Let’s hope that he can continue to progress forward as the season rolls on, and his counterpart, Chris Bell, can begin to contribute in meaningful ways as well. Quarterback Malik Willis and the organization as a whole would be significantly better for it. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas

title: Miami Dolphins Fans Sound Off On Game One
summary: Well that didn’t go like any of us would have wanted but probably a lot like many of us expected. Our Miami Dolphins traveled west to take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a game that they lost. Following the game I asked the following question: What is your overall take from today’s first game […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins runs the ball against Nakobe Dean #17 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the first quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well that didn’t go like any of us would have wanted but probably a lot like many of us expected. Our Miami Dolphins traveled west to take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a game that they lost. Following the game I asked the following question: What is your overall take from today’s first game of the season under the new coaching staff with the overhauled roster for your Miami Dolphins? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game? I know this is only one game and thus a very small sample size of what we have as a team overall, but even with that in mind, what about today’s game gave you hope going forward, and what did you see that still seriously worries you going forward? Below is a random seletion of your thoughts and answers- Redwood_ points out that all we have seen thus far is more of the same. It seems like every 6-7 seasons the Dolphins completely tear down the roster to the studs, and end up with BY FAR the worst talent in the NFL. That certainly appeared to be the case against the Raiders, who it should be noted (1) were without Brock Bowers, and (2) are widely predicted to be one of the worst teams in the league this season. The starting OL is supposed to be a strength but could never get anything going for Achane. The pass rush was completely non-existent. The special teams were horrific, giving up far too much yardage on punt returns AND kickoff returns, plus Patterson missed a 41-yard FG. Hafley was supposedly preaching toughness and physicality during training camp, but there was zero toughness or physicality against the Raiders. The 2019 Dolphins were horrible, but under Flores they played very hard, and they got better as the season went along. Those exact two things are what Hafley needs to get from these 2026 Dolphins. Luvs2drnk has a little sarcasm for our former HC. But hey, at least McDaniel showed everyone why he’s the best OC in the league. Zen4Phins is taking a realistic and long-term point of view on where this team is at this point. Thought they played alright for their 1st game. Wasn’t a really good game for Willis but it coulda been a 8 or 9 sack day if it weren’t for his legs, although he held the ball too long sometimes. Special teams may be a tougher area to improve on given our lack of depth and I kinda hold my breath when they kickoff. I think I’m gonna absolutely love watching that defense develop though. D line was getting pushed around a bit and hopefully Grant can help when he gets healthy. Thought Johnson and Rodriguez were tackling everyone. Honestly, I am not disappointed. I’m really excited about the change in the air and this was game 1. I Hate Sports sees the struggle lasting long beyond this week. We shall see what OC Bobby Slowik game plans next week now that he will have some tape of the 49ers D. I don’t expect to have a remote chance in any game until Week 7 vs the Jets after a Week 6 BYE. SabanpickedCulpepper points to a play in the game that could have swung momentum towards Miami but LV didn’t allow that to happen. Not sure if LV series after we score at the beginning of the 3rd Q was talked about But it was HUGE We get the int. Turn that into a TD and then LV goes down lickidy split(2:30min) and answers with a TD Totally deflated the team and it showed Just my opinion Jsutton15 has a solid and long list of tweaks this team could make as it clearly needs plenty of “tweaks” Here are some things I saw and you tell me what you think Asking Brewer to take on a DT on a run up the middle by himself is not using him properly. He is actually more suited for a wide and inside zone running scheme. if you run up the middle have Sav give him help so then he can scrape off and go after backers which is what he is good at. Willis needs to be in shotgun more and taught how to properly do the read option. Making the defense account for him keeping it will help the blocking. If he is under center, which is fine, you need to execute a couple of bootlegs where he has the option to run or throw. When under center I didnt see the use of play action passes. Thats half the point of putting a qb under center, so use it. Didnt see the use of a screen to keep LV’s dline from teeing off. Kick off coverage was abysmal but not hard to fix I did see alot of fight in the team which is half the battle Let Brooks rush the passer more because he cant pass defense anyway and his strength is aggressive tackling Believe it or not but the young recievers didnt do too bad considering their first start, so their is hope Overall, with a few less mistakes they had a shot in this one. If this game happened around game eight after improving with experience, it would have been different heatforlife points to the chance you take bringing in an unknown commodity vs the known commodity. u bring in a harbaugh u know your going to be good eventually.u bring in a hafley? ImRightYoureWrong says buckle up buttercup, this ain’t getting easier any time soon. Overall takeaway, this is a confirmed bottom 3 team. Loooooooooong season ahead. Pod of Dolphins seems to be boycotting next weeks game. Good thing I went to the golf course. Is time to get a new hobby, please do not watch the next Dolphins game vs SF JUK has some takes on a couple of coaches and a unit that looked horrible yesteday. Coaching watch. I’m worried about Slowik (which I was when we hired him). We only threw 10 passes between 0-10 air yards and couldn’t or didn’t attack the middle of the field at all, we had one completion between the numbers all day. The deep stuff is great but it’s too boom or bust if you go to it all the time. Hated the 3rd and short call on the first field goal drive and didn’t think he called enough wide zone either. Haf was hard to judge. Our coverage was soft and he couldn’t scheme up pass rush when we couldn’t win our 1:1s. But things might have looked different if we get those stops on their first two scoring drives and it’s hard for a play caller when your line is shoved off the ball a lot Special teams was awful. This team needs to win at the margins, not give them prime starting field position over and over. The most depressing moment of the game was getting the pick to start the second half, scoring then immediately letting them into our half on the return. Molly Polly II points to the OL having some issues with communication. Just one of a long list of issues for this coaching staff to address. O line appears to have commo issues. Whatever the problem we should have the rite players to fix this, while Willis must realize he doesn’t have much time. Douglas looked good tho….IMO his route running skills were on full display. We appeared to shine at times then screw it up before we could celebrate! HunztheMighty knows it could have been worse. Yeah, I guess so… I saw it as a glass half full day. It could have been worse. A few of the rookies flashed. Willis is a very different player than Tua. I dont see us winning more then a handful of games but I see us getting a little better every week. (Hope Springs Eternal) FLexile just wants to see gradual improvement. I’d take that! As long as they play better each week lest a couple of hiccups, they will be fine. Bill Moody says don’t be dissapointed when you knew it was going to look like this. “The are who we thought they were.” Buckle up, it gonna be a long season boys and girls. Don’t expect much and you won’t be disappointed. NCDolfan points to a lot of the most painful parts of yesterday but at least one bright part. Bad. Not enough Achane and bad plays for him outside 1st drive. DT. Horrible. Johnson picked on a lot. Willis forced some passes Good. Douglas showed up. Willis can extend plays-should have…

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Week One
summary: Miami Dolphins football is back… for better or worse. On Sunday, our beloved South Florida franchise was dominated by a Kirk Cousins led Las Vegas Raiders team. The first game of the Jeff Hafley era didn’t go according to plan, but that doesn’t mean it was a meaningless affair. This season will be all about […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins looks on prior to a pre season game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins football is back… for better or worse. On Sunday, our beloved South Florida franchise was dominated by a Kirk Cousins led Las Vegas Raiders team. The first game of the Jeff Hafley era didn’t go according to plan, but that doesn’t mean it was a meaningless affair. This season will be all about learning and growing as an organization — for both the players and the coaching staff. Each week, we’ll pick one “Fins Up” individual of the week to indicate someone whose play is trending upwards, and one “Fins Down” individual who is moving in the opposite direction and needs to improve if the team is going to find success. Fins Up Week One’s “Fins Up” player is rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez — the only rookie defender wearing the green dot allowing him to have a direct line of communication with the coaches. To be given that distinction in your first NFL game is already something to be proud of, but his play on Sunday was also a bright spot in an otherwise relatively poor defensive performance by Miami. Rodriguez had 14 total tackles — second only to Anthony Hill Jr. of the Tennessee Titans in Week One. He also allowed just 7 receiving yards while being targeted three times in coverage. Miami’s rookie linebacker will look to build on his positive Week One performance next Sunday when the Dolphins clash with the San Francisco 49ers. Fins Down Week One’s “Fins Down” individual is special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. His unit was responsible for multiple long kickoff returns, which allowed a Raiders’ offense without stud tight end Brock Bowers to face short fields on numerous occasions. As a result, Miami’s mishmash defense couldn’t hold and Las Vegas scored 27 points against the Dolphins on Sunday. Tabor is a respected veteran coordinator in the NFL, so hopefully Miami’s Week One performance in that department is an anomaly that will be soon forgotten as the season rolls on. However, if the unit continues to struggle, Jeff Hafley may be forced to make a tough decision regarding Tabor’s job status earlier than anyone would have hoped.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders
summary: Well, folks… get ready for a long season of Miami Dolphins football. With a 27-13 defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week One, the Jeff Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan era in Miami got off to a rocky start. While fans of the team expected some growing pains, a win against the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, folks… get ready for a long season of Miami Dolphins football. With a 27-13 defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week One, the Jeff Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan era in Miami got off to a rocky start. While fans of the team expected some growing pains, a win against the team that earned the number one overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft didn’t seem to be an outlandish ask. Whoops! Before anyone panics, just remember that the Dolphins aren’t playing with a full deck right now. With a record-setting amount of dead cap holding this roster back, the team is beginning their latest rebuild with one hand tied behind their backs. It’s going to look ugly at times this season, but hey, we’re Dolphins fans. We’re used to this. GOOD Caleb Douglas has record setting performance for rookie receiver in Miami While it wasn’t a good day for the Miami Dolphins’ offense as a whole, rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had himself an historic day. In fact, Douglas’ performance was a record setting one. His 94 receiving yards were the most for a Dolphins rookie in his first game as a professional in team history. Caleb Douglas has the most receiving yards (94 and counting) by a Dolphins player in their NFL debut. — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) September 13, 2026 When Douglas was selected in the third-round of the 2026 NFL Draft, plenty of people scoffed at the pick. The Texas Tech product was overdrafted according to many national pundits. Well, it doesn’t matter where you’re selected once you hit the field on Sundays — and on this Sunday, Douglas proved that he belongs in the National Football League by nabbing five passes. Here’s hoping he continues to stack good games en route to a successful rookie season. BAD Dolphins offensive line gives up 5 sacks in loss With his first pick as Miami’s general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan invested in the team’s offensive line, taking Kadyn Proctor out of Alabama to start at left guard. His message was clear — the team needed to be better up front if they wanted to find success on offense. Unfortunately, on Sunday against the Raiders, despite the mobility of quarterback Malik Willis, the Dolphins still gave up five sacks. It’s early, and there will be plenty of time to work on things from a pass protection standpoint, but if offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik wants to push the ball downfield — which seemed to be the second-half gameplan — Miami’s offensive line will need to be better moving forward. Or maybe Slowik needs to adjust his plan of attack… UGLY Dolphins defense couldn’t stop the run If you take old man Kirk Cousins’ five carries out of the equation, the Dolphins defense gave up 136 yards rushing on 32 attempts — 4.25 yards per carry — to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had 102 yards rushing on 23 carries himself. Time and time again, the Raiders found themselves in short yardage situations on second and third downs because Miami’s defensive line couldn’t handle the Las Vegas rushing attack. That is not a recipe for success for a defense that is filled with young, unproven talent across the board. It won’t get any easier for the Dolphins next weekend. They’ll travel to San Francisco to face Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers — a team that just ran for 174 yards on 30 carries against the Los Angeles Rams in Week One. ___ The Dolphins came out swinging against the Raiders, unfortunately they didn’t seem to land any blows. The team starts off the Jeff Hafley era with an 0-1 record and the schedule only gets harder from here. Do you think Miami will improve in Week Two against the 49ers or are we in for more of the same — if not worse — against San Francisco? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: Vikes Views: Nincompoop of the Week – Packers @ Vikings
summary: The taste of victory is sweet, especially against the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings dominated the 2nd half after a questionable decision to pull points off the board by Matt LeFleur. The Packers continued their choking ways from last season and the Vikings cruised to victory. Matt LaFleur Why is LaFleur a Nincompoop? Going for it […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings and Head Coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers talk on the field prior to the game on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The taste of victory is sweet, especially against the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings dominated the 2nd half after a questionable decision to pull points off the board by Matt LeFleur. The Packers continued their choking ways from last season and the Vikings cruised to victory. Matt LaFleur Why is LaFleur a Nincompoop? Going for it on 4th and 1 to extend the lead isn’t the worst decision in a vacuum. It’s more the continuation of the calamidy of errors that seems to happen to LaFleur’s teams in the 4th quarter. He’s unable to respond when the pressure is on. The Packers has no response to the most predictable thing in the NFL, Brian Flores blitzing. LaFleur’s team looked like a D-III school facing an SEC team in the 4th quarter. Javon Bullard Why is Bullard a Nincompoop? Bullard is going to be the face of the entire Packers defensive penalty situation. There is a point to playing physical, within the rules of the game. The Vikings defense is proof it can be done and done very well. The roughing the passer penalty was questionable, but the Packers earned the penalties. It was a large part of why the team lost the game. Undisciplined football lead to their collapse and that is on LaFleur and the players themselves. Theo Jackson Why is Jackson a Nincompoop? Christian Watson’s 81-yard touchdown wasn’t just a bad play. It was the kind of mistake that normally cost your team the game. Jackson took a poor angle, misplayed the ball, and gave Green Bay a free touchdown. With Harrison Smith nearing the end of his career, every snap is an audition. Sunday wasn’t a passing grade. Kyler Murray Why is Murray a Nincompoop? First, I wish him a speedy recovery. The hit was cheap and I don’t want to see anybody get hurt. That said, his first official pass as a Viking was pure chaos. Murray chucked the ball up like it was 4th and 8 against the Giants in the playoffs. Instead, it was second-and-eleven in the first quarter of Week 1. After nine NFL seasons, you’d hope for a little more discretion than that.

title: A Brief Refresher on the Emergency Quarterback Rules
summary: When Kyler Murray went back to the locker room yesterday during the Minnesota Vikings’ victory over the Green Bay Packers, there was a bit of confusion on social media. . .at least from what I saw. . .about what the Minnesota Vikings could do at quarterback. Yes, Carson Wentz was the backup and J.J. McCarthy […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: J.J. McCarthy #9 (L) and Max Brosmer #12 of the Minnesota Vikings look on prior to the start of the game against the Baltimore Ravens during a 2025 NFL game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Kyler Murray went back to the locker room yesterday during the Minnesota Vikings’ victory over the Green Bay Packers, there was a bit of confusion on social media. . .at least from what I saw. . .about what the Minnesota Vikings could do at quarterback. Yes, Carson Wentz was the backup and J.J. McCarthy was the emergency quarterback, but what do those things mean? Well, I wanted to use this space to take a minute to clarify a few things about the emergency quarterback rule and how it works. Hopefully this will alleviate some confusion going forward. First of all, the emergency quarterback is technically inactive on game day. That’s why their name comes out as part of the inactive list ninety minutes before game time. He must be designated as the emergency quarterback as part of that list. The emergency quarterback can only enter the game in the event that the #1 and #2 quarterback are deemed unavailable for play, whether due to injury or disqualification. A team can’t put their emergency quarterback into the game for performance-based reasons. If Carson Wentz had gone out there yesterday and thrown six interceptions, the Vikings would have had to keep running him out there as long as he was still medically cleared to play (or didn’t get himself ejected for. . .I don’t know, something). Conversely, if a team does put their emergency quarterback into the game after their first two quarterbacks get injured and one of their top two quarterbacks then gets cleared to return, the emergency quarterback must immediately come out of the game in favor of the active quarterback. If the active quarterback is re-injured, the emergency quarterback can come back into the game. In addition, a team’s emergency quarterback must be on the 53-man roster, per the NFL rulebook . The Emergency Third Quarterback must be on the club’s 53-player roster; the player cannot be an elevated Practice Squad player. The club’s starting quarterback (QB1) and its backup quarterback (QB2) must also be on the club’s 53-player roster. That means a team can’t elevate a player from the practice squad and make them the emergency quarterback. This is where things might get a little tricky for the Vikings if Kyler Murray isn’t able to go against Chicago. If Murray isn’t able to go this coming Sunday and the Vikings want to have three quarterbacks on the roster when they face the Bears, they will have to release or waive a player from the main roster so they can sign Max Brosmer from the practice squad. That would, at least until Murray is healthy enough to play again, give them four quarterbacks on the main roster and leave them short somewhere else. If you want the actual, “letter of the law” verbiage behind the third quarterback rule, it’s all at the link a little further up there. But that should pretty well summarize everything so that everyone knows how the rule works going forward. At this point, it seems more likely than not that we’re going to have to reference it again at some point this season.

summary: Minnesota Vikings starting quarterback Kyler Murray will start Week 2 in the league’s concussion protocol, and according to at least one NFL insider, the initial indications for his availability for the team’s matchup against the Chicago Bears on Sunday are not positive. On ESPN’s Get Up morning program on Monday, Adam Schefter reported that it […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Minnesota Vikings starting quarterback Kyler Murray will start Week 2 in the league’s concussion protocol, and according to at least one NFL insider, the initial indications for his availability for the team’s matchup against the Chicago Bears on Sunday are not positive. Adam Schefter is pretty much ruling Kyler Murray out vs the Bears already. He also reports that the Vikings are/were "not pleased" by the hit that knocked Kyler Murray out vs the Packers They believe, per Schefty, that the league "should have gone after Javon Bullard during the… pic.twitter.com/7UqIIZERqn — Minnesota Sports Fan (@realmnsportsfan) September 14, 2026 On ESPN’s Get Up morning program on Monday, Adam Schefter reported that it appears unlikely that Murray will be able to suit up on Monday when the Vikings travel to Soldier Field to face their NFC North division rivals. Murray went out midway through the first quarter of Sunday’s opener at U.S. Bank Stadium, as he left the pocket and was scrambling for extra yardage. He slid to the turf and was hammered by Javon Bullard, drawing a flag for unnecessary roughness. Murray was helped off the field and immediately went back to the Vikings’ locker room, where he was diagnosed with a concussion and ruled out for the game shortly thereafter. If Murray is unable to go, it will be Carson Wentz taking the reins for the Minnesota offense. Wentz played efficiently enough after taking over for Murray, completing 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, but the Vikings will likely need significantly more out of him and the rest of the offense if they want to keep up with a Bears team that dropped 59 points in their regular season opener against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. We will be monitoring Kyler Murray’s situation as the week continues, but the early indications are that things are not looking positive for QB1 to be leading the Vikings offense into Chicago on Sunday.

title: 2026 NFL Week 2: Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears
summary: The Minnesota Vikings will continue their tour of the NFC North, taking to the road for the first time in 2026 to face their rivals from the Windy City, the Chicago Bears. Both of these teams took home victories in Week 1. The Vikings, despite losing Kyler Murray early in the contest, rallied from twelve […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings will continue their tour of the NFC North, taking to the road for the first time in 2026 to face their rivals from the Windy City, the Chicago Bears. Both of these teams took home victories in Week 1. The Vikings, despite losing Kyler Murray early in the contest, rallied from twelve points down late in the third quarter to take home a 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. Meanwhile, the Bears had an offensive explosion against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte, as they ran for nearly 300 yards and had six rushing touchdowns in a 59-37 win. These two teams split their two matchups in 2025. The Vikings opened last season at Soldier Field on Monday Night Football, and got a dramatic come-from-behind victory, as J.J. McCarthy rallied the team from a fourth-quarter deficit to defeating the Bears, 27-24. It looked like the Vikings might get a second dramatic win over the Bears, but Chicago won with some dramatics of their own. A big kick return by the Bears after the Vikings scored the go-ahead touchdown put Cairo Santos in position for a game-winning 48-yard field goal as time expired to give the Bears a 19-17 win and a split of the season series. The Vikings already have questions at quarterback, as Murray’s status in the concussion protocol will be something to monitor throughout the course of the week. If he is unable to go, Carson Wentz will step in as the starter again with McCarthy backing him up. Kickoff for this one is slated for noon Central Time, with coverage being provided by the FOX family of networks. We’ll be putting all of our stories for this week’s game in this stream so you can easily find them. title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Packers at Vikings
summary: Man I love when they beat the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings gave us a scare with the slow start to the game. That sinking feeling was helped along with the nasty hit that knocked out Kyler Murray for the game, and likely the next one. However, the team showed resilience and climbed back into the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after scoring a two point conversion during the fourth quarter the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Man I love when they beat the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings gave us a scare with the slow start to the game. That sinking feeling was helped along with the nasty hit that knocked out Kyler Murray for the game, and likely the next one. However, the team showed resilience and climbed back into the game. The closing quarter was a defensive masterpiece from Brian Flores. This team has some gumption. Kevin O’Connell This team could’ve easily fallen apart to boos at home. KOC has shown his system can work with just about anyone at QB. He once again maintained his composure after losing his starting QB. The offense ended the game with four straight touchdowns, granted only one drive was more than 30 yards. Finishing in the Red Zone and winning the turnover battle decided the game. KOC’s offense was efficient when opportunities presented themselves. The Vikings consistently finished drives with touchdowns instead of settling for field goals. Brian Flores You can’t mention the coaching staff without talking about Brian Flores. It was a rough start with the Packers starting the game with three straight scoring drives and a touchdown to end the first half. The Vikings defense settled down and only allowed three points in the 2 nd half. The 4 th quarter drive list for the Packers was Turnover on Downs, Fumble, Interception, Turnover on Downs. The defense handed the offense possessions at the Packers’ 1-yard line and 14-yard line. The inventive pressures were too much for the Packers’ OL and Jordan Love. It was as dominant as you’ll ever see a defense play a quarter. Carson Wentz It’s not easy to maintain focus around the constant attention JJ McCarthy and Kyler Murray received this offseason. Wentz put in the work and got ready to play, despite the distractions. He didn’t put up a ton of yards, mainly because he didn’t have to. Wentz wisely leaned on veterans Justin Jefferson and TJ Hockenson. Quick, efficient and professional game from Carson Wentz. Justin Jefferson It’s painfully obvious Jefferson was the only real weapon the Vikings had on Sunday. He caught just about everything that was thrown his way. Jefferson comes to play every Sunday and doesn’t complain about the constant QB carousel. He’s on this list almost every week and it’d be hard to justify leaving him off this week. Myles Price Price looked dangerous every time he returned a kick. There were a couple of shoe-string tackles that saved the Packers earlier in the game. His 61-yard return in the 3 rd quarter started the comeback. It was a huge momentum swing, and the offense was able to take advantage. You never know where the spark might come from, and price took advantage of the little bit of opportunity he was given. Honorable Mentions: Will Reichard – perfect as usual, is he already the GOAT Vikings kicker? Andrew Van Ginkel – a lot of the defensive guys could be listed, but he had the fumble recovery on Love in the 4 th quarter. Harrison Smith – just glad he’s playing again.

title: Kyle Williams among Patriots ready to step up after A.J. Brown injury
summary: The New England Patriots are set to be without star wide receiver A.J. Brown for at least the next month after he landed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. It’s a significant loss for the Patriots’ passing attack, but one that will not force the team to overhaul its offensive approach. Instead, New England […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Kyle Williams #18 of the New England Patriots looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots are set to be without star wide receiver A.J. Brown for at least the next month after he landed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. It’s a significant loss for the Patriots’ passing attack, but one that will not force the team to overhaul its offensive approach. Instead, New England will count on a group effort to replace its top wideout. “I mean, we’re trying to install here and putting guys in spots that are best for them and best for us. And so, I don’t know how much we want to tweak things,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “We’ll go through our game plan, and just like we did when A.J. was out there – sometimes he was the X, sometimes he was the F, the Z. You know what I mean? We’ll have to move guys around to different positions.” Among those that is expected to see an increase in playing time is second-year wide receiver Kyle Williams, who played 12 snaps in the opener, mostly in relief of Brown in the second half. “We want to get Kyle involved. I’ve tried to talk about that,” Vrabel said. “I’m hopeful that Kyle can find a role for us and find a way to help us, using his speed and catch and run opportunities like we saw last year at times or some shot-type plays.” In his limited Week 1 action, Williams was not targeted by Drake Maye. But moving forward, a more “locked-in” and “focused” Williams is ready to take on a bigger role now that he has a better understanding of Josh McDaniels’ offense in his second season. And while his big-play ability was on display last season and this preseason, he knows he has more to offer in that role. “A lot. I mean, if I wanted to really go, I’d give you a Christmas list, for real,” Williams said. “But I can do a lot, man. And just when those opportunities present itself, that’s when I’ll be able to show it. But I know I’m more than just speed.” Veteran Mack Hollins will also continue to see more opportunities come his way. Hollins led all Patriots wide receivers with 50 snaps in Week 1 while also leading the team with 51 receiving yards “Mack’s always taking advantage of his opportunities. I think that the quarterback knows he’s going to be in the right spot when he’s supposed to be there,” Vrabel said. “Mack’s been through that a lot, and we’re comfortable being able to move him around as well in those multiple positions.” The Patriots will also need more from free-agent addition Romeo Doubs. In his Patriots debut, Doubs finished with zero catches across his three targets. Doubs has a bad drop on a wide-open pass that proceeded an interception, while another target in his direction was also picked off. Still, his head coach is not losing any faith. “He dropped a pass. You know what I mean? Guys, everybody drops a pass. Everybody misses a tackle,” Vrabel said. “You talk to him the same way you always talk to him. Figure out a way to make a play to help us win, and he did a lot of great things during camp, just like everybody did. And so, I know he’s excited to get back out there, get to work and to find a way to help us win.” While the Patriots wide receiver room — which also includes Efton Chism III — is a deep group, removing Brown from the equation will be a significant loss to overcome. The star receiver started strong in the opener, recording three catches for 26 yards while drawing a 40-plus-yard pass interference penalty to set up the team’s first score. “Everybody’s disappointed for him, and he’s disappointed,” Vrabel said. “He wants to play. He’s a competitor, and we’ll have to get him back as quickly as possible. Obviously at a four-game window, and make sure that he’s ready to go mentally and physically when he does get back.” Brown’s high-ankle sprain is reportedly expected to keep him out closer to six weeks. While the team is hoping for a speedy recovery, the receiver group is ready to pick up the slack in the meantime. “Just hoping for a speedy recovery, get him back on the field, because we definitely do need him. But I mean, one man down is the next man up,” Williams said. “I think that’s everybody’s mentality in every room. So, we just got to keep approaching how we’ve been approaching it from the spring all the way up until now, and just hopefully nothing really changes or alters what we’re trying to do.”

title: Patriots kickoff return unit has started showing signs of life
summary: Even though their 2025 season was a success overall, the New England Patriots entered the offseason intent on improving several areas that ultimately fell short of expectation the previous year. One of those was kickoff return. While they were tops in the league in punt return average, in large part due to Marcus Jones continuing […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - FEBRUARY 08: WR Kyle Williams (18) of the New England Patriots catches the ball before the Seattle Seahawks versus the New England Patriots Super Bowl LX game on February 8, 2026, at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Even though their 2025 season was a success overall, the New England Patriots entered the offseason intent on improving several areas that ultimately fell short of expectation the previous year. One of those was kickoff return. While they were tops in the league in punt return average, in large part due to Marcus Jones continuing to play at a Pro Bowl level, their kickoff runbacks were far less successful. Despite using seven different returners, New England finished only 19th in the NFL with an average of 25.5 yards per runback. During last week’s season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, that number jumped to 26.8. Despite this being the smallest of all possible sample sizes, head coach Mike Vrabel saw some positives. “I thought Kyle [Williams] had a couple decent returns,” he told reporters during a press conference on Monday. “Reggie [Gilliam] — that’s been a strength of his, whether he’s playing at the front line, whether he’s playing as an off returner. So, hopefully we can clean some of those things up. I thought Kyle ran decisively. It didn’t look timid. The timing of all these plays, it’s so critical that the returners can judge it, get moving into the football and not be backing up with their hips going back, and then they catch the ball; now the coverage has already started and the timing’s off.” The Patriots started their 2025 campaign with Antonio Gibson as their primary returner, but a torn ACL forced the team to change plans. Efton Chism, D’Ernest Johnson, TreVeyon Henderson, Terrell Jennings and even Rhamondre Stevenson received opportunities to run back kicks, as did Kyle Williams. The latter, together with practice squad running back Lan Larison, filled that role last Wednesday. Williams only ran back two kicks, but he gained exactly 29 yards on both of them — a 2.6-yard improvement compared to his 2025 regular season average — and added 0.8 expected points for his team. For the 2025 third-round draft pick, the jump from his rookie season to his sophomore campaign is more than just statistical. “It’s just a comfortability with the new kickoff,” he explained at his locker on Monday. “You come from college, and you don’t really do too much special teams in college. So, being able to transition to do that in the league and going into the second year, it’s a lot more comfortability for where I can hit those gaps. … “I know what I’m looking for. I know where my track should be. I know where my blocks are going to be set up at. And so, when you are able to know that, your running style is able to transition. It makes things a lot easier.” Whether or not Williams will remain the Patriots’ primary kickoff returner with fellow wide receiver A.J. Brown now on injured reserve remains to be seen. Either way, despite the positive start, his head coach still sees the potential to get better as well. 2There’s just a lot of things that we can continue to improve as far as starting back there with how we catch it, and then obviously the matchups and the angles that get created on that play,” said Mike Vrabel. “There was one where we had some confusion which is unfortunate. You can’t have free runners on the kickoff. That’s not something that you want to do. That’s not good for player safety and welfare. But I felt like there are some glimpses there that we could get going.”

title: New Patriots DT DaQuan Jones ‘still has some good snaps ahead of him’
summary: A.J. Brown’s high-ankle sprain and subsequent trip to injured reserve created an open spot on the New England Patriots’ 53-man roster. They could have opted for another wide receiver to fill it, but instead chose to bring in a veteran defensive lineman: DaQuan Jones was signed to a one-year contract over the weekend. Jones has […]
full_text: A.J. Brown’s high-ankle sprain and subsequent trip to injured reserve created an open spot on the New England Patriots’ 53-man roster. They could have opted for another wide receiver to fill it, but instead chose to bring in a veteran defensive lineman: DaQuan Jones was signed to a one-year contract over the weekend. Jones has a lot of positive attributes. He is a veteran of 12 NFL seasons and a combined 179 games, and at 6-foot-4, 320 pounds should help the Patriots shore up their interior defensive line. He also has worked with Mike Vrabel before, and the Patriots head coach seems to have high hopes for the 34-year-old. “We’ve had some experience with him in Tennessee,” Vrabel said about Jones on Monday. “We got to see him most recently in Buffalo. He’s a veteran interior player that I think still has some good snaps ahead of him.” Having played college football at Penn State, Jones started his career as a fourth-round draft pick with the Titans in 2014. He spent seven seasons with the organization, including the final three under Vrabel. Later, he also played for the Panthers and the Bills, accumulating a combined 394 tackles and 21.5 sacks since entering the league. Despite his experience and proven qualities as a big-bodied disruptor in the middle, Jones remained unsigned since entering free agency in March. He did visit with the Patriots in mid-August but was not signed at the time — a possibly deliberate decision: a vested veterans such as Jones being on the Week 1 roster would guarantee his salary for the remainder of the season. And so, instead of signing before the season opener, he signed with the team afterwards. According to the man himself, that decision was not a difficult one. “When Mike calls, it’s kind of hard to say no to him,” he told Mike Reiss of ESPN.
