title: NY Giants John Harbaugh ‘couldn’t pass up’ chance to tackle Malik Nabers
summary: During training camp, New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said he couldn’t imagine Malik Nabers returning to action from his 2025 torn ACL before getting at least some physical contact during practices. After Nabers played Sunday in a 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys, Harbaugh’s “tackle” of Nabers during a walk-through practice last week was […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Getty Images During training camp, New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said he couldn’t imagine Malik Nabers returning to action from his 2025 torn ACL before getting at least some physical contact during practices. After Nabers played Sunday in a 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys, Harbaugh’s “tackle” of Nabers during a walk-through practice last week was a popular topic of conversation. “It just kind of evolved into an opportunity to tackle,” Harbaugh said. “And I couldn’t pass it up, I guess. But no, it was good. It was fun. It was all in fun. Lot of laughs. Some guys gave me a sideways look. Some of the players were like, what are you doing? So it was good.” Harbaugh, in his 19th season as an NFL head coach, said it wasn’t the first time he had done that. “I do tackle guys or imitate tackling guys because I really couldn’t tackle them in real life, I’m sure,” Harbaugh said. “But I have done that before. So, it wasn’t a first.” Here are more takeaways from Harbaugh’s Monday afternoon Zoom call with New York media. Tackling the ball security issue Harbaugh was not happy about the Giants fumbling the ball four times against the Cowboys, though they were fortunate enough to get three of those fumbles back. “One of the things that is one of those non-negotiables is ball security,” Harbaugh said. “We’re putting the ball on the ground entirely too much. It’s got to change. We’ve got to make the change on that. Every single ball carrier has got to make sure that it gets better. “And it’s up to us as coaches. We’ve got to drill it. We’ve got to teach it. We’ve got to make sure that we do it better because the ball’s on the ground four times and that’s just not even close to being acceptable.” Pancake Pat’s value The Giants’ offense won the physical battle with the Cowboys’ defense on Sunday night. Giants fullback Patrick Ricard, who followed Harbaugh from the Baltimore Ravens, was a big part of that. Why does the fullback position continue to be important for Harbaugh in a league where many teams don’t even have one on their roster? “When you study what we do, it becomes self-evident because the jobs and the roles that he’s being asked to play are built into our offense,” Harbaugh said. “Not everybody has those, but a lot of people do. “Pat does his thing his way, you know, and there’s some things that I’m sure some of the [Kyle] Juszczyks of the world can do maybe better, if you want to call it that. But there’s a lot of things that Pat can do that nobody else can do. Nobody in the world can do some of the things that Pat Ricard can do. And that’s good for us. That’s unique for us. So it helps us be who we are. It builds into our team persona, our team identity. And we love that.” Jaxson Dart assessment The Giants’ second-year quarterback was 23 of 29 with three touchdown passes against the Cowboys. Harbaugh’s re-watch of the game left him even more impressed than he had been watching it live. “I thought his accuracy was really good,” Harbaugh said. “He’s on time. The rhythm passing, if you want to call it that, getting the ball out on time was really good, in critical situations, especially when we needed to convert against man or zone. But numerous times against zone, he was able to put the ball right where it needed to be, right on time. And that was a big plus for us.”
author: Ed Valentine

title: PFF grades for the NY Giants’ 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys
summary: The John Harbaugh era got off to a rousing start last night with the New York Giants defeating the division rival Dallas Cowboys 28-20 at a raucous MetLife Stadium. (When was the last time “raucous” and “MetLife” appeared in the same sentence about a Giants game?) Let’s see what the analysts at Pro Football Focus […]
full_text: Malik Nabers after a catch on Sunday. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The John Harbaugh era got off to a rousing start last night with the New York Giants defeating the division rival Dallas Cowboys 28-20 at a raucous MetLife Stadium. (When was the last time “raucous” and “MetLife” appeared in the same sentence about a Giants game?) Let’s see what the analysts at Pro Football Focus thought of the individual player performances. Offense Focusing first on the passing, Jaxson Dart’s 23 of 29, 230-yard, 3 TD, 0 INT performance was given a grade of…65.8, smack in the middle of their “average” range. I’m sure fans will take Dart’s highly efficient game, as evidenced by his excellent 134.2 NFL passer rating last night, every week. PFF, though, grades on degree of difficulty and taking care of the ball. Dart didn’t have any interceptions, but in PFF’s eyes he had two turnover-worthy plays, which they see as being just as bad. He also did not have any “big-time,” throws, i.e., balls placed accurately into tight windows and especially those that go deep downfield for explosive plays. Dart only threw three balls beyond 20 yards and only completed one. To quote Seinfeld, “Not that there’s anything wrong with that,” but that’s what PFF values. Dart did what he had to do to win the game. In the long run, he’ll have to show that he can hurt opposing defenses deep on a consistent basis, but for one game the short-range passing game was just fine. Let’s look at the effect of pressure: Dart was an amazing 19 of 22 when kept clean, including all three of his TD passes. When pressured he was 4 of 7 for 57 yards, but both of his TWPs came under pressure. Moving on to the pass blocking: The starting offensive line played every snap last night. They were penalty-free against Dallas’ formidable pass rush and did not allow a sack, but the individual performances were uneven. Jermaine Eluemunor had a clean game at right tackle, as did right guard Sisi Mauigoa in his first NFL game. Surprisingly, Andrew Thomas played below his standards with two hurries allowed, but neither of those were on “true pass set” plays that PFF feels are the best measure of offensive line performance. John Michael Schmitz (two hurries) and Jon Runyan Jr. (two QB hits and a hurry) were as usual the weak links in the line, but they weren’t terrible. Next, the run blocking: The run blocking was fairly uneven. Thomas was his usual dominant self in the run game, and Eluemunor was fine, but JMS and Runyan were their usual subpar selves. Mauigoa had a rough go of it as well in his first NFL start. Of note is that wide receiver Malachi Fields did a nice job in 29 run blocking snaps. Now let’s look at the receiving: Unsurprisingly, Isaiah Likely led the group with a great 82.8 grade, his only blemish being a fumble. Likely caught every one of the eight balls thrown his way, including 2 TDs and two contested catches, and quickly established himself as Dart’s go-to guy, taking over the Wan’Dale Robinson slot receiver role to some extent (17 slot snaps). Malik Nabers (73.0) had a successful return, catching 6 of 9 balls, and Devin Singletary (71.7) kept catching those swing passes from Dart until he ran out of real estate and scored. Darnell Mooney, Theo Johnson, and rookie Malachi Fields also had successful games, with Mooney getting the second most snaps in the slot. Of note was that the receiving corps had zero drops. Odell Beckham Jr. was not targeted at all but played 11 snaps. Finally, the rushing: Cam Skattebo ran the ball more often than any other Giant; he did good things (a TD) and bad things (a fumble), the two canceling each other to give him an average 67.4 grade. Dart was the Giants’ second most frequent rusher (so much for putting him in bubble wrap after all his blue tent visits last year), and only 3 of those were scrambles, but he was effective running the ball with a 78.1 grade. Devin Singletary had a nondescript 6 rushes; his contribution was mainly on those swing passes. Tyrone Tracy only ran the ball twice, because on the second one he once again let a defender punch the ball out. That was it for him for the day. We’ll see if he gets out of Harbaugh’s/Greg Roman’s doghouse next week in LA. Defense Four players played all 58 defensive snaps: Linebackers Tremaine Edmunds and rookie Arvell Reese, and safeties Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin. Five others played most of the defensive snaps: Abdul Carter (53), Greg Newsome II (52), Brian Burns (49), and Dru Phillips and Deonte Banks (48 apiece). Everyone else was on the field less than half the time. Abdul Carter was the clear leader, with a spectacular 90.3 composite grade over all facets of defense. Let’s look at the individual components. First, the pass rush: Carter was the Giants’ best pass rusher (83.7) with a hit and three hurries. Chauncey Golston was equally productive with a hit and three hurries in fewer snaps but graded overall only an average 67.2. Kayvon Thibodeaux was second in pressures with three, including one QB hit, but his overall pass rush grade was only 48.2. Brian Burns had a quiet day with just a single pressure. In case you were wondering how Dennard Wilson was going to use him, rookie Arvell Reese only rushed the QB four times. Next, the run defense: Overall the Giants’ run defense got a 54.3 grade from PFF, in the middle of the individual game grades they received last year. Yesterday, there was some good news for the run defense: Free agent IDL signing D.J. Reader scored a very good 74.5 with a tackle and an assist on 10 rushing plays. Brian Burns (71.5) and Abdul Carter (70.0) were in the Very Good category. The bad news was that the main free agent IDL signing, Shelby Harris, graded an awful 35.7 with no tackles. Recent signing C.J. Okoye (39.7) had one tackle that qualified as a stop (an unsuccessful run as judged by down and yards to go for a first down). Still, too many players had subpar run defense grades to think that the Giants’ run defense problem is solved. Finally, the pass coverage: A reminder: If a receiver is open, PFF will grade the player covering him down regardless of whether the quarterback threw to that target or went elsewhere. The good news: Safety Jevon Holland played one of his best games as a Giant (73.2 coverage grade), giving up only one reception for 9 yards and hustling to intercept Dak Prescott. Newcomer Tremaine Edmunds also had a successful Giants debut with a 71.7 grade; he surrendered six catches but for only modest yardage. Elsewhere things didn’t go so well. Dru Phillips (31.3) continued to show that he has trouble covering NFL receivers, with three defensive pass interference penalties and a missed tackle. Greg Newsome (40.4) only gave up one catch for 8 yards but apparently was letting receivers get open based on that low grade. Paulson Adebo (45.4) only played nine snaps but was targeted three times and gave up two catches. Arvell Reese also graded low (47.1), giving up three catches in three targets, but only for 23 yards. Tae Banks (48.9) had good and bad – the four catches he gave up in seven targets were only for 23 yards, and one attempt was a pass breakup..but another was a TD.
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: Malik Nabers on his NY Giants comeback: ‘Yeah, it’s time’
summary: Hope season for the New York Giants lasted longer than most teams this year, and so too did the questions that hung over their offseason. With the second-to-last kick-off of opening weekend, Giants fans had to wait, and wait… and wait to find out what their team would look like in 2026. Likewise, they also […]
full_text: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers celebrates after beating the Dallas Cowboys | Getty Images Hope season for the New York Giants lasted longer than most teams this year, and so too did the questions that hung over their offseason. With the second-to-last kick-off of opening weekend, Giants fans had to wait, and wait… and wait to find out what their team would look like in 2026. Likewise, they also had to wait until the last minute to find out whether star receiver Malik Nabers would even play against the Dallas Cowboys. Nabers’ status remained unclear even into Sunday afternoon, and reports eventually emerged that Nabers would be a true game-time decision. Even Nabers himself wasn’t sure if he’d be ready to go against the Cowboys. He even told his family to not come to the game, in case he wouldn’t be able to play. “I really didn’t know; my family didn’t even come to this game because it’s a one-on-one battle that you have go through. You have to do it for yourself,” he said after the game. “I didn’t want everybody here, I didn’t want my family here and I feel like I let them down by not playing, so I had to do it for myself first. I had to go out there, feel it out, feel like I was doing it and I felt good.” It was ultimately decided that Nabers would test his surgically repaired knee prior to the game against the Cowboys and make his decision based on how it felt. And even then, Nabers was nowhere to be seen when the media arrived at the press box, at least not until he came out for a dynamic warmup prior to the game. Malik Nabers stretches on the field pic.twitter.com/YWW33tXVf7 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 13, 2026 Then the announcement was made: Malik Nabers wasn’t among the inactive players. The Giants’ star receiver would make his return against the Cowboys. “The deciding factor was when I got out there, I just felt good.” Nabers said. “I felt good, I got a little chill through my body. I was like ‘Yeah, it’s time, it’s time’.” “I got a sense about three hours before the game, maybe two and a half, somewhere in there, when he went out and tested it and he felt ready and that’s when the decision was made,” Giants head coach John Harbaugh said. “It was his call. He had been cleared medically, but he had to feel right. He had to feel like he was ready to go and he could protect himself and perform the way he wanted, and he did. Malik played a great game. He played a heck of a game.” “I decided in warmups; really during warmups I felt really good, I felt good running around,” Nabers added. “I was catching really (well), I stretched really (well), warmup went pretty well. I just felt like it was time to go.” Even quarterback Jaxson Dart wasn’t sure whether his top target would be able to play or not. At least not until he was able to see Nabers’ body language during warm-ups. “I didn’t really want to ask for a while” Dart said. “So, I was just watching him during the warm-ups, and I was trying to keep my distance and I was able to see this from his, like, you know, his communication, I guess. And then I saw him give one little nod before he came in and did routes on air, and then I went over and told (Giants quarterback) Jameis (Winston) that I think Uno’s (Malik Nabers) playing, and I was just ecstatic from that point on.” Ecstatic for good reason. While it was the Giants’ punishing running game that ground the Cowboys down, Nabers was invaluable for Dart. He was targeted on a team-high 9 of Dart’s 29 pass attempts, catching 6 for 69 yards, including several key gains. “He’s just a guy where, no matter what the coverage is, no matter who they put out there on him, you have all the confidence in the world that he’s going to make a play,” Dart said of Nabers. “And I think that we were all not 100 percent sure what was going to happen. So, I was just super stoked. I think that once he was able to feel those lights and feel the game-day environment, maybe he had a little bit of adrenaline, and then he’s just a guy who wants to play for this team, loves the game. And I’m so happy that he was able to come back and have a game like this where he was just able to play really, really efficient and good football.” In other words, Nabers played winning football, and his play helped the rest of the team play winning football. Which is exactly what they set out to do from the start. “We got guys in here that expect to win,” Nabers said. “During the walk-through I looked at everybody’s eyes, and I could tell from everybody’s eyes that they were ready to play. There was no doubt in anybody’s mind that we weren’t coming out here giving our best foot forward and winning this game. Harbs’ (Giants Head Coach John Harbaugh) speech before the game yesterday, I (saw) it in his eyes that he knew we were coming out to play. We were coming out to play hard and that gave me all the confidence I needed.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: ‘Things I think’ about Giants-Cowboys: ‘Unbelievable environment’ best sign of all
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — That was different. Yes, the simple fact that the New York Giants won a season-opener on Sunday night was different. The Giants had lost six of seven season-opening games against the Dallas Cowboys prior to Sunday’s impressive 28-20 victory. They had started 10 of the 13 previous seasons 0-2 or worse. […]
full_text: Isaiah Likely celebrates with fans after the Giants’ victory over Dallas on Sunday night. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — That was different. Yes, the simple fact that the New York Giants won a season-opener on Sunday night was different. The Giants had lost six of seven season-opening games against the Dallas Cowboys prior to Sunday’s impressive 28-20 victory. They had started 10 of the 13 previous seasons 0-2 or worse. So, sure, Sunday was different in that sense. What was really different, though, was the atmosphere inside MetLife Stadium throughout the night. Fans of the Cowboys, Philadelphia Eagles, and other teams have made a habit in recent years of infiltrating and taking over the Giants’ home stadium. Not Sunday night. Maybe it was emotions from the 9/11 commemorations by the Giants. Maybe it was the beginning of the John Harbaugh Era following a summer of optimistic reporting about the state of the team. Maybe it was the introductions of Malik Nabers, who played, and Odell Beckham Jr., who officially returned. Whatever it was, the atmosphere inside MetLife Stadium was electric. From the second the Cowboys stepped on the field things were different. Dallas was booed so vociferously it was impossible to notice that there were thousands of Cowboys fans in the stadium. Long after the game ended, loud “Let’s Go Giants” chants from happy Giants fans reverberated around the building. Harbaugh called it an “unbelievable environment.” “This crowd, I’m telling you, man, the parking lot. The parking lot was off the chain driving in here. It was packed! I’m talking like four and half hours before the game,” Harbaugh said. “I get here early now, and I’m thinking it’s going to be easy to get in here and it wasn’t. And then the stadium was just absolutely electric from beginning to end. The sideline was electric before the game. I mean the whole thing was just quite an environment. It was really great to be a part of it and to see our guys step up in that environment, to handle all that and to focus on the football. “It was more than I expected in all honesty. It was incredible. The stadium was unbelievable. It was everything that you would think, but it was more than I thought. It was really something. I want us to play well enough that we can create that atmosphere every single week here going forward throughout the season. That’s up to us. That’s our job as coaches and players to create a football team good enough to deserve that type of a stadium every time we play.” Sunday was a reminder of what Giants football can look and sound like when the team is going well. Players noticed. “New York likes winning,” Kayvon Thibodeaux said. “When we win, it’s fun.” It certainly was on Sunday. Veteran offensive tackle Jermaine Eleumunor, in the league since 2017, smiled when asked about the atmosphere. “I’ve never seen a crowd like that ever before,” Eluemunor said. “It just gets you going. You don’t want to disappoint that crowd. You want to keep that same crowd the entire season. The fans don’t know how much that means to everyone. It means a lot.” With the release last week of Darius Slayton, star left tackle Andrew Thomas is now the longest-tenured Giant. He has been with the team since 2020. Thomas said the playoff season of 2022 is the only other time he has experience a home crowd like that in MetLife Stadium. “It was great to see,” Thomas said. “It means everything. We play for the fans. We want to give them a good product.” Running back Cam Skattebo has talked in the past about wanting to be part of changing the expectations around a Giants team that has been mostly down-trodden since winning the Super Bowl at the end of the 2011 season. He said Sunday’s atmosphere was “beautiful.” “It was an amazing crowd. It was awesome to have everybody that showed up tonight be as loud as possible,” Skattebo said. “On third down you couldn’t hear anything. It’s been awesome to be able to be a part of this. “We’re gonna build on this. We want every home game to be like this. This is how every home game should be, whether it’s Sunday Night Football, Monday Night Football or if it’s just a regular game. They all should be this big. They all should be this wild.” Quarterback Jaxson Dart, who put together a spectacular 23 of 29, 230-yard, 3 touchdown performance, also lauded the atmosphere. “Seeing the crowd out there tonight, they had a huge impact in the game, just the energy and momentum. That stuff’s huge,” Dart said. “So, just everybody showing up, showing out on a big night like tonight, where it was bigger than even just the game itself, was just a really special environment to be in.” The Giants, of course, hope it was the start of something that will become a regular occurrence and not just an aberration. Here are more ‘things I think’ after Sunday’s game. Malik Nabers made a difference Nabers said he didn’t decided until he was on the field two hours before the game that he would play. He didn’t even have family in attendance because he didn’t want to be pressured to play if he didn’t feel right. “During warmups I felt really good, I felt good running around,” Nabers said. I was catching really (well), I stretched really (well), warmup went pretty well. I just felt like it was time to go.“ Nabers went, and went well. He finished with six catches for 69 yards. Give an assist to Harbaugh for helping Nabers realize he was ready for game action. Harbaugh, 63, apparently tackled Nabers during a walk-through at the end of the week. “We were all just chilling on the sideline. It was right before we were supposed to start our walkthrough, and things were just up in the air. We didn’t know exactly what was going to happen,” Dart said. “And me and Coach Harbs kind of had some conversations. He’s like, ‘You know what, like, I think that once he gets hit for the first time and realizes that he’s okay, then he’s going to feel confident.’ So I think in his mind that triggered, ‘Oh, maybe I should tackle him right then and there.’ So, we’re all just standing there, and then all of a sudden Leek goes down on the ground, and our team’s super protective of him. So we all turned to look, and it’s Coach Harbs tackling Leek, and then he pops up and he goes, ‘See, you’re all good.’” Jaxson Dart How good was the Giants’ second-year quarterback on Sunday? This good: Jaxson Dart with the best QB performance in Week 1. • EPA/Play: +0.73 (1st) • WPA/Play: +2.2% (1st) Every 5 plays, Dart added 3.5 expected points and 11% win probability for the Giants. pic.twitter.com/01OTeikQyu — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) September 14, 2026 Dart was in control throughout. He was on target. He forced maybe one pass all night. He used his legs on both designed runs and scrambles. He got out of bounds. He got down. When he took a late hit out of bounds it seemed like the entire Giants sideline jumped to his defense. “I felt very comfortable,” Dart said. “I thought that we just did a really good job of staying in progress throughout the game, whether it was the run game, whether it was the pass game. Thought our O-line just played their ass off, and that just helped everything around. So, I’m really just happy with how the offense executed. I thought Nags (Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy) called an awesome game, and I thought the guys just played really, really hard. So, it made my job a lot easier, and guys all over the place made a ton of plays, so I’m excited about that.” I told you so All summer I kept mentioning the idea that Isaiah Likely had become Dart’s favorite target in “gotta have it” situations. Well, among Likely’s eight catches on Sunday were a pair of touchdowns in the red zone, and four plays that produced first downs. I missed on this one I expected Najee Harris to play and Tyrone Tracy to be inactive vs. the Cowboys. After Tracy fumbled away a scoring opportunity Sunday night, I am pretty certain that is what we will see next week against the Los Angeles Rams.…
author: Ed Valentine

title: Jets don’t get much NFL power ranking love after their Week 1 win over the Titans
summary: The Jets are 1-0 after a commanding season opening win over the Tennessee Titans. The victory, however, did little to raise the team in this week’s NFL power rankings. NFL.com 24. New York Jets 1-0 The Jets looked like a professional, competent football team in Week 1. Geno Smith executed consistently and they dominated in […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets are 1-0 after a commanding season opening win over the Tennessee Titans. The victory, however, did little to raise the team in this week’s NFL power rankings. NFL.com 24. New York Jets 1-0 The Jets looked like a professional, competent football team in Week 1. Geno Smith executed consistently and they dominated in the trenches, shutting down the Titans’ offense while cruising in a game that could have been much more lopsided than the 23-10 final score indicated. Also, this is your invitation to hop onto the Adonai Mitchell bandwagon while seats are still available. ESPN 27. New York Jets (1-0) Week 1 result: Beat the Titans 23-10 Preseason ranking: 29 Non-QB newcomer debut: TE Kenyon Sadiq Sadiq had only four touches (three receptions and one rush), but he scored one of the Jets’ two touchdowns (on a 3-yard end-around), and his versatility enabled OC Frank Reich to use creative personnel packages. After missing most of training camp because of a hernia, the No. 16 pick was limited to 26 offensive snaps, but his role will continue to grow. Sadiq joined Hall of Famer Ozzie Newsome as the only two tight ends in history to score a rushing TD in his first career game. — Rich Cimini The Athletic 28. New York Jets (1-0) Last week: 29 Sunday: Beat Titans 23-10 What we learned: They’re not bottom-feeders In recent years, the only debate regarding the Jets in rankings like these was how far down to place them. But they showed they’re a better team than the Titans, which had to feel good against former Jets coach Robert Saleh, thanks to a strong running game and an efficient afternoon from new quarterback Geno Smith. Up next: vs. Packers, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET Yahoo Sports 27. New York Jets (1-0, LW: 29) We’ll likely look back at the Jets’ Week 1 win and realize the Titans really are that bad. However, allowing 195 yards to any NFL team is impressive. The Jets gained 367 yards and generally looked sharp in all ways on offense. Head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show improvement this season and he’s off to a great start, even if it was against Tennessee. Sports Illustrated 25. New York Jets (1–0) Last week’s ranking: No. 29 Last week’s result: beat Titans, 23–10 This week: vs. Packers Speaking of the Titans, I’ll understand the frustration that a win over Tennessee got the Jets a smaller bump than a Giants win over Dallas. David Bailey showed the foundation of what can be a good high-motor pass rusher. Sunday’s game against the suspect Packers offensive line should offer Bailey a few more chances to get at the passer—and a better indication of what we’re actually looking at in Florham Park. It clearly will take more than a win over the lowly Titans to improve perceptions of the Jets, but an upset win over the Packers in Week 2 likely will lead to a genuine rise.

title: New York Jets Flight Connections 09/15/26
summary: We are still feeling the high of a New York Jets victory on a Tuesday, but that isn’t the only thing we’re celebrating. Over the weekend, all of the moons and stars aligned for the green and white. The Jets won, the Dallas Cowboys lost, the Green Bay Packers lost, and the Indianapolis Colts lost. […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; New York Jets linebacker Demario Davis (56) breaks up a pass intended for Tennessee Titans running back Tyjae Spears (2) during the third quarter at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We are still feeling the high of a New York Jets victory on a Tuesday, but that isn’t the only thing we’re celebrating. Over the weekend, all of the moons and stars aligned for the green and white. The Jets won, the Dallas Cowboys lost, the Green Bay Packers lost, and the Indianapolis Colts lost. The Jets control their own first-round pick, the Colts’ first-rounder, and whichever pick ends up being worse between America’s Team and the Cheeseheads. So every time the Colts, Cowboys, and Packers lose, that’s excellent news for the Jets. The fan base can often be divided by the pro-tankers and the optimists. If we aren’t winning the Super Bowl, some fans have argued that tanking, losing on purpose, will better serve the team long-term because of the potential promised prince QB that can help turn everything around in the draft. Well, this year the arguments should die down. Why? I’m glad you asked, random person reading this article, because the Jets can have the best of both worlds. They can be competitive, win games, saving Aaron Glenn’s job in the process, while also getting that prized college QB, whoever that may be. Instead of rooting for the Jets to lose, root for the Colts/Packers/Cowboys to bite the dust. We have enough people fighting against us on a day-to-day basis; we don’t need to fight each other.
