title: 5 Up, 2 Down: Looking at stock after the Jets/Titans Game
summary: What a win! What a way to start the season! I’ve spent so many years hoping for the best and reluctantly seeing the worst that it truly makes me emotional when things play out so well. The Jets defeated the Titans 23-10, which makes it look a little better than the 23-3 thrashing that was […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a win! What a way to start the season! I’ve spent so many years hoping for the best and reluctantly seeing the worst that it truly makes me emotional when things play out so well . The Jets defeated the Titans 23-10, which makes it look a little better than the 23-3 thrashing that was occurring before a garbage-time touchdown dressed up the score. I looked at three things and was pleasantly surprised by how well the Jets kept Geno pressured minimally throughout the game. The few times he was pressured, he handled it well and even scrambled when he needed to! The Jets’ run defense was fantastic, and I believe this was the catalyst for the thrashing we saw. There was no room to run for Tony Pollard or Tyjae Spears, and as a result, Cam Ward was overwhelmed and outclassed by the Jets’ defense. Praise is deserved all-around, from the players to the coaches to the front office, because all their offseason efforts showed up in this game. The Jets gave out game balls themselves , but I’d like to identify a few people as well. Of course, the biggest benefit of this article is that the Jets would never give out a game ball for someone’s stock falling, and in the sea of celebration and jubilee, it’s still important to identify areas for improvement to ensure long-term success. And just in case you missed the first sentence of this paragraph, praise is deserved all-around. I’m just pointing out the ends of the spectrum: Stock Up Breece Hall The First Round Rookies Qwan’tez Stiggers The entire OL Jason Sanders Did you know that stat about Breece? I did, and I’ve known it for years, which is why I’ve been one of the biggest proponents of his contract extension from the beginning. This man is such a catalyst for Jets success, and I’m not convinced Jets fans and the media realize how valuable he is to the franchise’s overall vision. For those of you worried about him taking his foot off the gas now that he’s been extended, he accrued 100 rush yards and a TD in his first game post-contract. He added a couple of catches and plenty of blocks to further solidify his place as the franchise cornerstone bell-cow back he’s been paid to be. The first-round rookies had impactful debuts with the Jets in their own unique ways. Omar Cooper Jr. only had one catch but made the absolute most of it, racking up 26(!) yards after the catch and showing the playmaking that inspired Darren Mougey to trade up to get him. That one play transformed the drive from a ‘good drive’ to a scoring drive that put the Jets in prime position to score their first opening-drive TD on a Sunday in ten years. That TD was scored by fellow first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who also flashed playmaking prowess in that opening drive. On that touchdown he certainly looked faster than CMC and I can’t wait to see them both get larger chunks of the offense. And of course, praying for the speediest recovery for Cooper Jr. David Bailey also was no slouch in his NFL debut. The #2 overall pick found himself in the backfield early and often, leading the team with six pressures in addition to the four tackles he racked up. He proved to be a factor in the pass rush and in the run game, which was reflected in his playing more snaps than any defensive end. For comparison, among all D-Linemen, Bailey and David Onyemata played in 35 snaps while Harrison Phillips played 27 and Will McDonald played 25. On Special Teams, Qwan’tez Stiggers definitely made the most of his role and made several plays to nullify the Titans’ return and/or give the ball back to the Jets. Special Teams is way more than just punting and kicking field goals, and having someone like Stiggers has continued to pay dividends. I swear this isn’t a Geno snub – he was fantastic yesterday. 79% completion, 215 yards, and a 104 passer rating are all things of beauty. The only thing more beautiful was the time he had to throw. According to NextGenStats.com, his 3.04-second time-to-throw was the 8th-longest in the entire NFL this week, yet he was one of the least-pressured QBs. Knowing how badly their QB struggles under pressure, the big five men up front largely eradicated it. They also provided running lanes that led to two rushing touchdowns and a 4.4 YPC from their running backs. The more they can keep Geno unbothered for 3+ seconds, the more beautiful things we’ll see on offense. We all let out a collective groan when Jason Sanders was announced as the starting kicker for this week’s game, but I must say I was impressed by the final results. Was he perfect? No. Did he score more points than any other player in the game? Yes! Two field goals from 50+ is impressive, considering we didn’t even think he could hit from 40+ consistently. He also hit both extra points. I’m not saying kicking won’t be an issue moving forward, but I think the disdain we had from him leaving the Giants preseason game has already dissipated a bit after this successful performance. Stock Down Mason Taylor Clock Management I love Mason Taylor and am excited to keep seeing him and Kenyon Sadiq as consistent options for the Jets offense moving forward, but I think this past Sunday was an objective disappointment for Taylor. With the advantage of first-team reps all summer while Sadiq worked his way back from surgery, I was expecting Taylor to be the clear TE1 in the early weeks of the season. Instead, we got two catches for -2 yards, and a ‘drop’ that should’ve been called a fumble, but the refs very generously let the Jets keep the ball after review. On the 19-play drive, the Jets had a 3rd and 1 turn into a 3rd and 6 due to an untimely Mason Taylor false start. What looked like a touchdown drive ended in a field goal. Again, not bashing Taylor, and I may still even include him in my parlay next week, but this week was not a good game for the sophomore tight end. Also, there’s still more to be desired in this team’s overall clock management. I don’t want to name a specific culprit because I know some of you may be sensitive to criticism of certain people, but usually the head coach handles clock management. Of course, it ultimately didn’t matter because the Jets were such a better team on paper and on the field, but it physically pained me to see that pathetic attempt at a 2-minute drill to end the first half. What makes it worse is that the worst 2-minute drills I’ve seen in my life have all come from this regime’s Jets. In a game that matters, that’s a huge difference that decides games (see: the Giants’ execution at the end of the first half in SNF last night). Here’s to hoping they can get it fixed before it matters. Let’s go Jets.
author: thejameswudi

title: Jets Week 1 Stock Up, Stock Down
summary: The season is finally here. And for a change, the Jets get a rare Week 1 win! The caveat, of course, is that the Titans are the Titans. But still, it’s nice to take the wins where you can get them. Who helped their stock, and who hurt it? Let’s start with the stock ups. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets reacts against the Tennessee Titans during the first quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The season is finally here. And for a change, the Jets get a rare Week 1 win! The caveat, of course, is that the Titans are the Titans. But still, it’s nice to take the wins where you can get them. Who helped their stock, and who hurt it? Let’s start with the stock ups. Stock Up Olu Fashanu Now, I could mention the whole offensive line here, because I thought they were fantastic today. But I’ll mention Fashanu solely because, to me, he was the biggest X-factor for this team both this year and long-term. Fashanu has proven to be an average NFL left tackle in his career thus far. But entering Year 3 at just 23 years old, the hope and expectation is that the former first-round pick will develop into an impact LT for years to come. Today was a good start. Against the Titans, Fashanu allowed just two pressures, no sacks, and graded out above 74.0 as both a pass blocker and run blocker. The whole offensive line played well, but Fashanu was extremely efficient against a talented Titans front. This is exactly the type of performance the Jets need to see from him if he’s going to become the long-term answer at left tackle. Azareye’h Thomas I’ve recently said I’m kind of shocked about how little discussion Thomas has gotten surrounding the Jets this year. Cornerback is arguably the position where the Jets had the most question marks entering the season. Last year’s third-round pick quietly won the starting job opposite Brandon Stephens during training camp, and his first impression was quite good. You didn’t hear his name too often, which is a good thing for a corner. But when you did, it was normally because of a positive play. Thomas led the Jets in run stops with three, making a few terrific tackles on the perimeter, which was a huge weakness for this defense last year. The competition wasn’t extremely good, but outside of a garbage-time touchdown he gave up, Thomas was excellent for the majority of the game. On a big third down, Ward challenged him down the field, and Thomas played fantastic coverage, using the sideline to his advantage to force an incompletion on Elic Ayomanor. PFF agreed too with how Thomas performed, as he finished with an 80.3 overall grade and an 81.8 coverage grade. At only 22 years old, Thomas turning into a sufficient starting boundary corner would be an excellent development for the Jets this year. Once again, the competition wasn’t great, but it’s a good start. Kenyon Sadiq Listen, Sadiq didn’t do anything incredible. But considering the injuries and all the negative vibes we heard about him this offseason, the fact that he was even a contributor at all is a positive to me for the rookie tight end in Week 1. Sadiq only had three targets, but the fact that the Jets utilized more multi-tight end sets, something Frank Reich famously hasn’t done at his last two stops, makes me think there was at least some semblance of a plan for him. There will be a lot more to watch for with Sadiq, but it’s very clear that he’s extremely athletic on the field. This isn’t just a guy who tested well athletically but doesn’t look the part in pads. The touchdown wasn’t anything incredible, but it was a shrewd play call that used one of the Jets’ freak athletes to their advantage: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq reached a top speed of 20.09 mph on his 3-yard TD run, the fastest play by a Jets tight end as a ball carrier in the NGS era (since 2016). #NYJvsTEN | #JetUp pic.twitter.com/sx5voebKac — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 13, 2026 That’s exactly the type of thing I want to see from this offense. Find your good players and find creative ways to get them involved. Geno Smith The last person I’ll mention is Geno. I don’t think it was all positive for Geno. In the first half, I saw some questionable clock management decisions, including a boneheaded checkdown that ended the Jets’ chances of getting points before halftime. He also seemed a bit too slow with his decision-making to start the game. In the second half, though, I thought he was much, much better. I don’t think he had to do anything crazy considering the game script, but he was fairly accurate and efficient and was able to push the ball downfield. He ended with an 84.7 Total QBR, 0.26 EPA/play, and a 12.8 CPOE, all of which were elite numbers. Now, I think the game script helped him heavily. And I’ve said all offseason that the main way to get competent play from Geno is to protect him. The Jets showed a glimpse of what he can do when they do. Stock Down Now that we got the good out of the way, let’s get to the bad. Fortunately, there wasn’t much of it. Mason Taylor Let’s just say this was a brutal game for Taylor. And to be honest, he’s extremely fortunate it wasn’t worse. Taylor was targeted three times and had an inexcusable drop that arguably could have been a fumble. It happened in a spot on the field where it could have been completely game-changing. The other two targets resulted in catches, but one was a play that was doomed from the start, a tight end screen that went for negative yards and ultimately cost the Jets points. I can’t hate on him too much for making that catch. That was more on Geno. But if you wanted to see some progress from the second-year tight end, this wasn’t a good start. Arian Smith Sticking with the theme of 2025 draft picks, my other big loser of the game was Arian Smith. Again, I’ve long criticized the Smith pick. I don’t want to blame him for getting overdrafted. It was a boneheaded selection at the time. But for a guy entering his second season, one where I thought he was lucky to make the roster in the first place, you cannot drop a routine catch on your only offensive snap of the game. To me, it’s very clear where Smith will need to shift his focus if he wants to last in this league: special teams. With his straight-line speed, he very much could end up being a positive contributor in that facet of the game. We’ll see. Overall Overall, though, there were more highs than lows. The Jets haven’t been over .500 in nearly two years. Let’s take the wins where we can get them. The Titans might be really bad this year, but to be honest I don’t care. I’ll take it.
author: Jets012

title: The Jets’ plan worked perfectly in Week 1 win vs. Titans
summary: All 32 NFL teams enter the season with a plan. Change is something every team has to deal with. For those at the top of the league like the Seattle Seahawks, the change is replacing key coaches and players who had departed for greener pastures. For a team that was 3-14 like the Jets, the […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets reacts after the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images All 32 NFL teams enter the season with a plan. Change is something every team has to deal with. For those at the top of the league like the Seattle Seahawks, the change is replacing key coaches and players who had departed for greener pastures. For a team that was 3-14 like the Jets, the changes focus on upgrades. Of course all of these plans clash. The Tennessee Titans, the Jets’ Week 1 opponent, made plans to improve this offseason. They wanted new coach Robert Saleh to provide the team with fresh leadership and second year quarterback Cam Ward to take a major step forward. Everybody’s plan cannot possibly work. The teams making these plans compete directly against each other. That is something the Jets know all too well. This is a team with the longest Playoff drought in the league. It has been a decade and a half since the Jets saw the postseason. It has now been over a decade since the Jets so much ended a season with a winning record. Plan after plan has failed. A year ago Justin Fields was supposed to resurrect his career. Before that, Aaron Rodgers and a cast of big name veterans were supposed to take the Jets to the Super Bowl. Before that, the Robert Saleh-Zach Wilson combination was supposed to make the Jets a permanent fixture as an AFC contender. Before that, Adam Gase and Sam Darnold were supposed to do the same. We can hope the Jets’ plan will work before each season. Based on what the team did in the 2026 offseason, it was logical to believe it was likely the team would be improved. But we didn’t know for sure until they actually took the field. We couldn’t. I think this is what made this 23-10 dominating Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans so enjoyable. Everything went according to plan. If you had ask Jets fans how this team would find success in 2026 after a busy offseason, most probably would have laid out a blueprint similar to what we saw in this game. On the offensive side of the ball, a line anchored by two talented tackles would control the trenches. The Jets could run the ball effectively with Breece Hall and when he needed a rest Braelon Allen. The pressure would be off Geno Smith, who wouldn’t need to carry the offense. The veteran quarterback would just need to distribute the ball effectively to his pass catchers. Of course Garrett Wilson would be the go to guy, but Adonai Mitchell would emerge as viable second option. Still, rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper would chip in. On the defensive side of the ball, Aaron Glenn and Brian Duker would oversee a defense that looked far more prepared than what we saw from Steve Wilks a year ago. A new look edge group led by David Bailey would relentlessly get after the quarterback. In the middle of the field, Demario Davis would be stout and erase any problems. And so it was at least for this week. Look, the season in the NFL is a long one. The successful teams in this league perform at a high level consistently. It’s one thing to look great for one game. The season lasts four and a half months. This sort of effort has to be repeated over and over. The Jets drew an easy opponent in Week 1. The Titans figure to be one of the league’s worst teams. This was one of the few times the Jets will take the field in a regular season game with a pronounced talent advantage over their opponent. Beating other opponents like this won’t be as easy. Taking it a step further, a win doesn’t necessarily guarantee a great Jets season, but losing this game would have been a catastrophe. With that said, I haven’t known the Jets to avoid catastrophe too often in recent years. They also didn’t have the chance to play 17 games of consistent football this week, and they couldn’t choose their opponent. They could play one game against the team they were scheduled against. And they played that game against that opponent extremely well. There will be plenty of time to worry about future games and a tougher upcoming schedule. For now I’m just going to enjoy a truly outstanding Jets win and savor one season that has gone according to plan at least for the first week.
author: John B

title: Jordan Mailata says the Eagles’ offensive line needs to be more “stout”
summary: Stout (adjective): Strong, thick Stout (noun): Legendary former Eagles offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland The Eagles’ offensive line struggled against the Commanders in Week 1, and after the game, Jordan Mailata was talking to reporters and might have had a bit of a Freudian slip. “I just think we need to be more stout. More […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 14: Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata (68) chats with Philadelphia Eagles coach Jeff Stoutland during the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Philadelphia Eagles on December 14, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Stout (adjective): Strong, thick Stout (noun): Legendary former Eagles offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland The Eagles’ offensive line struggled against the Commanders in Week 1, and after the game, Jordan Mailata was talking to reporters and might have had a bit of a Freudian slip. “I just think we need to be more stout. More stout on the runs up front. I think everything was — we should’ve been able to pick up everything.” Obviously this was an unintentional double entendre, because the group really does need to be more stout, the adjective. But, they probably could be more Stout, the noun, too, because this veteran offensive line knows better than to make some of the self-inflicting mistakes they did on Sunday. That’s not a knock on Chris Kuper, either, but the standard was set before the new OL coach got to Philly, and their performance in Week 1 didn’t live up to it. Whether the Eagles OL needs to be more stout, or more Stout, they certainly need to play with better fundamentals and do a better job protecting Jalen Hurts. We learned on Monday that Landon Dickerson is headed for IR as he deals with a bone bruise in his knee, so the group will need to step things up even more with Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin stepping into that role.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Nick Sirianni explains why Eagles WR Hollywood Brown didn’t play Week 1
summary: The Eagles are 1-0 as the begin preparing for the Titans in Week 2, but head coach Nick Sirianni spoke with reporters on Monday after having a chance to watch Sunday’s film. He explained why Hollywood Brown didn’t play, and why they have to do better moving forward, as well as why Dallas Goedert is […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles answers questions during a press conference after a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are 1-0 as the begin preparing for the Titans in Week 2, but head coach Nick Sirianni spoke with reporters on Monday after having a chance to watch Sunday’s film. He explained why Hollywood Brown didn’t play, and why they have to do better moving forward, as well as why Dallas Goedert is so clutch, and what he saw from the running backs against Washington. When asked about certain individual performances, Sirianni kept coming back to this being the first game and everyone having things they need to improve. He spoke in support of Landon Dickerson following a rough performance, but shortly after the press conference, we learned the starting left guard was headed to IR . Here’s what the head coach had to say: On Hollywood Brown’s usage Sirianni said that they were rotating guys on Sunday, and while they know Brown could help them, it just didn’t work out. The head coach emphasized that they want to get the WR the ball because his speed is real, but there are some games in which players get shut out of catches, and some games that they get shut out of reps. “And quite frankly, just from my end, we want to get him in the football game. We’ll make a better effort to do that next time because I know the play making ability that he can bring with his speed but was pleased with how the wide outs played as a whole. Of course, there were things that you want back. They made a lot of plays down the field with different things with their job description. But I do want to see him in that football game and getting reps and contributing to this football team.” On Dallas Goedert’s ability Sirianni had a lot of positive things to say about Dallas Goedert, noting that the tight end has been so consistent throughout his time with the team. “He just has a knack to make plays. He’s been very solid in the run game; thought he was solid yesterday in that as well. I think Dallas has had different versions of his game shine at different times. What I mean by that is yesterday you got to see him catch the ball over the middle in space and get to the right spot, be a big target, make plays and finish. You’ve also seen through Dallas’ career how much of a dangerous runner he is when the ball is in his hands and how hard he is to bring down. You got to see that a little bit yesterday on the third down.” The head coach went on to talk about some of the more impressive moments from Goedert the past few years, highlighting some of his big sideline catches in critical playoff games. When the TE has to win one-on-one matchups, he’s able to do it in various ways on various routes, including some outside receiver routes and particularly in the red zone. Sirianni was sure to point out that Goedert’s success is not a surprise because he works his butt off to take his game to the next level. “He’s a great teammate. He’s consistent. Guys love being around him, so it was good to see him have a good game yesterday. I was pumped for him, and obviously all the things he did to help our football team win last night.” On the RB group Sirianni disregarded the notion that Saquon Barkley’s 42-yard run was just an outlier compared to the rest of the performance, and insisted that the explosive play count just as much as the other ones. “Being committed to the run game, sometimes that’s the way it goes. Not every play can be an explosive play in the run game. You want to make sure you’re staying ahead of the sticks. Now, that doesn’t mean that we ignore the issues that happened on those plays that averaged whatever. Some of them were negative plays, some of them were one-yard gains, some of them were six-yard gains. We’ll take those six-yard gains, but those plays count. When you’re committed to the run game like we are, you reap the benefits of that when you stick with it.” The head coach also talked about Will Shipley being on the field in some critical moments. He explained that sometimes in third-down they don’t want to sub out a guy if they’re trying to go tempo. “I think the best way to say, ‘Hey, why did Will Shipley get carries in those situations?’ Because we trust our backs. We trust every one of those guys. They’ve all shown to be able to make plays in different aspects. Obviously, Saquon’s our lead guy, as you guys know, and we’re really comfortable when Tank [Bigsby] and Will are in there and they’re getting carries and they’re getting protections. We’ve got a lot of faith in that group, and we’ll continue to have faith in that group because they continue to show us the things that they can do on a consistent basis.” On Jalen Hurts’ development “He made plays that only Jalen Hurts is capable of making at times across the entire league. With some of those new things that we were doing, I thought he did a nice job. Now, not a surprise to me. I was talking to somebody – we had 46 days or 47 days in training camp to get ready for that first game. We’re seeing that on a daily basis, that improvement.” He also admitted that they wouldn’t have put in some of the different things they did on Sunday if they didn’t think Hurts could execute at a very high level. On Makai Lemon’s debut “[Makai Lemon has] always done a good job since he’s been here of blocking, doing the right things, being in the right spots. Obviously, the ones that went to him yesterday didn’t equal out to be big yardage gains, but he did little things to help us win the football game that sometimes are unseen and unnoticed. Why that’s really important is while a young player is continuing to get used to the NFL and being able to make an impact, you have to trust that player. We trust him because he’s constantly doing the things without the ball that we need to help us win and that we know is going to help us win. That just builds confidence and allows players to develop, because I’ve been on the other side of that where maybe you didn’t trust the guy and you didn’t want to put him in there and then it was hard to get that guy going. So because of that trust we have in him, I think that’s going to help him continue to develop as a football player as we continue on through the season.”
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Landon Dickerson injury: Eagles guard headed to IR, admits he “was a complete liability” in Week 1
summary: There were a lot of things to address coming out of the Philadelphia Eagles Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, but arguably the biggest concern was starting left guard Landon Dickerson. Just one day later, the three-time Pro Bowler is expected to be heading to injured reserve, which means he will miss at least […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles guard Landon Dickerson #69 looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There were a lot of things to address coming out of the Philadelphia Eagles Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, but arguably the biggest concern was starting left guard Landon Dickerson. Just one day later, the three-time Pro Bowler is expected to be heading to injured reserve, which means he will miss at least the next four games. #Eagles are placing LG Landon Dickerson on Injured Reserve, NFL sources said. Dickerson has been playing with various ailments and clearly struggled in the opener vs. the Commanders. Looks like it will be Drew Kendall’s or Willie Lampkin’s turn at guard. Also depends on if… — Jeff McLane (@Jeff_McLane) September 14, 2026 For his part, Dickerson didn’t mince words about his performance on Sunday during a SportsRadio 94WIP appearance on Monday night. He also revealed that he got rolled up on during a training camp practice, which was still an issue. “I was a complete liability yesterday. Again, that was my fault. I know I said earlier in camp, I shouldn’t be out there until I feel healthy. A few weeks ago, got rolled up on in practice. I thought as weeks went by it would get better. It didn’t and we kind of went out there and finally got some imaging on it today, figured out what was wrong with it. Really the best plan going forward is to put me on IR so I can get this thing better to have a good stretch at the back end of the season vs. kind of what happened last year, go out there limping through 18 weeks. I don’t think anyone wants to see that again because that was just ugly. I don’t want to do that again because that was just some BS.” Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked about Dickerson’s performance in the season opener, and he highlighted the power the lineman plays with and the balance of that with occasionally allowing pressure. “I think what you what you see with Landon is his extreme power. He’s a big man who’s able to move guys off the spot. If you go back and you look at, OK so he gives up some pressures, all right. But he also caved in the side on Saquon’s long run on that third down, and just did a really good job of pushing their defensive tackle and displacing him, which is a big job description for him. He’s tough as heck. We’ve won a ton of games with Landon, and there’s a lot of good things that he can do. Just like every player on our team from yesterday’s game, and every coach for that matter, there’s good moments, and there are moments that we got to fix, and and that’s where we are, and can’t tell you how much I think of Landon and the player that he is, and particularly that power and that size where he can move guys off their off the spot at will, against their will.” With Dickerson sidelined, the Eagles will likely turn to Drew Kendall to step up into that role, or could even look to Willie Lampkin. The team might also consider making a change at center, with Cam Jurgens having a similarly difficult Week 1, which would impact which depth player they’ll turn to. Later in his radio show with 94WIP, Dickerson scoffed at the idea that this injury would push him closer to retirement, joking that he wouldn’t have paid seven figures to get his body right this offseason if he was close to done. The left guard fully expects to be able to return in four weeks. But it remains to be seen if this time off will truly get him right.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles-Commander snap counts: Dontayvion Wicks flashes as WR2
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton, Hollywood Brown INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles scores a touchdown against Mike Sainristil #0 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Excluding garbage time situations, it’s typically a good thing when the starting quarterback and offensive line are able to play the entire game. In this case, unfortunately, Landon Dickerson did not look very playable out there. Cam Jurgens didn’t have a great game, either. DeVonta Smith is WR1 and he was only off the field for three snaps. Smitty led the Eagles in targets with six, which produced three receptions for 53 yards. His sole special teams snap came when he logged the game-sealing onside kick recovery. Not an easy play with the ball bouncing at him like it was … but he managed to make the grab! Dallas Goedert was also only off the field for three snaps. He finished second in targets with five, making four catches for 77 yards and two touchdowns. This was the most receiving yards Goedert had in a game since the Eagles’ overtime loss to the Los Angeles Chargers last year. Goedert’s 43-yard reception was the longest he’s had since his 61-yard scamper late in the New Orleans Saints game in 2024. Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles, hat tip to The Ringer’s Philly Special) is clearly WR2. He ranked tied for third (with Makai Lemon) in targets with four, which produced two catches for 73 yards and one touchdown. Saquon Barkley accounted for 15 of the Eagles’ 18 running back carries. Makai Lemon saw a good deal of playing time as WR3. The results sure weren’t great ; his five targets produced three receptions for -5 yards. Washington’s defense clearly wasn’t fooled by those designed touches for the rookie first-round pick. As expected, Johnny Mundt spent most of his time blocking inline as TE2. Of his 20 snaps, 12 were spent as a run blocker and four came in pass protection. Which means he ran a route on just four snaps. Will Shipley played more than Tank Bigsby … and saw three times as many touches (three to one). Don’t love that. The Eagles underutilized Bigsby last year and they did again in Week 1 this year. My guy Darius Cooper was a beast on special teams, logging four tackles in one game! He didn’t see a target on offense despite the fact he looks more ready to help right now than Lemon does. Cooper DeJean had two offensive snaps as the player lined up behind the offense in victory formation. The offensive safety, if you will. TE3 E.J. Jenkins mostly played on special teams. DEFENSE DeJean played eight snaps at safety in his first game as the primary option on the back end next to Andrew Mukuba in base packages. Rough game for Coop in coverage. Jihaad Campbell was not the field for three defensive snaps. Jalen Carter logging 66 snaps in Week 1 stands out. Would be ideal to see more of a rotation there but we know by now that Vic Fangio likes to lean heavily on his top defensive linemen. Would be nice if the Eagles’ offense could manage to stay on the field more often to give Carter and the rest of the defense more of a break by not having to play so many snaps. With Jonathan Greenard out, Jalyx Hunt is the Eagles’ top edge rusher in terms of playing time. No surprise but here’s the confirmation. Marcus Epps briefly missed some time after getting banged up early in the game but he returned to be the Eagles’ safety next to Mukuba in non-base packages. Moro Ojomo saw the second-most defensive tackles snaps and obviously made a game-winning play by stuffing Washington’s two-point game-tying two-point conversion attempt. With Jonathan Greenard out, Nolan Smith is the Eagles’ second edge rusher. Jordan Davis ranked third in defensive tackle snaps. Pro Football Focus had him as the Eagles’ third-highest graded defender, only behind Zack Baun and Epps. Arnold Ebiketie playing the third-most edge rusher snaps was a bit of a surprise since it seemed like A.J. Epenesa was ahead of him. But Epenesa also seemed to get banged up in this game, so, that may have been a factor. Michael Carter II is a role player for the time being. Bryon Young saw some snaps in heavier defensive line packages. SPECIAL TEAMS Kelee Ringo continues to see a lot of special teams playing time. Big reason why the Eagles kept him on the roster. Braden Mann had an active day with seven punts, already tying his most from any game last year (which he did four times in 2025). Mann was a beast in terms of both booting the ball and pinning the Commanders back deep with good directional punts. Jake Elliott made a 35-yard field goal and went 3/3 on extra points. Ty Robinson was limited to special teams duty. Zero defensive snaps despite his emergence in the preseason. Fangio clearly doesn’t trust him. Britain Covey was temporarily elevated from the practice squad to be the Eagles’ punt returner. His four returns produced 37 yards for a quality 9.7 average. Fred Johnson and Markel Bell were limited to special teams duty. It’s unclear how the Eagles will handle replacing Jordan Mailata or Lane Johnson if they go down and it would be nice not find out what the plan is there if it means the starters remain healthy. Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin were also limited to special teams duty. Thought we might see the Eagles use Lampkin in a specialized role … but they did not. Maybe they’re saving that? Or maybe they’re not going to mess around with that knowing they might need him to actually play guard or center for them this season. Though I do believe Kendall is the top interior backup option ahead of Lampkin. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton, Hollywood Brown INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris The Eagles finally revealed their plan at QB2 (gasp!). It’s Dalton, which doesn’t inspire much confidence. Though I guess we’ll see if this is the case again in Week 2. With as weird as this backup quarterback battle has been, maybe there’s a non-zero chance they rotate it to where McKee is QB2 against the Tennessee Titans?! Guessing not but we’ll see. No playing time for Hollywood Brown, who did not have a very good summer. Not trusted to play on offense and not a factor on special teams … but the Eagles paid him a good chunk of change so he’s still here. Payton is QB4. Redshirt year for him, unless he manages to contribute on special teams at some point. The Eagles kept Moore on the roster only to not dress him for Week 1. You wonder why they wouldn’t just release him (he’s a vested veteran who isn’t subject to waivers) and try to get him back on the practice squad. Or, you know, they could actually play him. Based on what we saw in practice, he looks more ready to contribute right now than Lemon does. Could be nice to see more of a rotation behind the top two receivers (DeVonta and Wicks). We’ll see if Greenard is able to fully participate in practice this week or not. Week 3 might be more realistic for him. They shouldn’t need him to be able to beat the Titans. Another bonus to waiting for the Chicago Bears game is that it’s played on a Monday night, giving Greenard an extra day to get ready at that point. It’s a redshirt year for Morris as the tenth offensive lineman on the roster. Note that the Eagles still have one open roster spot after placing Eli Stowers on injured reserve .
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: NFL Week 2 odds: Eagles open as big road favorites against Titans
summary: The way I’d frame the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders? I’d say it’s a performance to build on. The offense as a collective clearly needs to be better. They only managed 10 first downs on Sunday … the fewest of any team in the league so far. Maybe Sean Mannion’s group […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 04: Tre Avery #30 of the Tennessee Titans breaks up a pass intended for DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on December 04, 2022 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The way I’d frame the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders? I’d say it’s a performance to build on. The offense as a collective clearly needs to be better. They only managed 10 first downs on Sunday … the fewest of any team in the league so far. Maybe Sean Mannion’s group can get it going against the Tennessee Titans? The Eagles are entering Week 2 as seven-point road favorites, according to FanDuel . This after the Titans, now coached by Robert Saleh, lost to the New York Jets by a final score of 23 to 10. Geno Smith completed 19 of 24 attempts for 215 yards and a 104 passer rating. The Jets’ top two running backs combined for 142 rushing yards and one touchdown on 32 carries (4.4 average). Until we actually see the Eagles prove they can block better, it might be hard to fully believe it. But you have to feel good about Jalen Hurts’ ability to make plays for this team after watching what he did against the Commanders. You also have to like Vic Fangio’s chances of being able to stifle the Titans’ offense, which managed a mere 195 yards yesterday. That’s 123 fewer yards than the Eagles managed to muster in Week 1. The Titans will be motivated to avoid two straight home losses to start the 2026 season but I believe in the Birds to emerge victorious. Will they definitely cover? I’ll lean yes, though I can’t say I’m 100% confident. What say you?
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles rookie report card: Need more from Makai Lemon
summary: The Eagles pieced together a divisional win over the Washington Commadners on Sunday, showing exciting flashes on both sides of the ball as they shook some rust off. While there is much to be encouraged about, the Eagles’ rookies are not among those reasons for optimism. Here are the big takeaways from Philadelphia’s 2026 NFL […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts as he walks through the tunnel against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles pieced together a divisional win over the Washington Commadners on Sunday, showing exciting flashes on both sides of the ball as they shook some rust off. While there is much to be encouraged about, the Eagles’ rookies are not among those reasons for optimism. Here are the big takeaways from Philadelphia’s 2026 NFL Draft class in Week 1. Makai Lemon: D It was to be expected that Makai Lemon would have a slow start to the season given his lack of participation in the offseason. He missed a lot of practice time due to his hamstring injury. But Sunday was still rough. Lemon was targeted four times, catching three passes and finishing the day with negative five yards. That is really tough, but it’s not all on him. Lemon’s usage was odd to say the least. Sean Mannion and company are still clearly trying to get a handle on what to do with this receiving group after DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Two of Lemon’s catches were on doomed screens and one was a short perimeter target. Given what Lemon was good at, I think he should live in the slot and eat up short targets there to get him going. Sunday was not his day, but it’s obvious the team wants him out there given 29 receiver snaps, which was the third-most at his position. Hopefully, going forward the Eagles find different ways to get Lemon involved as he gets more comfortable with the playbook. Other Observations Eli Stowers was placed on injured reserve as the Eagles put him on the backburner. That’s a bummer and I hope he can figure it out at some point this season. The good news for the Eagles is that Dallas Goedert looks awesome. Throwback to the Eagles drafting Goedert in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft and then Zach Ertz immediately having the best season of his career. Rookie blockers Markel Bell and Micah Morris are beginning this season as depth players; the former was active while the latter was a healthy scratch. That being said, Landon Dickerson looked rough yesterday. Hopefully it is just a one-off bad day for the three-time Pro Bowler, but he really didn’t look like himself. That is worth monitoring, and luckily the Eagles have the depth to fill in if Dickerson can’t go. Cole Payton was predictably inactive as QB4. No special teams role for him.
author: Benjamin Natan

title: The Takeaway: Not much new to see in the Eagles’ escape over the Commanders
summary: By the time Lincoln Financial Field’s clock struck 0:00 late Sunday afternoon and the Eagles had survived a 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, a palpable sense of relief could be felt by the fanbase. For the sixth straight time under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles won their opening game. It […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs against the Washington Commanders in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images By the time Lincoln Financial Field’s clock struck 0:00 late Sunday afternoon and the Eagles had survived a 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, a palpable sense of relief could be felt by the fanbase. For the sixth straight time under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles won their opening game. It is the longest active streak in the NFL and it is always better to start 1-0 than 0-1. Just ask the Dallas Cowboys. While the Eagles’ defense looked absolutely gassed by the end of it, they managed one last goal-line, two-point conversion stand, and spent the better part of the first three quarters limiting Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense for most of the afternoon. It was reminiscent of a season ago, when the defense carried an offense that had trouble maintaining consistency. Week 1 was our first opportunity to see what the new scheme was going to look like under Sean Mannion and how the passing game would function without A.J. Brown. It was also our first look at an offensive line that featured an injured-and-struggling Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson. We finally got to see if Hurts would spend more time under center, how that would affect the passing game and whether Saquon Barkley would be more productive in the new offense than he was a year ago. At the end of the day, the offense looked a whole lot like it did a season ago. And it was Jalen Hurts who saved them. There were entire quarters where the offense did nothing but go 3-and-out, but they also committed no turnovers. The short intermediate passing game over the middle was largely non existent, but there were several explosive plays and two TDs to Dallas Goedert up the seam. Saquon Barkley largely struggled again behind and offensive line that is nowhere near what it was in 2024, but broke off a long run and put up decent numbers otherwise. Baby steps, perhaps? Jalen Hurts, of course, remained the same, both in good ways and in bad. Hurts made the play of the game with his legs in the 4th quarter, converting a 3rd-and-18 with a 22-yard gain to help dig the Birds out of their offensive malaise. Jalen Hurts with a BIG gain of 22. 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/R0Fh8cdbXS — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 It was vintage playmaking by the still-fleet veteran, weaving his way through the defense to convert a first down when nothing was schemed open and his offensive line was leaking oil. And as in years past, it was Hurts’ deep balls and ability to play out of structure that generated most of the offensive output. There’s good news and bad news in that. The bad news is the Sean Mannion offense was supposed to create opportunities in the run and pass game for players. It’s only Week 1, and Mannion’s scheme deserves much more time to find its sea legs, but watching Dickerson and Jurgens struggle in both facets of the game was disheartening, to say the least. The run game looked a lot like it did last season and, as Tom Brady noted on the Fox telecast, there were times Hurts dropped his eyes and watched the pass rush when his first read was taken away. This is all going to take time. Patience is required, and hopefully it will all work out. In the meantime, Hurts spent much of Sunday improvising and relying on his previous strenghts — his legs and the bomb. The deep ball to DeVonta Smith along the sideline in the 3rd quarter was gorgeous, as was the toe-dragging catch by his new No. 1 receiver. Devonta Smith, First-Team All-Hands 🧤 pic.twitter.com/CJiasvVpay — TSN (@TSN_Sports) September 13, 2026 And his 64-yard deep bomb to Dontayvion Wicks in the 1st quarter was a thing of beauty. Jalen Hurts goes DEEP to Dontayvion Wicks for 64 yards! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/YWAd95NABQ — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 Like a season ago, the Eagles showed less play-to-play consistency, but more big splashes. It’s two different ways to score points and, on Sunday, it was enough against a Commanders team that, barring a few boneheaded mistakes, probably should have won. Defensively, Vic Fangio’s unit dominated for three quarters before the heat, humidity, and Daniels’ legs, wore them down. Zach Baun was incredible on Sunday, and the defensive line got persistent pressure on Daniels, if not sacks or turnovers. They made life uncomfortable for just about everyone. It was not Cooper DeJean’s best day, nor was it Jihaad Campbell’s. The safeties left gaps in the middle of the field. But it was enough. The big takeaway after Sunday’s 24-22 win was that it felt a whole lot like games the Eagles won last year. Never comfortable, ugly at times, finding a way to survive, overly reliant on Hurts to figure it out on his own. Happily, he did on Sunday. In Week 1, you take the win no matter how you get it, and hope things look a bit better as the schedule rolls along.

title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts starts the season strong
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Hurts looking good was my biggest takeaway from the Eagles’ Week 1 win. The offense as a whole was … uneven … but QB1 made big plays to carry the team to victory. His run to pick up a first […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Hurts looking good was my biggest takeaway from the Eagles’ Week 1 win. The offense as a whole was … uneven … but QB1 made big plays to carry the team to victory. His run to pick up a first down on 3rd-and-18 was massive and he made some really nice precision throws (see: Dallas Goedert’s first touchdown, DeVonta Smith’s sideline catch). The offense has a lot to clean up and improve upon … but it’s always easier to feel good about your favorite team’s outlook when the QB is playing well. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations as Eagles hang on for Week 1 win over Commanders – NBCSP Considering the pocket was breaking down snap after snap, Hurts was terrific Sunday. On the Eagles’ third possession, he heaved a perfect 64-yard bomb down the right sideline to the 6-yard-line to newcomer Dontayvion Wicks and after Cam Jurgens’ second penalty of the quarter, threw a dart to Dallas Goedert in the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown. Two spectacular throws on his sixth and seventh passes ever in Sean Mannion’s offense. Encouraging start. Later in the second quarter a terrific nine-yard TD pass to Wicks, and with six minutes left in the fourth quarter he found Goedert open over the middle and lobbed him a short pass that the veteran tight end turned into a 43-yard touchdown, longest by an Eagles tight end since Brent Celek’s 65-yarder in the historic comeback win at the Meadowlands in 2010. Considering how little help he was getting up front, I thought Hurts was outstanding in his first game working with Mannion. He also had some terrific runs – a 14-yarder on a 1st-and-20 in the third quarter and a 22-yarder on a 3rd-and-18 on the 4th-quarter TD drive. When he ran it was out of desperation under duress not out of any kind of set play. Hurts finished 14-for-25 for 203 yards with the three TD passes and no interceptions and a 122.2 passer rating along with 48 rushing yards on five runs before a couple kneel downs. He overcame a lot. The Early Bird: Four verticals & Jalen Hurts’ old tricks helped get Eagles over the line in season-opener vs. Commanders – PHLY Eagles Jalen Hurts let out a chuckle and a smile while he contemplated what he would say, and perhaps more tellingly, what he wouldn’t. The Eagles quarterback was asked about his first touchdown pass of the new season and the fact that it looked eerily similar to the final play of the season before. Hurts found Dallas Goedert running up the seam on the same four vertical route concept that had become the lasting symbol for the group’s offensive struggles in 2025 and the limited menu some blamed the 28-year-old signal caller for during the offseason. So what was going through Hurts’ mind after he ripped the throw high enough and far enough into the back of the end zone for only Goedert to make the play and promptly turned toward the sideline, shrugging his shoulders in celebration? “It’s a great play. It’s a great play,” Hurts said with a chuckle. “Y’all will dig. Y’all will try to figure something out.” Eagles-Commanders Postgame: Goedert, Ojomo Lead Eagles To 1-0 Start, Brandon Graham Breaks It Down – PHLY Eagles Postgame Show Jalen Hurts’ first game under Sean Mannion is in the books, as the Eagles held tough against a feisty Commanders team thanks to Dallas Goedert’s two touchdowns, a big day for Tay Wicks and characteristic tough defense from Zack Baun, Nolan Smith and crew. Two-time Super Bowl champion and future Eagles Hall of Famer Brandon Graham joins the show, along with Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf, plus insight from Fran Duffy, Miles Johnston and EJ Smith, live from the LINC. NFL Week 1: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games – ESPN Did the Eagles’ new offense pass the test Week 1? There was a boom-or-bust element to it, but the explosive plays carried them to a passing grade and a win over Washington. From WR Dontayvion Wicks’ 64-yard reception (a career high) to QB Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on third-and-18 to TE Dallas Goedert’s 43-yard score moments later, there was plenty to be encouraged about from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s debut. Some issues along the offensive front (left guard Landon Dickerson looked as if he was laboring) and long stretches of ineffectiveness brought back memories of 2025, but patience is required while Philly breaks in a new system. What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw three touchdowns, was timely with his runs and didn’t commit a turnover. The pass-and-catch between the signal-caller and new WR1 DeVonta Smith along the right sideline late in the third quarter was a thing of beauty. Hurts was at his best when attacking downfield, completing 6 of 9 such attempts for 176 yards. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Eagles vs. Commanders: The good, the bad, and the ugly – BGN Let’s see it through midnight green glasses: The Eagles won. Jalen Hurts took snaps under center. He threw down the middle of the field. The Eagles just happened to be playing against two new coordinators and a Wahington Commanders team that had to do more learning on the job than the Eagles did. The Eagles survived a 24-22 scare over Washington on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field to keep Eagles’ head coach Nick Sirianni a perfect 6-0 in season opening games and 35-14 overall. Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Hurts completed 14 of 25 for 203 yards and three touchdowns—two TDs down the middle of the field on third down. Hurts rushed for 46 yards and made some strong throws. His 22-yard scramble in the fourth quarter saved the game. He made sure nine different Eagles touched the ball. Hurts prides himself on finding ways to win—and it is what he did. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Commanders game – PhillyVoice 10) The ‘Thank You’ Award 🙏: The schedule makers. If the Eagles had played a better team, maybe this would have been a loss? We’ll never know. The Eagles will get another soft opponent Week 2 to work out the kinks when they travel to Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans, who lost decisively to the lowly Jets Week 1. Eagles Hold On For The Win – Iggles Blitz Neither team played well. The Eagles just made more winning plays and that proved to be the difference in the game. The Eagles have plenty of issues to work on. The OL was very up and down. Landon Dickerson really struggled. He allowed a sack, a TFL and was called for at least one penalty. Cam Jurgens drew a couple of flags. Jordan Mailata had one. They struggled to consistently block the WAS front on run plays. 2026 NFL season, Week 1: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com Eagles use big plays to outlast Commanders. Much like the last several seasons, the Eagles offense wasn’t pretty, but it got the job done, eking out a two-point win over a division rival. Philly’s offense was an inconsistent mess for much of the day, with the offensive line struggling to pick up the new blocking scheme, allowing far too many free runners into the backfield. However, Nick Sirianni’s club used a trove of big plays that made the difference. Saquon Barkley had a 42-yard scamper that helped set up a second-quarter score. title: 5 things we learned from the Steelers’ Week 1 snap counts
summary: Snap counts are just one statistic, but they do provide some clarity on the real hierarchy of a team’s depth chart when coaches tend to play coy in press conferences. After just one game, the Steelers’ depth is sure to change over the upcoming weeks of the season — and when facing teams that aren’t […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Payton Wilson #41 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Snap counts are just one statistic, but they do provide some clarity on the real hierarchy of a team’s depth chart when coaches tend to play coy in press conferences. After just one game, the Steelers’ depth is sure to change over the upcoming weeks of the season — and when facing teams that aren’t the Cooper Rush-led Falcons. Still, there are some lessons we can learn from Pittsburgh’s snap counts Week 1. Steelers snap counts Week 1 vs. Falcons pic.twitter.com/RStXLM8IhA — Brian Batko (@BrianBatko) September 14, 2026 T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward getting more rest This was one of the biggest takeaways from defensive coordinator Patrick Graham’s new Steelers scheme: workhorse veteran defenders T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward actually had time to catch their breath in-game versus the Falcons. Watt actually played the least amount of defensive snaps of the Steelers’ big three at outside linebacker with 38, but he was in the same range as Nick Herbig (39) and Alex Highsmith (41). Jack Sawyer contributed another 23. The increased rotation seemed to work, with Watt and Highsmith each recording two-sack games. Herbig (who played some off-ball linebacker versus Atlanta) and Sawyer weren’t left off the stat sheet either, combining for six total tackles. Heyward had an even larger reduction in snaps. After being the top-snapped defensive lineman in the entire NFL last season at age 36, the now-37-year-old played just 32 snaps (53%) defensively. Across the rest of the defensive line, Keeanu Benton logged 35 snaps, Derrick Harmon 24, and Yahya Black and Sebastian Joseph-Day had 18 each. Like Watt, Heyward responded with a monster game, still making an impact as a rusher and run defender, but recording an impressive three batted passes. Jalen Ramsey, Payton Wilson are every-down players Veteran defensive back Jalen Ramsey is set to count $17.2 million against the cap this year — it’s no surprise the Steelers want him to earn that on the field. It wasn’t exactly a surprise, but the Steelers took advantage of Ramsey’s versatility quite a bit against the Falcons, lining him up in the slot when in nickel defense, and moving him to safety opposite Jaquan Brisker in base. The end result was Ramsey playing all 61 of the Steelers’ defensive snaps on Sunday, with free agent addition Rayshawn Jenkins only recording 32 at safety. It’ll be interesting to see what the Steelers do with Ramsey after starting safety DeShon Elliott returns from injured reserve. Will the Steelers still pull a starting safety off the field for Ramsey in formations without a slot defender? Or will Ramsey start seeing more rest alongside Watt and Heyward? Slightly more notable was inside linebacker Payton Wilson playing 58 of the team’s 61 defensive snaps. Wilson struggled late in 2025, losing snaps to Malik Harrison, but seems to have returned to the role of an every-down linebacker. That trust from Graham was rewarded against Atlanta, where Wilson was all over the field, recording a team-best 13 total tackles. Germie Bernard still has work to do One player who was barely featured on Sunday was rookie second-round wide receiver Germie Bernard, who logged just three of the team’s 67 total offensive snaps. Roman Wilson, on the other hand, showed a clear lead in the team’s WR3 role with 37 snaps. After spending such high draft capital on Bernard, the Steelers still clearly have big plans for the rookie down the road. But for now, it looks like the WR3 job is Wilson’s to lose. Darnell Washington still a big part of the offense After being an extremely tight end-heavy team in 2025 under offensive coordinator Arthur Smith, the Steelers have shifted in a more 11 personnel-friendly direction under head coach Mike McCarthy. Week 1 offense early down personnel usage and QB alignment (pending MNF) Via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/QXNOVrYtg2 — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) September 14, 2026 Still, the Steelers have two of the NFL’s top-15 highest-paid tight ends, and the team made sure to use both against the Falcons, playing Pat Freiermuth for 49 snaps and Darnell Washington for 43. Freiemuth had a bit of a bounce-back performance after a quiet 2025, recording five catches for 46 yards and a score against Atlanta. Washington had just two grabs for 18 yards, but managed a highlight-worthy stiff arm and remained a key run blocker for the team. One of the biggest departures from the Arthur Smith era, beyond Freiermuth once again looking like a TE1, was a lack of heavy TE3 usage. Robert Tonyan logged just two offensive snaps Sunday, although Riley Nowakowski did see eight in a fullback/H-back role. Core special teamers emerge As expected, the Steelers have a new group of primary special teamers this season. However, standouts such as Carson Bruener (24 snaps — 80%), Ben Skowronek (18) and Jack Sawyer (24) remained big pieces of the third phase of the game. Rookies Robert Spears-Jennings (23 snaps), Daylen Everette (16), Riley Nowakowski (17), Eli Heidenreich (13) and returner Kaden Wetjen (10) were also contributors. Interestingly, Nick Herbig isn’t off special teams duties yet despite signing a big contract this offseason. He logged 11 special teams snaps on Sunday, while T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith each had zero. While some veteran backups such as Rayshawn Jenkins (10 snaps), Cole Holcomb (17) and Brandin Echols (20) were big parts of Pittsburgh’s special teams, Tonyan (three) did not see many snaps in that phase of the game.
author: Ryland Bickley

title: Will the Steelers offense take a step forward?
summary: If you subtract a spectacular defensive play from T.J. Watt, the Steelers offense contributed a lackluster 13 points against an Atlanta Falcons defense down its top two pass rushers on Sunday. The end result was still a 20-13 win, but during his Monday press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy was largely critical of the team’s […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you subtract a spectacular defensive play from T.J. Watt, the Steelers offense contributed a lackluster 13 points against an Atlanta Falcons defense down its top two pass rushers on Sunday. The end result was still a 20-13 win, but during his Monday press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy was largely critical of the team’s offensive output. McCarthy said the Steelers’ defense “carried the water,” adding that he expected better from the offense and that his own play calling was “herky jerky.” The good news? There are still 16 games left in the regular season, and the Steelers offense showed plenty to get excited about on Sunday. A lot of that lies with the quarterback. After a 2025 season where Aaron Rodgers often looked too willing to revert to a dink-and-dunk passing game, he looked more like a gunslinger against the Falcons. He was extending plays. He was pushing the ball deep. He recorded several “wow” throws even if his core of pass-catchers recorded some drops, failed to complete several more contested grabs or were blatantly interfered with on a few reps. Alright… Aaron Rodgers was balling with some of these throws. DK Metcalf left some explosive plays on the table, and there was an opportunity for maybe another 150 yards. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/i5Ix8E2AyK — Tommy Jaggi (@TommyJaggi) September 14, 2026 According to Next Gen Stats, Rodgers set highs or near-highs for his Steelers career in time to throw and air yards per target on Sunday. His passing map also showed him accessing every area of the field. The last time the #Steelers played the #Falcons in 2024, Justin Fields didn't throw anywhere near the middle of the field and Falcons FS Jessie Bates III. Aaron Rodgers had no such problems on Sunday. https://t.co/zMkgrwlqKQ pic.twitter.com/PkqRAGR8V5 — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) September 14, 2026 If Rodgers can keep pace, the passing game woes should improve. It was an especially rough game from top receiver DK Metcalf against Atlanta, and second-rounder Germie Bernard still isn’t rotating in with the starters. But the addition of Michael Pittman Jr. and increased involvement from Pat Freiermuth and Roman Wilson have the Steelers’ group of pass catchers already looking much stronger compared to last year. The right side of the Steelers’ offensive line was probably the weakest spot of the offense, as expected, but rookie first-round Max Iheanachor could be on track to enter the starting lineup soon. And while the Steelers’ run game was incredibly inconsistent against the Falcons on Sunday (a league-worst 28.6% success rate through Week 1), the team still managed three eight-plus-yard runs in the fourth quarter to finalize the win. Of course, it bears repeating this was against a Falcons defense without especially high expectations this season — and down both James Pearce Jr. and Jalon Walker. While it’s easy to see the good aspects of Pittsburgh’s season-opening performance on offense and expect big strides forward, it’s also important to note opposing defenses will likely be better as well down the road. Do you expect a step forward from the Steelers’ offense after a low-scoring output Week 1? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments!

title: Lions called Steelers about Joey Porter Jr trade
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to be at a standstill as it pertains to cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The former second-round pick and the franchise failed to get a contract extension done ahead of Week 1, and the Steelers don’t negotiate contracts in season. Porter didn’t play in the team’s Week 1 win over the Atlanta […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Joey Porter Jr. #24 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on from the field during an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to be at a standstill as it pertains to cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The former second-round pick and the franchise failed to get a contract extension done ahead of Week 1, and the Steelers don’t negotiate contracts in season. Porter didn’t play in the team’s Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons, and it was reported by Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport that the Steelers would listen to trade calls for the rising star cornerback. In the 36+ hours since that report, at least one team has reached out. Per Jeff Risdon, the Detroit Lions have been in contact with the Steelers regarding a potential trade for Porter. “I can tell you that I know that the Lions have approached the Steelers,” Risdon reports . “I don’t know how receptive the Steelers were. I don’t know what the Lions offered, if anything. I know that they have talked. I got that from a reliable source from the Pittsburgh side.” In terms of what the Steelers are hoping to get in return, John Maakaron of Lions on SI reports that Pittsburgh would like as much as two first-round picks in exchange for Porter. “League sources tell Lions On SI the Steelers are interested in potentially as high as two first-round picks,” Maakaron writes . “The starting point for a deal to be made is believed to be one first-round pick and a higher day two selection.” The Indianapolis Colts traded a pair of first-round picks to the New York Jets in exchange for cornerback Sauce Gardner. However, he already signed an extension. Any team that would want to trade for Porter would also have to give him an extension, which would naturally cheapen the trade compensation i.e. Trent McDuffie only garnering one first-round pick, two 2026 Day Three picks, and a 2027 third-round pick. That said, Detroit is in a position where a lockdown cornerback could be the difference between making a deep run in the playoffs and a potential Super Bowl berth, which would be more than worth a first-round pick. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Steelers Week 1 grades in win over Falcons
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers took care of business to kickoff the 2026 season, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 to begin the year 1-0 and win their third consecutive season opener. And while a win is always great, there is also always good and bad aspects of each contest to dissect. Each week, Joey Bray and I […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers took care of business to kickoff the 2026 season, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 to begin the year 1-0 and win their third consecutive season opener. And while a win is always great, there is also always good and bad aspects of each contest to dissect. Each week, Joey Bray and I will present our grades from the most noteworthy players and aspects of the Steelers, so let’s dive into Week 1 grades. QB Aaron Rodgers ​ Jarrett Bailey: The 24-of-40 box score doesn’t do Rodgers’ justice. I discussed it earlier in the day , but there was over 100 yards through the air left on the field due to drops, penalties, and a missed pass interference call that could have been a touchdown had DK Metcalf not been interfered with. Rodgers was constantly pushing the ball downfield, averaging over 10 yards per target. That was promising to see. He protected the ball, he put is pass-catchers in position to make plays, and looked largely comfortable doing it. Grade: B Joey Bray: There is plenty of reason for optimism about Rodgers after yesterday. Going into Monday Night Football, PFF gave Rodgers an 85.7 grade for his performance, first among all quarterbacks. Perhaps the most encouraging part of Rodgers’ performance for me was how much he pushed the ball down the field. Rodgers posted an ADOT of 10.5 in Week 1 after posting a 6.16 mark last season. The legendary quarterback was let down by his receivers on several occasions during the contest. The rust of not playing all preseason seemed to be apparent all afternoon, as the receivers and Rodgers seemed to be just a tick off timing-wise with one another. If a few more throws are caught, we could be talking about a much different grade for Rodgers. Although I am encouraged by his overall performance, the stats don’t jump out enough to warrant an A: Grade: B ​WR DK Metcalf ​ Jarrett Bailey: When you’re making the money DK Metcalf is making, 40 yards on 10 targets just won’t cut it. He had a pair of OPI penalties, one of which negated a 19 yard catch and run. The drop over the middle of the field in the second half would have been a gain of at least 20, likely more if he is able to keep running with the ball, and he was unable to drag his feet down the sideline on a 4th-and-3 toss from Rodgers. The Steelers need more from Metcalf. Plain and simple. Grade: D Joey Bray: It’s hard to put into words how disappointing Metcalf was in Week 1. On ten targets, the receiver brought in just four of them for 40 yards. The drops that plagued Metcalf throughout this contest are by far the biggest issue. The resounding booing that ensued after Metcalf dropped a ball over the middle that would have almost certainly resulted in a nice chunk gain afterwards spoke volumes to just how fed up fans are becoming. Metcalf needs to be better. After a disappointing first season in Pittsburgh and added help in the receiver room, this was supposed to be the time for Metcalf to break through. Instead, it was more drops and two more personal fouls to cost his team yards in the season opener. Grade: F ​Run game ​ Jarrett Bailey: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for just 61 yards on 18 carries. I don’t put the onus all on them – the offensive line could have been far better. especially when it comes to Dylan Cook. Regardless, it’s concerning that Pittsburgh couldn’t get anything going on the ground against a mediocre Falcons defensive front. The New England Patriots have one of the top defensive lines in football, and the Steelers head to Foxborough in Week 2. A lot of things better get cleaned up between now and then. Grade: D Joey Bray: The Steelers offense did not have to do much to escape with a victory in this one. It was Jaylen Warren who paced the running back room with ten carries compared to eight for Rico Dowdle. The fact that the Steelers only amassed 58 yards rushing is worrisome, even though it’s only Week 1. Atlanta’s defensive line was beaten up before the game even started, so I anticipated a much more run-heavy approach. Dowdle’s 1.9 yards per carry was concerning. Warren outclassed Dowdle on the ground and as a receiver, consistently looking more explosive and effective when on the field. Dowdle will have to pick up the efficiency if the Steelers run game is going to take a step forward this season. Grade: C- ​Pass Defense ​ Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers allowed just four receptions to Falcons receivers, only one of which went for north of 20 yards. Without Joey Porter, the likes of Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel, and Jaquan Brisker led the secondary to a great day that featured two interceptions and Cooper Rush completing just 12 passes. Grade: A Joey Bray: No Joey Porter Jr.? No problem. I was willing to give the Steelers’ pass defense a pass in this one, given that they were without their top corner and arguably their best safety, DeShon Elliott. However, I don’t need to give them a pass, because they did exactly what they were supposed to do against Cooper Rush. Jaquan Brisker stepped up in a big way with his interception, and we can even count TJ Watt in with the pass defense after one of the most impressive defensive plays you will ever see. 90 of the Falcons’ passing yards came on dump-offs to Bijan Robinson. Drake London was the Atlanta receiver with the most yards, and he recorded just 29 yards on two catches. This secondary is not nearly as good without Porter Jr. in the lineup, but you have to be impressed with the way they performed yesterday. Grade: A ​Special Teams Jarrett Bailey: I’m still trying to figure out what happened on that field goal where Cam Johnston gets the snap, bails, and throws it out of bounds. Chris Boswell also missed a field goal, which is a rare sight. The Falcons also averaged 30 yards per kick return. Grade: D- Joey Bray: ​I don’t have the adjectives to describe whatever happened on the “attempted” field goal where Cam Johnston took the snap and threw the ball out of bounds. From my view, it looked like the snap came early and nobody was prepared for it. We saw a rare Chris Boswell missed field goal in the 4th quarter from 56 yards out. With no big returns by Kaden Wetjen and two big missed opportunities, it’s tough to say much positive about the special teams this week. Grade: F Let us know what you think in the comments .
