full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: T.J. Watt #90 of the Pittsburgh Steelers takes the field prior to a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off the 2026 NFL season with a victory over the Atlanta Falcons at home, 20-13. The close score is a reminder that any team can be beaten and shouldn’t overlook any potential opponent. The Falcons started Cooper Rush at quarterback and gave the Steelers everything they could handle. The offense has things to clean up, but the Steelers’ defense was on full display, including a massive performance from T.J. Watt. Watt finished his season debut with four pressures, two sacks, two hurries, two tackles, and four defensive stops. PFF awarded Watt a 92.3 defensive grade, 81.4 run defense grade, 73.9 tackling grade, and a 90.8 pass rushing grade. Did I mention the pick-six? I didn’t? Well, that’s important too, since it was the deciding factor on Sunday. Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen spoke to the media after the game and doesn’t understand the criticisms tossed at Watt. “I saw how they talk about him online,” Queen said. “It’s crazy how a guy can be dominant for so long, and then one year he gets hurt … and everybody tries to turn the page on him.” Queen isn’t wrong. The hoopla of Myles Garrett being traded to the Los Angeles Rams following his record-breaking sack season and DPOY award has pushed Watt out of the conversation because of his injury in 2025. Sunday was a remarkable reminder that with Watt leading the stingy Steelers defense, the EDGE rusher is as good as anyone on any given Sunday. Recency bias is a real thing, and marveling at Garrett’s accomplishments last season shouldn’t discredit Watt, nor remove him from any conversation. If Sunday is any indication, Watt has heard, or not heard, his name in the best EDGE rushers in the league conversation and wants to change the narrative and perception. title: Mike McCarthy critical of his play calling against Falcons
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 1-0 in the Mike McCarthy era after a victorious homecoming against Atlanta on Sunday. In front of McCarthy’s family and friends coaching the team he grew up watching and cheering for, the veteran head coach delivered a 20-13 win in the season opener. But it wasn’t the prettiest of offensive performances […]
full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 1-0 in the Mike McCarthy era after a victorious homecoming against Atlanta on Sunday. In front of McCarthy’s family and friends coaching the team he grew up watching and cheering for, the veteran head coach delivered a 20-13 win in the season opener. But it wasn’t the prettiest of offensive performances for the Steelers. Pittsburgh totaled 264 yards of offense and only 58 on the ground. Atlanta gained more first downs (16-15) and the Steelers as a unit committed seven penalties for 52 yards. McCarthy described the rhythm on offense as “herky jerky” and took responsibility for not having the Steelers fully ready to play. “I would say it’s what I expected it (to be),” McCarthy said in his weekly press conference on Monday . “At the end of the day, you have a chance to perform. It’s what I expect as far as having everybody healthy. It was good. I thought the week of training going into it was a little herky jerky. I think that carried over in some parts of the game.” Aaron Rodgers targeted DK Metcalf 10 times but only connected four times, partially due to two plays that could have been called pass interference and a few drops by Metcalf. McCarthy even called himself out for his playcalling decisions. “I thought the play-caller on offense was herky jerky,” McCarthy said. “I didn’t think I did a great job getting the players into a rhythm at certain parts of the game. I thought we had some very good sequences where it looked like we were going to take off.” The Steelers finished 3-13 on third down, missed a field goal, and had a botched 62-yard field goal attempt in an overall sloppy performance by the offense and special teams. T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith each recorded two sacks and Watt’s pick-six in the fourth quarter put the game away. “In my experience in the league, it’s unfortunately the way it goes in September,” McCarthy said. “Teams come out of training camp a little differently.” It was the first time Rodgers, Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Pat Freiermuth, and others were on the field together in a meaningful game with McCarthy calling the plays. The team faces the New England Patriots in week two, looking to go 2-0 and establish a new era of the Steelers offense. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Mike McCarthy done discussing Joey Porter Jr.’s contract dispute
summary: Talking to the media the day after the Steelers’ season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy still faced a number of questions regarding a player who didn’t even suit up on Sunday. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was the lone rostered Steelers player to be ruled out in Week 1, with a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Joey Porter Jr. #24 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Talking to the media the day after the Steelers’ season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy still faced a number of questions regarding a player who didn’t even suit up on Sunday. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was the lone rostered Steelers player to be ruled out in Week 1, with a back injury designation. Porter missed much of the summer on the Physically Unable to Perform list with that reported injury, but he was also in the process of wanting an extension from the team. Porter made a point of not ruling out sitting out of games if he didn’t receive a contract by Week 1 — and the Steelers famously don’t negotiate in season — leading to questions regarding if his absence against the Falcons was truly injury-related at all. However, McCarthy took responsibility for the decision to rule out Porter to open the season. “It was my decision — I’m in charge of the 48 (active players on game day),” the Steelers’ head coach said Monday. “You have a week of training. We spoke a couple of times last week. My concern for Joey, obviously, is to get him to a spot no different than everybody else in training camp.” McCarthy said Porter is still ramping up physically after missing so much time over the summer. “If players who go through that first ramp-up period that aren’t ready to go, they don’t participate fully in the padded practice — I don’t really see this any different from that,” he said of Porter. McCarthy still acknowledged the contract angle of the situation. “Now, it is different that there’s a business component to this, and that’s really a whole other topic,” he said. “But as far as Joey’s participation in practice, he’s communicating with the trainer every day, he’s communicating with the strength and conditioning coach, and also his position coach, Jason (Simmons), and Joe (Whitt Jr.) and (defensive coordinator Patrick Graham). We’ll get him out there when he’s ready to go through a full practice.” McCarthy said he didn’t have a medical update on the star corner. “I haven’t met with the trainers or the training staff yet today,” he said. “I don’t even have the full report of the work in that area yet, but hopefully we’ll have a good plan for him for Wednesday, hopefully we’ll do more.” According to Next Gen Stats, the Steelers played exclusively zone coverage when facing the Falcons’ drop-back passing game. Porter is known as a press-man specialist at cornerback, and McCarthy was asked how that situation could affect the cornerback. “Great question, that I’m not gonna answer,” replied McCarthy. He added that Porter has looked good in recent practices. “(Porter) did a couple of one-on-one drills in Thursday’s practice — first time I saw him up close. I was impressed.” McCarthy said, “Yeah, I’d expect him to play,” when asked if Porter would take the field when his ramp-up is over, although the head coach didn’t answer whether that period would be weeks or days. McCarthy described Porter’s business situation as an “individual” one. When asked again if the situation could become a distraction, he said he was done answering questions on the topic: “This is the most I’ve, frankly, ever talked about a business situation. So I think I’ll stop right here.”

title: The morning after: Aaron Rodgers needs more from his receivers
summary: Aaron Rodgers’ Week 1 box score does not do him justice in the slightest. The 42 year-old quarterback was slinging the pill all over the yard in the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 20-13 win to kickoff the season, but it was a victory that could have been much more convincing had Rodgers gotten help on some high-quality […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ Week 1 box score does not do him justice in the slightest. The 42 year-old quarterback was slinging the pill all over the yard in the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 20-13 win to kickoff the season, but it was a victory that could have been much more convincing had Rodgers gotten help on some high-quality throws from his receivers. Rodgers finished the day 24-of-40 for 221 yards and a touchdown. However, at least one other score was left off the board, and multiple big gains slipped through the hands of DK Metcalf. The potential touchdown came when Rodgers launched a deep ball to Roman Wilson. Contact was made, but the third-year receiver fought through it, jumped in the air, and had the ball in his hands. When he came do the ground, the ball popped out, erasing what would have been a 44-yard score. Metcalf had an especially forgetful day. On 10 targets, he totaled just four receptions for 40 yards. One was called back due to his second offensive pass interference of the day, erasing a 19-yard gain. Metcalf was also unable to drag his feet on a well-thrown Rodgers ball down the sideline that would have gone for 21, and he dropped Rodgers’ best throw of the day between two Falcons that would have gained 20. In totality, those plays kept 104 yards and a touchdown off the board for Rodgers and the Steelers. Had those been caught, we’d be talking about a 28-of-40, 325 yard performance from the four-time MVP and a strong 27-point outing to begin his farewell season. Rodgers himself didn’t seem too bothered, though, as he noted explosive plays were there to be had. “I think we did a lot of good things,” Rodgers told Pam Oliver after the game. “We had a chance to be really, really explosive. We had a couple drops, couple off-targets, couple non-calls that looked like penalties. So that changes the stats. We had a 40-yard PI that could have been a touchdown. We had a couple other ones that could have been big plays… it’s good to be out of here 1-0, though.” The future Hall of Famer also made sure to praise his teammates, Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt, for their outstanding performances. “T.J. played unbelievable,” Rodgers said. “He’s been on a different level this entire camp. I’m so proud of him [and] I love the way he leads. And Cam is the epitome of a Pittsburgh Steeler. To be able to share this team with them, to be able to share the leadership opportunity is really, really special in my last year and I’m just so thankful to just be back out here and play the game I love with guys I really respect and love as well.” Rodgers and the Steelers will clearly be launching the ball more in 2026, which is a refreshing development. As is the group Rodgers calls “The old guys” continuing to halt time in its tracks. It’s the morning after game day, and we have much more to dive into. Welcome back, T.J. Watt We, and everyone else in the Steelers media space, have talked extensively about Watt’s performance, but with good reason. After two down seasons, the latter of which saw the three-time sack leader notch just seven takedowns of the quarterback after getting a massive pay day, many assumed we had seen the best of Watt. But maybe we had just seen the best of Watt in a Mike Tomlin-Teryl Austin defense. The usage of the edge rushers has been a hot topic for years now. The lack of innovation and movement along the defensive line made Pittsburgh’s approach predictable. Plus, as Watt aged, his snap count stayed largely the same, naturally making him less explosive as games, and the season as a whole, went on. On Sunday, Watt played 38 snaps – the fewest of Pittsburgh’s top three edge rushers. Mike McCarthy and Patrick Graham realize the fresher Watt stays through the game, the greater the chance for explosive plays. I’d say two sacks, three tackles for loss, and his first career pick-six is all the evidence we need that this scheme change, as well as a lower snap count, will reinvigorate the former Defensive Player of the Year and see him look more like the superstar we grew used to seeing week in and week out. New Steelers defenders show up big A pair of new Steelers defensive backs left their mark in their first action wearing Steelers colors. Pittsburgh native Jaquan Brisker picked off Cooper Rush to set up an Aaron Rodgers touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and finished the day with six tackles. Jamel Dean also had a nice outing, finishing with five tackles and a forced fumble on Bijan Robinson that killed a Falcons drive and forced a punt. Dean allowed just 31 yards through the air when targeted, and Brisker picked off the only pass that came his direction. The Steelers allowed just four receptions to receivers all afternoon with only one of those receptions going for more than 20 yards. Yes, it came against Cooper Rush, but that’s how it is supposed to look when you face a bad quarterback. The secondary did its job and then some, even without Joey Porter Jr. Quick-hitters Michael Pittman had a quiet, but strong debut, catching all three passes thrown his way for 58 yards. Talked about it yesterday, but Cam Heyward is ridiculous. Three pass deflections at the line of scrimmage. He is just seven shy of the NFL record for defensive linemen. Max Iheanachor should start Week 2. Dylan Cook was bad, and the run game suffered in large part because of it. Was good to see Pat Freiermuth start off on the right foot. He was vocal at the end of last season about the frustrations he had in seeing his snap count go way down. He handled it like a good teammate does, and is now back to being a top-notch pass-catching tight end. Don’t let Alex Highsmith get lost in the shuffle. Due to Watt and Heyward’s big performances, you’d be forgiven if you forgot Highsmith had two sacks, as well. Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: Kenneth Walker III wanted to prove he was a lead back when he left the Seattle Seahawks to sign with the Kansas City Chiefs in a huge free agent move. The Super Bowl MVP spent 2025 sharing lead back duties with Zach Charbonnet, but the Chiefs made it clear that Walker was going to be […]

(Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The final game of Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is an all-AFC West affair between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos. While Patrick Mahomes’ return from his ACL tear is the main story, for Seattle Seahawks fans we’ll get an early glimpse of two October foes (Broncos in Week 6, Chiefs in Week 7), as well as a look at an old friend in a new uniform. Kenneth Walker III started his Seahawks career as the Offensive Rookie of the Year runner-up, which has been lost to history for some reason. In fact, he garnered the most first-place votes but finished second to Garrett Wilson through the ranked choice system. He ended his Seahawks career with an electrifying Super Bowl 60 performance, rushing for 135 yards and picking up an extra 26 as a receiver on his way to game MVP . The rest of his career in between that time frame was a mixed bag of excitement, frustration over decision-making, and injuries. It’s a different style of offense in Kansas City, but Walker was clearly brought over in free agency to boost a moribund attack that had ground to a halt with Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt. Walker had more explosive runs by himself last season than the entire Chiefs team. But Kansas City’s offensive line was not impressive in 2025, and the Chiefs won’t have left tackle Josh Simmons tonight. Denver’s defense was excellent last season and figures to be elite again this year. It could be tough sledding for the Chiefs offense again despite high expectations. What will we see out of K9 in his first snaps as the lead Chiefs back? Whether you’re rooting against the Chiefs or not, are you pulling for Walker to have a good debut? title: Ex-Seahawks Boye Mafe, Cody White make huge plays in Week 1 wins with new teams
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have had Sunday off after their Week 1 Wednesday victory over the New England patriots, but there were a couple of former Seahawks from last season’s Super Bowl team who made big impacts on their new teams. As part of a revamped Cincinnati Bengals defensive front, edge rusher Boye Mafe’s debut […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 13: Boye Mafe #53 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may have had Sunday off after their Week 1 Wednesday victory over the New England patriots, but there were a couple of former Seahawks from last season’s Super Bowl team who made big impacts on their new teams. As part of a revamped Cincinnati Bengals defensive front, edge rusher Boye Mafe’s debut couldn’t have gone much better. The free agent pickup recovered a Bucky Irving fumble in the first quarter, which led to a Cincinnati touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. BENGALS FORCE ANOTHER TURNOVER TBvsCIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wbAduFk3WR — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 But Mafe is paid first and foremost to generate pressures and get sacks. His first sack as a Bengal doubled as Baker Mayfield’s third lost fumble of the game. Mafe was matched up against the elite Tristan Wirfs, and while Mafe was initially not a factor in the rush, Mayfield thinking he had infinite time in the pocket was woefully misguided, and Boye was lurking. OPEN SACK SEASON. 😤 #TBvsCIN at 1:00 PM on Fox pic.twitter.com/biYgNfO2gs — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) September 13, 2026 Cincinnati burned five minutes off the clock on its ensuing drive and kicked a field goal to go up 33-20, eventually hanging on for a 33-27 win. Mafe was involved in two of Cincinnati’s four takeaways, which is a promising start for a defense that has been subject to heavy criticism over the past few years. Meanwhile, it was a winning debut for Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, whose offense looked sharp in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins. The former Seahawks offensive coordinator’s first game ball, however, was not to Ashton Jeanty after his 147-yard, two-touchdown performance. It was to wide receiver Cody White, who was released by the Seahawks during roster cuts and signed to the Raiders practice squad . White was elevated to the game day roster, playing 11 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. While White had no catches and just one target, his special teams value he showed in Seattle came through for Vegas on this touchdown-saving tackle on Dolphins returner Jaylen Wright. Instead of a 27-20 game late in the third quarter, the Dolphins ended up turning a red zone possession into a missed field goal, no points, and didn’t touch the Raiders red zone for the rest of the afternoon. . @Raiders WR Cody White earned that game ball after he made a game-changing play on special teams 🗣️ @insidetheNFL Week 1 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/ve4UaZgSNV — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 And lastly, while Riq Woolen’s Philadelphia Eagles debut showed just one tackle and no passes defensed, he also had no penalties committed and was part of why the Washington Commanders passing game struggled to function for most of the afternoon. Jayden Daniels had no success throwing the ball when he was the primary cover guy. Terry McLaurin might has well have been on a milk carton as a missing person. Riq Woolen in his first start as an Eagle (37 coverage snaps): 🔒4 targets 🔒0 catches allowed 🔒0 yds Prettttty good. — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) September 13, 2026 Across 22 matchups with #Eagles corners Riq Woolen and Quinyon Mitchell, Terry McLaurin finished with 0 catches on 1 target, per @NextGenStats . pic.twitter.com/S7agtU0xEc — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson) September 14, 2026 All things considered, a very good day at the office for Super Bowl champion Seahawks in their new digs. And we still have the Kansas City Chiefs debut of Kenneth Walker III to look forward to on Monday Night Football .

title: Steelers fans growing frustrated with DK Metcalf after mistake-filled Week 1
summary: On a wild, high-scoring opening Sunday of the NFL season, one game that was a complete eyesore to watch was the Pittsburgh Steelers laboring to a 20-13 win over an Atlanta Falcons team that was forced to start third-string quarterback Cooper Rush at the last minute. Mike McCarthy’s Steelers debut might have ended in a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dk Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is tackled by Mike Hughes #21 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images On a wild, high-scoring opening Sunday of the NFL season, one game that was a complete eyesore to watch was the Pittsburgh Steelers laboring to a 20-13 win over an Atlanta Falcons team that was forced to start third-string quarterback Cooper Rush at the last minute. Mike McCarthy’s Steelers debut might have ended in a victory, but the complete lack of efficient offense from both teams made for tough viewing. Perhaps Pittsburgh could’ve won more comfortably if not for some big errors by former Seattle Seahawks star DK Metcalf, who might be testing the patience of the Steelers fanbase in year two with the team. Metcalf caught four passes for 40 yards on 10 targets, but that doesn’t begin to tell half the story of DK’s day. He was dinged for at least two drops and flagged twice for offensive pass interference. Drops, body positioning, and penalties are essentially the three biggest issues that have plagued him throughout his career, even when he was an All-Pro in 2020. DK Metcalf today: – 9 targets – 3 catches – 26 yards $33M a year. pic.twitter.com/foZlfOU3bG — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) September 13, 2026 DK Metcalf is a good starting NFL WR He should be excellent. Every year, he attacks targets with positioning that limits him from making the play. This is a jump up and through target to turn and catch with overhand attack. This attack would get his body and feet into position… pic.twitter.com/TfW9Sx6e60 — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 13, 2026 2 offensive pass interference penalties on DK Metcalf in 1 half. WTF. pic.twitter.com/yG8uiYMaro — Andrew Fillipponi (@ThePoniExpress) September 13, 2026 In DK’s defense, the officiating did seem to work against him as far as defensive pass interference. This probably is a catch if A.J. Terrell doesn’t flagrantly take away his right arm without a penalty. Another missed pass interference call in Pittsburgh on DK Metcalf… clear as day pic.twitter.com/1bENOXrKKw — RGF (@rgfray1) September 13, 2026 But the main story for Metcalf is that he was an unreliable target for Aaron Rodgers. In contrast, Michael Pittman Jr caught all three of his targets for 58 yards. It’s possible over the course of the season that Pittman becomes the main option for Rodgers over Metcalf, which would put DK’s contract under extra scrutiny. Steelers fans wasted no time expressing their frustrations over Metcalf’s performance. What i watched yesterday from DK Metcalf was horrendous. As a WR in the NFL to drop a ball at the rate he does while also being paid 33 million a year is baffling. Metcalf is the prime physique to over power defenders, with the speed to seperate. His main flaw is that he… pic.twitter.com/wLNd8hQfyV — RodgersBurgh (@realisticPGHfan) September 14, 2026 DK Metcalf is going to have a rare 0.0 PFF grade this week. And that's only because they can't go negative. Another big drop. #Steelers https://t.co/xzAjG6qZRa — Ross McCorkle (@Ross_McCorkle) September 13, 2026 DK Metcalf with the drop. Beautiful throw — Jeff Hartman (@JHartman_PIT) September 13, 2026 Holy shit DK Metcalf with another drop. Take him off the fucking field. — Zach | Tic Tac Takes (@TicTacTakes) September 13, 2026 I’m tired of DK Metcalf. This guy got overpaid to drop passes not be able to separate. Pickens would stink in this style of offense but at least he was exciting when he did something. I’m over this shit. — Turner (@Lockdown_Steel) September 13, 2026 And since social media can produce an echo chamber, here’s what our SB Nation brethren at Behind The Steel Curtain wrote : Stock Down WR DK Metcalf This was a terrible showing from Metcalf. The Steelers receiver was called for a pair of offensive pass interferences in this contest. Matcalf was targeted 10 times in the game, but finished with just four catches for 40 yards. The most deflating part of this performance, though, were the crucial drops. Rodgers and Metcalf seemed to be just a tick off timing wise form each other all game, resulting in a few downfield passes bouncing off the hands of Metcalf. In the third quarter, Rodgers hit Metcalf over the middle right in the hands and the receiver was not able to bring it in. The play resulted in a resounding boo from the crowd. If the Steelers offense is going to take a step up in 2026, Metcalf is going to need to step up. Of course, Metcalf can go off for 9 catches and 120 yards and a touchdown against the New England Patriots, but that’s the Metcalf story in a nutshell. He was one of the most productive receivers in Seahawks history through his six seasons in Seattle, so it’s not like he’s a draft bust of any sort. But it’s also clear that his skill set is very limited and it just so happened that explosive plays down the field worked out pretty damn well with Russell Wilson and (to a lesser extent) Geno Smith. Late career Aaron Rodgers probably is not a good fit for Metcalf’s strengths, and this era of two-high coverage shells also has helped neuter DK as a vertical threat. As an aside, Metcalf recently did an interview with The Athletic , and the subject of the Seahawks winning the Super Bowl after he asked out of Seattle was brought up. He said he had no regrets. “I live with my decisions every day… they’re very well thought-out decisions to where I know the consequences, know my benefits from every decision that I make,” Metcalf says. “I got brothers on (the Seahawks), still friends on the team. So I congratulated them, but nobody’s sour over an ex unless you really miss them. So no, I wasn’t sour.” I don’t think Seattle has any regrets about the trade, either.

title: An All-22 review of Jadarian Price’s encouraging Seahawks debut vs. Patriots
summary: I’ve missed writing this weekly column. As a Seattle Seahawks fan and someone who loves the draft, one of the things I look forward to most is getting to study how Seattle’s rookies perform once the games actually count. Unfortunately — or perhaps fortunately, and I’ll explain why later — there isn’t much tape to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks hands the ball off to Jadarian Price #8 against the New England Patriots during the first quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve missed writing this weekly column. As a Seattle Seahawks fan and someone who loves the draft, one of the things I look forward to most is getting to study how Seattle’s rookies perform once the games actually count. Unfortunately — or perhaps fortunately, and I’ll explain why later — there isn’t much tape to work with from this season opener. We had just 24 snaps from the rookie class to analyze. So, let’s take a look at some of the key plays from the game. All data used in this article was taken from PFF . Jadarian Price, Running Back — 24 snaps Price carried the ball 10 times for 52 yards, good for a 5.2-yard average. Overall, he showed good vision, played with a strong attitude and displayed more explosiveness and straight-line speed than I expected coming into the season. At this point, it looks like the praise he received throughout Hard Knocks was legitimate. Price correctly reads LB #14 coming downhill on this Duo run and bounces outside. The issue: two cuts cost him some explosiveness. With more reps, this should become one decisive cut. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:08:14.660Z This might be the snap that gives Price the clearest indication of what he still needs to improve, although there is nothing alarming here. Seattle appears to be running a Duo concept , a gap-scheme run that uses vertical double teams at the line of scrimmage while allowing the running back to read the second level and choose his path based on the linebackers’ movement. Price reads linebacker No. 14 coming downhill toward the line of scrimmage rather than flowing laterally, so he correctly decides to bounce the run outside. The biggest area for improvement is what happens next. You can see Price make two separate cuts, and on the second one he loses a little of his speed and explosiveness. Again, this is not some glaring mistake, especially in a rookie’s first NFL game. With more experience, Price should become quicker with this read and get to the outside with one decisive cut rather than having to make two adjustments. I believe this was Price’s only pass-blocking snap. Probably smart by Seattle: he’s willing, but still inconsistent in protection. He has the tools, but this is an area where experience—and Holani—can help. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:09:14.375Z I may have missed one, but I believe this was Price’s only pass-blocking snap of the game. That’s probably a smart decision by Seattle. It’s not that Price is incapable of blocking, or unwilling to do it, but he is clearly inexperienced in pass protection and has shown both good and very poor reps in that area. He did catch two passes for six yards, but pass protection is something he’ll need to develop gradually. In the meantime, George Holani can continue to provide some of that experience in the backfield. Nothing flashy, but the little things matter. The OL creates little room, yet Price stays with the read, keeps his track and lowers his pads to squeeze out the yards.Watch Anthony Bradford’s block on No. 24—it creates just enough room to finish the run. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:10:18.050Z Nothing particularly flashy here, but the simple things are often underrated. The offensive line doesn’t create much separation, yet Price trusts the design, stays with his first read and, even with very little room to work with, lowers his pads and gets what he can. Also, keep an eye on Anthony Bradford’s block on No. 24. It helps create just enough room for Price to finish the run. Price’s discipline stands out on this outside-zone run. A gap opens between Abe Lucas and Anthony Bradford, but he doesn’t get baited inside. He stays on track, turns the corner and then hits another gear once he gets north. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:11:23.473Z One thing that stood out throughout Price’s tape is how disciplined he appears to be. He doesn’t seem overly eager to abandon the play design in search of something that isn’t there. Seattle runs another outside-zone concept here. At one point, a gap appears between Abe Lucas and Anthony Bradford, but notice where Price’s eyes are. He doesn’t get sucked inside by the opening. Instead, he stays committed to working toward the edge. Once he turns the corner and gets going north, the explosiveness shows up again. Discipline doesn’t mean lacking creativity. On this outside-zone run, Price stays on his track until he sees a better lane inside, then cuts decisively and gets north. He finishes through contact instead of dancing around defenders. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:12:10.133Z Being disciplined doesn’t mean lacking creativity. Seattle runs another outside zone here, and this time the concept works particularly well. Price sticks with the initial track until he recognizes a better opportunity. Once he sees the lane inside, he makes the cut, turns upfield and takes on the defenders rather than trying to dance around contact. He eventually gets tackled, but there is plenty to like about the way he finishes the run and fights through contact. This might be Price’s most impressive speed rep. Another outside zone, but watch how quickly he gets downhill before No. 24 can close. He slips the tackle, gets north and hits another gear.And somehow JSN avoided a block-in-the-back flag here. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:13:58.706Z This was one of the snaps that surprised me most in terms of Price’s speed. It’s another outside-zone run, and pay attention to how quickly Price gets moving before No. 24 can get to him. He manages to escape the tackle attempt and once again gets himself going north. The officiating crew had already made several questionable decisions throughout the game, so perhaps they were trying to avoid adding another controversial call by not flagging JSN for a block in the back here. Either way, once Price gets through it, you can see what his athleticism can bring to this offense. He appears to hit another gear once he gets north, and that acceleration is something worth watching as his role develops. Bud Clark, Defensive Back — 0 snaps Clark was one of the rookies I had the most confidence in coming into the season, so seeing him land on injured reserve was particularly disappointing . There simply isn’t any defensive tape to evaluate yet, but his absence is significant when you consider the injuries Seattle has already dealt with in the secondary. Julian Neal, Cornerback — 0 defensive snaps With Seattle’s secondary dealing with multiple injuries, Neal could have had an opportunity to work his way into the defensive rotation. Unfortunately, his injury during training camp significantly slowed his development. He saw only special-teams snaps in the opener, so there isn’t much to evaluate from a defensive standpoint yet. Beau Stephens, Guard — 0 snaps Stephens was inactive for the opener. He showed some development during the final preseason game, but the fact that he was inactive suggests he still has some ground to make up on Seattle’s offensive line. At least for now, the coaching staff appears to have others names. That’s notable considering Christian Haynes, the player Stephens was competing with in the preseason, had previously lost his starting opportunity to Sataoa Laumea — who is no longer even in the NFL. For Stephens, the first step is simply getting active on game day. Avery Smith, Cornerback — 0 defensive snaps Because Smith is a rookie, even though he was not drafted or originally signed by Seattle, he’ll be included in this weekly rookie tracker. Like Neal, Smith did not see any defensive snaps despite the injuries in Seattle’s secondary. His work came…

title: NFL Week 2 odds: Seahawks open as heavy road favorites vs. Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are comfortable favorites against their division rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. After opening the 2026 season with a 13-10 comeback victory over the New England Patriots, the Seahawks will hit the road for their first away game of the season when they visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 20. According to […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are comfortable favorites against their division rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. After opening the 2026 season with a 13-10 comeback victory over the New England Patriots , the Seahawks will hit the road for their first away game of the season when they visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 20. According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook , Seattle is a 5.5-point favorite (-110) . The Seahawks’ moneyline is -235 , while Arizona sits at +194 . The game total is currently set at 41.5 points . That makes Seattle a relatively significant road favorite, but the betting line comes with an important wrinkle: Drew Lock is expected to start at quarterback against Arizona with Sam Darnold sidelined by his injury. Darnold suffered the glute injury on Seattle’s opening drive against New England and did not return. Lock took over and ultimately helped the Seahawks complete the comeback, finishing the game 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown. The latest reports indicate that Darnold is expected to miss the Cardinals game, putting Lock in line for his first start of the 2026 season. That makes the -5.5 spread particularly interesting. Seattle is being asked to cover more than a field goal on the road despite making a quarterback change just one game into the season. Arizona won’t be an easy opponent, either. The Cardinals opened their season with a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , giving them a victory on the road before returning home to Seattle. The Seahawks, meanwhile, are coming off a defensive performance in which they intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to help overturn their only 10-0 deficit and get the opening night victory. That combination helps explain why the total is relatively low at 41.5 points . FanDuel’s current market projects a game in which Seattle is favored to win, but not necessarily one expected to turn into a shootout. And, honestly, what else should we expect from a game in Glendale? There’s nothing particularly normal about playing the Cardinals in the desert, where these matchups have a habit of turning chaotic and unpredictable. Seattle should be prepared for another one of those games.

title: Dolphins offer 49ers a chance to build on their most surprising Week 1 strength
summary: That the 49ers are massive favorites over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 will be absolutely no surprise to anybody. San Francisco is coming off a huge win over the Super Bowl favorites, while the Dolphins are likely to be in the conversation for the first overall pick and were beaten comfortably by the Las […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That the 49ers are massive favorites over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 will be absolutely no surprise to anybody. San Francisco is coming off a huge win over the Super Bowl favorites, while the Dolphins are likely to be in the conversation for the first overall pick and were beaten comfortably by the Las Vegas Raiders in their opener. Still, given the 49ers have the added issue of recovering from their travel back from Australia, it’s not too much of a stretch to consider this a potential ‘trap game’ for the 49ers. But Kyle Shanahan and his staff are unlikely to feel the need to remind the team about taking the matchup seriously and, if the 49ers perform at anywhere close to the levels they produced in Melbourne, then the meeting with the Dolphins should offer a significant opportunity for them to have more success in what was a surprising area of strength in Week 1. Despite the concerns about the 49ers’ defensive line depth going into the season, the San Francisco pass rush impressed in the 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams, albeit without recording a sack of Matthew Stafford. Indeed, the 49ers racked up a 41 percent pressure rate against the Rams, with that number better than any single-game pressure rate they managed throughout 2025. And, going against the Dolphins’ offensive line, the 49ers’ defensive front has a clear opportunity to build on that performance and register some sacks, even in a game in which they will be going against a mobile quarterback in Malik Willis. Miami’s offensive line endured an extremely difficult Week 1 in the Dolphins’ loss to the Raiders, surrendering five sacks, with Willis pressured 17 times in a difficult debut for the former Green Bay Packers quarterback. While Maxx Crosby did the bulk of the damage with two sacks, all three of the Raiders top edge rushers were able to get impressive push against Miami, Crosby (3.58), Kwity Paye (3.84) and Malcolm Koonce (3.9) all had average separation from the quarterback on pass rushing plays that was well under the league average of 4.58 yards, per NextGen Stats. In other words, the Raiders’ top outside pass rushers each had consistent success shrinking the pocket for Willis, with their performances likely to offer encouragement to Niners defensive end Nick Bosa and the rest of a defensive line that produced an encouraging Week 1 showing. With doubts surrounding the depth on the interior and on the edge, the 49ers entered this season with plenty of concern externally about their defensive line. One game against the Rams will not allay those doubts and a strong performance versus Miami in Week 2 will not do so either. However, if the 49ers’ front can shake off the effects of their travel and take advantage of a very favorable matchup, it could be a confidence-boosting step towards this group exceeding expectations.

There were some timely upsets, some close battles, and then some blowouts between good teams. Kansas City had one of those games. The San Francisco […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) We had a fun NFL slate wrap up in blowout fashion on Monday night, as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 to cap a memorable Week 1. There were some timely upsets, some close battles, and then some blowouts between good teams. Kansas City had one of those games. The San Francisco 49ers had another when they beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 back on Thursday night in Australia, marking one of the best Week 1 wins on the slate (if not the best). Heading into the season, the 49ers were viewed as the clear No. 3 team in the NFC West. After one week, they arguably look the strongest, with the Seattle Seahawks dealing with an injury to quarterback Sam Darnold. Week 2 power rankings in the NFL were released by several publications on Tuesday morning. Let’s take a look at where the 49ers rank among the pack. ESPN: No. 5 San Francisco jumped up four spots from No. 9 to No. 5 in ESPN’s Week 2 power rankings, although they remained third in the NFC West. Here’s the top five teams on their poll: 1. Buffalo Bills 2. Seattle Seahawks 3. Baltimore Ravens 4. Los Angeles Rams 5. San Francisco 49ers Despite the win over the Rams, the 49ers remained one spot behind them in the rankings. They also remained behind the Bills, who beat the Houston Texans 36-31 on the road in a thriller, as well as the Seahawks and Baltimore Ravens. While the Seahawks (No. 2), Bills (No. 3), and Rams (No. 1) were all in the preseason top-five, the 49ers (No. 9) and Ravens (No. 8) both made considerable jumps after Week 1. The Athletic: No. 1 The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall wasted no time anointing the 49ers at No. 1, pointing to their offense after the 27-7 beatdown last Thursday. “After the franchise’s drama-filled offseason and with questions about the aging roster, the 49ers had no trouble moving the ball against the Rams. Brock Purdy threw for three touchdowns, the running game (including rookie Kaelon Black) looked good and Raheem Morris’ defense was great. It’d be hard to draw up a better start.” Here’s how the top five looked: 1. San Francisco 49ers 2. Seattle Seahawks 3. Buffalo Bills 4. Chicago Bears 5. Baltimore Ravens The Rams fell from No. 1 to No. 6 here, followed by the Kansas City Chiefs, who jumped from No. 14 to No. 7. FOX Sports: No. 7 Despite the marquee win, the 49ers didn’t move considerably here in FOX Sports’s power rankings, jumping just three spots from No. 10 to No. 7. Here’s all the teams ahead of them. 1. Baltimore Ravens 2. Chicago Bears 3. Seattle Seahawks 4. Buffalo Bills 5. Los Angeles Rams 6. Cincinnati Bengals All of these teams were ahead of the 49ers in FOX Sports’s preseason power rankings. “They heard all the talk about the dream team Rams and became L.A.’s worst nightmare. If the Niners stay healthy, they actually could end up the best team in the dangerous NFC West,” FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacciano wrote. USA Today: No. 2 The 49ers jumped up five spots in USA Today’s power rankings up to No. 2, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks, who beat the New England Patriots in the season opener without Sam Darnold. “Their “Sleep tight” tweet served as the mic drop of Week 1 after the Niners, who were at least close to full strength after juggling so many injuries in 2025, stuck it to the apparently jet-lagged Rams in Australia,” USA Today’s Nate Davis wrote. “The NFC West is already shaping up as a three-way heavyweight bout once again, and the Niners − if healthy − have certainly shown they’ve got the goods to be a Super Sunday threat.” Behind them were the Buffalo Bills, Chicago Bears, and Los Angeles Rams. The Niners definitely surprised most in Week 1, having strong play to go in the trenches to support their well-rounded team. Things are a lot different in Week 2, as they’ll host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, where they’re already a massive 13.5-point favorite.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

full_text: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) I was watching two more of our opponents play on Monday Night Football, and I feel even more confident in predicting that the 49ers will beat the Broncos in week 4… and slightly less confident that we can beat the Chiefs in week 16. Denver’s ILB Alex Singleton had 5 missed tackles, so not only is he a liability in the passing game, he’s also struggling in his supposed strong suit. On offense, the only player making anything happen was the TE Evan Engram (with some decent pop from RJ Harvey in the run game). That tells me that Kansas City’s linebackers are still gettable, so George Kittle and the two-headed rushing attack will be especially important come December. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Where 49ers rookie Kaelon Black aims to improve after impressive Week 1 debut “He runs hard,” McKivitz said of Black, “and I have the bruises on my back to prove it.” Black, a star last season on Indiana’s national championship team, has made a great impression on his veteran teammates. It is easy to see why the 49ers selected him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft with the No. 90 overall selection. But he has left his mark in more ways than one. “When you got a young back who’s ready to run hard and doesn’t question himself, that’s what we look for in this offense,” McKivitz said. “When he sees a hole, he hits it. “He reminds me a little of JP (Jordan Mason) but with a little more juice. It’s nice to have a guy like that. He’ll learn some things. Hopefully, he’ll open his eyes and not run into me. But it’s exciting to have a guy like that.” ….“I heard them, and I feel so bad,” Black said. “I told them, ‘Sorry,’ multiple, multiple times. I’m just so down hill. I’m trying to grind out as many yards as I can. Sometimes it happens. But it’s definitely something I can be better at.” 11 Winners from the 49ers’ blowout win over the Rams “Sumer Sports tracks impact plays for offensive linemen, and the Niners had three players in the top 45 in Week 1: (6th) Connor Colby – 5 (13th) Jake Brendel – 4 (36th) Trent Williams – 3 Impact plays are defined as “highlight plays where a player demonstrates exceptional execution relative to their role and alignment.” During Colby’s five, he displaced the defender he was blocking by multiple yards. …One of the few bright spots on defense toward the end of the season last year was Stout. He was third on the team in impact plays with four. Stout’s IQ was on full display. He had a quarterback hit, a run stop where he recognized what was coming before the ball was snapped, and only allowed three yards in coverage on three targets.” 49ers named trade fit for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. by ESPN insider “The 49ers’ cornerback rotation looked stout Thursday against the Los Angeles Rams, but seasons are long, and Porter would help the defense immensely,” Fowler wrote. “San Francisco has eight draft picks in 2027 and around $45 million in cap space. Porter opposite Deommodore Lenoir would form a stout 1-2 cornerback combo.” Kawakami: Why there are so many weird takes on the 49ers (and why they don’t care) (paywall) “The big-picture point, though, is that the 49ers are structurally different with Marathe gone and York on the sidelines. And I think the 49ers will act in a subtly different way through this season — with a very big emphasis on what might happen at the trade deadline and then again after the season when some more big negotiations come up. We know that York recently moved back to Ohio, we can guess he’s likely to get a fairly long suspension (six months seems to be the best supposition) that will officially take him off the board, and we know that he used to be in team HQ all of the time, discussing plans with Lynch and Shanahan and everybody else. He’s not doing that now. He might not do it for a long time. I’ll also note that York’s been very protective of his image, which is a main reason he’s had such good relationships with national reporters. York likes to believe he’s the most knowledgeable and smartest guy in any conversation, and I imagine it’s been tough to know that the video of his arrest and his mug shot will flash into everybody’s minds whenever his name comes up. During owners’ meetings. Around employees. Whenever he shows up to games in the future. Or just in the community at any time.….. ….And it’ll likely be months before York is a major part of the 49ers’ decision-making process. Marathe is gone, too. Until now, those were the two hard-liners in the 49ers’ negotiating process. Think of the acid 2022 Deebo Samuel talks. The times Marathe almost traded Brandon Aiyuk in 2024. The laughable leaks about possibly cutting or trading Trent Williams last spring. All the big negotiations that pushed into training camp and beyond. Who was orchestrating all this? Every time I asked somebody who’d know, I was told: Marathe and York. There’s a chance that new CEO Al Guido will become the new negotiating hawk in this franchise, but I don’t think that’s his style. I think Shanahan and Lynch have always had a lot of freedom to make moves, but without York and Marathe on site, there might not be anybody who has or would want veto power over them. And I think Shanahan and Lynch will avoid overplaying their hand, but I also believe they’ll get swift approval for any potential big move in the next few months. A trade for a veteran defensive lineman — say, old friend DeForest Buckner? — as a finishing move for a playoff run, even if it adds a big salary to the payroll? Who says no?” Fred Warner reveals sports psychologist’s advice that ‘saved’ his NFL career “My fourth year, I was coming off my first All-Pro, my first Pro Bowl, a new deal,” Warner explained. “I wasn’t quite right with my body. My knee was kind of bothering me a little bit.” The BYU alum individually finished with 79 solo tackles, five tackles for loss, three interceptions, and one sack in 2020. After a historic season, something changed heading into Year 4. “I went into that camp, and I wasn’t performing like I was supposed to,” Warner admitted. “I remember I went into that season and I was thrown off the whole year. I started letting that outside noise fester in my brain a lot. It took me reaching out to a sports psychologist that I followed on Twitter.” In 2019, the NFL instituted a mandate that all teams employ a part-time behavioral and mental health clinician. Warner proactively found help on his own through social media. “Jim Renfro … I still haven’t even met him to this day,” Warner stated. “It was all over the phone. We talked through things. He told me, ‘You’re the lion, at the end of the day. Sometimes the Lion doesn’t get the kill. That doesn’t mean that they’re not a Lion.’ “
author: Yinon Raviv

title: Should the 49ers buy more into the RB committee after Week 1?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers dismantled the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, thrashing them 27-7 in a dominant performance where they excelled in all phases of the game. One of the most notable takeaways was how San Francisco neutralized the Rams’ defensive line, as they were able to run the ball 30 times for 174 […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers dismantled the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, thrashing them 27-7 in a dominant performance where they excelled in all phases of the game. One of the most notable takeaways was how San Francisco neutralized the Rams’ defensive line, as they were able to run the ball 30 times for 174 yards with quality play from the offensive line. Heading into the season, a key question I had was how successful the 49ers would be on the ground after a rough 2025, and if they would diversify the carries after Christian McCaffrey led the league in touches. Well, McCaffrey wasn’t the team’s leading ballcarrier, as rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black actually had 14 carries to McCaffrey’s 10, while the duo combined for 133 rushing yards. Black looked quick and exploded vertically for quality gains behind great holes from the offensive line. He was able to spell McCaffrey quite a bit, even though the star still had a major workload with five catches and eight targets in addition to his 10 carries. It was reported after the game that McCaffrey dealt with cramps, which could’ve led to some more of the carry distribution. But Black looked quite good in his first NFL action, which came after a ton of offseason discourse regarding the value of where he was drafted in April. Now, heading into Week 2, should the 49ers continue leaning more into the commitee, or should McCaffrey regain his tremendous workload, with Black sprinkling in? When discussing the 49ers rushing attack, I’ve noted how valuable McCaffrey is to the offense, even when he isn’t touching the ball, just because how much defenses focus on him. But if the offensive line continues to play well as a run-blocking unit, Black could be a viable option as a runner who fits very well into what San Francisco does on the ground, while also being a quality pass protector. This could be a strong strategy amid all the injuries to keep McCaffrey healthy and fresh later in the season, which the 49ers have expressed their desire to do this offseason. Now, there will be plenty of closer games for San Francisco than Week 1, which probably skews the touch share towards the star running back. But even a 70/30 split would be more optimal than what San Francisco has had the last few seasons. McCaffrey posted snap counts of 83 and 81 percent in his last two fully healthy seasons with the 49ers, and had closer to an 80/20 split with Brian Robinson last year as he led the league in touches. Using McCaffrey more as a receiver, where defenses are forced to account for his superb talent, could also keep the running back fresher. San Francisco already showed it can be quite dominant on offense with its current group of pieces, as Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and George Kittle is a strong trio of receiving options. The ceiling is extremely high with McCaffrey also involved in that mix. Weeks 2 and 3 should give us a better picture of how the 49ers will deploy their backfield, but it seems they’re finally buying into a running back split after spending a ton of draft capital at the position over the last few years.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers listed as a potential trade target for disgruntled Steelers CB
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be a trade target for just about every position out there as the season goes along. Week 1 was a mirage, and the battle of attrition can prove to be costly. One area where the 49ers did not struggle in Week 1 was at cornerback. Renardo Green was flagged for […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - DECEMBER 21: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter, Jr. (24) watches during the Pittsburgh Steelers versus Baltimore Ravens NFL game at M&T Bank Stadium on December 21, 2024 in Baltimore, MD. (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will be a trade target for just about every position out there as the season goes along. Week 1 was a mirage, and the battle of attrition can prove to be costly. One area where the 49ers did not struggle in Week 1 was at cornerback. Renardo Green was flagged for defensive pass interference. Deommodore Lenoir had an illegal contact penalty. But outside of that, they performed about as well as you could ask that group to, all things considered. That didn’t stop the 49ers from landing on a list of teams who could trade for Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.: The 49ers’ cornerback rotation looked stout Thursday against the Los Angeles Rams , but seasons are long and Porter would help the defense immensely. San Francisco has eight draft picks in 2027 and around $45 million in cap space. Porter opposite Deommodore Lenoir would form a stout 1-2 cornerback combo. Green and Jack Jones missed practice ahead of Week 1. If this had come out before Thursday’s game, it would’ve felt more realistic. The defense is essentially an injury away from Ephesians Prysock being active and needing to play. But that was not the case. In fact, Raheem Morris used dime personnel on eight plays, where Jones would come in, and there would be five cornerbacks on the field at once. That’s a sign that Morris has confidence in that group. Porter Jr. is playing in the final year of his rookie contract. If injuries pop up down the line, his name will come up. However, this feels like the 49ers were nothing more than a team thrown into the mix, with little reasoning other than that they presumably had a hole at the position before the season began. The former second-rounder has good numbers and plenty of ball production throughout his career, but something always seemed missing from Porter Jr. If that weren’t the case, the Steelers would be more eager to retain him long-term.

title: What will the 49ers do during De’Zhaun Stribling’s absence?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers made it back from Australia with a big victory, but rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury and will miss some time. Stribling started the game with veteran Mike Evans, which is a sign of his big involvement. Unfortunately, after just over 20 snaps, Stribling was carted off. His […]
full_text: (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers made it back from Australia with a big victory, but rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury and will miss some time. Stribling started the game with veteran Mike Evans, which is a sign of his big involvement. Unfortunately, after just over 20 snaps, Stribling was carted off. His timeline is unclear at the moment, and the 49ers will have to replace the speedy rookie. The plan after Stribling left the game changed to Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel being used at different spots as receivers. That’s probably the easiest answer. Jordan Watkins wasn’t active Thursday night and will likely provide depth on game days with Jacob Cowing. As George Kittle continues to ramp up, his involvement in the pass game will increase. Bringing Samuel back looks better by the day, as the versatile receiver will see much more playing time at different positions and be used as a chess piece. I would bet on Robinson and Evans to start in two-receiver sets, with Samuel sprinkled in situationally. We did see a shift in playing time for the running backs, and Christian McCaffrey can be used as a receiver as well. Kaelon Black can take on a larger snap share, and McCaffrey can be used more as a receiver to maintain involvement and lighten his workload. The hope is Stribling doesn’t miss much time, nor will he require an injured reserve stint. Christian Kirk can be available after Week 4 and is a candidate to gain snaps when healthy. Adding Darius Slayton from the New York Giants as a free agent is something the 49ers should consider, even when Stribling is healthy. Slayton joining and bumping Watkins down makes the receiver room more formidable. Sure, it didn’t work out in New York, but a change of scenery could be the ticket for the talented receiver. A room of Evans, Robinson, Slayton, Samuel, Stribling, and Cowing is an excellent blend of skill sets. As a betting man, I believe the 49ers will lean on their vets in the building and reassess the group when Kirk returns and when Stribling’s timeline becomes clear. Ultimately, the Stribling injury is a bummer, but the 49ers are well positioned to replace the rookie and welcome him back as another weapon when he recovers fully. Kyle Shanahan and the 49ers offense can manage to remain efficient and explosive. Getting the rookie back and ramping up down the stretch will only make this offense more dangerous.
author: Jason Aponte

title: 11 Winners from the 49ers’ blowout win over the Rams
summary: When you outclass your opponent in the way that the San Francisco 49ers did to the Los Angeles Rams, it’s difficult to come up with multiple “losers.” The Niners won by 20, but it felt like the margin was greater. Brock Purdy’s QBR was 50 points higher than the other starter. The running game averaged […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you outclass your opponent in the way that the San Francisco 49ers did to the Los Angeles Rams, it’s difficult to come up with multiple “losers.” The Niners won by 20, but it felt like the margin was greater. Brock Purdy’s QBR was 50 points higher than the other starter. The running game averaged 1.6 yards per carry more than the Rams. The vaunted defense we heard about all offseason was wearing the wrong jersey. Sprinkle in a couple of special teams plays, and it was a butt-kicking, through and through. Here are the winners and losers from Week 1. Winners The offensive line Sumer Sports tracks impact plays for offensive linemen, and the Niners had three players in the top 45 in Week 1: (6th) Connor Colby – 5 (13th) Jake Brendel – 4 (36th) Trent Williams – 3 Impact plays are defined as “highlight plays where a player demonstrates exceptional execution relative to their role and alignment.” During Colby’s five, he displaced the defender he was blocking by multiple yards. Four linemen — Brendel, Williams, Dominick Puni, and Colton McKivitz — allowed one pressure each on 36 pass-blocking snaps. Colby allowed two pressures. As a unit, they combined for four total blown blocks — two against the run and two against the pass. The 49ers led all teams in rushing success rate at 56.7%, five percentage points better than second place. Brock Purdy faced the second-lowest pressure rate, while the running backs benefited from the fourth-most yards before contact of the week and only 7.1% of their carries resulting in a stuff —good for the third-best mark of Week 1. According to Sports Info Solutions, all five starters earned multiple points in Week 1, with Colby and Puni leading the way with 3 points earned. For reference, Colby earned six total points in 425 snaps as a rookie. There’s no denying the scheme, like a heavy dose of screens or different motions, played a significant role in the play of the line, but that shouldn’t take away from how effective they were Raheem Morris Against an offense everyone projects to be tops in the league, Morris allowed the 3rd-lowest EPA per play and passing success rate. Despite losing his starting defensive tackle the week of the game, Morris devised a scheme that held one of the most dangerous rushing attacks to the sixth-worst EPA per rush mark of the week. Morris gave Sean McVay a swirlie and stuffed Matthew Stafford in a locker. The Rams don’t go four quarters without reaching double digits. Stafford usually has a few touchdowns a game and is somewhere around 275 yards. Puka Nacua has made a habit of terrorizing NFC West opponents. Outside of a long Nacua reception, the Rams rode the struggle bus for much of the game. Morris designed blitzes that got home, mixed in coverages that led to turnovers, and was two steps ahead of McVay all game. Osa Odighizuwa Odighizuwa managed four pressures in 18 pass-rush snaps. He’s precisely the kind of pesky interior pass rusher the Niners have been craving for years. That 22.2% pressure rate is good for the fifth-best among all defensive tackles in Week 1. Unlike some pressures, there was no fluke or fluff here. Odighizuwa hit the quarterback on four separate occasions, which made up for half the number of times the Niners defense as a whole hit Stafford. He is just what the doctor ordered for Morris. Fred Warner Only five players had more run stops than Warner in Week 1. Every one of those players played at least five more snaps than Fred, with some playing as many as 24 more snaps. Warner had multiple plays where he defended Nacua 1-on-1. He broke up a pass on one of those plays. Warner and his 11 tackles all came at timely moments. The Rams had an opportunity to make it a game again in the third quarter, but Warner and Jaden Dugger halted their plans in the backfield on a goal-to-go situation. The most telling Warner stat was how seldom Stafford threw it over the middle. You can’t quantify this in Warner’s favor, but it’s a sign of respect from a veteran quarterback who knows better than to test a future Hall of Famer: Warner takes away the part of the field where today’s offenses want to target the most. Nick Bosa We’ll do our best to leave Warner and Bosa off these lists throughout the year, as they’re expected to perform great. But it’s been nearly a full year since we’ve seen Bosa. The assumption was that he’d take some time get his feet underneath him. Well, not this guy. Bosa hit Stafford on the first play from scrimmage. It was the quickest pressure of the defense, checking in at two seconds flat. He tied Colby for a team-high five impact plays. Three of those came in the first quarter. It’s refreshing to be reminded that your edge defenders can be run stoppers. Bosa had a tackle for loss early and added another in the third quarter. He joined Warner with another stop two plays later. Best of all, Bosa humiliated a tight end whenever the Rams blocked him with one. Mike Evans Evans caught six of his seven targets for 49 yards. When he was targeted is why he’s on the list. Over half of his targets came on late downs. Evans added at least a point in EPA on three different routes. It would have been four, had he not dropped his final target. Evans was 3-for-3 against man coverage and was also perfect out of the slot. Brock Purdy, knowing he has Evans as a fallback option on third downs, is quite the luxury to have. Evans caught five of his six targets on third down, and both red zone targets. Upton Stout One of the few bright spots on defense toward the end of the season last year was Stout. He was third on the team in impact plays with four. Stout’s IQ was on full display. He had a quarterback hit, a run stop where he recognized what was coming before the ball was snapped, and only allowed three yards in coverage on three targets. Raheem Morris manipulates the protection to get exactly what he wants. The top DCs will always attack the back. He uses Bosa's gravity to his advantage here. Warner walks up to occupy the center. The line slanting basically makes it a 1-on-1 drill for Stout vs. the RB. No chance pic.twitter.com/DMbTeV63xJ — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 11, 2026 Stout picked up where he left off last season. Honorable mentions: We could list another 10 players if we wanted to, but Keion White, Jack Jones, Renardo Green, and Deebo Samuel were all close to making the list.
author: Kyle Posey

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers in first place after Week 1; the Rams are not
summary: Welcome to the weekly NFC West recap. For those of you new to the program, we’ll do a rundown of how the San Francisco 49ers are faring against their other NFC West rivals and any news from those games that might be noteworthy. And we begin things with who is in the lead. First, all […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the weekly NFC West recap. For those of you new to the program, we’ll do a rundown of how the San Francisco 49ers are faring against their other NFC West rivals and any news from those games that might be noteworthy. And we begin things with who is in the lead. First, all the NFC West teams won this weekend—except the Los Angeles Rams. Of those three, the 49ers are in first place after Week 1. Divisional games are considered a “game and a half” in terms of value, and since that was the only NFC West game this weekend, the 49ers start out on top. Don’t get too excited; it is Week 1 after all. Last year the 49ers beat the Seahawks in Seattle, and then the season happened. Regardless, starting the season with not just a win, but a divisional win can only help in January tiebreakers. Everyone else? Whatever. San Francisco 49ers (1-0)/Los Angeles Rams (0-1) Oh, you know what time it is. It’s time to RAM IT . I don’t know about you, but I really, really enjoyed that 27-7 thumping the 49ers handed the Rams on Thursday. Obviously, just because it’s the Rams, it’s already enjoyable, but seeing the 49ers look so crisp and efficient while the Rams look the opposite (especially after all the offseason hype) brings a lot of optimism about what the 49ers could do. Just stay healthy. Please, 49ers? Speaking of health, the 49ers got nailed by the injury bug twice. Tight end Jake Tonges went down with what was later said to be MCL-related and “not good.” A bit less severe was wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, who went down with what is speculated to be a grade 2 deltoid sprain . This is the first time I learned the ankle has a “deltoid,” but leave it to the 49ers to teach me about every ligament in the human body you can sprain or tear. Stribling is expected to be out for at least a month, and surgery is on the table. Given that this is his rookie season and the 49ers are already dealing with the absence of Ricky Pearsall, we can all hope Stribling gets healthy sooner rather than later. Things could have been worse; when you see a player carted off the field (which happened to Stribling), it usually indicates something devastating. Making any declarations from Week 1 is a terrible idea, and I’m sure the 49ers might have some challenges in Week 2, even against the Miami Dolphins, but if they can stay healthy, I don’t see why someone can’t see them as a threat to the NFC (not just the West). As for the Rams, again, it’s Week 1. When they play the 49ers in Week 14, they will have Aaron Donald (and whether he’s still got it or not is left to be determined), and Myles Garrett will probably be a much different player than the one who laid a goose egg on the stat sheet Thursday. That is, of course, if the Rams have Garrett back by then. It came out Sunday that the defensive lineman will undergo knee surgery and head to injured reserve. The minimum is four games, but there’s no timeline on when Garrett will be back on the roster. Not good, especially when the Rams have some tough games coming up. Outside of the defense, some might think Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford might be on the “decline” after one game. Just because they brought in the backup to protect Stafford from getting blasted in garbage time doesn’t mean anything. We’ve also seen Stafford play bad games before, so Week 1 in Australia doesn’t indicate anything. Should Stafford be a bit less efficient this year, the Rams have plenty of talent on offense around him to prevent that side of the ball from taking a nosedive. Seattle Seahawks (1-0) The defending Super Bowl champs began their season against the New England Patriots. The first points weren’t scored until six minutes into the second quarter. And things imploded in the fourth quarter, when Drake Maye threw three straight interceptions that led to points and a 13-10 win for the Seahawks. It wasn’t all roses for the Seahawks, however. Quarterback Sam Darnold left with an injury to his hip five plays into the game, leaving Drew Lock to fill in. Darnold is expected to miss some time. It’s not a fracture, so at the moment it’s not thought to be season-ending, but he will miss some time. Lock went 16-of-22, 187 yards for one touchdown. Simply having zero interceptions means he was far more efficient than Maye. The Seahawks don’t have a favorable schedule the next few weeks, with the Arizona Cardinals, Washington Commanders, and Los Angeles Chargers coming up, so if Darnold is going to be resting up, Seahawks fans will be hoping Lock doesn’t tip things over. Arizona Cardinals (1-0) Sure, the 49ers win over the Rams was a surprise, but there was no bigger surprise than the Cardinals beating the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers were favored by 9.5 points. Or were the Cardinals favored? I really don’t know because the final score was 26-14, Cardinals. Looks like those points wouldn’t be needed. The game was relatively close until the fourth quarter. That was when stuff like this happened: Cardinals block the punt and will take over near the goal line! AZvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AKdFclsKgP — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 The Cardinals have Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, but the Chargers have Justin Herbert. And for a team like the Cardinals, you’d think Herbert would do better than going 17 for 27 and handing the game away with a costly interception. Then again, Herbert’s offensive line was not helping him at all as the Cardinals’ pass rush was in the backfield on the regular. The stat sheet says Herbert was sacked three times, but it sure felt like a lot more. The win puts the Cardinals into a tiebreaker with Seattle—one we aren’t going to break down in Week 1. Are the Cardinals better than we thought? Again, it’s Week 1. We’ll see how they do next week in their first NFC West matchup. Onto Week 2 If the 49ers are going to deal with any jet lag in their return from Australia, it at least will be against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. The Dolphins didn’t have a great Sunday, losing to the Las Vegas Raiders 27-13. That’s the start of what many think will be a bad season. The Seahawks and Cardinals will be giving us our second NFC West matchup of the season. I want to say the Seahawks won’t have trouble with this, but after Sunday’s upset—and Seattle’s issues with their quarterback—who knows. The game is in Arizona, so take what you will from that. The Rams will host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. While we shouldn’t hold our breath, a Giants victory here would open the floodgates for chaos next Tuesday with the Rams, an anointed “super team” in the offseason, starting 0-2. The Giants didn’t have many issues against the Dallas Cowboys, but the Rams are a massive difficulty spike over the Cowboys. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next vs. Miami Dolphins TIE – 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: at Arizona Cardinals TIE-2nd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Seattle Seahawks 4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: vs. New York Giants (Monday Night Football)

title: 49ers open up as nearly 2-touchdown favorites against the Dolphins
summary: The San Francisco 49ers were underdogs in Week 1. After the beatdown they put on the Rams, it might be months until they’re not favored to win. According to the Week 2 odds on FanDuel Sportsbook, the Niners are favored to beat the Miami Dolphins by 13.5 points, with the total on the game listed […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers were underdogs in Week 1. After the beatdown they put on the Rams, it might be months until they’re not favored to win. According to the Week 2 odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Niners are favored to beat the Miami Dolphins by 13.5 points, with the total on the game listed at 45.5. Generally, large spreads with low totals are a sportsbook’s way of telling you a blowout is coming. The 49ers allowed one touchdown against the Rams. The Dolphins’ lone touchdown against the Raiders came when they were gifted the ball at midfield to begin the third quarter after a Kirk Cousins interception. Cousins threw two interceptions, and the Raiders went 5-for-13 on third down, yet they still scored 27 points, scored a touchdown on three of their four red zone trips, and lived in Dolphins territory. Ashton Jeanty had a field day. He went over 100 yards, while rookie Mike Washington averaged nearly six yards per carry on seven attempts. That’s impressive when you factor in Cousins only completed one pass beyond 10 yards. Going from the Rams to the Dolphins is the definition of stepping down in class. One team was the Super Bowl favorite heading into 2026. The other was penciled in for a top-three pick. A big reason is its inexperience and lack of offensive threats. Malik Willis had a QBR of 29.4, thanks to taking five sacks. He was also Miami’s leading rusher, with 39 yards. The Dolphins receiver with the most targets was Malik Washington, a 6th-rounder from the ’24 NFL Draft. Rookie Caleb Douglas was the second-leading receiver in targets. He’s a unique challenge at 6’4″. But this will be the second game of his professional career. It’s the home opener, so the 49ers shouldn’t be lethargic. A letdown after a win over a divisional rival is always a worry, but it’s Week 2. That should not be an issue for San Francisco. This is a spot where they need to handle business and get out of this contest healthy.
