title: Dave Canales: Panthers need to 'play way better football'
summary: After watching film, the coach said Carolina needed to play smarter and Derrick Brown reminded everyone that it's just one game.
full_text:
Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Sunday after the team's 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears that he needed to watch film before pointing fingers at the problems from the historic defensive downturn. After watching the tape Monday, Canales said the team could have played smarter, noting penalties, poor technique and other mental gaffes.

 "We played hard," Canales said. "We played with great effort. The guys were together. All those things are true. Playing smart, that's where we fell short. And it was about executing our plan. It was about timely and costly penalties. Certainly, the turnovers ... against a really good team. That's not something that you can do to play the championship football that we need to play."

 The Bears' offense produced 552 net yards -- Chicago's third-most yardage earned in the Super Bowl era -- with 291 collected on the ground. The 59 points were the most allowed in Panthers' franchise history. The six rushing touchdowns produced by Chicago -- the most in a season opener since 1922, according to ESPN Research -- were shared by three players, including quarterback Caleb Williams , who also threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns for a 124.1 traditional passer rating.

 "We knew how they were going to attack us," Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke said. "We practiced a lot of their concepts, and we got a lot of their concepts on game day. And we executed a good bit, but just the run game bit us in the ass today and we gotta be a lot better there."

 

 And yet, Canales' main takeaways after watching the film focused on turnovers and penalties.

 The Panthers' offense and special teams coughed up the ball twice on lost fumbles. Quarterback Bryce Young threw an interception on a pass to wideout Jalen Coker to end the first half, and the offense was stopped while failing to convert on a fourth-down play at the end of the third quarter. But even taking away the 17 points the Bears scored off those mishaps, Chicago still had a five-point advantage over Carolina because of what the defense allowed on the other side.

 The penalties, though, were inarguably a crux for the Panthers' letdown. Carolina was flagged 11 times for 84 yards, but it was more about the timing of infractions that lost ground. Team captain Derrick Brown was uncharacteristically charged twice -- once for roughing the passer and once for offside -- with the first penalty leading to a touchdown and the second negating an interception by fellow lineman Bobby Brown III  and leading to another Bears score.

 "S--- like that can't happen," Derrick Brown said after the game.

 Week 1 was the latest in a long line of defensive meltdowns for the Panthers under coordinator Ejiro Evero, who was hired by Carolina in February 2023 under coach Frank Reich. But it was also the biggest one to date, topping a brutal back-to-back stretch to end the 2024 season, when the defense gave up 551 yards to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 17 and 537 yards in the season finale against the Atlanta Falcons .

 "I like our system," Canales said Monday. "I like our scheme. I've seen this scheme work at a high level, and I've seen us work in this scheme at a high level."

 "It sucks, but it's one f---ing game," Derrick Brown said Sunday. "We've got a whole season."

 

 In 52 regular-season games as the Panthers' defensive coordinator, Evero's unit has given up the highest allowed scoring average in the league at 26.7 points per game, following Sunday's 59-point offering to the Bears. During that span, his group also ranks 26th in the league with a 345.9 yards allowed average per game.

 The unit also ranks second worst in the league during Evero's tenure in defensive EPA (expected points added) with a minus-250.9 points mark, according to ESPN Research. The defense is also allowing the highest Total QBR in the league (58.3) during that stretch.

 Following Sunday's loss, the Panthers rank last in points (minus-8.92) and yardage (minus-56) margin averages per game during the Evero era. But it is also worth noting that the offenses, largely anchored by Reich and Canales, have been among the bottom-third of the league throughout Evero's tenure.

 "I feel like we could just be better as a whole," outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen said about the defense's performance Sunday. "I feel like we could have been more disciplined as a whole unit and just as a whole team in general."

 

 During his second season at the helm, Evero's defense was the worst in the league against the run, allowing 179.8 yards per game. The unit also finished last in total yards average, giving up 404.5 yards per game. But last season, the unit improved across the board, ranking 20th in run defense (123.3 rushing yards per game) and 16th overall (327.2 total yards per game).

 The Panthers added safety Tre'von Moehrig , outside linebacker Patrick Jones II and defensive linemen Bobby Brown III and Tershawn Wharton in free agency during the 2025 offseason. They also selected outside linebackers Umanmielen and  Nic Scourton  and safety Lathan Ransom in the 2025 draft.

 This year Carolina continued to beef up its defense, paying a fortune for outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and inside linebacker Devin Lloyd . They drafted defensive tackle Lee Hunter , cornerback  Will Lee III, safety Zakee Wheatley and linebacker Jackson Kuwatch as well. Plus, they signed veteran linebacker Bobby Okereke on Aug. 31.

 The Panthers didn't have Wharton, Jones and Scourton due to injury and Wheatley was a healthy scratch in Week 1. So, while the investment in the defense over the past two years wasn't in full force, the rest of the accumulated talent did little to stop the onslaught of Williams and D'Andre Swift .

 "Players and coaches alike gotta be better," DT Bobby Brown III said after going through Monday's meetings. "Players didn't execute all the time. Coach [Evero] already told us he didn't get us in the best calls all the time. But when we did have the call right and we felt like we [were] in good positions, everybody didn't show up and make the plays that needed to be made."

 Canales maintained Monday that the unit has the right talent to turn things around.

 "And that was one of the things I did share with the team today, I said, 'Look, I wouldn't have been able to sleep if I felt like we didn't have the pieces that we need right in this room.'" Canales said. "And a true statement to those guys. But we need to collectively come together and play way better football than that."

title: Who are the winningest NFL coaches of all time?
summary: From Belichick to Reid, there are many iconic coaches in NFL history. Who has the best career record? Check out the stat breakdown now.
full_text:
Only four head coaches in NFL history have won 300 career games across the regular season and postseason. Kansas City Chiefs  coach Andy Reid was the last to cross the 300-win plateau.

 Reid recorded his 300th career victory on Jan. 18, 2025, when his Chiefs defeated the Houston Texans 23-14 in the AFC divisional round.

 Reid, who signed a five-year, $100 million extension with the Chiefs in April 2024, entered the 2026 season looking to add to his career win total and close the gap between him and the NFL's all-time winningest head coach, Hall of Famer Don Shula.

 Let's take a look at which head coaches have the most career victories in NFL history (including both regular-season and postseason play):

 *Active NFL head coach 

 5. Tom Landry, 270 wins 

 Landry was the Dallas Cowboys' head coach for an NFL-record 29 years in a row and the team had 20 consecutive winning seasons, which is also a league record. Landry led Dallas to two Super Bowl wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI and the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. He was named the NFL's Coach of the Year in 1966 and the UPI NFL Coach of the Year in 1975. Landry was an innovator, with the 4-3 defense among his creations. He was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 *4. Andy Reid, 308 wins 

 Reid is the only head coach in NFL history who has won 100 games with two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles (coaching the team from 1999 through 2012) and the Chiefs (he has coached Kansas City since 2013). He led the Eagles on multiple deep playoff runs, including a Super Bowl in 2004 and three straight conference finals from 2001 to 2003. However, he wasn't able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy until he arrived in Kansas City. He has turned the Chiefs into a juggernaut, winning three Super Bowls. Reid is an offensive mastermind and quarterback whisperer. He'll likely continue to rack up wins moving forward with Patrick Mahomes , Travis Kelce & Co.

 

 3. George Halas, 324 wins 

 Halas was a co-founder of the NFL and creator of the Bears. For 10 years, he served as player-coach-executive for the Bears (which is how he earned the nickname "Mr. Everything"). In 1930, he retired as a player and focused on ownership, but he would later return to coach the Bears several times. Halas led the Bears to eight NFL championships, tying Belichick's number of titles. Halas coached the team for 40 years and had just six losing seasons. He helped create the T-formation system and used it to set an NFL record for the biggest blowout in league history: a 73-0 win over the Washington team in the 1940 NFL Championship Game. Halas was selected as the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1963 and 1965, and he was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 2. Bill Belichick, 333 wins 

 Belichick is considered by some as the greatest coach in all of professional sports, as he has won an NFL-record eight Super Bowls (six as a head coach with the Patriots and two as an assistant coach with the Giants). He also ranks first among all NFL coaches in playoff wins with 31. Belichick was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 2003, 2007 and 2010. Many franchises have hired away Belichick's assistants and tried to replicate his "Patriot Way," but it hasn't been the same without him. If Belichick returns to NFL coaching, he is just 26 regular-season wins from surpassing Don Shula as the winningest regular-season coach of all time. 

 1. Don Shula, 347 wins 

 After playing in the NFL as a defensive back for seven seasons, Shula decided to retire and become a coach. He got his first head-coaching opportunity in 1963 with the Baltimore Colts, whom he led to the NFL championship in 1968. From 1970 through 1995, Shula had a legendary run as head coach of the Dolphins. Shula led the Dolphins to a pair of Super Bowl victories (in Super Bowl VII and Super Bowl VIII). Miami had a perfect season in 1972, making Shula the only coach in NFL history to go undefeated. He was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1964, 1967, 1968 and 1972. Whether you're just counting regular-season wins (328) or including playoff wins (347), Shula is the winningest coach in NFL history.

 Be sure to check out ESPN's NFL coverage , including scores ,  standings , stats , schedules , and more.

title: Cashing in: Bengals rookie Howell impacts pass rush
summary: Howell believes the SEC made him ready for moments such as Sunday, when he had four QB pressures in the Bengals' win.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Just before he officially made his NFL debut, Cashius Howell was playing video games with his friends when he thought about something that sounds absurd when said out loud.

 Before he emerged as one of the best Cincinnati Bengals rookies in recent memory, he was a young defensive end transitioning from playing in the MAC at Bowling Green to being in the SEC with Texas A&M.

 And in hindsight, that was tougher than getting acclimated in the NFL.

 "Not like the NFL is easy or anything -- this is the best people in the world -- but I feel like it was more of a struggle trying to get from the MAC to the SEC than it was the SEC to the NFL, if that makes sense."

 It really shouldn't. But the last few months, including Sunday's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , shows why it does. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Howell matched defensive end Boye Mafe with a team-high four quarterback pressures.

 While defensive coordinator Al Golden playfully scoffed at the various analytics used to measure players, there was no disputing Howell's immediate impact.

 "He showed up [on Sunday]," Golden told reporters on Monday.

 Five months after the Bengals drafted him, it still seems incredulous to some at Paycor Stadium that Cincinnati was able to take the reigning SEC Defensive Player of the Year.

 Golden recalled that entering the draft, as many as 10 Bengals personnel out of a ballpark of maybe 12 people gave Howell a first-round draft grade. But after the first 32 picks went off the board, Howell was still available.

 The next day, he went to the Bengals with the 41st overall pick. And since then, the transition has been virtually flawless.

 Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims , considered one of the team's top ascending talents, said Howell is one of the best rookies he's lined up against in his three years in the league.

 As good as he looked against the Bengals in offseason workouts and training camp, the real eye-opener came in the joint practice against the Chicago Bears . Howell held his own against Chicago's Darnell Wright , who ranked fourth in the NFL last season in pass block win rate as a tackle (ESPN/Next Gen Stats).

 That was enough to not only warrant a closer look but validate the same feeling that Golden and others felt during draft weekend.

 "I don't know he fell to us in the second round," Mims said on Monday. "I don't know how that was possible. But I'm very glad he's on our team. He's going to be a great, great addition for us."

 Bengals defensive end Shemar Stewart was teammates with Howell at A&M in 2024, one year before Stewart declared for the NFL and the Bengals drafted him in the first round. And he doesn't seem to recall Howell having any learning curve when he arrived in College Station.

 "I just remember him dogging people out, doing people in," Stewart said with a big laugh. "That's the first thing that comes to mind when it comes to Cash."

 In his final year at A&M, he was second in the SEC with 11.5 total sacks. And in his first true NFL action, Howell made an early impact.

 In the first quarter, he shed Tampa Bay tight end Cade Otton before forcing right guard Cody Mauch into a holding penalty. The pressure helped Cincinnati's  Kris Jenkins Jr . secure the sack.

 

 Howell officially didn't register any stats while playing on 44% of the team's defensive snaps. But his output showed how a defensive lineman can affect the game without ending up in the stat book.

 While Howell has had a pleasant start, Stewart knows things will get tougher for his fellow Aggie as the season continues.

 "It's a long year," Stewart said. "It's not like college. It's definitely a lot harder on your body. You're going to be mentally and physically tired because rookies just have a lot more things to do on your plate."

 Howell is well aware of that. He said playing in the SEC, a conference filled with pro prospects, has allowed him to adjust to the NFL game speed while meticulous offseason work prepared him for the physical rigors of the league.

 And despite all the praise and early returns, Howell is fixated on keeping a short-term outlook instead of focusing on the potential of a promising rookie season.

 "I thank God in advance for whatever he has in store for me," Howell said. "Whatever that may be, I'm prepared for it. But I feel like it will be good."

title: Ben Johnson, Ravens DBs lead top NFL quotes from NFL Week 1
summary: Sometimes the highlights come from the postgame pressers. Here's a look at the top quips and comments from around the league in Week 1.
full_text:
The NFL season has just begun, but players and even coaches have been in midseason form after their opening games, providing plenty of interesting moments during postgame speeches in the locker room, interviews at the podium and on social media.

 Ahead of the first "Monday Night Football" matchup of the year between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos , we rounded up the best quotes from around the league on Sunday.

 

 "He had 124 [yards] on the ground, three touchdowns and a brand-new f---ing contract." -- Chicago Bears  coach Ben Johnson 
 The Bears coach was fired up for his team in the locker room after beating the Carolina Panthers in a 59-37 shootout.

 While handing out game balls to his players, Johnson made sure to mention star running back D'Andre Swift 's recent massive payday. It was reported two days ago that Swift and Chicago had agreed to a three-year, $33.75 million extension .

 

 

 "I'm Malaki Starks, and I'm a dawg." -- Baltimore Ravens DB Malaki Starks 

 During his usual postgame stream on social media with teammates following a victory, defensive back Marlon Humphrey caught up with Starks. The Ravens throttled the Indianapolis Colts 41-23 , posting over 500 total yards of offense.

 While Starks was giving an honest breakdown of his team's performance on Sunday afternoon, Humphrey was having none of that. Instead, Humphrey told the sophomore safety to let the world know just how talented he is.

 

 

 "Plain and simple, we got our ass whupped." -- Colts DT DeForest Buckner 
 While it was all smiles and laughs for the Ravens on Sunday, their opponent's locker room was anything but. Indianapolis allowed 506 total yards and gave up 41 points, its second-most points allowed in a season opener in the past 10 seasons, according to ESPN Research.

 When asked about his team's performance in its home opener, Buckner didn't hold back.

 

 "I guess I've got to get 200 [touchdown passes] now. I'll keep that one." -- Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence 

 Lawrence threw for four touchdowns in Sunday's 34-10  win over the Cleveland Browns , but one of them was more special than the rest. His second TD toss to rookie receiver Josh Cameron was the 100th of his career. However, it was also Cameron's first career NFL catch.

 Knowing this was a special moment for the rookie pass catcher, Lawrence graciously let Cameron keep the ball. But he won't be so generous with the one from his 200th touchdown pass.

 

 "Waited a long time to be a head coach in this league, man. It's freaking awesome. And we're not where we want to be, and they better get us now." -- Cleveland Browns  coach Todd Monken 
 The first-year head coach expressed his disappointment following a defeat to the Jaguars. However, Monken offered some optimism for the future, too.

 He focused on his young group improving, while pinpointing that they just "didn't play well today." Monken spent 10 seasons as an assistant coach in the NFL before getting his first head coaching job. Therefore, the blowout loss presumably won't get him too shook up, as he added: "You're not going to get me down."

 

 

 "There's a time and place for everything." -- Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels 
 Washington suffered a narrow two-point defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles following a failed 2-point conversation late. One play that might have had an impact on the outcome happened early in the fourth quarter.

 Daniels connected with wide receiver Stefon Diggs for a 10-yard touchdown to make it a one-point game. However, Diggs celebrated by leaping on the goalpost and received a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty. It pushed the Commanders' PAT back, though the kick was good anyway. After the game, coach Dan Quinn said the team would have gone for two if Diggs wasn't penalized. 

 Washington's quarterback reflected on Diggs' penalty postgame.

title: Inside Patrick Mahomes' remarkable return from knee injury
summary: On Dec. 14, Mahomes, after suffering the most significant injury of his career, vowed to be back for Week 1. Here's how he did it.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Positioned next to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes , at the start of what would be a nine-month odyssey, was the MRI machine. The results of the scans that Dec. 14 day revealed the most significant injury of Mahomes' nine-year career: a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

 As the minutes passed, more people entered the room inside the Chiefs' training facility, located a few hundred feet from Arrowhead Stadium -- team head trainer Rick Burkholder; Mahomes' agent, Chris Cabott; Mahomes' wife, Brittany; coach Andy Reid; general manager Brett Veach; and club owner Clark Hunt. Together -- less than an hour after Mahomes had crumpled to the turf, grabbed his knee and screamed in pain -- the group began contemplating next steps.

 At one point, someone looked at the calendar. The first Sunday of the 2026 NFL season was scheduled for Sept. 13, 273 days away. While exploring surgical options, a phone call was made to Dr. Dan Cooper, the renowned Dallas Cowboys  head team physician who specializes in knee and shoulder injuries. Cooper presented a proposition to Mahomes: If he wanted to return to the field as soon as possible, giving himself a chance to be back in uniform for the start of the Chiefs' 2026 campaign, he would need to fly from Kansas City to Dallas the next morning to have surgery.

 

 "I'm willing," Mahomes responded, "to do whatever it takes."

 Throughout his rehab and recovery, Mahomes has said that same sentence many times. And his exhaustive, day-after-day actions have led to him achieving his mission -- one that began next to the MRI machine 274 days before Kansas City's season opener.

 When the Chiefs opened their season Monday against the Denver Broncos , Mahomes, 30, was available and started under center, tossing two touchdowns and running for another in a 31-10 victory.

 "It's incredible," Veach said. "That's a guy that defines what leadership and what the face of a franchise should look like. He gave up an entire summer. He just attacked [the rehab]. Everybody in the building sees it. The level of sacrifice is something that has been an example throughout the entire organization."

 Mahomes' injury punctuated Kansas City's disappointing 2025 season. Following the two-minute warning in the team's Week 15 game against the Los Angeles Chargers , Mahomes tried to rally the Chiefs to a game-winning drive. He scrambled out of the pocket, rolling to his right. With defensive end Da'Shawn Hand chasing him from behind, Mahomes threw the ball away. But a few steps later, Mahomes planted his left foot, which stuck into the turf, and hyperextended his knee, the knee bowing to the outside of his leg, which damaged his LCL.

 

 The Chiefs' 16-13 loss to the Chargers eliminated Kansas City from the playoffs, the team's first time missing the postseason since 2014.

 "I wasn't playing my best at the end of last year before I got hurt," said Mahomes, who rushed for a career-high 422 yards and five touchdowns last season. "I think I ran a little bit too much."

 One reason Mahomes and the Chiefs selected Cooper is his experience repairing two of the four main stabilizing knee ligaments 24 hours after injury, including reattaching the LCL.

 Aaron Borgmann, the founder of Borgmann Rehab Solutions and a former physical therapist and athletic trainer with the Chiefs, said most players wait a week or sometimes longer before having the surgery because of how much their knee has swelled. By having an expedited procedure, Mahomes avoided that wait. Also in his favor: He did not have any artery, nerve, joint surface or meniscal damage, according to Burkholder.

 "For [most people], it's 10 days for an MRI, it's another doctor's visit and then another week to schedule surgery and so on," said Borgmann, describing general practices involving a torn ACL. "But we're not professional football players. I stand on this: NFL players of today have the best medical care in the world due to our healthcare system and our availability of imaging.

 "We have more doctors associated with NFL teams than any other professional sport in the United States. It is the best medical care you can find in the world."

 Even before his surgery, Mahomes wrote on his social media accounts, vowing to not fail his expectations.

 "I [will] be back stronger than ever."

 

 

 AWAITING MAHOMES ON Day 1 of 274 was Julie Frymyer, one of the Chiefs' top assistant athletic trainers. In his first rehab session, less than 24 hours after the surgery, Mahomes gritted his teeth and grimaced in pain while Frymyer assessed his muscles and worked to make sure the knee didn't swell up.

 Mahomes and Frymyer had been through such a scene many times before for three other injuries over the quarterback's career.

 Since Mahomes became the Chiefs' starter in 2018, Frymyer has been one of the team's most sought-out trainers. Mahomes on numerous occasions has credited much of his success in recovering from injuries faster than the average player to Frymyer -- and not to the fan theory that he possesses healing powers similar to Marvel character Wolverine. Also helping him, according to Frymyer and various others in the Chiefs organization, is Mahomes' remarkable ability to tolerate pain, whether during a game or in the team's training room.

 

 Frymyer's first major assignment with Mahomes occurred Oct. 17, 2019, when Mahomes dislocated his right kneecap while attempting a quarterback sneak.

 "I remember going into that halftime and he's trying to talk me into [him] going back out and playing," Reid said of Mahomes. "That [mindset] is huge for that position. You've got a lot of eyes on you. Guys are going to watch how you go about your business."

 With Frymyer's help, Mahomes surprised the Chiefs by missing just two games, returning to the field 24 days later. Before his 2025 knee injury, that was the longest absence of his career. A few months later, Mahomes led the Chiefs to their first Super Bowl victory in 50 years. The following year, during the postseason, Mahomes returned seven days after sustaining a painful turf toe in his left foot -- while also having a concussion from the previous week. Back on the field, he excelled, leading the Chiefs to Super Bowl LV, where they were beaten by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 Frymyer became well-known among Chiefs fans and trainers in the NFL after the 2022 postseason, when she administered almost around-the-clock treatment and therapy for eight consecutive days after Mahomes experienced a painful high sprain of his right ankle in a win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the divisional round. Despite his limited mobility, Mahomes once again carried the Chiefs back to the Super Bowl, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles for the franchise's third championship.

 "I trust her so much," Mahomes said of Frymyer, who last year starred in a State Farm commercial alongside the quarterback and pop singer Meghan Trainor. "There's days you come in [and] you're tired. I mean, you're sore. But she makes sure I finish the entire workout -- and I'm going to do it the right way. She knows when to pull back on some days.

 "It lets me go out there and work and not have to think about if I'm doing too much [or] am I doing not enough."

 

 Unlike those previous, brief rehabs, Frymyer this time had to find the correct balance of when to motivate and when to encourage Mahomes through a monthslong process.

 The most grueling days were in late December, when he couldn't walk. While wearing a protective brace, Mahomes couldn't sleep with much comfort. Christmas Day was not ideal, either. Instead of playing with his teammates, Mahomes watched the Chiefs lose to the Broncos from a suite inside Arrowhead Stadium, his crutches nearby.

 "The toughest part was the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around," Mahomes said. "I remember sitting at the [training] table and watching us play those last few [road] games and how much it…

title: Best and worst NFL teams' travel: 49ers, Seahawks, Steelers divulge it all
summary: ESPN spoke with several players and team executives about team travel and the feedback that serves as the basis for the latest NFLPA survey grades.
full_text:
As the NFL prepared for its first regular-season game in Australia to open the 2026 season, careful thought was put into how to get the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers the nearly 8,000 miles from California to Melbourne.

 The league -- with help from the teams -- settled on a Qantas Airbus A380. The planes had 84 lie-flat seats, ensuring each player had a bed on the flight. Each charter flight flew with four pilots, 22 cabin crew and one traveling charter manager on board.

 In comparison, when the Pittsburgh Steelers flew to Dublin in September 2025, they flew on Aer Lingus as part of a partnership with the airline. A player, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Aer Lingus was "like Spirit," a low-cost carrier that shut down earlier this year. The player also said that only a handful of players had business class seats, which were allotted by seniority.

 There are no guidelines in the current NFL collective bargaining agreement on team travel, and there hasn't been much to show there's a correct way to do it. The last two times the Rams played internationally, they flew into the country the day before. The result didn't go their way this season against the 49ers, but it did last season in a blowout victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Teams currently have the freedom to travel when they choose for international games.

 

 It is a topic that is especially important given the NFL's international expansion as the league will play a record nine international games in 2026. The NFL currently has the ability to play up to 11 games outside of North America, including a yearly contest at Wembley Stadium involving the Jaguars based on the current agreement with the NFLPA.

 What appears to matter to players is the accommodations teams dedicated to travel on domestic and international trips. In February, ESPN obtained the results of the NFLPA's 2026 report cards , which are anonymous surveys done annually that include grades on categories with everything from the team's facilities to treatment of families to head coach and general manager.

 In the newest NFLPA surveys, the 49ers received a C-plus in the team travel category and the Rams a B. The Steelers, Philadelphia Eagles and New England Patriots were the only three teams to receive an F. The Miami Dolphins received an A, the highest grade in the category. Among the top four teams in the category -- the Dolphins (A),  New Orleans Saints (A-minus), Seattle Seahawks (A-minus) and Denver Broncos  (A-minus) -- there were common themes about what makes for a positive team travel experience: having personal space and leg room on a flight (including the ability to recline seats to a laying position), the condition of the plane, the amenities available and advance notice given for the team travel schedule. 

 The report cards are based on a survey of 1,759 players (around 80% of the NFL) across the league, administered from Nov. 3 to Dec. 11, 2025.

 This is the fourth year the NFLPA has conducted these surveys. ESPN spoke with more than a dozen players, coaches and front office executives about "team travel" and the feedback that serves as the basis for the NFLPA's grades.

 Linebacker Kaden Elliss , who reunited with the Saints after three seasons with the  Atlanta Falcons , said he doesn't necessarily need "luxury all the time where you go" when traveling with the team, but that it's nice to feel taken care of by the organization on the road.

 "It is nice to know that you give everything you can, you put everything you can into it and it's nice to know and it's very apparent when you have an owner that's willing to do the same," Elliss said. "I think [Saints owner Gayle Benson] just has a really awesome track record of, like, we're going to make sure we want to be the best and we're going to be the best in everything we do, including travel."

 

 

 THE LIE-FLAT SEATS were not the reason Niners wide receiver Mike Evans decided to sign with the 49ers in free agency. But it certainly didn't hurt. In early March, Evans reached out to longtime Niners tight end George Kittle to learn more about how the team is run. Among the many topics that came up was plane seating and how the team travels.

 "He was a big fan of how we traveled with the lay down [seats] stuff and he's like, "Yep, I never had that,'" Kittle said. "And I was like, 'It's crazy, but welcome to the 49ers.'"

 Evans got an early taste of what travel with the Niners will look like when he and his teammates opened the season in Melbourne. Though the NFL began its international series in 2007, this trip required the longest flight NFL teams have ever taken for a regular-season game.

 The two teams handled it differently, with the 49ers landing a week before to practice there. Los Angeles spent almost the same amount of time in the air (29 hours) than on the ground (36 hours) in Melbourne. Although the teams made the final decisions, both head coaches said they talked to players about how they would handle the travel.

 While in Melbourne, 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey and fullback Kyle Juszczyk spent time at the Saint Haven Club, a spa less than a mile away from their hotel.

 There, the team arranged for players to have access to everything from hyperbaric chambers to red light to hot and cold plunge to massage to acupuncture -- "literally everything" the team needed to take care of their bodies almost 8,000 miles from home, Juszczyk said.

 "Honestly, we've had more out here than we usually have [at home]," 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa said.

 The setup was part of the work the NFL and the 49ers did for months in an attempt to make sure the athletes were as prepared as possible to spend their week of travel on the road.

 The 49ers are no strangers to a weeklong stay, as it is something they've done in recent years to acclimate to their travel schedules. In 2022, the Niners spent time in Colorado Springs, Colorado, before playing in Mexico City in an effort to adjust to the altitude. They'll do that again before their Mexico City game against the Vikings in Week 11. San Francisco has also done the same at IMG Academy in Florida (2019) and The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia (2020, '21 and '22).

 

 When the Steelers flew to Dublin for their Week 4 game last season, they opted to fly on the overnight Thursday to arrive Friday morning before the Sunday game. In comparison, the Jaguars spent the week before they played the Rams last year at a hotel outside of London. 

 The Steelers went straight to the hotel from the airport with a brief window to settle in before practicing at the field on the property. 

 Steelers coaches, a player said, told the players not to fall asleep on the Friday after they landed, a task the player found challenging.

 That player had previously played in an international game with another team and spent the week in Europe. On that trip, the player said he had a lie-flat seat on the plane.

 "I think if they're going to have us travel to the other side of the [world] to produce them some money, then I think they should do us the common courtesy to letting us stay the whole week so we can at least experience the place that we're traveling to," he said. "Y'all want us to make so much money for y'all, but y'all don't care about us enough to say, 'OK, well we're going to take y'all out there, then guess what? We're going to take care of y'all.'

 "I don't know if it's the league owners or if it's the NFL as a whole, but the NFL's always been like that. It's more about how they're viewed outwardly than how we view them inwardly." 

 

 
 THOUGH INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL has been top of mind given the recent trip to Melbourne and the Dallas Cowboys ' Week 3 contest to Rio de Janeiro against the Baltimore Ravens , even domestic travel has its challenges.

title: QB Malik Willis takes blame for five-sack Dolphins debut
summary: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Willis still has his 'total confidence and faith' after a rough debut for Miami.
full_text:
LAS VEGAS -- Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis might be sore after his first start for his new team.

 Willis was pressured 17 times in Sunday's 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders , and was sacked five times as the Raiders defense took advantage of obvious passing situations in the second half.

 He leaves his Dolphins regular season debut tied with Tyler Shough and Deshaun Watson for the most sacks taken in the NFL this week, but he was quick to accept all the blame for what he called a "quarterback stat."

 

 "I've got to watch the tape, but you can just blame them all on me," Willis said after the game. "I've got to take care of the ball and I've got to do right by my offensive line and get the ball out and that's everybody. It takes all 11. We got to make sure the receivers are in the right spot, got to make sure I'm doing the right thing. We got to make sure our backs are doing the right thing and it all works together -- but you can blame the sacks on me.

 "Sacks are a quarterback stat and I'm going to take the O-line out after that."

 Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 220 yards and an interception Sunday, adding a 14-yard rushing touchdown that proved to be Miami's lone touchdown of the day. Trailing by multiple scores, the Dolphins' offense almost exclusively passed the ball in the second half and Las Vegas' pass rushers pinned their ears back as a result.

 When facing pressure, Willis completed 5-of-9 passes for 113 yards, notching a 100.5 passer rating with a completion percentage over expectation of 5.9%.

 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Willis still has his "total confidence and faith," adding that he thought his quarterback made great plays with his legs and arm. But Miami's offense as a whole, he said, was "inconsistent."

 "Part of the plan to win was to keep the ball moving forward," he said. "I thought the penalties killed us. They forced us into a lot of passing situations that were crucial that you really don't want to be in against that team ... Just like most of the units today, I thought it was inconsistent and that's how we kind of played the game today."

 

 Throughout the game, Miami struggled to find easy completions for Willis and he spent an extraordinary amount of time trying to keep plays alive in the backfield in search of an open receiver.

 Willis finished with an average time to throw of 3.21 seconds, the fourth-longest time of any quarterback in Week 1. He also led the NFL this week with an average air yards per attempt of 13.6 yards, and was off target on 22% of his throws, which was the fourth-highest percentage in the league this week.

 He did find success when targeting rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas , who finished with a game-high 94 yards on five catches.

 "I think he's been doing a great job trying to continue to learn and get better," Willis said of Douglas. "He's had a great camp and learned a lot from OTAs and I think he's doing a great job of wanting to get better and wanting to be out there and make plays ... I think (offensive coordinator) Bobby (Slowik) put him in a position to get a couple going and I think it just worked out that way for today."

 The Dolphins will remain on the west coast, practicing in Northern California this week ahead of their Week 2 game against the San Francisco 49ers (4:25 p.m., E.T., FOX).

 Both Hafley and Willis said the trip provides a distraction-free opportunity for players to bond and lock into their on-field assignments while they prepare for 49ers defense that held the Los Angeles Rams to 290 yards of offense in Week 1.

title: New York Jets, Giants both start 1-0 for first time since 2009
summary: The summer of New York is gaining strength as the Jets and Giants both started off their respective NFL seasons hot.
full_text:
The summer of New York is gaining strength in its late stages.

 

 The New York Giants and New York Jets both won their Week 1 matchups Sunday. The Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on "Sunday Night Football," and the Jets beat the Tennessee Titans 23-10 earlier in the day.

 Victories for both of New York's NFL teams in Week 1 are a rare sight. This is the first time the Giants and Jets have each started a campaign 1-0 since 2009, according to ESPN Research. It's also the first time they've both been above .500 at any point of a season since Week 14 in 2022.

 

 The other team in New York, the Buffalo Bills , won its opener as well, defeating the Houston Texans 36-31 . That makes all three teams undefeated in Week 1 for the first time since 2008.

 A hot start for the two current MetLife Stadium tenants brought opposite outcomes in 2009.

 Two seasons after a Super Bowl victory, the Giants began 5-0 in their final season at Giant Stadium. They then lost four straight games and split wins and losses from Week 11 to 16. The final defeat coincided with a Cowboys win that eliminated the Giants from playoff contention for the first time since 2004.

 Rex Ryan began his first season as Jets head coach in 2009, and two months in, it looked like the Jets might have to find a new leader. They had a 4-6 record after a 3-0 start to the year. It would mark their worst stretch of the season as the Jets won five of their next six games to reach the playoffs.

 New York would beat the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC wild-card round. The Jets then took down No. 2-seeded Los Angeles Chargers in the divisional round to reach the conference championship game for the first time since 1998. The No. 1-seeded Indianapolis Colts ended the Jets' run, but New York would be back in the conference final the following season. It hasn't made the playoffs since.

 Week 2 pits the Jets and Giants against two NFC teams. The Jets host the Green Bay Packers , while the Giants visit the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football" (8:15 ET on ABC/ESPN).

 Regardless of the outcomes, Jets and Giants fans will always be able to brag about Week 1.

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Steelers QB, who is entering his 22nd season in the league, is chasing records, and ESPN will be chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots .

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

 

 That Rodgers is still chasing records in 2026 is somewhat of a surprise after he suggested at times during the 2025 season that he was nearing the end of his career.

 "It's the twilight of my career," he said after beating the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland on Oct. 5, 2025. "I used to say five, six, seven years ago, I was on the back nine. But I'm teeing off on 18 right now."

 In that win, Rodgers made two more noteworthy entries into the record books: most completions of 50-plus yards and second quarterback in NFL history to throw 60 or more touchdown passes against multiple franchises.

 But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that ever-growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Maybe it took him a couple of shots to reach the green, or maybe he took his time finding his shot on the fairway. Either way, the 18th hole is in sight, and Rodgers is crouched in front of his ball, squaring up the putt.

 "I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said on the first day of training camp. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired. And I talked to the wife, and she said you can do one more year. I said, 'We'll see if it works out.' And it kind of all came together."

 Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 1 he has appeared in 288), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 1, he has 232) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes (he only threw for 1 in Week 1). And after Week 1, he needs 3,505 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo and lines up his putt on the 18th green. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 

 
 Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INTs, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1:  Steelers 20, Falcons 13 
 Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard 
 Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth  for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the  Green Bay Packers , per ESPN Research.

 After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

 "No, keep doing it," Rodgers said, urging his coach to keep calling passes. "Keep doing it."

 And although Rodgers and the Steelers got the win, the quarterback struggled under the pressure from the Falcons' front. He completed 3 of 12 attempts under pressure and was sacked twice. And continuing the trend from last season, Rodgers was also 3-of-12 on throws of 15 or more air yards. Some of those incompletions, though, were the result of drops by his receivers.

 "I liked the plan from Mike," Rodgers said. "I liked the playcalling. We took some shots. I felt like we had really close to having one of those really good games. If we come down with a couple of those, it obviously looks a little different on the scoreboard and stat sheet and stuff, but love my guys, love  DK [Metcalf] .
